title: Commanders may add help at running back after Jeremy McNichols's foot injury
summary: The Commanders may need to add some help at running back this week.
full_text: The Commanders may need to add some help at running back this week. Jeremy McNichols hurt his foot in Sunday night's win over the Eagles and head coach Dan Quinn said at a Monday press conference that there is concern about the injury being a significant one. "They're gonna do some more scans as we get through tomorrow ," Quinn said, via the team's website. "But it's enough that we're concerned today. I'll give you an update as it goes to Wednesday, but it's something that the team for sure is concerned with." Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on injured reserve and must miss at least two more games before he'll be eligible to return in Week 11. Quinn said the two injuries make an addition "something that we'll have to discuss" in the coming days. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler are the healthy backs on the 53-man roster. Craig Reynolds and Devin Neal are on the practice squad.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bengals DE Cashius Howell had wrist surgery
summary: The Bengals are set to be without rookie defensive end Cashius Howell in the coming weeks.
full_text: The Bengals are set to be without rookie defensive end Cashius Howell in the coming weeks. Head coach Zac Taylor said at a Monday press conference that Howell had wrist surgery after being injured in Sunday's overtime win over the Titans. Taylor did not specify a timeline for the second-round pick's return, but the Bengals have not put Howell on injured reserve at this point so that suggests they think he can return without missing four games. Howell has played around 40 percent of the defensive snaps this season. He has six tackles, two tackles for loss, a sack and five quarterback hits. With Howell out of action, 2025 first-round pick Shemar Stewart could see more playing time. Stewart played on Sunday, but was a healthy scratch the week before due to the other options at defensive end in Cincinnati.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike Macdonald: We lost in all three phases
summary: Monday night's game in Seattle featured a pair of 2025 NFC playoff teams who would like to be back in the postseason this year and it ended with the Bears celebrating a 34-17 win over the defending Super Bowl champions.
full_text: Monday night's game in Seattle featured a pair of 2025 NFC playoff teams who would like to be back in the postseason this year and it ended with the Bears celebrating a 34-17 win over the defending Super Bowl champions. The Seahawks had made it a three-point game early in the fourth quarter, but a 39-yard screen pass to Kalif Raymond converted a key Bears third down on the next drive and the roof caved in on the Seahawks from there. The Bears ended the night with 111 more offensive yards than the Seahawks and their defense thwarted Seattle on 10 of their 11 third down attempts over the course of the night, which led Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald to say after the game that "there's no other way to sugarcoat" the way his team got beat. Seahawks kicker Jason Myers missed an extra point and had a field goal blocked and the Seahawks committed several personal fouls to add to their woes on a night when the Bears were clearly better across the board. "They made it happen, and we didn't," Macdonald said, via the team's website. "It's a team effort; we lost as a team. In all three phases, we can have better plans, we can coach it better, prepare our players better, and we can play better. We'll go back to work and go attack the heck out of it. The margins in our league are too small, and when you don't do the things that it takes to win, that's how a game like that shapes up. It was a team effort. We lost in all three phases ." The Seahawks overwhelmed the Chiefs in a Week 7 win, but Monday night was the kind of step back that explains why they're 4-4 on the season. Having it happen against another NFC contender at home makes the blow more painful and Macdonald said the Seahawks "have some work to do" if they're going to position themselves for another run at the end of this season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Wil Lutz has made 113 straight extra points, most in the NFL since the 2015 rule change
summary: It's been three years since Broncos kicker Wil Lutz missed an extra point.
full_text: It's been three years since Broncos kicker Wil Lutz missed an extra point. After hitting both his extra points in Sunday's win over the Chiefs, Lutz has now made 113 consecutive extra points without a miss. That's the longest streak in the NFL since the 2015 rule change that moved extra points back by 13 yards. The previous record of 112 consecutive extra points was set by Justin Tucker with the Ravens. “I’ve [said] a hundred times how much I value the extra point . I value them a lot. But my goal isn’t to break the record, it’s to make every one the rest of the season, so whatever that number is at the end of the season," Lutz told Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette . Lutz's last missed an extra point when he doinked one off the upright against the Bills on November 11, 2023. Lutz made up for that with the game-winning field goal as time expired in a 24-22 victory. The 32-year-old Lutz first entered the NFL as an undrafted rookie in 2016 with the Ravens, who weren't seriously considering him for a roster spot as they had Tucker, who was the best kicker in the NFL at the time. But Lutz impressed then-Ravens coach John Harbaugh enough that when it came time to cut Lutz at the end of the preseason, Harbaugh personally called then-Saints coach Sean Payton to recommend Lutz. Payton brought Lutz to New Orleans, and then traded for Lutz when Payton became coach of the Broncos. By having faith in Lutz, Payton has ensured that he'll have nothing to worry about on extra points.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jim Harbaugh: I want Khalil Mack to be here and Khalil Mack wants to be here
summary: Jim Harbaugh shot down a question about the Chargers potentially trading defensive lineman Khalil Mack before next week's deadline.
full_text: Jim Harbaugh shot down a question about the Chargers potentially trading defensive lineman Khalil Mack before next week's deadline. “I want Khalil Mack here," Harbaugh said. "Khalil Mack wants to be here. He’s one of the pillars of our team.” Harbaugh said he isn't even thinking about the November 10 trade deadline and is instead looking to get ready to play the Texans this week. Harbaugh said General Manager Joe Hortiz and Assistant General Manager Chad Alexander might be looking at trades, but he isn't. "I'm focused on the Texans. I know Joe, Chad, our organization are always looking to improve the team," Harbaugh said. "I'm focused on getting it turned, forging ahead, striving in every way to play winning football." The 0-7 Chargers are the NFL's only winless team, and at this point there's no trade that could make them playoff contenders in 2026. So whether Harbaugh is thinking about it or not, it seems likely that the Chargers would be willing to trade a player on their roster for a draft pick, if they get a decent offer in the next week.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jeffery Simmons: Felt great to get my first sack as a Chicago Bear
summary: "The emotions, especially during the national anthem, the emotions were coming and coming," Simmons said.
full_text: It didn't take long for Jeffery Simmons to get his first sack as a Bear. Simmons took Sam Darnold down on the Seahawks' fourth offensive play on Monday night, and he said afterward that as soon as he saw that they were blocking him one-on-one, he knew a big play was coming. "If you block me one-on-one, I need to win the one-on-one. If I don't win a one-on-one, the coaches should be on me. I hold myself to a high standard," Simmons said. "It felt great to get my first sack as a Chicago Bear in my first game." Simmons always drew a lot of double teams during his All-Pro seasons with the Titans, and he drew plenty on Monday night in his first game since the Titans traded him to the Bears as well. He said he challenged his fellow Bears defensive linemen to take advantage of it when he was getting double teamed. "If I'm getting a double team, I expect them to win their single block," Simmons said. "We don't need to blitz. I feel like if we can win at the line of scrimmage without the blitzes, that makes the guys' jobs on the back end that much easier." Simmons played 55 defensive snaps, by far the most of any Bear in the game. He played 87 percent of the Bears' defensive plays, which was exactly his snap count percentage for the Titans this season before he was traded. The Bears made a big investment in Simmons, trading two first-round draft picks for him, and they got a big return immediately. In the moments before kickoff, Simmons said he was trying to keep his emotions in check by reminding himself, "It's just football." But it was hard not to be emotional. "The emotions, especially during the national anthem, the emotions were coming and coming," Simmons said. Simmons said after the game that it means a lot to him to be playing meaningful football. The Titans are 1-7 and the Bears are 6-2 and Simmons knows the blockbuster trade was an opportunity for him to compete for a Super Bowl.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Ravens K Tyler Loop could be headed for injured reserve with groin injury
summary: When it comes to injuries, the Ravens have far bigger issues than having a healthy kicker.
full_text: ' When it comes to injuries, the Ravens have far bigger issues than having a healthy kicker. Still, their kicker isn't healthy. Coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Monday that Tyler Loop has "been dealing with something," and that he could "potentially may go on IR." If he has been dealing with something, the Ravens haven't disclosed it. Loop had appeared on none of the injury reports issued through eight weeks of the 2026 season. The first injury report released in advance of Thursday night's game against the Jaguars reveals that Loop has a right groin injury. Loop missed a field goal in Buffalo on Sunday, his fourth of the season. Jake Moody is currently on the Baltimore practice squad. He'd presumably be signed to the 53-man roster if/when Loop ends up on injured reserve.
author: Mike Florio

title: Monday Night Football: Jeffery Simmons, Caleb Williams lead Bears to 34-17 rout of Seahawks
summary: The Bears acquired Simmons on Thursday, and he had six tackles and a sack, and Williams threw for 247 yards.
full_text: Welcome to Chicago, Jeffery Simmons. Simmons had a dominate debut with the Bears, who acquired him from the Titans on Thursday. He made a team-leading six tackles, with a sack, a pass defensed and two tackles for loss, and the Bears limited the Seahawks to 252 yards. The Bears rolled to a 34-17 victory over the Seahawks on Monday night. Chicago is 6-2, and the defending champions fell to 4-4. The Seahawks didn't help their cause, with three unnecessary roughness penalties in the second half, including two on special teams. Kicker Jason Myers missed an extra point and had a 33-yard field goal blocked. Sam Darnold threw an interception on a pass tipped by Austin Booker and picked by James Lynch, who returned it 16 yards to the Seattle 6. The Seahawks quarterback was sacked three times and hit six, including a sack and three quarterback hits by defensive lineman Montez Sweat. Darnold never seemed comfortable against Simmons, Sweat and the Bears defense, as the Seahawks went 1-for-11 on third down. Star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba kept Seattle in it in the first half and finished with six receptions for 118 yards and a touchdown. Darnold was 17-of-34 for 188 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. The Seahawks had five three-and-outs and five punts against Dennis Allen's defense. The Bears gained 363 yards against the Seahawks vaunted defensive unit, with Caleb Williams going 24-of-34 for 247 yards and a touchdown. D'Andre Swift had second-half touchdown runs of 1, 5 and 5 and finished with 27 carries for 69 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bears answer Seahawks, up lead to 27-17
summary: The Bears have had an answer for the Seahawks all night.
full_text: ' The Bears have had an answer for the Seahawks all night. They did again midway through the fourth quarter. After the Seahawks closed to within three points with 11:46 left, the Bears scored their own touchdown with 8:28 left. D'Andre Swift's 5-yard touchdown run has the Bears back on top by two scores, 27-17. The Seahawks shot themselves in the foot on the kickoff after Cooper Kupp's touchdown catch. Mike Morris was called for unnecessary roughness after pushing Bears returner Zavion Thomas out of bounds. Six plays later, the Bears were in the end zone. The Seahawks had a chance to get off the field, with the Bears facing a third-and-9 at the Seattle 44. Kalif Raymond, though, had a 39-yard run around the right end before Nehemiah Pritchett saved — if only briefly — the touchdown. Swift walked in on the next play. The Bears have outgained the Seahawks 344 to 193.
author: Charean Williams

title: Seahawks convert Bears' fumble, now trail only 20-17
summary: The Bears let the Seahawks back in the game when tight end Colston Loveland fumbled.
full_text: '' The Bears let the Seahawks back in the game when tight end Colston Loveland fumbled. Seahawks defensive lineman DeMarcus Lawrence forced the fumble and recovered it at the Chicago 25. The turnover came three plays after Bears defensive lineman Austin Booker blocked the 33-yard field-goal attempt of Jason Myers. The Seahawks took advantage of the takeaway, going 25 yards in three plays. Cam Lewis' interception of Sam Darnold in the end zone was negated by Clark Phillips' defensive holding penalty. Jadarian Price had runs of 9 and 4 yards sandwiched between Phillips' penalty, and Cooper Kupp scored on a 7-yard reception. On the 2-point try, Tory Horton caught Darnold's pass in the end zone. The Seahawks trail only 20-17 with 11:46 remaining in the fourth quarter.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jacoby Brissett becomes an obvious trade candidate
summary: By sending eight-game starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett all the way to No. 3 on the depth chart, the Cardinals have sent a clear message to the rest of the league, eight days from the trade deadline.
full_text: '' By sending eight-game starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett all the way to No. 3 on the depth chart, the Cardinals have sent a clear message to the rest of the league, eight days from the trade deadline. Make us an offer. The question becomes whether anyone will, and whether based on the games to be played in Week 9 anyone will need to. Currently, the Ravens are scrambling to find healthy bodies at the position — and quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork was the quarterback coach in Arizona last year, when Brissett started 12 games. Any other contender could be one snap away from needing Brissett. And the Vikings, who should be (even if they aren't) thinking about potential upgrades to Kyler Murray, could make the Cardinals a call. Beyond teams that could be in a position to consider Brissett as the starter are contenders who may not be thrilled with their current primary backups. In L.A., for example, it could make sense to have a more experienced understudy to Matthew Stafford for the stretch run. Brissett's new contract had most of the paid out as a signing bonus; his base salary is a very affordable $1.3 million. Now in his eleventh season, Brissett has played for six teams: the Patriots (twice), the Colts, the Dolphins, the Browns, the Commanders, and the Cardinals. He has 109 regular-season appearances, with 73 starts.
author: Mike Florio

title: D'Andre Swift's TD run gives Bears a 20-9 lead on Seahawks
summary: The Bears have taken control in Chicago.
full_text: The Bears have taken control in Chicago. They put together a 10-play, 69-yard touchdown drive after both teams opened the second half by going three-and-out. D'Andre Swift's 1-yard touchdown run, and Cairo Santos' PAT have the Bears leading 20-9 with 5:38 remaining in the third quarter. Rome Odunze had catches of 23 and 22 yards to get the drive going. Quarterback Caleb Williams is now 22-of-31 for 227 yards and a touchdown. Odunze has four catches for 87 yards, and Luther Burden has seven catches for 56 yards. Swift has 16 carries for 39 yards and a touchdown. Seahawks defensive lineman Leonard Williams was injured on a tackle of running back Roschon Johnson for no gain with 7:37 left in the third quarter. He is in the sideline medical tent, but the Seahawks have not updated his injury.
author: Charean Williams

title: Most Cowboys players left facility on Monday before locker-room media availability
summary: The day after an embarrassing home loss to the Cardinals — who have never lost at AT&T Stadium — many of the Cowboys' players skipped a session with the media covering the team.
full_text: The day after an embarrassing home loss to the Cardinals — who have never lost at AT&T Stadium — many of the Cowboys' players skipped a session with the media covering the team. "The Cowboys just had locker room availability, but majority of roster left the facility before we got in there ," Jon Machota of The Athletic said. "No players were interviewed. Can’t say I remember that happening before." There's an explanation, as there often is. Via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News , the "player programs ended earlier than scheduled , which is why the locker room was almost empty during media availability." Making players available in the locker room is one of the basic weekly obligations for all teams. Whatever the reason, it's likely few were inclined to say anything about Sunday's game. Especially since the Cowboys blew a 14-point lead at home for the first time in franchise history. Against a two-win team that has inexplicably owned the Cowboys in recent years.
author: Mike Florio

title: Monday Night Football: Bears lead Seahawks 13-9 at halftime
summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught a 43-yard touchdown with 30 seconds left in the half to draw Seattle closer.
full_text: '' Defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons made his Bears debut on Monday night, while left guard Quenton Nelson made his Seahawks debut. The teams traded for what they considered a missing piece last week. Simmons has had an immediate impact with five tackles, a sack and two tackles for loss. The Bears held the Seahawks to six first downs and 114 yards, most of it coming on the final drive of the half, and allowed Seattle to convert only 1-of-6 third downs. Seahawks punter Michael Dickson was busy, with four punts. The Bears lead 13-9 at halftime. Chicago's opening possession went 80 yards in 17 plays and lasted 8 minutes and 32 seconds, the Bears’ 11th drive of 5-plus minutes this season. Luther Burden scored on a 1-yard touchdown reception. Cairo Santos kicked field goals of 44 and 38. The Bears had 208 yards, with Caleb Williams going 17-of-25 for 165 yards and a touchdown. Luther Burden has six catches for 53 yards and a touchdown, but D'Andre Swift has only 26 yards on 11 carries. Star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba has kept the Seahawks in it, with 92 yards and a touchdown on four catches. The Seahawks trailed 13-3 when Smith-Njigba caught a 43-yard touchdown pass with 30 seconds left in the half. Jason Myers, though, missed the extra point. He kicked a 27-yard field goal early in the second quarter. The Seahawks had only 29 yards on four drives in their first half to go with scoring drives of 45 and 71 yards. Sam Darnold is 7-of-15 for 94 yards and a touchdown. Jadarian Price has four carries for 13 yards in his return, and Zach Charbonnet has three carries for 7 yards in his 2026 debut. Price and Charbonnet are the only other players with a reception besides Smith-Njigba, combining for three receptions for 2 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Sean McVay won't say much about the "soreness" in Matthew Stafford's throwing arm
summary: Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford threw only 25 passes on Sunday.
full_text: Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford threw only 25 passes on Sunday. But he emerged from the win over the Chargers with some sort of arm issue. Stafford was spotted after the game with ice on his throwing arm. Coach Sean McVay didn't say much when asked about it on Monday. “You'll have to talk to him about that," McVay told reporters. "He's had some soreness there. I think he'd be better equipped once you guys talk to him to answer that. I can't attest to stuff that I'm not necessarily aware of.” If it's an issue, McVay will be aware of it soon. Come Wednesday, the Rams will be filing their first practice report in advance of Sunday's game at Washington. If Stafford is getting any treatment on the arm, or if he doesn't fully participate in practice, he'll be listed. Stafford has, of course, a long history of playing through anything and everything. Some ice on his arm won't keep him from playing.
author: Mike Florio

title: Nick Sirianni: Eagles will stick with Tanner McKee, Sean Mannion despite offensive woes
summary: The Eagles have lost six in a row and rank 30th in the NFL in points per game, but Nick Sirianni said Monday that he isn't making a change at offensive coordinator or quarterback.
full_text: The Eagles have lost six in a row and rank 30th in the NFL in points per game, but Nick Sirianni said Monday that he isn't making a change at offensive coordinator or quarterback. Sean Mannion will continue to call plays, and Tanner McKee will remain the starting quarterback with Jalen Hurts out for the year. "I'm not making any changes there," Sirianni said about his coaching staff, via Tim McManus of ESPN. "It is on all of us to figure out how to get things going in the right direction. Obviously, right now they're not. But again, this is the ultimate team game, and we're in the problem-solving business. Right now, we have to find answers to help us get going offensively. Again, that brunt falls on myself; that falls on Sean; and we're going to do everything we can to get ourselves out of this." The first-year playcaller has had to make do without Hurts, right tackle Lane Johnson, center Cam Jurgens, running back Saquon Barkley and wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks at times this season. Hurts played five games before going on injured reserve with blood clots; Johnson retired after three games; Jurgens played four games with the Eagles before a trade to the Ravens; Barkley has missed two games and been limited in others with injuries; Smith has missed four games with a hamstring injury; and Wicks has missed two games with an ankle injury. The Eagles are averaging 17.1 points a game. McKee has started the past three games, completing 63.2 percent of his passes for 639 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions. "Tanner's our guy. We're not making any changes there," Sirianni said. "Again, how do we find solutions? That could be within scheme; that could be within how our schedule is, practice plays. Everything's on the table for us in that aspect. But right now, this is where we are, and we're trying to find solutions there. We're looking at everything as far as what we can do differently as coaches." McKee's backup, Joe Milton, only arrived in Philadelphia on Oct. 16, signing from the Cowboys' practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Bears' 17-play drive on their opening possession gives them a 7-0 lead
summary: The Bears had an almost perfect drive to open Monday Night Football.
full_text: The Bears had an almost perfect drive to open Monday Night Football. After the Bears forced the Seahawks to go three-and-out, Michael Dickson had a punt downed inside the 5-yard line only to have Rodney Thomas inexplicably slide into the ball and into the end zone for a touchback. The Bears then went 80 yards in 17 plays. It was the most plays the Seahawks have allowed on a drive this season. The drive lasted 8 minutes and 32 seconds, the Bears' 11th drive of 5-plus minutes this season. The Bears were 3-of-4 on third down and converted a fourth-and-1 on D'Andre Swift's 5-yard run from their own 49. Luther Burden scored the touchdown on a 1-yard touchdown pass from Caleb Williams, who was 8-of-10 for 58 yards. Burden had four catches for 23 yards and tight end Colston Loveland three catches for 27 yards. The Bears lead 7-0.
author: Charean Williams

title: QB Joe Fagnano estimated as limited in Ravens' practice with ankle injury
summary: The Ravens know Lamar Jackson (right thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) won't play Thursday night.
full_text: ' The Ravens know Lamar Jackson (right thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) won't play Thursday night. They hope third-string rookie Joe Fagnano will. Fagnano, who played 40 snaps in his debut after Jackson and Huntley left with injuries Sunday, has an ankle injury. The Ravens listed him as a limited participant in their walk-through practice. "To Joe's credit, he's kind of fighting through a couple things he's dealing with," coach Jesse Minter said Monday. "But expect him to have a chance to play on Thursday." The Ravens signed quarterback Austin Reed to their practice squad on Monday. The Ravens, who play the Jaguars on Thursday, listed defensive lineman Calais Campbell (rest), safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) and kicker Tyler Loop (right groin) as non-participants. Jake Moody is in line to kick for the Ravens on Thursday night. Outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson (ribs/finger), running back Justice Hill (groin), offensive guard Vega Ioane (knee), nose tackle John Jenkins (knee), offensive tackle Roger Rosengarten (ankle), offensive guard John Simpson (back), linebacker Roquan Smith (foot) and offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) were estimated as limited. Tight end Matthew Hibner (hand), running back Adam Randall (neck) and cornerback Nate Wiggins (stringer) were full participants.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jaguars estimate DE Travon Walker as a non-participant Monday
summary: Jaguars defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton (torn quad) and safety Eric Murray (elbow) are out for the season.
full_text: Jaguars defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton (torn quad) and safety Eric Murray (elbow) are out for the season. They were two of four players on the team's roster listed as non-participants on Monday's injury report. The Jaguars did not practice but were required to issue an injury report ahead of Thursday night's game against the Ravens. Running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) and defensive end Travon Walker (rib) were also listed as non-participants. Walker had his third sack of the season in Sunday's win over the Colts but played a season-low 28 snaps. Offensive lineman Ezra Cleveland (knee/ankle), linebacker Branson Combs (shoulder), safety Antonio Johnson (ankle), cornerback Jarrian Jones (ankle), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) and running back Chris Rodriguez Jr. (hand) were listed as limited.
author: Charean Williams

title: Chargers TE David Njoku is expected to return to practice this week
summary: Chargers tight end David Njoku likely will return to practice this week, coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday.
full_text: Chargers tight end David Njoku likely will return to practice this week, coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday. Njoku, 30, went on injured reserve after injuring his fibula in Week 2 and missed the past five games. He caught six of eight targets for 67 yards and no touchdowns before his injury. The Chargers have leaned on Oronde Gadsden and Charlie Kolar in Njoku's absence. In his 10th season, Njoku has totaled 390 catches for 4,129 yards and 34 touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Monday Night Football: Zach Charbonnet, Jadarian Price are active for Seahawks vs. Bears
summary: The Seahawks will officially have running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price for Monday Night Football.
full_text: '' The Seahawks will officially have running backs Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price for Monday Night Football. Both players are active. Charbonnet will make his 2026 debut after returning from a torn ACL that ended his season in the divisional round of the playoffs in January. He set career highs in 2025 with 730 rushing yards and a team-high 12 touchdowns. The Seahawks activated Price from injured reserve on Monday, and he is active for the first time since Week 3, when he injured his chest. He has 32 touches for 140 yards and two fumbles. Offensive guard Quenton Nelson will make his Seattle debut after a trade from Indianapolis this week. He will play left guard with Grey Zabel moving to right guard. The Seahawks won't have outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu, who was doubtful with an ankle injury, or back up quarterback Drew Lock, who was questionable with a right elbow injury. Jalen Milroe will backup Sam Darnold, with Lock designated as the emergency third quarterback. Wide receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee), offensive tackle Charles Cross (ankle), running back Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring), nose tackle Brandon Pili (back) and offensive guard Beau Stephens are the team's other inactives. The Bears won't have cornerback Malik Muhammad (toe). He was limited in practice and given a questionable injury designation. The Bears' other inactives are running back Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), quarterback Case Keenum, defensive tackle Jayden Loving, offensive lineman Jordan McFadden and defensive tackle Jordan van den Berg.
author: Charean Williams

title: Cowboys DBs Caleb Downs, P.J. Locke in concussion protocol
summary: The Cowboys had injury to go with the insult of Sunday's 33-30 meltdown overtime loss to the Cardinals.
full_text: The Cowboys had injury to go with the insult of Sunday's 33-30 meltdown overtime loss to the Cardinals. Coach Brian Schottenheimer said defensive back Caleb Downs and safety P.J. Locke are both in concussion protocol. Downs, a first-round rookie, has played 509 defensive snaps — 92 percent — and 45 on special teams. He has totaled 52 tackles, a sack, a pass defensed and two forced fumbles. Locke just returned from injured reserve, missing five games with a foot injury. He returned to practice Oct. 23. Schottenheimer also said outside linebacker Malachi Lawrence has an ankle injury "that might be a little bit longer" to recover from. Lawrence, the team's other first-round rookie, has played 226 defensive snaps and 40 in special teams. He has totaled 13 tackles, a sack and two passes defensed.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ravens QB Joe Fagnano "fighting through a couple things," has "a chance" to play Thursday
summary: The Ravens are short on healthy quarterbacks with Thursday's game against the Jaguars on the horizon.
full_text: ' The Ravens are short on healthy quarterbacks with Thursday's game against the Jaguars on the horizon. Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve with a thumb injury that requires surgery and could end his season. Tyler Huntley had to leave Sunday's game as well and is dealing with a toe injury that has Joe Fagnano in line to make his first NFL start. Fagnano's availability sounds like less than a sure thing, however. He took a low hit from Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver in the second half of the Ravens loss and head coach Jesse Minter didn't commit to him making the start this week. "We’re kinda working through some things," Minter said. "To Joe’s credit, he’s kinda fighting through a couple things. Expect him to have a chance to play Thursday." The Ravens signed Austin Reed to their practice squad on Monday and he could find himself in the mix for playing time during his first days with the team.
author: Josh Alper

title: Todd Monken expects to see sacks start to "pile up" for Jared Verse
summary: Browns defensive end Jared Verse made a fair amount of noise heading into Sunday's game against the Steelers, but he was mostly silent on the field in Pittsburgh.
full_text: Browns defensive end Jared Verse made a fair amount of noise heading into Sunday's game against the Steelers, but he was mostly silent on the field in Pittsburgh. Verse had one tackle in the 27-6 Steelers win and that continued the slow start to his Browns tenure. Verse had 8.5 sacks and 34 quarterback hits in 20 total games for the Rams in 2025, but had no sacks and six quarterback hits since coming to Cleveland in the Myles Garrett trade. At a Monday press conference, Browns head coach Todd Monken was asked about the lack of splash plays and whether the expectations for immediate impact were unrealistic. Monken preached patience while expressing confidence that bigger things are coming for Verse. “Well, I think it’s too early to say anything. I mean, I love the way Jared works every day since he’s come here, just like all of our guys, he loves to work," Monken said, via a transcript from the team. "He likes being on the field and practicing. And I think it’s a matter of adapting to our style, which is, you know, there are some things that aren’t as similar to what he was used to doing with the Rams and the attack style. And I think it’s just a matter of time before, you know, he really gets comfortable in what we’re doing defensively. And it’s unfair to compare him to Myles Garrett. I think that’s always been unfair. Myles is in an elite category of his own. That’s okay. I mean, that’s who he is. But we just need Jared to be the best version of Jared, and I think we’re going to continue to see growth there. And again, what will help us? Be ahead in games, force the other team to throw it, and I think you’ll start to see his sacks start to pile up.” The Browns have a 5-3 record despite the lack of contributions from Verse, but their hopes of making a playoff push over the second half would feel stronger if he starts making more headlines with his play than his locker room quotes.
author: Josh Alper

title: John Harbaugh admits calling Amy Adams Strunk about Jeffery Simmons trade
summary: Giants coach John Harbaugh apparently ruffled some feathers in Nashville by making a phone call to Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk in an effort to spark trade discussions for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.
full_text: Giants coach John Harbaugh apparently ruffled some feathers in Nashville by making a phone call to Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk in an effort to spark trade discussions for defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons. And Harbaugh doesn't care about any "code" that he may have violated by going over the head of Titans G.M. Mike Borgonzi. Harbaugh admitted to reporters on Monday that he made the call. And he vowed to make similar calls, if it's in the best interests of the team. " I did, I did ," Harbaugh said regarding whether he called Strunk. "I left a message. . . . Because you turn over every stone. You know, gonna try everything. I mean, I just, I'll put it out there, man, we're open for any call. Anybody wants to call us or call anybody. Call." Next came a discussion about songs that send the "call me" message, from the Blondie song of that name to the more recent Call Me Maybe . "Let's put that out there," Harbaugh said. "Put that out there. It was kind of, like, fun to see the outpouring of interest in that. I enjoyed it. We're not like — we're not part of any secret society oath that says you can only talk to somebody. We're not in that. We didn't get memoed on that. We're not in that agreement. So like I said, anybody can call us. We won't be adhering to that particular agreement." Amen to all of that. The only rules that should matter are the written rules. Those who tiptoe around unwritten rules undermine their chances to get shit done. Besides, calls between teams happen at many different levels. There isn't an exclusive G.M.-to-G.M. network of bat phones. In this specific case, the Giants apparently weren't getting anywhere with Borgonzi. So they got creative, and resourceful. As we understand it, they didn't hear from the Titans to see if they'd match or beat the offer the Bears made for Simmons. Which would seem to be the sensible thing to do before finalizing a deal — unless the Bears expressly set a firm and quick take-it-or-leave-it deadline that prevented the Titans from exploring whether more could have been gotten from another team.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: Kendrick Bourne has a fractured tibia, will miss the rest of the season
summary: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said at his Monday press conference that wide receiver Kendrick Bourne could miss the rest of the season with a leg injury he suffered in Sunday's overtime win over the Cowboys and a report on Monday evening says that will be the case.
full_text: ' Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said at his Monday press conference that wide receiver Kendrick Bourne could miss the rest of the season with a leg injury he suffered in Sunday's overtime win over the Cowboys and a report on Monday evening says that will be the case. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Bourne suffered a fractured tibia . He does not need surgery, but does need three months to recover and will not be able to return to action this season as a result. Bourne had one catch on Sunday and 26 catches for 263 yards while appearing in all eight Cardinals games this fall. Michael Wilson, Simi Fehoko, Devin Duvernay, and Reggie Virgil are the other wide receivers on the active roster in Arizona.

title: Packers to sign QB Cam Miller to practice squad
summary: The Packers are signing free agent quarterback Cam Miller to the practice squad, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
full_text: ' The Packers are signing free agent quarterback Cam Miller to the practice squad, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports. The Dolphins waived him Aug. 30, and he remained a free agent until Monday. The Packers have Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor on the active roster. They still list Kedon Slovis on the practice squad. The Raiders made Miller a sixth-round pick in 2025, and the Dolphins signed him off of Las Vegas' practice squad late last season. Miller, 25, has never appeared in a regular-season game.
author: Charean Williams

title: Lions lost linebacker Jimmy Rolder to season-ending hamstring injury vs. Vikings
summary: Lions linebacker Jimmy Rolder will miss the rest of the season after suffering a hamstring injury on Sunday against the Vikings.
full_text: ' Lions linebacker Jimmy Rolder will miss the rest of the season after suffering a hamstring injury on Sunday against the Vikings. Rolder's injury has been largely overlooked because it happened on the same play as the very scary injury suffered by linebacker Jack Campbell, who remains hospitalized. Rolder's injury isn't as serious but is a big one for the Lions, as Rolder is a rookie who had been playing an increasingly important role on Detroit's defense. Rolder was the Lions' leading tackler in their win over the Vikings. "Jimmy Rolder is going to require surgery, or he could, this is a significant injury, he'll be out for the season," Lions head coach Dan Campbell said. A fourth-round pick out of Michigan, Rolder has also been one of the Lions' top special teams players this season. The Lions suffered several injuries on Sunday, including two different plays when two different defensive players were knocked out of the game. Dan Campbell said the Lions had to rally to finish the game strong without several key players. "Everybody goes through it and it's our time," Campbell said. "We overcame a lot of adversity, so I was proud of that, too." Rolder will go on injured reserve. Campbell said the Lions' other injured players are still being evaluated for this week.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Patriots waive S Elliott Davison
summary: The Patriots waived safety Elliott Davison, the team announced Monday.
full_text: ' The Patriots waived safety Elliott Davison, the team announced Monday. Davison, 24, signed with the Patriots' active roster from the practice squad on Oct. 19. title: Khalil Mack trade proposals: Bears reunion headlines 3 deals Chargers could make before NFL deadline
summary: The winless Chargers reportedly remain reluctant to move Mack, but there are some show-stopping deals that could still be possible
full_text:
Prior to their latest loss, the Los Angeles Chargers reportedly remained steadfast in their unwillingness to trade Khalil Mack before the league's Nov. 10 deadline. But after another loss on Sunday dropped them to 0-7, the Chargers may need to seriously reconsider that stance.
Of course, a strong offer could change anyone's mind about trading Mack, a future Hall of Fame outside linebacker who is deep into the back-nine of his career. Instead of spending one of his final years on a team going nowhere, the 35-year-old Mack would surely prefer to have a chance to win a championship, something that has eluded him to this point in his career.
While no longer in his prime, Mack is still a productive pass rusher who can help a title-contending team that needs help in that area. Fortunately for Mack, there are several teams that fit that description. The Chargers are his biggest roadblock.
Realistically, a fifth-round pick would be fair compensation for Mack, but there's probably no chance that happens. The Chargers' reported reluctance and the number of teams that are likely interested in Mack will drive up the price.
Here are three possible mock trades the Chargers could make if they decide to deal Mack.
Despite already trading for Jeffery Simmons , the Bears are reportedly still interested in Mack, who had a memorable, four-year run in Chicago from 2018-21. Mack's arrival in Chicago would further bolster the Bears' Super Bowl prospects.
Let's be clear. The Bears would probably have to overpay for Mack with a third-round pick. That's why they would probably try to get something back in the form of a late-round pick, whether that's in the 2027 or 2028 draft. In this mock trade, the Bears are able to move up a round on Day 3.
Chicago just showed that they are willing to go big if that means getting the player they want. No one will criticize the Bears for trading a pair of first-round picks to the Titans for Simmons if he helps them win a Super Bowl. The same could be said for this mock trade.
Lot of moving parts here, with the biggest one being the Chargers getting a third-round pick for Mack. Los Angeles would also get some players who can help them this season. Palmer played with Justin Herbert from 2021-24 and Chubb adds a veteran.
Buffalo would improve its draft stock and get an extra late-round pick in 2028. The Bills would also get a replacement for Palmer in Johnston, a former first-round pick who could use a change of scenery. Most importantly, Buffalo would get a much-needed pass rusher who can complement Greg Rousseau , who has nearly half of the Bills' entire sack total through eight weeks and is the only Bills player with more than 1.5 sacks.
A trade between Harbaugh brothers? Why not?
The Giants lead the NFC East despite having one of the league's worst pass rushers. They also need help at running back and pass catcher. John Harbaugh is familiar with both Kolar and Mitchell dating back to his time with the Ravens . Jim Harbaugh would get Singletary (who, like Johnston, would benefit from a change of scenery) and draft picks to help jumpstart the Chargers' inevitable rebuild.

title: Could Tyson Bagent save Ravens' playoff hopes? Lamar Jackson injury raises a costly trade question
summary: OC Declan Doyle knows Bagent from Chicago, but does that familiarity justify a potentially expensive trade for a mostly unproven player?
full_text:
The Ravens are 4-4, Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve after undergoing thumb surgery on his throwing hand, and suddenly Baltimore has a much bigger problem than anyone could have imagined even just a few days ago.
Jackson had already missed three games with a high-ankle sprain before returning Sunday against Buffalo, only to injure his thumb on his first play back . Backup Tyler Huntley also left that game with a toe injury; undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano was pressed into action and looked like, well, an undrafted rookie who had taken exactly zero reps with the first team. And with the NFL trade deadline approaching, Baltimore has to decide whether to stick with its current QB room or find help elsewhere.
The Ravens could look to trade for an experienced quarterback . But there's another option worth considering: a younger, largely unproven backup whose upside -- and familiarity with Baltimore's offense -- could make him an appealing target. And that brings us to Bears backup Tyson Bagent.
According to Pro Football Talk , Baltimore could explore trading for Bagent, although acquiring him "won't be cheap." How expensive? Chicago Tribune reporter Brad Biggs suggested back in February that it could take a second-round pick, or equivalent compensation, to convince the Bears to make a deal. That wasn't a reported asking price, but it tells you something about how Chicago values its backup quarterback.
And if you're Baltimore, that's where things get complicated. Because while Bagent might give the Ravens their best chance to remain competitive until Jackson returns -- assuming he returns this season -- we're still talking about a former undrafted free agent with six career starts, three touchdown passes and nine interceptions.
So how much is that worth? And what does history tell us about teams trading valuable draft picks for largely unproven quarterbacks?
The answers are … interesting.
There's an obvious reason Bagent's name has surfaced in connection with the Ravens, and it goes beyond their suddenly depleted quarterback room. Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle spent last season in Chicago in the same role, where he worked directly with Bagent.
And Doyle wasn't shy about how he felt about the quarterback.
"Tyson is no-nonsense," Doyle said during training camp in 2025 . "He's businesslike. Football's really important to him."
That familiarity matters. Doyle knows what Bagent does well, where he struggles and, perhaps most importantly, what he can reasonably be asked to do. And because Doyle helped implement Ben Johnson's offense in Chicago before bringing elements of that system to Baltimore -- including pre-snap motion, play-action and formation versatility -- Bagent would arrive with some familiarity with the concepts and expectations.
That doesn't mean Bagent will suddenly play like Jackson. And the Ravens wouldn't ask him to. They need somebody who can execute what's being asked, protect the football and give Baltimore a chance to win while Jackson recovers.
But what should the Ravens be willing to give up for that?
We went back through quarterback trades dating to 2007, focusing on players who had started 10 or fewer NFL games before another team acquired them. We looked at their performance before the trade, what their new teams gave up and, most importantly, what happened after they arrived.
And there have been some clear successes, starting with Matt Schaub.
Houston sent Atlanta two second-round picks and swapped first-round selections in 2007 for Schaub, who had started just twice in three seasons with the Falcons. He became Houston's starter for seven seasons, throwing for more than 23,000 yards and helping the Texans reach the playoffs twice.
A decade later, San Francisco sent New England a second-rounder for Jimmy Garoppolo, who also had just two NFL starts. The trade came at the 2017 deadline, and Garoppolo went 5-0 after taking over as the starter for a 1-10 team that finished 6-10. He eventually went 38-17 as the 49ers' starter and helped them reach the Super Bowl.
Schaub and Garoppolo, it turns out, are the exceptions.
Indianapolis traded former first-round receiver Phillip Dorsett to New England for Jacoby Brissett in 2017. Brissett started 30 games for the Colts, with 31 touchdowns and 13 interceptions. Dallas, meanwhile, gave up a fourth-rounder for Trey Lance in 2023 to serve as Dak Prescott's backup. The former No. 3 overall pick started just once for the Cowboys before leaving in free agency.
Then there's Joshua Dobbs, who was traded three times. Jacksonville gave up a fifth-rounder for him in 2019 and never started him. Arizona traded for him in 2023, got eight starts and a 1-7 record, then sent him to Minnesota, where he briefly became one of the NFL's best stories before eventually losing his starting job.
The most encouraging recent example? Malik Willis.
Originally a 2022 third-round pick, Tennessee traded Willis to Green Bay for a seventh-rounder in 2024 after he'd struggled through three starts with the Titans. All Willis did for the Packers was go 2-1 in three starts, throwing six touchdowns without an interception during his time there.
Of the 10 trades we looked at, only five resulted in the quarterback starting at least eight games for his new team. Just three -- Schaub, Garoppolo and Brissett -- made 16 or more starts.
It's not an exhaustive list, but the larger point is hard to miss. Teams routinely trade for quarterbacks they believe can offer more than they've shown. Occasionally, they find a long-term starter. More often, they're giving up future draft picks for somebody who never becomes the answer.
Of course, evaluating quarterbacks isn't as simple as comparing stat lines, particularly when they've barely played.
Schaub found success playing for Gary Kubiak in Houston, while Garoppolo benefited from Kyle Shanahan's offense in San Francisco. And Willis looked like a completely different quarterback when Matt LaFleur built Green Bay's game plans around what he did best.
Matt Cassel offers another example. The former seventh-rounder played well in place of an injured Tom Brady in New England in 2008, then struggled during his first season in Kansas City. But when former Patriots offensive coordinator Charlie Weis arrived in 2010, Cassel threw 27 touchdowns against seven interceptions, made the Pro Bowl and helped the Chiefs win the AFC West. He never sustained that level of success after Weis left.
None of this happens in a vacuum. Coaching, scheme and supporting cast all matter and what a quarterback accomplished in one offense doesn't necessarily tell us what he'll do in another.
Which brings us back to Doyle and Bagent.
We looked at this question earlier in the season when Seattle lost Sam Darnold , and the findings were revealing.
From 2015-2025, 41 teams were above .500 after losing their starting quarterback. Their backups went just 55-82, yet 24 of those teams still made the playoffs. Twelve won at least one postseason game, and four eventually won the Super Bowl.
So, yes, good teams can survive losing their starter. But there's a catch, and it's a big one.
Among those teams, 67.9% made the playoffs when the backup needed to start just one to three games. That fell to 38.5% when the replacement started at least four games, and just 16.7% when the absence stretched to seven or more starts.
Baltimore currently isn't above .500, but the point remains: Asking a backup to keep a talented team competitive for two or three weeks is one thing. Asking him to do it for two months -- or potentially the remainder of the season -- is something else entirely. Especially when the quarterback you're asking to do all this may not be on the roster right now.
And that's what makes Jackson's uncertain recovery timeline so important. The Ravens aren't necessarily looking for somebody to replace their franchise QB. They're looking for somebody who can keep the season from getting away from them before he returns.
Based…

title: Mock trades for Jaguars' Brian Thomas Jr.: Why Chiefs, Raiders could stand out as top fits
summary: Thomas has struggled after an outstanding rookie year
full_text:
Amid a difficult 2024 season, then-rookie wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr . was a major silver lining for the Jacksonville Jaguars . The first-round selection had 87 receptions for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns in his debut campaign, earned a Pro Bowl honor and finished fourth in a loaded Offensive Rookie of the Year race.
Now, the situation has done a complete 180. The Jaguars are 5-2 and one of the best teams in the NFL , but Thomas is merely a fringe contributor. His 10 catches this year rank fifth on the team, and his 117 yards are tied for fifth. He has played 44% of the team's offensive snaps, the third-highest among wide receivers, but a figure that has fluctuated week to week. He played just 21% of the snaps in a narrow Week 6 loss to the Texans before playing 52% of the snaps (and catching a touchdown pass) in a blowout win over the Colts . That touchdown snag was his first catch since Week 4.
Coach Liam Coen and quarterback Trevor Lawrence backed Thomas and highlighted his importance on several occasions.
"I was super excited," Lawrence said of the touchdown pass Sunday. "It's a team game, and you want to see all your teammates have success, especially the situation with BT. I mean, the guy's so talented, he's a great player, and obviously hasn't been the easiest for him lately, but he's been working extremely hard to make plays."
The Jaguars have a deep stead of receiving options: Wide receivers Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers , tight end Brenton Strange and running back Bhayshul Tuten all have more catches than Thomas does. But Thomas also adds a deep downfield element that no one else on the team does, even if it hasn't resulted in many box score contributions.
If the Jaguars are willing to part ways with Thomas — and that's a major "if" — there would be plenty of suitors. Here are four who could make sense, along with the packages they could offer.
In this instance, we'll use the trade package for another 2024 first-round wide receiver who's had many ups and downs, Marvin Harrison Jr. , as a framework. The Texans sent 2027 second- and seventh-round picks to the Cardinals for Harrison and a 2027 sixth-round pick.
Chiefs receive: WR Brian Thomas Jr. Jaguars receive: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 sixth-round pick
The Chiefs have an extra third-round pick in 2027 from the Trent McDuffie trade and a desperate need for a wide receiver who can stretch the defense. Patrick Mahomes has not completed a pass 20+ yards downfield in any of his last three games. In Sunday's crucial loss to the Broncos , the Chiefs' leading receiver was running back Emmett Johnson , followed by tight end Travis Kelce . Rashee Rice , the team's leading wide receiver, is mostly a quick-game target whose production comes after the catch.
The big question with this trade is why Jacksonville would want to help out a fellow AFC contender. It's much easier to simply keep Thomas Jr.
Steelers receive: WR Brian Thomas Jr. Jaguars receive: 2027 third-round pick, T Dylan Cook
Again, the big question here is "Why would the Jaguars help out another team with playoff aspirations?" That's why this offer is bigger than the two that follow, from either non-AFC or non-contending teams.
The Steelers, who have been hit hard by injuries, could try to sweeten the deal by adding Cook, a backup tackle. The Jaguars recently lost Anton Harrison for the season, stretching their tackle depth very thin. Cook lost his starting spot to Max Iheanachor , but he has been a capable starter before.
Raiders receive: WR Brian Thomas Jr. Jaguars receive: 2027 third-round pick
The Raiders, unlike the Chiefs and Steelers, are not expected to contend this season. Even though they're 4-4, they're 1-4 over their past five games and have a tough schedule upcoming. Furthermore, the Raiders have a clear and obvious need at wide receiver, both currently and in the future when No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza takes over for Kirk Cousins . Brock Bowers is a star, but finding a complement is critical. Thomas could be the answer if he rediscovers his rookie-year form, or he could just be part of the answer. Regardless, making a run at Thomas would be within reason.
Commanders receive: WR Brian Thomas Jr. Jaguars receive: 2027 fourth-round pick, DT Shy Tuttle
The Commanders are a team that could go one way or the other ahead of the trade deadline. They're only 2-4-1, but they play in the woeful NFC East. Week 9 will be crucial; if the Commanders can spring an upset of the Rams , they could shift toward buying. If they lose and the Giants and/or Cowboys win, selling could make more sense (though coach Dan Quinn and GM Adam Peters will be keen on keeping their jobs, meaning they might not want to sell).
Thomas was a college teammate of Jayden Daniels at LSU. The Commanders would look at this as an investment for the present but also for the future. Terry McLaurin is out for the season, and there's a potential out in his contract this offseason. Stefon Diggs is on a one-year deal. Throwing in Tuttle could help push this deal over the edge, as Jacksonville is looking for interior defensive line help after DaVon Hamilton's injury .
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL Week 9 picks and score predictions: Packers ruin Tom Brady's trip to New England, Jaguars destroy Ravens
summary: John Breech makes his Week 9 NFL picks, including Jacksonville cruising past a short-handed Baltimore team and Green Bay spoiling a star-studded weekend in New England
full_text:
With the NFL season heading into Week 9, we are officially halfway through the year, which makes right now the perfect time to hand out some midseason awards. Actually, I'm only handing out one award, and it's going to me, and I don't even want it: It's the award for worst picker from Week 8.
I went 8-6 last week, which ended up being the worst record out of our experts here at CBS Sports in Week 8. I clearly spent way too much time trying to find a Halloween costume and not enough time researching my picks. Next year for Halloween, I'm going to go as someone who's good at picks, so I guess I'll be dressing up as Jamey Eisenberg.
Eisnenberg, who is our long-time NFL fantasy analyst here, might want to just make NFL picks full time because he went 12-2 last week. Also, he's 69-49-3 against the spread this year. I might have to copy his picks this week.
So will I actually copy Jamey's picks? Probably not, but let's get to the picks and find out for sure.
Actually, before we get to the Week 9 picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here . Also, as you probably know by now -- because I point it out every week -- I'm in charge of the NFL newsletter here at CBSSports.com. If you want to subscribe, all you have to do is click here and enter your email address . I'm going to eat one piece of my six-year-old's Halloween candy every time someone signs up. My dentist is going to love this.
Speaking of things we love, let's get to the picks.
If you had asked me at 10 a.m. ET on Nov. 1 who was going to win this game, I probably would have picked the Ravens , but a few things have happened since then:
Those two injuries mean the Ravens will likely go into this game with an undrafted rookie ( Joe Fagnano ) as their starting quarterback, but that's not even a guarantee because he's dealing with an ankle injury. The Ravens literally might have to run the wishbone offense on Thursday. You have to be desperate to run the wishbone and I think the Ravens are there. Bill Walsh actually implemented for a game in 1987 when he had to use a replacement quarterback while the regular players were on strike.
October 5, 1987 Bill Walsh Employs the Wishbone In the second half of the first MNF game to feature "replacement players" during the 1987 players' strike, the 49ers legendary head coach utilizes the "wishbone" offense against the Giants and head coach Bill Parcells. Walsh —… pic.twitter.com/EoXESclJi1
The Ravens could also run the wing-T. Basically, any offense from 1934 would work at this point. They could even call the Buccaneers ' for a few tips. They just won a game without throwing a single pass. The Ravens might have to do that this week.
So the Ravens don't even know who their starting QB will be this week, and to make matters worse, they have to face what might be the best team in the AFC. If Week 8 was any indication, the Jaguars have finally figured out how to run the ball again and when they run the ball, they're virtually unbeatable. Since Liam Coen took over as head coach, the Jags are 10-1 when they rush for at least 110 yards and they did that in Week 8 by rushing for a season-high 183 yards in a 42-7 win over the Colts .
When the Jaguars can run the ball, that takes some pressure off of Trevor Lawrence and he seems to thrive in those situations. In Week 8, Lawrence completed just 10 passes, but he threw for 210 yards and three touchdowns while finishing with a 153.3 passer rating.
Do you want to know how absurd that is? Those stats made Lawrence the first player in 55 years to finish with at least 200 passing yards, three touchdown passes and a passer rating of 150-or-higher on 10 completions or fewer. The last player to pull that off was Roger Staubach and he did that while playing for the Cowboys in 1971. Did I mention that the Cowboys won the Super Bowl that year? Because the Cowboys won the Super Bowl that year.
I'm not saying the Jags are going to win the Super Bowl this year or am I saying that? I don't know anymore. Pete Prisco made the Jags his preseason pick to win the Super Bowl and I can't comprehend living in a world where Prisco nails a prediction like that.
Jaguars Super Bowl Champs?! 👀 @PriscoCBS predicts that Jacksonville will defeat Dallas in Super Bowl LXI Do you agree? 🤔 pic.twitter.com/ehm4qv8MI8
I'm going to cut Pete some slack and ignore the Cowboys part of that prediction.
I don't know if the Jags are going to win the Super Bowl, but I do think they roll to a win on Thursday night.
PICK: Jaguars 30-13 over Ravens
For just the second time, Spain is hosting an NFL game, and the biggest winner might be everyone flying into Madrid this week. I've only been to Spain once, and they were handing out free shots of Jagermeister at the airport. And as we all know, you haven't lived until you've done free shots of Jager in a Spanish airport before noon. At least that's what I tell myself.
This seems like a solid idea: Free samples of jagermeister at the airport. I'll know what I'll be doing until takeoff pic.twitter.com/EGYk4XKEwE
I'm not sure if the shot guy is still there and I feel like someone needs to investigate, so I'll be heading to Madrid this week to find out. I will definitely report back my findings.
This is the fifth NFL game being held in Europe this year, and so far, the team that leaves later in the week has had a major advantage in each game. The team that has arrived on Friday has gone 4-0 this year. If you're wondering who has the travel advantage this week, the answer is NO ONE. The Bengals and Falcons will both depart on Tuesday night and spend their entire practice week in Madrid. I hope they've brushed up on their Spanish.
The bad news for the Falcons is that there's rain in the forecast for Sunday, and based on what I saw in Week 8, they might want to just forfeit if it rains, because they are arguably the worst team in NFL history when it comes to playing in the rain. Actually, forget that whole forfeit thing; the stadium in Spain has a retractable roof, so weather won't be a problem. That's good news for the Falcons.
🚨🏟️𝗨𝗡𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗟 The new Santiago Bernabéu equipped with a retractable roof is ready ahead of todays game against Getafe. pic.twitter.com/orCvRtdaBY
The other good news for the Falcons is that they could not have asked for a better matchup after an embarrassing loss on Sunday. The Bengals defense has given up 621 yards to tight ends this year, which is the second-highest number in the NFL. Kyle Pitts is on my fantasy team and this might be the first time all year where I actually feel confident about starting him. I've let my team know that no one is safe and that I will start cutting people if we don't start improving. And I will start with Kyle Pitts if he doesn't go off against the Bengals.
Another reason this is a solid matchup for the Falcons is that they have Bijan Robinson . The Bengals are giving up 4.8 yards per carry this year, which is the fourth-worst number in the NFL, and now, they have to face Robinson, who is averaging 5.2 yards per carry. That seems like a recipe for disaster. Basically, the Falcons offense is built to exploit every weakness on the Bengals' defense.
Also, if you watched the Falcons play the Buccaneers in Week 8, you may have noticed that Atlanta's defense can't stop the run, but that might not matter in this game, because the Bengals can't run the ball.
I think what I'm trying to say here is that the Falcons might put up a lot of points. However, that probably won't matter because the Bengals have Joe Burrow . Over his past three games, Burrow is averaging 314.7 passing yards and 4.3 touchdown passes per game. During that span, he became the FIRST quarterback in NFL history to throw at least four TD passes with a completion percentage of 70% in three straight games.
Burrow is currently on fire. Oh, and did I mention that he practically requested to play in Spain back in 2025 after the NFL announced…

title: NFL reinstates James Pearce Jr. after eight-game suspension: Why EDGE returns at critical time for Falcons
summary: Pearce's insertion into the lineup could be the lift the Falcons need to emerge as the NFC South's top team
full_text:
The NFL reinstated Atlanta Falcons edge rusher James Pearce Jr . on Monday, ending the eight-game suspension it handed down before the season began. Pearce will be eligible to play in Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, and coach Kevin Stefanski said last week that the plan is for him to see action in the Week 9 contest. Stefanski said upon Pearce's reinstatement, though, that it is too early to tell how much he will play in his first game back.
The Falcons released Jared Ivey and Drake Jackson in corresponding moves with Pearce's activation to the 53-man roster.
Pearce's legal troubles early in the 2026 offseason resulted in a violation of the NFL's personal conduct policy, the league ruled. He was arrested on Feb. 7 following a domestic dispute with his then-girlfriend, Rickea Jackson, who stars for the WNBA's Chicago Sky.
After his arrest, Pearce faced three felony charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person. He also faced a felony aggravated stalking charge, but that was later changed to a misdemeanor. A charge of aggravated battery of a law enforcement officer was dropped.
Pearce entered a 12-month pre-trial program, and once it is complete, all the charges will be dismissed. He must also stay out of legal trouble for a six-month period and attend therapy sessions as part of the agreement he and his representation reached in the case.
During the legal proceedings, Pearce remained in communication with the Falcons and remained in good enough football shape to potentially be available for Week 9.
"He's done everything that we've asked him, everything that he's been allowed to do," Stefanski said on Monday . "He's done a great job."
Expectations for the Atlanta defensive front heading into the first half of the season were modest given Pearce's suspension and the loss of fellow edge rusher Jalon Walker for the year due to a torn ACL. The second-year players combined for 16 sacks as rookies, and Pearce finished third in Defensive Rookie of the Year voting. Fielding a defense without two young standouts figured to limit the Falcons' ability to pressure the pocket. Instead, they have done more than stay above water in that regard.
The Falcons rank seventh in quarterback pressure rate despite blitzing on only 24.1% of snaps. They stand 15th in pass yards allowed per game. That production is, at worst, serviceable for a unit lacking its two projected top pass rushers.
Now Pearce arrives poised to potentially take the operation to another level.
"I don't see it as a challenge," Stefanski said of inserting a new player into the edge rusher rotation. "I see it as a positive to add a good player to the mix. I think the way [Jeff Ulbrich] and the defensive staff have constructed this rush plan, obviously married up with the coverage plan, I think it's beneficial to all parties to do your job. But adding another good player to the mix is a good thing."
The Falcons have been solid but not spectacular at defending the run, as they rank 15th in yards allowed per game and eighth in EPA per rush allowed. Last week's performance against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , however, heightened concerns over the defense's ability to contain opposing ball carriers. The defense surrendered a whopping 324 rushing yards to a one-dimensional Buccaneers offense that did not complete a single pass. It did not help that Atlanta could not move the ball, either, but the run-stopping effort played as large of a role in the 16-0 loss as anything.
If Pearce levels up as an all-around defender in 2026, he will improve against the run. His greatest impacts come almost exclusively from rushing the passer and stepping back into coverage, so the next step in his development is to threaten ball carriers at or behind the line of scrimmage. The Falcons need that kind of play in order to rebound from their worst showing against the run this year.
Pearce is just one player who will be available for only about half of the season, but his return alone could uplift the Falcons in their hunt for the NFC South title. No team in the division owns more than three wins, and this race is trending toward delivering a sub-.500 champion for the second time in as many years. Since every game matters immensely in such a tight battle, one or two standout performances from Pearce could be the difference between spots in the standings.
This is a critical time for Pearce to regain eligibility, because the Falcons are about to embark on their toughest four-game stretch yet. On the docket are dates with the Bengals, Kansas City Chiefs , Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions , who are all in play for postseason berths. Even the Cleveland Browns, after that, are more competitive than expected this season, and that contest is on the road.
There is no more important time than now for Atlanta's defense to take a step forward, and Pearce can help the unit do so.
