Running back Zach Charbonnet , who tore his ACL in Seattle's NFC divisional round playoff win against the San Francisco 49ers in January, is primed to make his 2026 season debut. He doesn't have a game status on Seattle's final injury report, indicating he will be available to play. The situation for First-round rookie running back Jadarian Price is slightly murkier.
Why the lack of clarity with Price's situation? That is because Price, who has missed the last four games with a chest injury while on injured reserve, would need to be activated by 4 p.m. today. Seattle, however, has already designated Price to return with ESPN among those reporting he will play.
"We're going to let the transaction speak for itself on that one," coach Mike Macdonald said.
If the defending Super Bowl champions are going to defeat the high-flying Bears attack led by quarterback Caleb Williams , the Seahawks will need to run the football. Doing so will not only keep Williams on the sideline but also slow down Chicago's pass rush. That second part is key for Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold since he has the NFL's worst expected points added (EPA) per dropback when pressured at -0.63. That's why Seattle traded for Quenton Nelson , and there's a likely chance Nelson will be able to block for both of the Seahawks' top backs in his Seattle debut.
"We have a plan for Zach and with JD," Macdonald said on Saturday . "If we were to make a move, that would happen on Monday to my knowledge. We'll see if that's what we do. We have some things going on roster-wise that we're working through right now, but we have a plan for Zach."
The Seahawks don't have to activate Price on Monday, but they have two more weeks to make a decision on his status before he would be required to move to season-ending injured reserve. On the off chance Price isn't activated for Week 8, Charbonnet would likely share the rushing workload with Emanuel Wilson . Wilson leads the Seahawks in rushing yards (403), rushing touchdowns (three) and carries (111) .
author: Garrett Podell

title: Cardinals name Gardner Minshew as starter, Carson Beck No. 2: What's next for Jacoby Brissett?
summary: Brissett has been demoted to third string after Arizona's comeback win against the Cowboys
full_text:
There have been two surprising developments relating to the Arizona Cardinals ' quarterback situation following Sunday's dramatic, come-from-behind win over the Dallas Cowboys .
Prior to Sunday's game, Jacoby Brissett was the starter, fellow veteran Gardner Minshew was the backup, and rookie Carson Beck was Arizona's emergency, third-string quarterback. There's a completely new order now.
On Monday, head coach Mike LaFleur announced Minshew as the team's new starter. Beck will move to the No. 2 spot while Brissett is now the third-string quarterback.
The decision to switch starting quarterbacks was surprising enough; LaFleur's announcement that Brissett, the team's starting quarterback for the majority of the last two seasons, was being demoted to the emergency third spot is the real jaw-dropper.
Statistically, Brissett wasn't bad during the season's first seven games. But he struggled against the Cowboys before being replaced by Minshew, who caught fire with three touchdown passes while completing 73.9% of his attempts. Minshew's heroics helped turn a 27-17 deficit with 3:54 left into a 33-30 overtime win. The win improved the Cardinals' record to 3-5.
GARDNER MINSHEW II TO MICHAEL WILSON TO TIE IT LATE 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/t74fyZqpPF
Minshew, 30, has had a roller coaster NFL career. A 2019 sixth-round pick, Minshew started his career in Jacksonville before having stops in Philadelphia, Indianapolis, Las Vegas and Kansas City prior to coming to Arizona this season. His best season was back in 2023, when he earned his first Pro Bowl nod after going 7-6 as the Colts ' starting quarterback.
Beck, a 2026 third-round pick, showed potential during this past preseason, going 15-of-19 for 188 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions. His college career included a prolific 2025 season at Miami that ended with an appearance in the College Football Playoff National Championship.
Minshew will make his debut as the Cardinals' starting quarterback next Sunday in Seattle against the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks .
LaFleur was non-committal when he was asked about Brissett's future with the team beyond this week. That's usually one of the first indicators (another being a demotion) that a player is likely being dealt.
The Ravens were the first team to come to mind when the news of Brissett's benching broke. Baltimore desperately needs help at quarterback after losing Lamar Jackson to a possible season-ending injury . Backup Tyler Huntley is also expected to miss some time after injuring his toe during Sunday's loss to the Bills , leaving undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano as the only healthy quarterback on the roster.
If the Ravens are going to salvage their season, they need to stabilize their quarterback position as best they can. Brissett would help them do that. He could serve as Baltimore's new starting quarterback or at least be a viable backup for Huntley whenever he is cleared to play.
On paper, a trade between Baltimore and Arizona for Brissett seems easy. The Ravens need a quarterback, and the Cardinals have one they're not using. It could be as easy as that if both teams agree on the trade terms before the league's Nov. 10 trade deadline.
The Cardinals need to be realistic here, though. The Ravens need a quarterback, but they're not going to give away too much for a quarterback who just lost his starting job. Baltimore is also probably realistic in terms of its situation. Without Jackson, and playing in a division where every team has a winning record, the odds of the Ravens doing much this season are slim with or without Brissett, who — if nothing else — could help the Ravens remain competitive.
It would be surprising if the Ravens and Cardinals didn't at least discuss a trade involving Brissett. From the outside, a sixth-round pick sounds fair, or a fifth-round pick in exchange for Brissett and a seventh-round pick. Either way, the Cardinals shouldn't expect to get much in exchange for Brissett, whose time in Arizona has been a disappointment.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Seahawks vs. Bears prediction: Caleb Williams faces toughest test yet in Seattle defense
summary: The Bears take their surging offense into Seattle for a matchup with one of the NFL's best defenses
full_text:
In the Week 8 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Seattle Seahawks host the Chicago Bears . Seattle enters this game fresh off a victory over the previously undefeated Kansas City Chiefs , snapping a two-game losing skid. The Seahawks' defense is settling in and once again looks like one of the best units in the league, but faces one of its toughest tests of the season on Monday night.
Chicago enters having won both of its games since starting quarterback Caleb Williams returned from injury, improving to 5-2 in the process. The Bears have looked like one of the best offenses in the NFL whenever Williams has been on the field, but they, too, face arguably their toughest test of the season on Monday evening.
Will Seattle make it back-to-back wins, or will the Bears ruin their evening with a road upset?
Chicago has scored, 59, 31 and 30 points in the three Caleb Williams starts that were not played against the Minnesota Vikings in a driving rainstorm. The Bears piled up 552, 368 and 405 yards in those three games, and turned the ball over only twice in those contests.
For the season (including the game against Minnesota), Williams has completed 71% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt, both of which are career-high figures. He has thrown five touchdowns against one interception and rushed 24 times for 128 yards and two additional scores.
Williams has generally thrown short passes, with an average depth of throw of only 7.0 yards, according to Tru Media. Despite that, he has created explosive passing plays at the third-highest rate in the league (10.7% of dropbacks). That's thanks in large part to the fact that the Bears are averaging 6.4 yards after catch per completion on his throws, the fourth-best mark in the league.
The Seahawks, though, limit YAC as well as just about any team in football. They've allowed only 4.5 yards after catch per completion, which ranks third-best in the NFL. They play shell coverages a lot of the time, and they rally to the ball and tackle as well in the secondary as anybody. Their defensive backs and linebackers rarely miss opportunities to bring ball-carriers to the ground.
The Bears generally want to run the ball more often than almost any team in the league, with a 48.7% rush rate, according to Tru Media. The Seahawks are elite at stopping the run, however, as we saw last week against Kenneth Walker III . D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson will have their work cut out for them here, even against a defense that plays a lot of nickel and dime and doesn't load the box.
The Chicago offensive line will have to do a lot of work to move Seattle's defensive front off the ball, which has proven extremely difficult for opposing lines this year.
Seattle's offense is built almost entirely around the exploits of superstar wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba . JSN leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards, 43 receiving first downs and eight receiving touchdowns. He has been targeted on 36.3% of the team's pass attempts, which ranks as the No. 1 mark in the NFL. So does his 33.9% targets-per-route-run rate, which is narrowly ahead of CeeDee Lamb's .
Smith-Njigba has more receptions than the next three closest players on the Seahawks: AJ Barner , Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed combined for 53. His 867 yards are also considerably more than the 562 that trio has combined as well. They are ancillary pieces at best, and typically they are scarcely involved in the offense. Shaheed is also out on Monday night, which means the secondary options will be even more limited than usual.
The Bears, like everyone else in the league, do not have anyone who can cover Smith-Njigba. It's not possible. The best chance to limit him is to get to Sam Darnold and force hurried decisions that lead to turnovers. Darnold, despite missing time due to injury, leads the NFL with eight interceptions.
Under pressure, he has been dreadful, completing only 26 of 66 passes for 331 yards, two touchdowns and four picks. He ranks second-to-last in the league in EPA per dropback on pressured plays, per Tru Media. If the Bears can get into his face, they can force him into mistakes and flip the game on its head.
Something that will help them in that effort is the arrival of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , who is a game wrecker on the interior. Simmons is among the league leaders in both pressures and sacks when lined up inside. He'll have to deal with what is now one of the best guard duos in the league in Quenton Nelson and Grey Zabel , and Simmons could also see his snaps limited in his first game with his new team. (Nelson is likely to play a full complement in his Seattle debut, given how reluctant teams are to rotate offensive linemen.)
The Seattle running game should get a boost from the expected returns of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price . Charbonnet hasn't played all season after tearing his ACL during last year's Super Bowl run, while Price has been out since Week 3 with a chest injury. The combination of Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has largely been ineffective, and even if Charbonnet and Price can generate slightly below-average efficiency, they'll represent an improvement over the incumbent duo. The Bears have given up an average of 4.4 yards per carry this season, which ranks 23rd in the league.
Seattle's defense is looking like the unit we expected it to be coming into the year. The Seahawks just shut down Kenneth Walker last week; they should be able to do the same to D'Andre Swift. That puts the entire game on Williams' right shoulder. He can handle that, of course, but it's incredibly difficult to do against Mike Macdonald's unit. That's especially true if the Seahawks get Price and Charbonnet back in the lineup at running back and can run the ball with some degree of success. Pick the Seahawks to take care of business at home.
Prediction: Seahawks 24, Bears 20
author: Jared Dubin

title: 1-on-1 with Pittsburgh's Jalen Ramsey: How he views state of the Steelers, offense's improvement
summary: A Super Bowl champion with the Rams, Ramsey spoke with CBS Sports about where he sees the Steelers organization at 6-2 this season
full_text:
A horde of media quickly engulfed the locker of Steelers defensive back Jaquan Brisker following Pittsburgh's Week 8 win over the Browns . The media was hoping to get Brisker's response to Browns pass rusher Jared Verse's comments leading up to the game, and Brisker obliged in spades .
Just a few feet away, Jalen Ramsey — one of the NFL's most well-known and accomplished players — quietly went about his business at his locker. It felt like a good time to ask the eight-time Pro Bowl and three-time All-Pro defensive back about the current state of the Steelers, who enter their Week 9 bye at 6-2 and in sole possession of first place in the AFC North.
Ramsey, who turned 32 on Oct. 29, is in the middle of his 11th NFL season and his second season with the Steelers, who acquired him via a trade with the Dolphins in June 2025. During his first nine seasons in the NFL, Ramsey established himself as one of the NFL's premier cornerbacks. In 2021, he won a Super Bowl while being a valued member of the Los Angeles Rams .
In his first season with the Steelers, Ramsey was named to his eighth Pro Bowl after filling the stat sheet with 88 tackles, 3.0 sacks, an interception and eight passes defensed while helping Pittsburgh win its first division title since 2020.
This season, despite dealing with a broken wrist, Ramsey has continued to play at a high level. His signature play through the season's first eight weeks was his sack on the final play of overtime that sealed Pittsburgh's win in Tampa in Week 6.
I asked Ramsey about the wrist injury, his one-plus seasons with the Steelers, and Pittsburgh's ascending defense (the Steelers haven't given up a touchdown in seven quarters) and its potential as a championship-caliber unit.
I'm sure you're used to playing through injuries at this stage of your career, but a broken wrist is a broken wrist. How are you still able to be such a physical and tenacious player with an injury of that magnitude?
JR: "God, and a couple pain meds (laughs) and just clearing my mind and going to do it."
What still motivates you? I mean, you're a Hall of Famer.
What keeps you so passionate and so willing and wanting to play through injuries? And to continue with the tenacity you play with?
JR: "I just think that God has blessed me with a gift and to play football. I don't want to take that for granted any time, no matter the circumstances. And I like playing for my teammates and the fans and the organization. So just that in itself."
You've been on a Super Bowl championship team. I know it's way too premature to put crazy quotes out there...
What is, in your opinion, the state of this team now, and maybe even from more of a defensive standpoint, where do you think this team is through eight weeks?
JR: "I think we're in a good spot going into the bye week. We've had some highs during the season, but we've had a couple lows as well at different points. And I think that's good to have that type of journey throughout the season at different times, so we can kind of get in our groove, and we can feel kind of the differences at times. So, I think we're in a good spot. That's all I'll say. I don't want to compare anything. I just think we're in a good spot."
How nice is it to have a running game that runs for 200 yards and kind of keeps you guys off the field like that?
JR: "Yeah, I think what our offense is doing right now in terms of their balance, especially our running game, that's a defense's dream. That's all I say. I think anybody on the defensive side would say that."
A lot of Steeler fans already kind of look at you as a career Steeler, even though you haven't been here very long. How does it feel to be embraced by the fan base that identifies you as a guy that plays like some of those great Steeler defenders of the past?
JR: "The Steelers have had amazing players in their defenses all throughout the history of this organization — from the front end, the linebackers, the secondary. They've had guys that I've looked up to when I was younger, in high school and college and stuff like that. I kind of model my game after a few people and just their tenacity and the way that they played the game. Their passion, their heart, their physicality, fierceness, and I've tried to play that way my whole career.
"And obviously, getting traded here last year, it was great to be embraced, knowing that I played the game that way, and that's how they like it around here."
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Jack Campbell injury updates: Lions LB remains in hospital, but 'indications are positive'
summary: The All-Pro linebacker suffered what appeared to be a serious injury vs. the Vikings
full_text:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was strapped to a backboard and carted off the field after appearing to suffer a serious injury during the team's Week 8 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings .
Following the 19-15 victory, Lions coach Dan Campbell told reporters he had no further information on Jack's status, other than that he was receiving medical care. He stayed in the hospital overnight for evaluation, and the team announced it would provide more information when it had it available. Monday afternoon, the team provided the following statement:
Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital. Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time.
Shortly after that update, Dan Campbell met with the media, and though he did not share any further updates, he did ask for continued prayers and say he had a chance to visit Jack in the hospital Sunday night and talk with his family.
"It was good, it was positive," Dan Campbell said. "Got to see his parents, talk to his wife, and everybody's in good spirits. It's about the recovery, and it's a small setback. That's the family. They're very positive. So that's good in that regard."
Campbell also said "a lot of people went over there" when asked if teammates were able to visit Jack, though he acknowledged there were lots of tests being run, so not everyone could visit with the linebacker.
On the first play of the fourth quarter, Jack Campbell and teammate Eric O'Neill combined to tackle Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson . Campbell then went limp. While lying prone, Campbell was not seen moving before trainers reached him. After about 10 minutes, Campbell was strapped to a backboard and carted off the field.
Prayers up for Jack Campbell. pic.twitter.com/dZsTw6zEj1
The Lions announced that Campbell was transported to a local hospital to be evaluated for a neck injury.
It was an emotional scene at Ford Field. The entire Lions team went over to see their teammate off, while the defense gathered for a moment to rally after seeing one of their leaders go down.
The Lions defense takes a moment after Jack Campbell was carted off. @ErinAndrews has more. pic.twitter.com/uvy9PfrITI
In seven games this season, Campbell recorded 57 tackles, two QB hits and a fumble recovery. Just six months ago, he signed a four-year, $81 million extension that made him one of the highest-paid off-ball linebackers in the NFL .
Campbell was selected with the No. 18 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Iowa, just six selections after the Lions drafted running back Jahmyr Gibbs . The 26-year-old had a career year in 2025, recording 176 tackles, nine tackles for loss, five sacks, three forced fumbles and four passes defended. He was named a First Team All-Pro and earned his first Pro Bowl bid.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: 2026 NFL trade deadline QB rankings: Mac Jones, Kirk Cousins lead 10 best targets
summary: With the Ravens, Eagles and other teams potentially searching for help, we rank 10 quarterbacks who could be available before the Nov. 10 deadline
full_text:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is fast approaching, and already some major deals have come down across the league. For instance, the Chicago Bears just made a blockbuster trade, sending multiple picks (including two first-rounders) to the Tennessee Titans for star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . The defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks also landed All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson in a trade with Indianapolis. Those deals may have been the first, but there will certainly be more before the Nov. 10 deadline.
Most of the conversation surrounding the deadline has largely centered around pass rushers, running backs and wide receivers. That said, the quarterback market could also heat up as a few teams across the NFL could be on the hunt for a signal caller. That includes both the Baltimore Ravens and Philadelphia Eagles , who each lost their starting quarterbacks. Then, there's the Minnesota Vikings , who could also eye an upgrade at the position with Kyler Murray struggling despite the team's 6-1 start to the year.
With that in mind, we combed the market and identified 10 veteran quarterbacks who could be available for the right price on the trade market.
Milton is on the active roster of the Eagles after he was signed off of the Cowboys practice squad. He's backing up starter Tanner McKee , who ascended the depth chart in the wake of Jalen Hurts being put on the shelf with blood clots in his lungs. While Philadelphia would lose some depth at the position, Howie Roseman could see shipping away Milton as an opportunity to continue gaining future draft capital, albeit in the Day 3 range.
The 26-year-old was a sixth-round pick of the Patriots in 2024 out of Tennessee and spent his rookie season in New England before he was traded to Dallas in the spring of 2025. He's appeared in five games over the course of his career (one start) and has completed 69.8% of his passes for a 90.4 career passer rating. Milton is still raw, but has ability that could make him an intriguing addition.
Keenum has started games this year for Chicago, so while he may be 38, he has recent starting experience that could be useful for a team looking for a QB. After Caleb Williams and Tyson Bagent got hurt for the Bears earlier this year, Keenum started the club's Week 3 matchup against Philadelphia and impressed. He completed 24-of-34 (70.6%) for 247 yards and two touchdowns, while adding another score on the ground in a 27-7 win over the Eagles.
Keenum also saw some action in Week 5, but the results were not as prolific, completing 11-of-19 for 108 yards and an interception. Still, he's shown an ability to come in and play at a serviceable level, which is really all you can ask for at this time of the year when searching for a quarterback.
Dalton is another notable name who could be had, as he's in a crowded quarterback room with the Atlanta Falcons . The 39-year-old began the year with the Philadelphia Eagles, but was released by the team on Oct. 9. He then signed on with the Falcons, who released Cooper Rush to make room for him on the roster. Dalton is currently in a quarterback room that consists of starter Michael Penix Jr. , Tua Tagovailoa , and undrafted rookie Jack Strand .
Dalton made a brief appearance in the Eagles' Week 3 loss to the Bears, attempting one pass that was intercepted. While that doesn't exactly instill a ton of confidence, Dalton is a seasoned veteran who has 16 years and 169 career starts under his belt.
The Colts are blowing it up. They already traded away Nelson and DeForest Buckner , and Jonathan Taylor seems like he could be next if the price is right. If Indy is willing to move that caliber of player, trading Anthony Richardson for any sort of return should be on the table even after benching Daniel Jones late in the Week 8 loss to Jacksonville.
Richardson has been a bust so far for the Colts after they selected him with the fourth overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft out of Florida. The 24-year-old is 8-7 as a starter and has a career completion percentage of 50.9% to go along with a 68.0 career passer rating. His raw ability and untapped potential could be of interest for a QB-needy team wanting to pick up a lottery ticket. For a rebuilding team like Indianapolis, extracting any value on the roster -- particularly for a player like Richardson, who is going to be a free agent this offseason --  makes too much sense.
Winston is the backup in New York after he lost the starting job to J.J. McCarthy . After Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury, Winston initially got the nod and the 12-year veteran largely struggled, despite a 2-1-1 record as the starter. He completed 57% of his throws and had seven passing touchdowns to go with five interceptions over six games played. Most notably, Winston's arm strength appeared diminished, which helped pave the way for McCarthy -- who they acquired in a trade with Minnesota -- to leapfrog him on the depth chart.
While Winston may be past his prime, he's started 13 games over the past three seasons, so he's not the coldest quarterback on the market.
Minshew might be the new QB1 in Arizona, which could eliminate him from this list. However, the Cardinals should eventually see what they have in rookie Carson Beck , so if they can get value for someone like Minshew, it'd be negligent not to pull the trigger. After coming in for the benched Jacoby Brissett , Minshew helped lead Arizona to a fourth-quarter rally against the Cowboys and pulled off the upset win in overtime. The veteran completed 17-of-23 for 188 yards and three touchdowns in the winning effort.
The 30-year-old began his career as a sixth-round pick of the Jaguars in 2019 and has bounced around the league since being traded out of Jacksonville in 2021. In all, Minshew has made stops in Philadelphia, Indianapolis, Las Vegas, and Kansas City before arriving in Arizona, so he is no stranger to jumping into new systems. He's started 47 games over the course of his career and is 17-30 as a starter.
Brissett could be one of the quarterbacks who is truly available on the trade market, especially after he was benched for Minshew against Dallas last week. The 33-year-old started the first eight games of the season for Arizona, owning a 3-5 record while completing 63.3% of his throws and a 79.7 passer rating. Brissett started 12 games for the Cardinals last year and had a 94.1 passer rating, so his production has slipped rather dramatically in 2026, which has since led to him finishing that Week 8 victory on the bench.
If Arizona is going to turn the keys over to Minshew, it makes Brissett expendable, especially with rookie third-round pick Carson Beck waiting in the wings. Brissett has started in 73 games over the course of his career and is 23-50 in those contests.
Caleb Williams is back healthy, which could make Bagent expendable. He was initially the top backup when Williams went down with a hamstring injury earlier this year, but had to give way to Case Keenum as the Week 3 starter after he landed in concussion protocol. Once he was cleared, Bagent did get the nod in Week 4 against New York, where he completed 25-of-34 for 268 yards and an interception.  The following week, he started against the Packers , but was eventually benched for Keenum after completing 57.1% of his throws and two interceptions.
If Chicago feels comfortable with Keenum serving as the primary backup to Williams, Bagent becomes an intriguing trade chip as he's only 26 years old.
Cousins' future in Las Vegas is directly linked to the development of No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza . If the Raiders believe the rookie is ready to ascend atop the depth chart, Cousins becomes expendable on the trade market and maybe the most sought-after quarterback this deadline. After all, he's 4-4 as the Raiders starter, has thrown 19 passing touchdowns, and has a 101.4 passer rating through eight starts. He's had at least two passing touchdowns in seven of his eight games played…
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Should Ravens trade for QB after Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley injuries? Possible candidates to watch
summary: Baltimore could be without Jackson for the rest of the year
full_text:
The Ravens ' quarterback situation went from disappointing to dire to destitute in a hurry Sunday. In his return from an ankle injury that cost him three games, Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that will require potentially season-ending surgery on Baltimore's first offensive play, and backup Tyler Huntley left shortly thereafter with a toe injury.
That left the Ravens with emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano , an undrafted rookie . He went 10-for-21 for 91 yards and an interception, looking very much like an undrafted rookie, as the Ravens went down quietly, 36-10, against the Bills . What looked like a chance to turn the season around now looks like a game that could end Baltimore's season, for all intents and purposes. The Ravens are 4-4 and have lost three straight. Monday, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Huntley will miss extended time with turf toe, a bothersome injury that can last for weeks.
The Ravens have little time to wallow. They play the Jaguars on Thursday night. Currently, Baltimore has one available quarterback on its active roster (Fagnano), and even he was in discomfort late after taking several big hits. The Ravens don't have another quarterback on their active roster or practice squad; Skylar Thompson is on IR.
So where does Baltimore go from here at the position? There are many factors to consider.
Regardless of whether the Ravens can continue to contend or not — and it's very much looking like the latter — they owe it to all parties involved to get a quarterback.
They owe it to the rest of the team, which is still fighting. Baltimore is 4-4, which isn't good, but isn't completely out of it. It's not as if the team is dead in the water, just trying to finish out a completely lost season. There's still Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers on offense and plenty of stars on defense. If there's any hope Jackson can return on the sooner end of the recovery spectrum, Baltimore's players deserve a chance to keep their season afloat.
They owe it to coach Jesse Minter and offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, the latter of whom has been excellent this year. Forcing Minter, a first-year head coach, to resort to an undrafted rookie free agent would be extremely difficult. Since 2000, only one team with a rookie head coach has started an undrafted rookie quarterback in multiple games: the Jets with Brady Cook last year. The Ravens do not want to resemble the Jets whatsoever.
They owe it to Fagnano, too. He is a really nice story, someone who started his college career as a walk-on at FCS program Maine and finished it with a superb seventh-year senior season at UConn. He earned a spot on the roster with a stellar showing at rookie tryouts, then throughout the early offseason, and then in training camp and the preseason. But to stick him with an extended starting role would be unfair to him, just as it would be for Minter and Doyle.
And the bottom line is the Ravens have to add someone . They can't have one quarterback on the active roster. Austin Reed makes sense as a temporary solution to join Fagnano, as he was at least with the team this offseason, but he has never taken an NFL snap.
Unfortunately, it's not like capable quarterbacks grow on trees. There's a shortage of passable starting quarterbacks, much less backups or backups to backups. But that doesn't mean it would be impossible to find one.
Rapoport said he'd expect the Ravens to consider quarterback trades. Two names he floated were Bears backup Tyson Bagent and Cardinals recently benched starter Jacoby Brissett .
Bagent, 26, makes sense for a few reasons. First and foremost, he was with Doyle in Chicago last year. Second, it's unclear whether he's even Caleb Williams ' primary backup right now. He performed decently in a win over the Jets earlier this year but struggled badly in a loss to the Packers the following week. Overall, he has zero passing touchdowns and three interceptions in three games (two starts) this year.
Case Keenum , on the other hand, played well in his lone start, a win over the Eagles . He got the nod after Bagent had missed much of the week of practice with a concussion, though Bagent returned to primary backup thereafter.
The Bears clearly value Bagent. They gave him a multi-year extension last season. He has shown promise in extremely small sample sizes. He has some creation ability and athleticism, which are helpful in Doyle's offense. All of that also means he wouldn't be cheap, either. There's little reason for Chicago, in a win-now season, to part with Bagent. What if the Bears need a spot start from a backup late in the year? Maybe Baltimore could sweeten the deal by sending a depth piece of their own to Chicago in the deal.
The Ravens must determine how much they want to invest in saving the next few weeks. Bagent would be on the pricier end, and it's not as if his performance this season has inspired much confidence. If Baltimore believes he could eke out a couple of wins, though? Maybe it's worth it.
Brissett has been the Cardinals' de facto bridge starter this year, but he may have lost that position Sunday, when he was benched. In his place, Gardner Minshew threw for three touchdowns in Arizona's stunning 33-30 overtime comeback win over the Cowboys . Mike LaFleur did not commit to Minshew being the starter going forward, but it'd be hard to imagine he's not.
That will be especially true if the Ravens come knocking regarding Brissett. Over the past two seasons, out of 30 quarterbacks, Brissett ranks ...
He is exactly what he has been during his entire career: a low-level starter or high-level backup who has gotten an opportunity to be the starter only when the need arises.
But the need is there for Baltimore, and perhaps Arizona feels the opposite. Minshew is pretty similar in terms of overall player archetype, and the Cardinals also have rookie Carson Beck . If Arizona feels OK with Minshew and Beck, and it can get a solid draft-capital return for Brissett, it could make sense to do so, especially at this point in the Cardinals' long-term timeline.
There are some other names that could be considered, though Bagent and Brissett stand out as more natural/sensical picks. If Baltimore goes elsewhere, though, here are a few names worth mentioning. View this as throwing names at a wall and seeing what sticks.
In the coming days, you'll likely hear Mac Jones ' name bandied about in connection to Baltimore.
It doesn't seem particularly realistic. Kyle Shanahan has said many times he wants to keep Jones, and the 49ers , like the Bears, have legitimate Super Bowl aspirations right here, right now. If the 49ers needed a spot start — or even just a few series — from Jones to win a game, it would be worth it. Unlike the Bears, though, the 49ers don't have a second legit backup. Kurtis Rourke has never played an NFL snap.
The Ravens would likely need to blow away the 49ers to have any shot at Jones, and that simply hasn't been Baltimore GM Eric DeCosta's M.O. Instead, Bagent and Brissett seem like top options, with a flyer on a younger, potentially intriguing player also a legitimate route for the Ravens to take.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Jaguars lose standout DT DaVon Hamilton: Trade partners for Jacksonville include Cowboys, Colts
summary: Hamilton has been a stud for one of the league's best run defenses
full_text:
One of the best, most underrated players on one of the best, most underrated teams in the NFL has suffered what appears to be a season-ending injury. Jaguars defensive tackle DaVon Hamilton tore his quad in Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts , per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , a massive blow for a team with legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. Hamilton is expected to miss the rest of the year, though he'll undergo further testing Monday.
Hamilton, 29, has been a crucial fixture up front for the 5-2 Jaguars. Jacksonville leads the NFL in yards per rush allowed (3.4), rushing yards per game allowed (77.4) and defensive rushing success rate (61.9%). No opponent has run for more than 56 yards against the Jaguars this year.
Hamilton even filled in as an emergency long snapper in a win over the Eagles earlier this year. Hamilton ranks ninth in Pro Football Focus' run defense grades for interior defensive linemen. Of Hamilton's 16 tackles this season, 15 have come on run plays (the other one is a half sack), and 12 have been on plays that gained 3 or fewer yards.
"So important," Liam Coen said in September about Hamilton. "... He's so stout. He plays the two gap, whatever gap and a half, he can play it all. He can disrupt if he does need to get into the backfield and pierce things. ... He's so selfless. He works his tail off, and there are not many guys that are better examples for what we're hunting up out of a Jaguar than DaVon."
Now, though, the Jaguars will be hunting for his replacement. In fact, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , the Jaguars were already in the market for interior help before Hamilton's injury. Jacksonville does have Arik Armstead , Ruke Orhorhoro , Matt Dickerson and third-round rookie Albert Regis on the interior, but none is nearly as stout against the run as Hamilton.
Here are five options Jacksonville could pursue:
It's impossible to tell what Jerry Jones will do at the trade deadline — and really at any point, ever — but he's never been afraid to make a deal. Otito Ogbonnia isn't a flashy name, but he could be exactly what the Jaguars need. Defensive tackles are rarely flashy names, anyway. Ogbonnia has actually been very good against the run this season: eighth in PFF's run defensive grades for interior defensive linemen, one spot ahead of Hamilton. The Cowboys just blew a lead against the lowly Cardinals . Regardless of what grand plans Jones has, this team should sell at the deadline. Ogbonnia, on a one-year deal, could fetch a solid third-day pick. It almost makes too much sense for both parties.
Yes, this would be an in-division move, but the Colts are imploding and should happily move any player they can; DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson trades last week could be just the tip of the iceberg. While Jonathan Taylor watch is very much on, Grover Stewart is another name to watch. He's a longtime anchor in the middle of the Colts' defense who has a long history of health and production.
Jowon Briggs impressed last year but isn't having his best season in 2026, and he's on a one-year deal. Still, he's only 25, and New York could be looking more into keeping him around rather than parting ways. If they feel stronger about the latter, though, they could get a decent deal. Briggs offers versatility as a player who can play tackle or end, and a fresh start could be good for him. Jacksonville has done well with a lot of journeymen on defense.
The Cardinals are going nowhere, and in the first year of a rebuild under coach Mike LaFleur, Roy Lopez and Andrew Billings are the exact type of veterans Arizona should be looking to flip for draft assets. Lopez signed a two-year deal this summer to return to the team he spent 2023-24 with, and he has played well plugging the middle. Billings just returned from an injury in Week 8 and had a sack in the win over the Cowboys. Either one could be helpful for Jacksonville.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Trey McBride taunts Caleb Downs as Cowboys rookie's struggles reach alarming level
summary: Dallas rebuilt its defense around first-round pick Caleb Downs, but his coverage struggles and costly mistakes were exposed
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys blew a 14-point lead twice against the Arizona Cardinals in a 33-30 overtime defeat. And owner Jerry Jones had many fingers to point during the ugly aftermath.
"It just really is glaring in a negative way how we could be where we were and end up losing that ball game," Jones said. "We had a great chance right at the end to win the game, and had everybody out there that can win games for us, and of course. didn't get it done. So it was a couple of games within the game really that was also telling, and we just just did not play well enough at all to win that ball game. Not well enough after you had the lead the way we did and had the opportunities we had to win that ball game. So it's an indictment of the whole show."
The jarring thing about Dallas' defensive collapse and their overall defensive struggles in 2026 is that the Cowboys' front office made an effort to ensure something like this wouldn't happen after their 2025 meltdown. Defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus was fired and replaced by Christian Parker. Jones traded for Rashan Gary , signed two new safeties and a new cornerback, drafted two defensive players in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft (Ohio State safety Caleb Downs and UCF edge rusher Malachi Lawrence ), and traded for Joey Porter Jr .
Yet, they still profile as one of the NFL 's worst defenses across the board.
Third down conversion rate allowed
Dallas traded up one spot to draft Downs 11th overall to be a focal point of its new-look defense, working in the hybrid nickel corner/safety role. It's a role that earned Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean a first-team All-Pro selection in Philadelphia last season. Trey McBride , a 2025 first-team All-Pro who leads the NFL with 66 catches in 2026, was far from impressed with Downs on Sunday.
After he beat Downs for a 15-yard gain on third-and-6 with 2:30 left in the first half on Sunday, McBride taunted him.
"First-round pick? You're a first-rounder?," McBride said to Downs, via Fox Sports . "For what? For what? First round for what?"
That was far from the only miscue for Downs in Sunday's loss. Downs had an angle to tackle Tyler Allgeier behind the line of scrimmage, but he took a bad pursuit angle and completely whiffed. Allgeier exploded through the Cowboys' defense for a 63-yard rushing touchdown, Arizona's first of the day. That play gave the Cardinals the belief they could actually pull off their eventual comeback.
Tyler Allgeier breaks free for a 63-yard rushing TD! AZvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/PuMUPt7CLa
Downs was also bullied on a block down the field on a 52-yard run by Allgeier down the left sideline. Allgeier is now the first player this season with multiple runs of 50-plus yards in a single game.
Block in the back? Maybe Froholdt abused Caleb Downs 💀 pic.twitter.com/FO81QINMoK
Obviously, the Cowboys allowing an NFL-worst 152.8 rushing yards per game is a team effort, but Downs certainly has a hand in that effort. He did also team up with defensive tackle Kenny Clark to stonewall No. 3 overall pick running back Jeremiyah Love on a fourth and goal at the one to force a turnover on downs on Sunday. Overall, Pro Football Focus assigned Downs a 68.8 run defense grade through the first eight weeks of the season, which ranks 46th among 98 qualified safeties.
In coverage, Downs has allowed 20 of the 24 passes thrown his way to be completed (83.3%) for 230 yards and three passing touchdowns, per TruMedia. That's good for a 9.6 passing yards-per-attempt average and a 146.2 passer rating against as the primary defender in coverage. For reference, 158.3 is a perfect passer rating. Among 174 players with 20 or more passes thrown their way this season, Downs' 146.2 passer rating allowed in coverage is the third worst in the entire NFL this season. Only Baltimore Ravens safety Malaki Starks (149.3) and Miami Dolphins cornerback Jason Marshall Jr . (154.2) have surrendered a worse passer rating against as the primary defender in coverage than Downs through eight weeks.
The Cowboys have been an injury-plagued secondary. Porter Jr. suffered an ankle injury on Sunday, and Downs himself didn't finish Sunday's game after entering concussion protocol in the fourth quarter. However, Downs has as big a role as anyone on Dallas' defense in their continued struggles in the opening half of the 2026 season.
author: Garrett Podell

title: Lamar Jackson injury throws huge wrench into looming contract talks with Ravens
summary: Jackson's current contract runs through the 2027 season
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens suddenly find themselves in an uncomfortable position. Of course, the most immediate issue for the organization is seeing Lamar Jackson suffer a right thumb injury on his first play back from a three-game absence due to a high ankle sprain. Now, the two-time NFL MVP needs surgery and could be sidelined for the rest of the season. From a big-picture view, however, the concern is more existential: How do they handle their future with Jackson?
One of the storylines that has hovered over the franchise is that Jackson is due for a contract extension. His current deal — a five-year, $260 million contract that, at the time, made him the highest-paid player in the league — runs out after the 2027 campaign. Jackson also has no guaranteed salary remaining on his current contract beyond this season.
Since signing that deal, Jackson has earned another MVP award (2023), was runner-up for MVP in 2024, and is 34-17 over his 51 regular season starts with a 110.1 passer rating. He's also 2-2 in the playoffs over this stretch with a 105.8 passer rating. More recently, he looked great in new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's system, as his yards per attempt (10.1), air yards per attempt (10.9) and 70.8% completion rate in four games played entering Week 8 were all on pace to be career highs.
Those will be just some of the figures he and his camp will likely point to as they once again look to reset the market at the position, as every player of his caliber aims to do when they sit down at the negotiating table.
That said, the Ravens may have some trepidation this time around, particularly as these injuries start to pile up. Before this thumb injury that could knock him out of Baltimore's final nine games of the year, he had already been sidelined for three games with an ankle injury. Last year, Jackson missed a total of four games due to back and hamstring injuries.
Possibly resetting the market once again with a quarterback who is about to turn 30 in January and is starting to have injuries pile up is a risky endeavor for the franchise, which could result in another murky negotiation. If you remember last time around, it wasn't smooth sailing between Jackson and the Ravens leading up to their most recent agreement. In fact, Jackson requested a trade before ultimately inking his deal to remain in Baltimore, so there is some history of things getting spicy between these two sides.
With this latest right thumb injury adding to his growing list of ailments on his résumé, it throws a rather seismic wrench into these future talks.
Lamar Jackson heads to the locker room after his first pass attempt with an apparent hand injury. pic.twitter.com/JVUQYjJV8H
Along with Jackson, quarterbacks like C.J. Stroud , Caleb Williams , Jayden Daniels and Drake Maye are all due to sign extensions this offseason. Each of them will try to exceed Patrick Mahomes , who is currently the highest-paid quarterback in the NFL with an average annual value of $64 million per season. Dak Prescott is the only other quarterback currently making $60 million per season, but that will soon change with all of these signal-callers — including Jackson — up. Right now, 11 other quarterbacks are ahead of Jackson's $52 million AAV.
Does Jackson push to once again become the highest-paid player in NFL history when he signs his contract? Does he simply look to be among the highest-paid quarterbacks in the league? That distinction could be the difference between a deal getting done in somewhat quick fashion or dragging out throughout the summer.
For the Ravens, they may be painted into a corner. They'll rightfully have concerns about signing Jackson to another monster, possibly record-setting extension, but what else are they going to do? The organization is 7-14 without Jackson since his first start in Week 11 of the 2018 season (including playoffs).
It's hard to imagine Jackson playing on a lame duck contract, so they'll either need to sign him or trade him. Does the organization have the appetite to blow it up, ship the two-time MVP away and rebuild? Maybe it depends on how venomous these upcoming negotiations get.
The most likely option is that they pay him, no matter how much their hands shake as they slide the contract across the table. Whether it pays off with a deep playoff run or a Super Bowl is a different question entirely, especially as these injuries become more prevalent.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: Cowboys biggest loser from NFL Week 8; FSU starts coaching search after firing Mike Norvell
summary: Plus, Lamar Jackson played one snap before suffering another long-term injury
full_text:

title: Cowboys should consider trading George Pickens: 5 logical NFL deadline destinations
summary: Pickens received only four targets in Dallas' historic collapse against Arizona, adding urgency to the Cowboys' decision before the NFL trade deadline
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Shortly after Chad Ryland 's game-winning field goal went through the uprights to seal a 33-30 comeback, Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens flew down the hallway and into the locker room by himself. No other teammate, coach, or staff member moved faster to get into the locker room and out of AT&T Stadium after Dallas made ugly history with its blown 14-point lead.
Pickens first one to the lockers, jogged down the tunnel before most media could even set up @1053thefan pic.twitter.com/RVab4T1c5M
Pickens' lack of targets was glaring. CeeDee Lamb led the way with 11 targets on Sunday while tight end Brevyn Spann-Ford was second with five targets. Pickens caught two passes for 48 yards. Four targets in a game simply isn't enough.
Pickens hasn't been bad this season: his 533 yards receiving rank as the 15th most in the NFL in 2026, just behind Trey McBride and just in front of Garrett Wilson (527) and Ja'Marr Chase (492). He is still on pace to exceed 1,100 receiving yards, but it regularly feels like the Cowboys are leaving production out on the field. Since Schottenheimer blamed Pickens' lack of vigor for run blocking for the team's struggling offense in a loss to the Green Bay Packers, he has 10 targets across the last two games.
"If I had the answer, we'd get him involved. I'm not trying to be rude or whatever it is, but he made some plays. Anytime the ball went his way, he came up with them. He had the one, unfortunately came back for a holding," quarterback Dak Prescott said. ... "I'm not sure about even how many targets he had. As I told y'all before, I go through the reads. [I] try to throw it to the open guy and stay consistent and true to that. And so, I've got to go back and look at the film and see if I missed him, see if we could have went to him more, see if we could have went to CeeDee more. I feel like it was a game that CeeDee didn't have as many catches as per usual, but we still had a chance to win and should have won it."
With the NFL trade deadline coming up in eight days on Nov. 10 and the Cowboys off to a 3-5 start and appearing to be going nowhere, it would make sense for Dallas to field trade calls for Pickens. He is playing out the franchise tag, and he will command near-top-of-the-market value on his second multi-year NFL contract. Dallas will also have to deal with balancing cornerback Joey Porter Jr. 's contract situation, since he, too, is set to be a free agent after the season.
After trading away draft capital to get Porter Jr. and Quinnen Williams, Dallas could use some additional ammunition in its 2027 NFL Draft war chest. So who could be blowing up owner/general manager Jerry Jones' phone for Pickens if word leaks out that they will listen to trade calls for their 25-year-old Pro Bowl wideout? Here is a look at five potential landing spots.
Jerry Jones has shown he doesn't care about sending a young star player to a non-divisional rival: he traded Micah Parsons to the Green Bay Packers . The pairing of the 49ers and Pickens makes too much sense.
San Francisco is the NFC's top seed through the first eight weeks of the season, and they have $34.98 million in cap space, the third most in the entire league, per OverTheCap.com. There are no financial barriers to this deal.
Plus, they have a glaring need for Pickens given all their wide receiver injuries. Both Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) were ruled out of their last game played in Week 7. Three wide receivers are on their injured reserve list.
Lastly, the 49ers are all in for 2026 because of their aging core. Christian McCaffrey is 30, Evans is 33, Samuel is 30, George Kittle is 33, Kyle Juszcyk is 35, Trent Williams is 38 and DeForest Buckner is 32. Both Fred Warner and Nick Bosa are healthy right now, but they're both 29 with extensive injury histories.
The Chiefs failed to score a game-winning touchdown after having a second-and-goal at the one with 15 seconds left, and Kansas City was outscored 15-0 in the fourth quarter of their narrow 28-24 road loss against the Denver Broncos on Sunday. You know who could have made a significant difference for quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the fourth quarter in Week 8? The 6-foot-3, 200-pound Pickens.
Kenneth Walker III is starting to lose a little steam after being heavily relied upon to carry the Chiefs' offense on his back. After averaging 133 rushing yards per game and 6.3 yards per carry with six rushing touchdowns in Kansas City's first five games of the season, Walker III is now averaging 52.5 rushing yards per game and 3.0 yards per carry without a touchdown in the last two games.
That's because the Chiefs' passing game requires Travis Kelce to be their No. 1 target, something that isn't a sustainable formula over the course of an 18-week season and beyond. Also, it would be incredibly foolish to waste the rest of Mahomes' glory years. The three-time Super Bowl MVP quarterback is 31, but he hasn't been the same high-flying passer that he was with a true No. 1 wide receiver like Tyreek Hill. Without Hill since 2022, Mahomes' production has taken a notable dip.
Average air yards per pass attempt
* Ranks among 37 qualified quarterbacks since 2022
The Buffalo Bills are the AFC's No. 1 seed through the first eight weeks, and they are always in win-now mode with Josh Allen . Yes, the Bills traded for DJ Moore , but he is probably best as Buffalo's No. 2 receiver on a Super Bowl team. He missed Buffalo's last two games with a shoulder injury prior to returning in Week 8, and he hyperextended his knee in the Bills' 36-10 beatdown of the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens .
Allen hasn't had a true WR1 since the 2024 Stefon Diggs trade. Pickens could help him become the league's most efficient passer. That would probably be enough for the Bills to perhaps win their first Super Bowl in franchise history.
The Las Vegas Raiders trading for Pickens would be a case of taking care of the now and the later. The Kirk Cousins-led Raiders are 4-4 and just one game out of the AFC's No. 7 seed. Giving Cousins, whose 19 passing touchdowns rank as the second most in the NFL, Pickens to pair with Brock Bowers could really make Klint Kubiak's offense pop.
Among the players officially listed as wide receivers on the Raiders' roster, Tre Tucker , a 2023 third-round pick, is the best they have. He could also help accelerate Fernando Mendoza's long-term development. Pickens is just two years older than the 23-year-old Mendoza, so the quarterback could spend the bulk of his career with a high-caliber wide receiver in addition to the 23-year-old Bowers at tight end.
Perhaps living in Las Vegas would dull the novelty of going out on The Strip that Pickens and Lamb experienced when they visited for "Monday Night Football" last season.
Despite being 6-1 and the No. 2 seed in the NFC, the Minnesota Vikings have the sixth-lowest scoring offense (20.0 points per game) in the entire NFL. Their lack of rhythm in the passing game is a major reason for that, as their Kyler Murray-quarterbacked passing attack is averaging the second-fewest passing yards per game (165.6) in the entire NFL.
Yes, Minnesota has 2022 NFL Offensive Player of the Year Justin Jefferson and former first-round pick Jordan Addison at wide receiver, but its offense could clearly use another weapon to help Murray find his groove as a Viking. They have been rumored to be in pursuit of Jonathan Taylor , but perhaps Pickens could also help fix the issues on the offensive side of the ball.
author: Garrett Podell

title: NFL Week 9 early odds: Ravens become home underdogs to Jaguars after Lamar Jackson injury
summary: A look at where the odds and spreads currently stand heading into Week 9, including a big move in Baltimore
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens will likely have to go the rest of the 2026 regular season without star quarterback Lamar Jackson . The two-time NFL MVP made his return to action on Sunday after a three-game absence due to an ankle injury, but that comeback was very short-lived. On the first play from scrimmage for the Ravens offense, Jackson jammed his right thumb on Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau on a follow-through. That injury not only knocked him out of the game, but head coach Jesse Minter told reporters postgame that Jackson will go on injured reserve and will undergo surgery.
On top of this injury turning Baltimore's season upside down, it's also thrown the line for their Week 9 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars for a loop. title: Steelers' Jaylen Warren is 'on fire': Why the breakout running back keeps getting better
summary: Warren tied his career high with 143 rushing yards on his 28th birthday, continuing a breakout season that has made him the engine of Pittsburgh's offense
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- On a team that includes several future Hall of Fame players, Jaylen Warren was the talk of the Steelers' locker room following a 27-6 trouncing of the Browns that gave Pittsburgh the outright lead in the AFC North division.
Warren, who turned 28 on Sunday, celebrated the occasion by rushing for 143 yards (tying his career-high) and a touchdown on 17 carries. It was the second consecutive 100-yard game and the fourth 100-yard game of the season for Warren, a former undrafted rookie who in the midst of a career year.
"Jaylen is on fire," coach Mike McCarthy said afterward. "You can't get him the ball enough."
“Jaylen is on fire. You can’t get him the ball enough.” #Steelers coach Mike McCarthy on Jaylen Warren. pic.twitter.com/b3e2gtBCbQ
Why is Warren's level of success enhanced in Year 5? It starts with his featured role. On Sunday, Pittsburgh's offensive line bullied Cleveland's defensive front to the tune of 200 yards and three touchdowns on 33 carries. It was a unit that was clearly motivated to respond to Cleveland pass rusher Jared Verse's recent comments with their play on the field.
Most everyone who watched Sunday's game saw Steelers guard Mason McCormick's body slam of Verse in the first half. But just as telling was McCormick and center Zach Frazier sprinting to the other side of the field at the end of the first quarter. While his teammates were running, fellow Steelers lineman Brock Hoffman made a "feed me" reference to the Steelers' sideline, a subtle request to McCarthy to continue running the ball.
Pittsburgh's defense has also helped Warren and the offense. The Steelers' defense, which hasn't allowed a touchdown in seven quarters, has enjoyed more time on the bench while watching Warren do his thing.
"He's a bowling ball with teeth, man," said Steelers linebacker T.J. Watt , who had two of Pittsburgh's eight sacks of Deshaun Watson . "You can't get him down. Jaylen is just funny, man. He's the guy that's out there in December when we're practicing and it's like 12 degrees, he's in a T-shirt and shorts. You're like, 'What the heck?' That's just who he is. He's a hard tackle. He's a great locker room guy. Very selfless. But man, he loves football and you can see it in the way that he plays."
Cam Heyward, the longest-tenured Steelers player, gave Warren the ultimate compliment.
"I've been blessed to play with a lot of great running backs. Jaylen is not short of that," he said. "He's every bit as advertised. Having Rico [Dowdle] as well, they do a great job of being a 1-2 punch. When they're able to sustain drives, it means we're on the sideline and we can put our feet up."
Speaking of sustaining drives, that's what Warren did on his 51-yard run that came on a third-and-13 play. The play helped give the Steelers their first double-digit lead of the day.
"To be able to call a trap on third [and long] and get a first down is pretty wild," Rodgers said. "Didn't expect that. Can't remember the last time that happened when I was out there."
Jaylen Warren just went 51 yards on 3rd and 13 😳 CLEvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YD1Naon9lN
The biggest reason for Warren's emergence, though, is the man himself, although Warren's humility would never allow him to say that himself. Warren has only gotten better during his time with the Steelers.
After a somewhat disappointing 2024 season, Warren told CBS Sports that he planned to spend more time getting treatment at the facility. That change has clearly helped. Warren ultimately ran for a career-high 958 yards in 2025 and is currently on pace to have the most prolific rushing season by a Steelers running back since Le'Veon Bell.
"It's definitely paying off," Warren said on Sunday when asked about his extra time at the recovery table.
“I’d say it’s definitely paying off.” #Steelers Jaylen Warren on some of the changes that have led to his success. pic.twitter.com/J6JV2Gm0s5
Lastly, Warren's intangibles are another reason for his success. His team-first attitude has made him a locker room favorite. His teammates want him to succeed, which is evident every time he makes a big play and whenever his teammates are asked about him.
“Love having him on our team. He’s a fantastic teammate, and he’s making a lot of plays.” #Steelers Aaron Rodgers on Jaylen Warren. pic.twitter.com/RtCUght8GR
For Warren, it's about being the best player he can be so he can help the Steelers achieve their Super Bowl goals. That mindset helped him make the Steelers' roster as an undrafted rookie, and it's serving as the main catalyst for his breakout season.

title: Wilson's 2027 NFL mock draft: Browns trade up for QB, five passers land in Round 1
summary: Jets, Titans and Browns all have multiple first-round picks
full_text:
Hey, fun story: Remember when the 2027 QB class was supposed to be loaded? We spent the summer talking about six or seven potential first-rounders , including two names — Dante Moore and Arch Manning — who entered the season as my QB1 and QB2. Two months later, Moore's season is over after suffering a concussion vs. USC in late September, and Manning has been so inconsistent we're wondering whether he should even enter the draft .
And, now, for the third straight draft cycle, the preseason QB hype hasn't come close to matching what we've seen on the field. That doesn't mean there aren't first-round passers in this class; it just means figuring out which ones deserve to be there.
Darian Mensah is my QB1 , and while the competition Miami has faced leaves some (possibly many) questions unanswered, he's been consistently outstanding. Meanwhile, Drew Mestemaker has gone from a quarterback few people were talking about to the most buzzworthy one after a hot start in Stillwater. I wrote about him after he outplayed Moore and Oregon early in the season , and we'll have to see if he decides to return to school for 2027.
And it's worth remembering that my preseason First-Round Readiness Score (FRED) model was higher on Mensah, Mestemaker and Jayden Maiava (all first-rounders in this mock draft) than some of the bigger names in this class. Meanwhile, Moore and Manning entered the season with more questions than their preseason draft projections might have suggested. Two months through the season, and what we've seen on the field has largely backed up what the model was telling us.
Of course, there's one name we haven't talked about, and he happens to be the best player in this class. He's also not a quarterback. The last time a non-QB went No. 1 overall was in 2022 when the Jaguars took pass rusher Travon Walker. The last time a wide receiver was the first overall pick? Thirty-one years ago, when the Jets selected Keyshawn Johnson. Which brings us to Ohio State's Jeremiah Smith, who has been dominant since the day he arrived in Columbus.
I wrote back in September about why passing on him might be taking a bigger risk than drafting him high . He's big, physical, can win at all three levels and makes ridiculous catches look routine. Think Julio Jones or Terrell Owens or Calvin Johnson.
And yes, the still-winless Chargers (and current holders of the top pick in the 2027 draft) already have Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey, and they've invested plenty of draft capital at receiver in recent years. Doesn't matter. Because if you have the No. 1 overall pick and no one willing to trade up, you're taking Smith a million times out of a million. This isn't about filling the biggest need on your roster; it's about adding the best player in the draft. And when that player is that much better than everyone else, why overthink it?
So where does that leave us? With five quarterbacks in this first-round mock, no Manning for the second straight mock draft , and plenty of questions left to answer. As for the non-QB positions, offensive tackle leads the way with six players in this mock draft, followed by wide receiver with five.
Keep reading to see how all 32 picks shake out.

title: Cover 32: Why Jets have every reason to trade Breece Hall, plus Week 8 games balls, gaffes
summary: Tyler Sullivan dives into the biggest items from Week 8, including Joe Burrow's six-touchdown day and Chad Ryland's redemption
full_text:
The New York Jets set the NFL ablaze at last year's trade deadline. The club made a couple of seismic moves, shipping away corner Sauce Gardner and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams for a collection of draft picks. Fast-forward about 12 months, and they're being eyed again as a seller. For the most part, folks have pondered the possibility of star wideout Garrett Wilson being available, but the organization has slammed that door shut .
The door that should be kept wide open, however, is trading running back Breece Hall .
Following the Week 8 loss to the Raiders , New York is 2-6 on the season and will travel to Kansas City to face the Chiefs in Week 9 before the Nov. 10 deadline rolls in. In all likelihood, they'll have accumulated seven losses over their first nine games once they reach the deadline. That's a recipe for a team to look itself in the mirror, realize the 2026 campaign won't bear any fruit, and move pieces to build for tomorrow.
Hall fits the bill as a player who is more valuable to them as a trade asset rather than a contributor on the field. That's thanks, in part, to the emergence of fellow running back Braelon Allen .
As Hall has been sidelined with a quad injury, Allen has flourished in the starting role. Over the last five games with Hall on the shelf, Allen has started in each contest and has rushed for 504 yards on a 5.4 yards-per-carry average and has two rushing touchdowns. Allen is also averaging 3.92 yards per carry after contact over this stretch, which is elite. For reference, that's better than Derrick Henry (3.11) and Jahmyr Gibbs (3.39) this season.
In the loss, Allen remained one of the bright spots for the Jets, rushing for a career-high 147 yards on a 7.0 yards-per-carry clip.
Braelon Allen scores and now has 142 rushing yards on the day! LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/aGaC9Th33s
With Allen, a 2024 fourth-round pick, under team control through 2027 and on his rookie contract, Hall becomes an expendable piece that the Jets should exploit before the deadline.
When healthy, Hall is an electrifying piece out of the backfield, notching his first-ever 1,000-yard rushing season last year for the Jets. In three games this year, before missing time with this quad injury, he's posted modest numbers, totaling 265 yards from scrimmage. Still, he would garner plenty of interest on the trade market if New York puts him on the block, especially as he nears a return to the field. Despite not playing in Week 8, Hall was limited in practice all last week, signaling he's close.
There are a slew of teams interested in adding a back at the deadline, but the supply may be running thin. Jonathan Taylor and Saquon Barkley have been two big names circulating in the rumor mill, but neither may end up being moved. The Eagles effectively shut down any talk of them moving Barkley, while the Colts are not actively shopping Taylor and would likely need to be blown away with an offer to deal him.
This creates quite the opportunity for the Jets to cash in with Hall. They could deal him to an RB-needy team, further strengthen their treasure trove of draft capital, and turn the keys of the backfield over to Allen permanently.  They'd also get out from under Hall's contract, which runs through 2028 and sees his base salary jump from $5.16 million in 2026 to $13.1 million in 2027 and $14.1 million in 2028.
It makes too much sense to explore a trade and ship Hall to the highest bidder.
How Game Balls work: Six are awarded to standout players from the slate of teams that won their contests, and only one player on a team can get a game ball.
Joe Burrow needed to throw it all over the yard in Cincinnati's overtime win over the Titans on Sunday. The Bengals quarterback was clutch down the stretch, throwing an 18-yard touchdown to Tee Higgins to tie the game at 36 with just over a minute left in regulation. Then, he scrambled for what proved to be the game-winning touchdown. Burrow became just the second player in NFL history with at least 450 passing yards, five passing touchdowns and one rushing touchdown in a game (Norm Van Brocklin, 1951).
Joe Burrow today (passing + rushing): - 472 total yards - 6 total touchdowns 📺 CBS & @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/OSGgAriSWT
Allgeier was the key cog in Arizona's upset win over the Cowboys in Dallas. Amid a quarterback change midgame as the Cardinals went from Jacoby Brissett to Gardner Minshew , Allgeier was the steady presence out of the backfield. His 63-yard touchdown run at the end of the third quarter began the late rally, and he had another explosive run (52 yards) that set up another touchdown. Allgeier is the first player this season with two rushes of 50-plus yards in a game.
Tyler Allgeier breaks free for a 63-yard rushing TD! AZvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/PuMUPt7CLa
Bowers remains one of the biggest mismatches in the NFL and found paydirt twice in Las Vegas' victory over the Jets. This was his third career game with multiple touchdowns and his 11th career game with at least 90 yards receiving. That's tied for the second most by a tight end age 23 or younger.
Just throw it up to Brock Bowers LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/3XvS9rjBy2
The Steelers defense smothered the Browns en route to a 27-6 win in Pittsburgh. Queen was key among the star figures on the defensive side of the ball, leading the team with 12 total tackles and accounting for 1.5 of the eight total sacks they piled up on Deshaun Watson . He also forced a fumble by Watson on Cleveland's second possession of the game, which set up a Steelers touchdown.
Sack and a fumble forced by the Steelers defense 😤 CLEvsPIT on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/gDaB2D1rl9
Anzalone was one of the early tone setters for the Buccaneers as the defense shut out the Falcons , 16-0. As a unit, they created four turnovers, all of which were interceptions by Michael Penix Jr . Anzalone tallied two of those picks, and each of them came in the first quarter.
Alex Anzalone intercepts Michael Penix Jr. for the second time in the first quarter ATLvsTB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jWgIqEE7Ye
Tuten emerged from the Jaguars bye week and continued his ascent with a stellar two-touchdown showing in the blowout win over the Colts. The second-year back became the third player in franchise history with at least 100 yards rushing, 50 yards receiving and two total touchdowns in a game, joining Fred Taylor and Maurice Jones-Drew .
BHAYSHUL TUTEN RUNNING THROUGH DEFENDERS FOR A 39-YARD TD INDvsJAX on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/d2MvvxMdPw
All in all, Cam Ward had one of his better days as a pro, throwing for 304 yards and two touchdowns in a loss to Cincinnati. Despite that, he still showed some warts at the worst possible time. After Joe Burrow knotted the game at 36 apiece with just over a minute left in regulation, Ward led the offense to the Cincinnati 45-yard line, and it felt like the Titans were in a position to attempt a game-winning field goal.
However, after a seven-yard run to set up third-and-3, Ward did the only thing he couldn't do in that situation. The former No. 1 overall pick was sacked for a 13-yard loss, eliminating the possibility of a field goal attempt altogether.
Dexter Lawrence takes down Cam Ward for a sack in the final minute 💪 TENvsCIN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/V2ju4flSe1
Tennessee punted the ball away; the game eventually went to overtime, and the Bengals pulled off the victory.
Despite putting up 27 points in a win over the Browns, Steelers wideout DK Metcalf was essentially a non-factor, catching just one pass despite seeing a team-high six targets. Not only that, but he had one of the biggest gaffes of the slate in the third quarter.
