full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 01: Tyler Allgeier #22 of the Arizona Cardinals carries the ball against the Dallas Cowboys during the second half of an NFL football game at AT&T Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals went into training camp with one position group that was deemed to be no problem: the running back room. And now? RELATED: LOVE’S INJURY STATUS Against the Dallas Cowboys, a 33-30 victory on the road, the only healthy running back that remained on the roster during the game was veteran Tyler Allgeier. This ended up being a good thing because he balled out for 147 yards, scored two touchdowns, and was a key component of the win. Rookie Jeremiyah Love was deemed ready to play, but re-injured an ankle. Bam Morris, the game’s RB3, took a solid hit to the helmet from Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown and had to leave the game. Morris fumbled on the play with 21 seconds remaining in the first half. Dallas then drove into field goal range, but their kicker hooked it right. Neither running back returned to the game. This forced every carry onto the shoulders of Allgeier. In the game, he scored on a 63-yard run with :57 left in the third quarter, and on his next carry reeled off a 52-yarder. Which is all well and good, but after a long run like this, usually, the running back goes to the sideline and rests for a few plays. Not in this game. Allgeier stepped right back into the huddle. The next play called was Allgeier up the middle for four yards. So much for a well-deserved break. The team’s best asset So, what now? Surely, the Cardinals can’t go into every contest with a single running back. In training camp, the position group was viewed as a stacked room full of really good talent. There were suggestions and rumors that perhaps Arizona should trade a guy. James Conner was thought to be close to being ready to come back to the practice field. Same for Trey Benson. Bam Knight was re-signed in March from last year’s roster to a one-year deal. Corey Kiner was still under contract. Then, GM Monti Ossenfort selected Love with the third overall pick in the NFL Draft. Allgeier was one of the “splash” moves in free agency. He was seen as the new starting running back after several successful seasons with the Atlanta Falcons before Love was drafted. In August, the team was awarded Evan Hull off waivers from the Houston Texans, and he played well in preseason. Tre Stewart was signed in mid-August. The running back room was bursting with players and talent. Love, Allgeier, Conner, and Benson were viewed as a spectacular display of talent. Knight would most likely become a kickoff returner. Kiner was traded to the New England Patriots. Stewart was a last-day cut from training camp. Conner was placed on IR. Hull was signed to the practice squad. Benson was waived, then reverted to the team after he cleared waivers and was placed on the IR/injury list. Our inactives for today's game pic.twitter.com/4N0GMmtQX1 — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 1, 2026 So, the Cardinals began the season with Love as the starter, Allgeier as his backup, and Knight as RB3, with Hull on the practice squad. Meanwhile, the team kept a close eye on Conner’s recovery and hoped that one day he could return. With Love always a question mark, the coaches brought up Hull as insurance, but against Dallas, he was listed as inactive. Apparently, nobody consulted their crystal ball first. The injury front And now? Knight has a concussion, which is good news. The bad side is that this is usually 10 days before the player is reactivated. So, against the Seattle Seahawks, Knight won’t be available. They really need to let him completely heal. Franchise pick and they keep putting back out there. — Kelly Storms (@kellystorms) November 1, 2026 Now Love? All of us know he has had ankle issues since getting hurt in a preseason game. Since that time, he has injured both ankles. Against the Cowboys, Love suffered a new injury: a higher ankle sprain. Several media outlets are suggesting that, because Love keeps getting hurt with the same type of injury, the Cardinals should just shut him down, place him on IR, and allow him time to completely heal for next year. That leaves Allgeier and Hull to play out the schedule. This same scenario happened last year. All of the good starting backs became injured, and the team crawled their way towards the end of the schedule with practice squad running backs. Isn’t that what Arizona is dangerously close to becoming? If Allgeier becomes injured, the team’s run game will lie solely on Hull, a practice squad guy. Attrition happens to every team and is the resident evil during the back half of every NFL season. What should be done? For one, already on the Cardinals’ practice squad is veteran Jerome Ford, age 27. Elevate him now. Ford (5’-10”, 210 pounds) was a fifth-round draft pick of the Cleveland Browns in 2022. This was the time frame when Cleveland had both Nick Chubb, Kareem Hunt, and D’Ernest Johnson. Ford made the final roster and returned kickoffs. The next season, Chubb sustained a horrible knee injury, and Ford split carries with Hunt and had a career-high 813 yards on 204 carries with four TDs. He played four seasons with the Browns, so he has experience. During his career, he had 107 receptions for 647 yards, so he has been involved in the short passing game. That will give Arizona Allgeier, Ford as his backup, and Hull at RB3. Any other options? Veteran Cam Akers remains unsigned and would be a good backup. He has played in 59 NFL games with 17 starts. Cardinals fans will remember him from the Los Angeles Rams. Trayveon Williams was a sixth-round pick by the Cincinnati Bengals in 2019 and played 75 games in seven years. Or maybe Ossenfort can scour every team’s practice squad and find a healthy body. Almost every team has a minimum of one running back. Several teams have numerous RBs. Listed on other teams’ practice squads: Frank Gore, Jr. – Bills Jaleel McLaughlin – Browns Israel Abanikanda – Cowboys Dameon Pierce – Eagles Cash Jones – Falcons
author: Barry Shuck

title: What is the Cardinals’ head coach Mike LaFleur saying about a QB change?
summary: As an Arizona Cardinals fan, were you able to watch the game against the Dallas Cowboys? If not, find a YouTube source and watch it. The game is a tale of two halves. It is also a tale of two quarterbacks: starter Jacoby Brissett and his backup Gardner Minshew. RELATED: CARDINALS BENCH BRISSETT AND OFFENSE […]
full_text: Head coach Mike LaFleur (Photo by Chris Coduto/Getty Images) | Getty Images As an Arizona Cardinals fan, were you able to watch the game against the Dallas Cowboys? If not, find a YouTube source and watch it. The game is a tale of two halves. It is also a tale of two quarterbacks: starter Jacoby Brissett and his backup Gardner Minshew. RELATED: CARDINALS BENCH BRISSETT AND OFFENSE TAKES OFF For two quarters and one series, the Cardinals got into the Red Zone three times and could not cash in. They scored three points and had 130 yards of total offense. Brissett was sacked four times and held the ball too long. He overthrew several receivers numerous times. The team’s best target, TE Trey McBride, had one catch for five yards and only 22 rushing yards. Minshew came into the game during the second possession of Quarter 3. The Cardinals were down 17-3 after Dallas kicked a field goal right after the half, and Brissett led the offense to a six-play drive that ended with a punt after he was sacked twice. Minshew entered the game with 1:35 left in the third quarter. On first down, he connected with WR Devin Duvernay for seven yards. On second down, RB Tyler Allgeier took it to the house to the tune of 63 yards to cut the lead to 17-10. Keep in mind, all game, Dallas was in total control. All of their fans in attendance, all 90,763, knew for three quarters that their beloved Cowboys were going to win this game without any problems. In the end, the Cardinals took the game into overtime and won 33-30. Minshew had orchestrated two comebacks, one in overtime, and the other with 1:09 in regulation to tie the game at 30-all. In the first half, Arizona had 130 total yards, whereas when the final gun sounded, they had 437. Minshew threw three touchdowns. The offense suddenly could not be stopped, and every play, every decision was the correct path. Plus, the Cardinals are now 1-0 under Minshew and 3-15 under Brissett. During the post-game press conference, Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur addressed the quarterback situation going forward. He addressed many issues, such as injuries, but this article is strictly what Coach said about the quarterbacks. Here is what LaFleur stated: Q: Just kind of, where is this team right now that has to be exhilarating the way that ended up? A : I don’t know if there are any words that I can express about this team right now other than that they’re resilient and they just keep fighting. They’re always in the fight. That was a total team effort right there. Obviously, we didn’t do enough on offense, and that was a collective. That was not just on one person. That was collective. In the first half, our defense kept us around. They kept us around and had a really good offense. That’s a very good offense. And they played extremely well. Shoot, they averaged 3.6 yards per play today. And for the special teams to do what they did, miss the extra point, and then come back and be resilient. It’s just resilience, and I’m proud of those guys. MINSHEW MAGIC OH MY! pic.twitter.com/KCtTmz4Av4 — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Q: What went into your decision to sit Jacoby and play Gardner? A: I just I thought we needed a spark and again it had it was a collective deal. I need to be better with our scheme. Obviously, I need to be better with our play calling, and all of us need it. We we got a we got a lot to fix right now. I don’t want this last 30 minutes or 35 minutes to mask the stuff that we need to fix on offense because I know we’re a lot better than that. I know we can execute better than that. So, start this week. I’m just excited about this win right now. Q: So, if that was how it looked with those two, why not make that change earlier today or earlier in the season? A: Yeah, again, it was collective. That’s, I know what the story is going to be, and I understand that, and so does he. But that was collective, and it starts with me. Q: What were the things that Gardner did that unlocked the offense? A: Yeah, he did a good job. Obviously, extended a few plays, stuff like that. But I thought his timing was great. He’s had a lot of success in this league, guys, and he’s about as resilient as they come, too. If you ask Gardner, he’s ready at all times. I thought the guys made some plays for him, and he was getting the ball out of his hands. Obviously, kind of what unlocked it to start was he started with a six-yard completion to Duvernay. Then we have that long run by TA right there. And it just kind of somewhat unlocked and loosened them up. Like, that’s why you need explosives and big plays because it loosens people up. I’m going to flip it really quick because I can. The defense played awesome. But we ended up with three receivers, one running back, and our right tackle going down, and all those kinds of things. Then the quarterback change. And for those guys to continue to battle was unbelievable. I’ve never seen anything like it from an injury standpoint in the skill position in my life. Q: What was your message, or what does it take for a team mentally to stay in and force overtime with a new quarterback and stay in it? A: That’s what we all signed up for. It is what it is. Next man up, and we just saw that at the highest level that I’ve ever been a part of. It got to the point where you’re just like, Gardner doesn’t even know who he is throwing balls to at that point; you don’t know who’s mixing and matching and Mike’s (Wilson) hurting and stuff like that. I’m calling plays based on the formation, and Simi (Fehoko) and Mike are switching themselves at the end right there. So, Simi can do some of the grinder work because of where Mike was at. And Simi’s not feeling great either. Again, I think you guys can tell I’m at a loss for words in terms of just how I feel for that locker room right now. And I feel for the guys that got hurt because every single one of those guys put their body on the line. A lot of young guys in there that I’m excited to watch continue to grow. We’ll see what this list looks like tomorrow once we get back home and get a little bit more of a look at it. But yeah, proud of that locker room. Analysis Obviously, Coach LaFleur won’t divulge anything about the quarterback situation at this point. He will need to get input from OC Nathaniel Hackett, offensive quality control coach Brett Ekkens, and QB coach Matt Schaub. Only then will a decision be made. It was interesting that none of the reporters at the presser specifically asked Coach whether he would stick with Minshew going forward. Not that he would have answered it directly, but it just seemed like a logical conclusion. Another interesting point is that already today there have been a few reports that Brissett may be on the trading block. After all, the NFL trade deadline is November 10, and Brissett is 3-15 in his starts with the Cardinals in two seasons. Jacoby Brissett has ties to Falcons HC Kevin Stefanski. Atlanta is a logical trade destination, as are the QB-needy Baltimore Ravens. — Johnny Venerable (@JohnnyVenerable) November 1, 2026 These reports aren’t that Brissett should be benched because his play has regressed; it is that Brissett should be shipped off. Joey O’Donoghue of Arizona Cardinals Today podcast stated: “You can’t go back to (Brissett). I don’t care. Minshew has got to start here the rest of the way out. And if that’s the case, Jacoby Brissett, with a little over a week before the trade deadline, is a name to watch.” The Baltimore Ravens were down to their third quarterback this past weekend, a kid who went undrafted, Joe Fagnano. The Atlanta Falcons are another possibility. And right now, Brissett’s value would be at his peak. He has only sat one half of one game, so it’s not like Arizona has tossed him on the woodpile and is begging another club to take him. Brissett is in his 11 th season and has played in 109 NFL games with 73 starts. A quarterback-needy team wants a guy who has the experience to come in and not need much instruction. That…

title: Arizona Cardinals news: Cards earn ‘B’ in comeback win over Cowboys
summary: The Cardinals showed an immense amount of grit and emotional fortitude in their comeback win over the Cowboys, which included a quarterback switch from Jacoby Brissett to Gardner Minshew. Mike LaFleur earned his third win of his head-coaching career and it came in dramatic fashion. Kicker Chad Ryland missed an extra point attempt that would […]
full_text: The Cardinals showed an immense amount of grit and emotional fortitude in their comeback win over the Cowboys, which included a quarterback switch from Jacoby Brissett to Gardner Minshew. Mike LaFleur earned his third win of his head-coaching career and it came in dramatic fashion. Kicker Chad Ryland missed an extra point attempt that would have won it in regulation, but he came back to drill the game-winner in overtime. For their efforts, CBS Sports’ John Breech gave the Cardinals a “B” grade. Here’s what he had to say: ‘‘The Cardinals might have just found themselves a new starting QB. With the offense going nowhere, Mike LaFleur decided to bench Jacoby Brissett in the third quarter in favor of Gardner Minshew, and that gamble paid off big time. Minshew entered the game and immediately proceeded to have one of the best fourth quarters of any QB this season: He threw for 166 yards and three touchdowns, including a game-tying 13-yard score to Michael Wilson with just six seconds left in regulation. The Cardinals have plenty of weapons on offense; they just need a QB who can utilize them, and it’s possible that Minshew might be that guy. Minshew was so good that it wouldn’t be surprising if the Cardinals decided to start taking offers for Brissett before the trade deadline.” Was this the correct grade for the Cardinals? Should it be higher? Lower? Let us know below! title: Beaks & Geeks: Cardinals, Cowboys Winners & Losers: Arizona’s offense comes alive in second half in 33-30 win
summary: The Arizona Cardinals are at the point of the season where they need wins. Huge stats and highlight reels are nice, but victories are sorely needed. Today’s game against the Dallas Cowboys comes at a time when Arizona will either have a decent year or be picking in the Top-5 once again in April’s NFL […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TEXAS - NOVEMBER 01: Gardner Minshew #15 of the Arizona Cardinals celebrates 33-30 win in overtime against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals are at the point of the season where they need wins. Huge stats and highlight reels are nice, but victories are sorely needed. Today’s game against the Dallas Cowboys comes at a time when Arizona will either have a decent year or be picking in the Top-5 once again in April’s NFL Draft. RELATED: CARDINALS OFFENSE MOVES WHEN BRISSETT BENCHED The game might be the final for DE Josh Sweat and S Budda Baker, both of whom have been speculated as trade bait ahead of the November 10 NFL trade deadline. In this game, Arizona used their backup QB, backup RB, backup RT, their WR3, and their kick returner as another receiver. The injury list this upcoming week isn’t going to be pretty. At the final gun, the Cardinals won 33-30 in overtime. The Cardinals have beaten Dallas now five times in a row. So, who played well for the Cardinals? Who didn’t? ——————————————————————————– BEAKS Defensive stops – Dallas went for it on fourth-and-one from their own 32-yard line in the first quarter. Trot out the punter, right? The Cowboys, basking in their own glory while playing a two-win team, went for it. LB Mack Wilson read the running play by RB Javonte Williams and stuffed him for a two-yard loss. . @MackWilson forces the turnover on downs 😈 #AZvsDAL | @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/RuVK9s9Vy2 — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 1, 2026 LB Zaven Collins came off the edge for the sack on QB Dak Prescott, which forced Dallas to punt. L.J. Collier’s timely sack forced a Dallas punt late in the fourth quarter. Making the Cowboys have a three-and-out on their only possession in overtime was a huge series of downs. Josh Sweat had a decent second half, including a sack late that forced the Cowboys to think field goal instead of seven. S Andrew Wingard was very active and had several key stops and finished with seven total tackles. Frame it 🖼️ pic.twitter.com/f2k1wE2PgV — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 1, 2026 WR Michael Wilson – Holy smokes. Where was Wilson in the first half? He destroyed the Dallas secondary in the final two quarters. His 17-yard jet sweep in the extra period was the catalyst to get into field goal range. On the final drive before the regular time ran out, he snagged a 21-yard pass and then the game-tying touchdown, with both feet dragging. Quiet first half, but finished with 15 targets, 8 receptions for 111 yards, and one TD. LB Jack Gibbens – Seems like every week Gibbens is leading the Cardinals in total tackles. Against Dallas, that trend continued with 11 tackles. He reads the run very quickly, then makes up his mind and finds the correct gap. 63-YARD HOUSE CALL FOR 22 📞 #AZvsDAL | @NFLonFOX pic.twitter.com/a5VMl6P8WU — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 1, 2026 RB Tyler Allgeier – When Allgeier is told he is the lead back and isn’t going out of the game, he balls out. Both Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight sustained injuries in the first half, so it became the Allgeier Show. He had very few carries and yards in the first half, but made up for it after the half. Exploded for runs of 63 yards and 52 yards and was the difference in the game. Finished with 11 carries for 147 yards, a 13.4 yards-per-carry average, and scored two TDs. All in pretty much two quarters. This week’s “NFC Offensive Player of the Week.” QB Gardner Minshew – Here on ROTB , we ran an article and suggested that perhaps it was time to see what the other quarterbacks on the roster had to offer. After all, QB Jacoby Brissett has a 3-15 record as Arizona’s starting quarterback, so it can’t be any worse. So, you are the backup quarterback and come into the game in the third quarter. What do you do? Well, for one, you use all of the playmakers. That is what Minshew did with Allgeier, Wilson, and, of course, McBride. He didn’t spend a lot of time looking for other receivers and focused on the speedier Wilson and the sure-handedness of McBride. A DOT FROM GARDNER MINSHEW TO MICHAEL WILSON TIES THIS UP WITH :06 ON THE CLOCK! #AZvsDAL | 📺 Fox pic.twitter.com/xYLhtBVW3i — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 1, 2026 Lo and behold, the offense not only moved, but it also scored actual points. No, really, like touchdowns. What a sparkplug. Arizona scored 20 points in the final stanza, and moved the ball down into field goal range in the overtime period to get into field goal range all on Minshew’s arm and accuracy. In the end, the Cardinals not only had a win, but also totaled 467 yards in total offense. Minshew went 17 for 23 for 188 yards with three TD throws against zero picks or fumbles, was sacked just once, and had a 137.3 QB rating. Second half adjustments – You have to admire a head coach who can identify what isn’t working and offer changes for the second half instead of just cashing it in or staying with the game plan that obviously isn’t working. QB Jacoby Brissett had one series in Quarter 3 before he was yanked. The offense just wasn’t moving, and when it did, it could not score. The defense also blitzed a safety or a linebacker more in the second half, which made Prescott have to throw the ball earlier than in the first two quarters. And the ball was being distributed more to the Cardinals’ playmakers, Wilson and McBride, on a more frequent basis. Josh Fryar came in for the injured Jayden Williams at right tackle and held his own. And the long ball was incorporated, which made the Dallas cornerbacks back off the line pre-snap and helped the short passing game. DT L.J. Collier – Collier was immediately placed on the cow dung list when he pushed LT Tyler Guyton and got a 15-yard unsportsmanlike penalty. What happened was a pile of players was clustered from the previous play, which was a failed third down for Dallas. As players were getting up, Guyton shoved LB Gibbens, and Collier saw it. He then went over and body-slammed Guyton with both hands. Naturally, the referee only saw the second offender. Instead of setting up the punt return team, the Cowboys had a fresh set of downs. It was a knucklehead play. But Collier more than made up for it. With 3:58 remaining in the game, he batted a pass on a third-and-11. He sacked Prescott with 2:09 left in the game, and then halfway through the extra period, he was able to bat the pass down that became a Cowboys punt. ——————————————————————————— GEEKS First-quarter offense – QB Jacoby Brissett airmailed four passes in the opening quarter. RB Jeremiyah Love had minimal gains on the ground, then walked off with an injury. A beautiful nine-play drive was stuffed at the one-yard line on both third and fourth downs, with Arizona getting zero points. Then TE Elijah Higgins pops the ball up as Dallas LB Shemar James makes an interception and runs it all the way down to the Cardinals’ five-yard line. Two plays later, the Cowboys are up 7-0, but only because S Andrew Wingard doesn’t land on the fumble caused by the S Budda Baker hit on RB Javonte Williams. Only 22 rushing yards for Arizona, and the offense’s best pass catcher, McBride, had one catch for five yards. First-quarter possessions: punt, downs, INT. Missed opportunities – The Bam Knight fumble came as the second quarter was winding down, as the offense was getting near field goal range after WR Simi Fehoko hauled in a 17-yard pass. Not scoring any points after the offense got to the one in Quarter 1. Cardinals got the ball on the Cowboys’ 30 after the failed fourth-down attempt and scored no points. The missed PAT would have won the game outright. Missed tackles – Budda Baker, Jack Gibbens, Mack Wilson, Andrew Wingard, and Denzel Burke. CB Denzel Burke – He missed the tackle on WR CeeDee Lamb that should have been a loss in the second quarter, but ended up converting a first down instead. On the Cowboys’…

title: Falcons – Buccaneers Week 8 recap: Defeated in a downpour
summary: The rain made the field sloppy, the rain made the Falcons sloppy. In the end, they couldn’t beat a completely one-dimensional Buccaneers team on the road that barely even tried to pass the ball and seemed to relish how embarrassing that became as the game wore on. By the time the dust settled, the Bucs […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 1: Zach Harrison #96 of the Atlanta Falcons tackles Bucky Irving #7 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The rain made the field sloppy, the rain made the Falcons sloppy. In the end, they couldn’t beat a completely one-dimensional Buccaneers team on the road that barely even tried to pass the ball and seemed to relish how embarrassing that became as the game wore on. By the time the dust settled, the Bucs became the first team in over 50 years to win without completing a pass, and the Falcons made unfortunate history in multiple ways before it was over. If you’ve followed me for any length of time, you know that I believe one game is one game, and it’s best to patiently build the picture of what a team and/or players are over the course of a season. I get caught up in big days and big moments like anybody else and that bleeds into Sunday and even Monday, but then I try to make myself take stock of the bigger picture. I’ll be doing that again this week, but it rarely feels as tough as it does after this one. Michael Penix Jr. threw four interceptions and legitimately could’ve thrown three more, and he badly missed other passes that might’ve made a difference in this one. The offensive line didn’t do a great job of protecting Penix or opening lanes on a consistent basis. Tommy Rees and company called doomed screens, chose to pass on the rare occasions when the Falcons had short yardage situations and could’ve run, and just generally seemed ill-equipped to put together a working offense in a rainstorm. Jeff Ulbrich’s defense basically had one job—defend the run—and allowed the Bucs to gash them for over 300 yards even so. Nick Folk missed his field goal try and clearly isn’t going to be trusted in adverse conditions or beyond 50 yards the rest of the season, and Atlanta’s return game was once again basically nonexistent as the team struggled with field position. It’s incredibly difficult to find positives because there were so few in a game the Falcons lost 16-0 and barely seemed competitive in. Again, it’s one game, but the Falcons are now 1-2 against the division and that’s likely to matter down the line. It’s one game, but the Falcons may be asked to play again in the rain or snow or cold, and this will make you wonder if they can handle that. It’s one game, but the Falcons have a tough assignment against the Bengals abroad next week. It’s one game, but it’s at least the third time this year the Falcons have found themselves down early, struggling, and unable to come up with any answers to avoid the game turning into a legitimately blowout. It’s one game, but it’s a game that feels like the absolute worse games of the late Mike Smith era, the mid-to-late Dan Quinn era, the Arthur Smith era, and the Raheem Morris era. It’s one game, but it’s just about as terrible a game as you can imagine the Falcons playing. The Falcons, of course, can’t linger on it. They won’t be playing in driving rain in Spain a week from now, and may not actually have to deal with wet conditions the rest of the way, and they know that game was the outlier of all outliers in terms of their run defense having to put up with nonstop running and Penix playing about as poorly as he can possibly play. There’s only so much you can take away from a game you may not see again for a decade, in terms of conditions and opponent game plans, and getting stuck trying to fix what ailed them on this specific Sunday is unlikely to be a great use of their time. They have to get ready for a pass-first script from Joe Burrow and the Bengals and the weakest run defense they’ve faced in weeks, which will drastically change how they approach the next game. It pays to have a short memory in the NFL, and the Falcons will under a head coach as even-keeled as Kevin Stefanski. For those of us in the stadium and at home, though, this will linger and should linger. It’s the latest sizeable dent in the notion that this Falcons team is (or even can be) different than the many hapless ones that preceded it; the Falcons in the past few eras were capable of truly astonishing wins against teams they weren’t expected to contend against but fell to earth in dispiriting ways the following weeks. For these Falcons to truly be different, they have to have something more than a deeply inconsistent team that follows a dominant week or two with horrors that would make Stephen King blush. If this isn’t rock bottom for the Falcons by a mile, this season is over, no matter how grim the NFC South may be. Whether they continue to “same old Falcons” or find their footing, the Falcons can’t dwell on their ugliest losses this year. Unfortunately, it’s difficult for us not to do so. On to the full recap. The Good Bijan Robinson’s balance was such an asset on a very wet field. Over and over again, he went into the pile or survived an early onslaught to pick up extra yardage, something that would’ve been impossible for a lesser back with lesser ability. His ugly drop was the only significant stain on a quality (if somewhat quiet by his standards) day, especially because the Buccaneers run defense has long given him fits. If only Bijan had not been mothballed on critical late game short yardage situations, eh? Jahan Dotson had the biggest play of the game on offense, underscoring how dangerous he can be. He took a risky Penix pass, went around a defender, and turned on the jets for a 76 yard gain that should have set up Atlanta’s first scoring drive had the team not frittered it away. No other Falcon had more than 10 yards and Dotson had 95 on two receptions; it’s safe to say he bounced back this week even if he’ll always likely be inconsistent from week-to-week. Jessie Bates is on fire right now, and he made the play of the game in this one. With Baker Mayfield escaping the pocket after a busted play and flipping it backwards to Bucky Irving, the Bucs running back had a clear lane to the end zone…right up until Bates arrived and chopped hard at the ball. That forced a fumble that landed out of bounds, and per NFL rules, that meant Atlanta got the ball. It was a massive, six point swing when the Falcons would’ve been down 10-0, and exactly the kind of play that makes Bates worth every penny. Mike Hughes had a tremendous play on the first drive, with Baker Mayfield’s end zone bomb to Ted Hurst looking caught…until Hughes chopped it out of his hand at the exact right time to prevent a score and force Tampa Bay to settle for three. We’ve been justifiably hard on Hughes this year, but credit where it’s due. Maason Smith’s third down stop with the Bucs driving and threatening to move the game from “likely out of reach” to “entirely out of reach” was a huge play. I wished it had mattered more. Jake Bailey had a solid day at the office, pinning the Bucs inside their own 20 twice and averaging nearly 50 yards a punt. Paired with stingy work from Falcons special teams—they only allowed two punt returns for a combined eight yards—the punting game did its job. The Ugly Michael Penix Jr. had done a good job of taking care of the football, but he had been fortunate not to throw a couple of picks over the past few weeks that bounced off defender’s hands. That hot streak ended in this one in excruciating fashion, as Penix threw two first quarter interceptions right at Alex Anzalone, who he appeared not to see on both occasions. It was a gruesome performance that got worse, with Penix badly missing a wide open Kyle Pitts after shrugging off a sack attempt and then throwing his third interception on a half-hearted fourth down attempt in the second quarter. He then threw a fourth interception on another ill-advised throw to Charlie Woerner that was picked off by a leaping Zyon McCollum. The Falcons clearly planned to stay balanced despite the wet field conditions, and sticking with…
author: Dave Choate

title: Ravens could place Tyler Loop on IR, Jake Moody to kick vs. Jaguars
summary: The Baltimore Ravens will not have Tyler Loop for their Thursday night matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars and potentially much longer. Head coach Jesse Minter said on Monday that the second-year kicker could be placed on injured reserve with an issue he described as “something small that kind of became a little bit more.” Jake […]
full_text: The Baltimore Ravens will not have Tyler Loop for their Thursday night matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars and potentially much longer. Head coach Jesse Minter said on Monday that the second-year kicker could be placed on injured reserve with an issue he described as “something small that kind of became a little bit more.” Jake Moody, who was re-signed to the practice squad two weeks ago, will take over kicking duties in the interim. The Ravens’ first injury report of Week 9 revealed that Loop is specifically dealing with a groin injury. But even if he was healthy, he may not have been starting on Thursday night. The 2025 sixth-round pick has faced multiple waves of scrutiny since arriving in Baltimore as the handpicked successor to Justin Tucker, the latest coming after two missed kicks in the last three games. He shanked a 34-yard field goal on Sunday against the Buffalo Bills, just two weeks after a crucial miss from 49 yards in a 13-10 loss to the Cleveland Browns. Minter’s comments indicate that Loop’s groin had been bothering him for some time but recently worsened to the point that a stint on IR might be necessary. That would sideline the 26-year-old until after the Ravens’ Week 13 bye. Moody would have an opportunity to seize the kicking job for the rest of the season and maybe longer. Originally a 49ers third-round pick in 2023, Moody put forth a solid rookie campaign with an 84.0% field goal conversion rate that plummeted to 70.6% the following year. He entered 2025 on an extremely short leash and was waived by San Francisco after going one for three inside of 40 yards (one miss, one block) in Week 1. But across two games with the Bears and six with the Commanders, Moody converted 18 of his 20 field goals – including both of his attempts from 50-plus yards – and 13 of his 14 extra points.

title: Ravens sign QB Austin Reed to practice squad
summary: The Baltimore Ravens signed Austin Reed to their practice squad on Monday, adding some much-needed quarterback depth after injuries to starter Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano is set for his first career start in Week 9, but he will need a backup who knows Declan Doyle’s offense. Enter Reed, who […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - AUGUST 28: Austin Reed #15 of the Baltimore Ravens throws a pass during a preseason game against the Washington Commanders at M&T Bank Stadium on August 28, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens signed Austin Reed to their practice squad on Monday, adding some much-needed quarterback depth after injuries to starter Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano is set for his first career start in Week 9, but he will need a backup who knows Declan Doyle’s offense. Enter Reed, who not only spent part of training camp in Baltimore this past summer, but worked with Doyle in Chicago last year as well. He appeared in all three of the Ravens’ 2026 preseason games and completed six of his 12 passes for 59 yards, one touchdown, and one interception with 11 yards and a touchdown on the ground. Fagnano took several hits against the Buffalo Bills on Sunday and was listed as a limited participant in Monday’s walkthrough with an ankle injury. The Ravens’ offensive line has already let two quarterbacks get knocked out of the game, so Reed needs to take all of the reps he can get in case he is needed on Thursday night. The Ravens are still evaluating Huntley’s toe injury – reportedly a case of turf toe – and will likely wait for an update on his status before making another quarterback move. Fagnano and Reed will have to get through at least one game, but a swift return from Huntley could keep Baltimore moving forward without other additions at the position. A longer absence will put Eric DeCosta in a tough spot: sacrifice future draft capital to salvage what might be a lost season or cobble together a quarterback room from street free agents and/or practice squads around the league?
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens Report Card, Week 8: Another injury-riddled offensive implosion
summary: The Baltimore Ravens suffered a third consecutive loss in Week 8 and their second straight game losing by 20+ points, falling to the Buffalo Bills by a score of 36-10. Here are report card grades for the team’s position groups from yesterday’s defeat. Quarterback: F Lamar Jackson’s injury on his first play of the game […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Joe Fagnano #12 of the Baltimore Ravens throws a pass during the second half against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens suffered a third consecutive loss in Week 8 and their second straight game losing by 20+ points, falling to the Buffalo Bills by a score of 36-10. Here are report card grades for the team’s position groups from yesterday’s defeat. Quarterback: F Lamar Jackson’s injury on his first play of the game took the wind out of the team’s sails immediately. Tyler Huntley’s short stint in the opening quarter, prior to exiting with a foot injury, was eventful for the wrong reasons. Huntley’s four pass attempts resulted in zero yards and he lost a fumble in the Ravens’ own territory. Joe Fagnano made his NFL debut and played most of the game. After completing back-to-back throws immediately upon entering the game, Fagnano struggled. He completed 10-of-21 passes for only 93 yards with an interception and lost fumble. Fagnano also was banged up but finished the game. All three quarterbacks were under duress during their time on the field. Running Back: C- Derrick Henry broke his scoring drought and should have another touchdown, but it was called back due to a holding penalty. While he ran more efficiently than recent weeks (4.8 yards per carry), Henry only had 11 carries and the Ravens didn’t make a concentrated effort to ride him after Jacksonw went down. He also continues to be inconsistent as a pass-blocker. Justice Hill had seven touches for 35 total yards and Rasheen Ali was given a pair of carries as well. Wide Receiver: D+ The Ravens’ wideouts were victim to the team’s quarterback and pass protection struggles. However, it was still disappointing that Zay Flowers failed to catch any passes on five targets against a leaky Bills’ pass defense that was missing multiple players. Rashod Bateman and Ja’Kobi Lane each caught one pass for a first-down conversion, but that was the extent of production from the wide receiver room. Tight End: C- It was another quiet day for the Ravens’ tight end group. Like the wide receivers, they too have to be graded on a curve given the in-flux state of the quarterback position and pass blocking issues. Nevertheless, Mark Andrews continues to be make a minimal impact (three catches, 14 yards) and Matt Hibner was blanked from the stat sheet for a second straight game. Josh Cuevas caught one reception for 15 yards. Offensive Line: F The Ravens’ offense line struggled mightily in pass protection against the Bills’ front seven. The Ravens surrendered 12 quarterback hits and four sacks, with all three quarterbacks facing pressure consistently when on the field. Roger Rosengarten was beaten multiple times by Gregory Rosseau, Cam Jurgens appeared to miss linebacker blitz pickups, and both starting guards also allowed multiple hurries. They did better in run blocking this week, but it meant little in the grand scheme of the game. Defensive Line: C The Ravens did an okay job bottling up the Bills’ run defense for most of the game. While they wound up with 146 rushing yards, James Cook was limited to 3.8 yards per carry with a longest run of 16 yards and Josh Allen ran seven times for 30 yards. Broderick Washington made a huge defensive play by coming up with an interception off a dropped pass, which led to the Ravens’ only touchdown of the game. Nnamdi Madubuike was the only defensive lineman to record a sack or quarterback hit. Edge Rusher: C Trey Hendrickson and Mike Green each had a quarterback hit, with the latter also recording a half-sack in tandem with Madubuike. Hendrickson and Zion Young each made some plays against the run as well. Overall, though, the Ravens didn’t get a ton of disruption on Allen and failed to bring him down a few times. Linebacker: C+ Roquan Smith played much more inspired than he has in recent weeks, totaling 11 tackles with two pass breakups and a forced fumble. He had a huge first-half showing, but his impact tailed off as the game progressed late, along with the rest of the defense. Trenton Simpson had a quarterback hit with four tackles, and Teddye Buchanan had his most impactful performance so far this year with six tackles. Both Buchanan and Simpson were on the wrong end of open-field juke moves, but otherwise appeared to make no mistakes. Cornerback: C The Ravens’ cornerbacks were much better than last week, which was anticipated given they weren’t matching up with Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins again. Marlon Humphrey was beaten by D.J. Moore for a long 49-yard reception, but he was in position to make a play. He made a pass breakup on the very next play in the red zone and also nearly had an interception. Chidobe Awuzie had a nice pass defended as well in coverage of Kincaid and backup T.J. Tampa made an impact and his return to action. Tampa recovered a fumble and broke up a two-point conversion attempt. For the Ravens to be most successful in the backend, they might need to play Humphrey in the slot with Awuzie and Tampa taking outside corner reps opposite Wiggins. Keyon Martin, and Chandler Rivers when he was playing, often appear too undersized and overmatched. Safety: C Kyle Hamilton rebounded from an uncharacteristic performance last week with a better showing against the Bills. He finished with seven tackles, including another big tackle for loss on a conversion run attempt in the red zone. Malaki Starks made a few tackles against the run including one tackle for loss of his own. Starks was beaten by Dalton Kincaid for a late touchdown pass, and Kincaid also had a first-down catch with Hamilton in coverage early in the game. K’Von Wallace had six tackles, playing an elevated role again with Jaylinn Hawkins absent. Special Teams: C Rasheen Ali had a great kick return for 59 yards, where he appeared bottled up but then broke free for a huge gain. LaJohntay Wester had another quiet outing as a punt returner with just one return for two yards. Ryan Eckley also made some nice punts again, including a long 62-yarder. The biggest negative on special teams was another missed field goal from Tyler Loop, which came from just 34 yards out. In the grand scheme of a 26-point loss, one missed field goal is not a huge deal, but at the time it could have cut the Ravens’ deficit to three points.
author: Frank Platko

title: Ravens’ immediate QB options after Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley injuries
summary: The Baltimore Ravens lost their starting and backup quarterbacks during Sunday’s loss to the Buffalo Bills with just four days until a Thursday night matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve to undergo surgery on his right thumb, and Tyler Huntley is being evaluated for a turf toe injury that […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - AUGUST 29: Will Levis #8 of the Tennessee Titans and Tyson Bagent #17 of the Chicago Bears react after the Week 3 preseason game at Nissan Stadium on August 29, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens lost their starting and backup quarterbacks during Sunday’s loss to the Buffalo Bills with just four days until a Thursday night matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Lamar Jackson is headed to injured reserve to undergo surgery on his right thumb, and Tyler Huntley is being evaluated for a turf toe injury that could sideline him for a week or longer. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finished Sunday’s game under center but took several hits behind a porous offensive line. He expressed optimism about his ability to face the Jaguars, which would be his first career NFL start, albeit in unlikely and adverse circumstances. Fagnano’s backup, though, remains to be determined. The Ravens currently do not have another quarterback on their 53-man roster or practice squad and will have to make a signing right away to get him up to speed by Thursday night. A potential multi-game absence from Huntley could even inspire Eric DeCosta to sign multiple passer should the injuries continue to accrue. Entering Week 8 of the regular season, the pickings are about as slim as they get. The Ravens can easily find passers to get them through the coming weeks, but to keep their playoff hopes alive, they might have to consider a more aggressive move. Here are Baltimore’s top quarterback options: Familiar faces In the most immediate future, the Ravens need a quarterback who knows Declan Doyle’s offense well enough to play on Thursday night if needed. Austin Reed spent last offseason with Doyle in Chicago and part of this year’s training camp in Baltimore, making him a likely signing. He has never played in a regular-season game, though, and he would profile as little more than depth in case of another injury. Josh Johnson, who has two previous stints in Baltimore, could also be signed off the Bengals’ practice squad. He has not spent any time under Doyle, nor his two mentors, Sean Payton and Ben Johnson, but the 40-year-old journeyman is known for his ability to quickly pick up new offenses. He would give the Ravens a more veteran option under center should Fagnano falter. And then there’s – brace yourself – Cooper Rush. His disastrous spell as Jackson’s backup in 2025 loomed large after narrowly missing the playoffs, but he has some level of familiarity with the offensive personnel, if not the scheme. But if Rush is bad enough to be cut by the Falcons, who have fielded Michael Penix, Tua Tagovaioloa, and undrafted rookie Jack Strand this year… Practice squad pickings Outside of a street free agent, the Ravens could also poach a quarterback off another team’s practice squad. That could bring Baltimore back to Will Levis. The ex-Titan, now-Jet was reportedly under consideration during the run-up to the 2023 draft before Jackson agreed to his contract extension. Levis’ time in Tennessee was filled with turnovers – often accompanied by his comical freeze-frame reactions – and he would likely only bring more chaos to Baltimore’s current mess of an offense. Payton’s Broncos do not have a quarterback on their practice squad, while the Bears and the Lions – Johnson’s current and last team – only have rookies. But Hendon Hooker spent two (albeit unsuccessful) years under Johnson in Detroit and could brought in from Tennessee to learn a similar system. The former third-round pick has only thrown five regular-season passes in his career, all in 2024 at the end of Lions blowouts. Potential trades It’s worth mentioning the potential for DeCosta to trade for a quarterback, though that probably is not a solution to the team’s immediate needs on Thursday night. Tyson Bagent and Sam Ehlinger, who have spent time with Doyle in Chicago and Denver, respectively, could both be options. Getting Anthony Richardson from the Colts would be an ambitious and exciting move. And are the Ravens desperate enough to see what the Bengals would demand to bring Joe Flacco home to Baltimore? ‘Isn’t he retired?’ Jimmy Garoppolo seemed headed for retirement this offseason, especially after his former coaches in Los Angeles and Arizona went in other directions at quarterback. But he remained interested in playing with multiple links to the Giants as recently as last month. That would add a thin layer of irony if he were to sign in Baltimore after all of the Ravens who followed John Harbaugh to New York this offseason. Garoppolo appeared in three games for the Rams last season, but he has not thrown a regular-season pass since Week 18 of the 2024 season. He turns 35 years old today; how much does his arm have left? ‘Wait, he’s definitely retired!’ Russell Wilson did officially announce his retirement this offseason. But his arm, it seems, might still have some life: "Sean Payton you make like me, you may not but I'm picking YOU!" @DangeRussWilson HAS STILL GOT IT pic.twitter.com/5YUKWRqaiP — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) November 1, 2026 After seeing him nonchalantly drill the crossbar from 25 yards out in street clothes, you’re telling me DangerRuss couldn’t run play action and launch some moonballs to Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman? And, as Wilson so conveniently mentions, he does have some familiarity with Payton’s offense – and thereby Doyle’s. It was a terrible fit for his skillset, but, hey, knowledge is power, right?
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Top takeaways from the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Bills
summary: The Baltimore Ravens stacked insults upon injuries in Sunday’s loss to the Buffalo Bills. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s top takeaways from the worst game of the 2026 season: So many questions, so little time. Lamar Jackson’s right thumb injury will no doubt spark a new round of questions about his long-term future in Baltimore. But […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on from the sideline against the Buffalo Bills during an NFL football game at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens stacked insults upon injuries in Sunday’s loss to the Buffalo Bills. Here are Baltimore Beatdown’s top takeaways from the worst game of the 2026 season: So many questions, so little time. Lamar Jackson’s right thumb injury will no doubt spark a new round of questions about his long-term future in Baltimore. But the Ravens do not have any time to think about offseason contract situations right now. They need to take stock – particularly at the quarterback position – and figure out who is starting on Thursday night against the Jaguars. Reports of a turf toe injury to Tyler Huntley indicate that will likely be undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano. His potential backup is not currently on the Ravens’ roster. And then there’s the trade deadline in just nine days. Baltimore is 4-4 at the bottom of the AFC North; Jackson’s injury could effectively knock them out of playoff competition. Can Eric DeCosta make – or rather, take – the tough calls to part ways with valued veterans in exchange for future draft capital? These are the first of a series of tricky decisions the Ravens will have to navigate in the coming days, weeks, and months. Tyler Loop’s time is up. The Ravens have got to start holding players accountable for poor performances, and it should start with Loop after he missed a chip-shot field goal and landed the opening kickoff out of the bounds against the Bills. Kickers in the modern NFL should be able to be trusted on kicks under 50 yards. There may not be many better options on the street right now to replace Loop, but Baltimore has to start sending messages about what happens if you fail to do your job. – Dustin Cox The Ravens need a complete offensive line overhaul. Much has been made this season about the Ravens’ offensive line inconsistencies and struggles. While they’ve had poor injury luck and their ideal starting five has almost not played together at all, the offensive line’s performance in Buffalo was abysmal – and indicative that the Ravens need a full makeover up front. Roger Rosengarten, who is supposed to be a building block at right tackle, was dominated all afternoon by Gregory Rosseau. Ronnie Stanley continues to be penalized often and Cam Jurgens missed blitz pickups in the middle. Lamar Jackson couldn’t even go one play without being hit immediately on a play action. Poor pass protection has been a factor in Jackson’s injury struggles and now both backup quarterbacks picked up injuries in this game as well. Vega Ioane is clearly a long-term fixture, Jurgens was just traded for so the Ravens can’t give up on him too early, and maybe Rosengarten can turn things around. Nevertheless, the Ravens need heavy investment this offseason to infuse more talent on the offensive line to protect their franchise quarterback. – Frank Platko It’s going to be a long few months in Baltimore. Even if Jackson can return this year – and if the Ravens can keep their playoff hopes alive in the meantime – there will be virtually no margin of error to close out the season. Given the circumstances, a postseason appearance would qualify as some sort of a success, but it is clear that the Ravens, as currently built, are not a Super Bowl team. That was the expectation coming into the season, and anything short of that will be seen as a distinct failure in Jesse Minter’s first year as a head coach. Then comes the offseason, and along with it a host of tough roster decisions on overpriced, underperforming veterans. Sunday’s loss in Buffalo might have been a new low for the Ravens, but just because things can only go up from here doesn’t mean that they will anytime soon.

title: Ravens QB Tyler Huntley could miss TNF vs. Jags with suspected turf toe
summary: The Baltimore Ravens are evaluating backup quarterback Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley for a suspected turf toe injury, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. An MRI on Monday will shed further light on his status for Thursday night’s matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Huntley, 28, entered Sunday’s game against the Buffalo Bills after starter Lamar Jackson injured his […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 1: Tyler Huntley #5 of the Baltimore Ravens throws the ball as he's getting tackled during the first half against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens are evaluating backup quarterback Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley for a suspected turf toe injury, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. An MRI on Monday will shed further light on his status for Thursday night’s matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Huntley, 28, entered Sunday’s game against the Buffalo Bills after starter Lamar Jackson injured his throwing hand on the first snap of the game. He faced constant pressure and was hit multiple times before leaving the game in the second quarter. Undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano finished the game under center while taking several shots of his own, though he “hopes” to be ready to play on Thursday. Jackson is set to land on injured reserve to undergo surgery on his right thumb, which will sideline him for at least four games. Huntley would be in line to start in his place, as he did in Jackson’s three-game absence following a Week 4 high ankle sprain. However, confirmation of his initial turf toe diagnosis will almost certainly keep him from playing in Week 9 – and potentially longer. Instead, it will likely be Fagnano making an unlikely first start of his NFL career vs. the Jaguars, who boast an elite run defense but have struggled against opposing passers this year. The former UConn starter could only complete 10 of his 21 passing attempts for 91 yards and an interception on Sunday afternoon, good for a paltry 4.3 yards per attempt and a 40.0 quarterback rating. Getting reps with Baltimore’s first-team offense will give him a chance at a better showing against Jacksonville, but Fagnano will clearly be facing an uphill battle. Huntley largely struggled in his five appearances this year. His numbers through the air are at or above league-average, but his underpowered arm limited the Ravens’ downfield passing game. He was not helped by a leaky, banged-up offense line that slowed the run game and far too often allowed rushers right in his lap. Turf toe injuries can linger, especially for a quarterback whose game is built on his mobility. Huntley could miss not only Thursday night’s game, but more contests after that, potentially positioning Fagnano for multiple starts. The Ravens will already need to add quarterback depth just to get through the week, but a longer-term absence from Huntley could force them to make a more substantial move.
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Seattle Seahawks vs. Chicago Bears, ‘MNF’ Week 8 fan discussion
summary: Week 8 of NFL action comes to a close this evening with a juicy-on-paper matchup between the Seattle Seahawks and Chicago Bears for Monday Night Football. It’s true that a disproportionate amount of primetime games this season have been NFC-exclusive affairs, far too many of them snoozefests featuring NFC East teams and matchups pitting losing […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - DECEMBER 26: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears throws the ball during an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Soldier Field on December 26, 2024 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 8 of NFL action comes to a close this evening with a juicy-on-paper matchup between the Seattle Seahawks and Chicago Bears for Monday Night Football . It’s true that a disproportionate amount of primetime games this season have been NFC-exclusive affairs, far too many of them snoozefests featuring NFC East teams and matchups pitting losing teams against one another. Tonight is different, thanks to what’s certain to be a playoff-hungry atmosphere in Seattle. The NFC West and NFC North are two of the most competitive divisions in football, lest we forget the Seahawks are the current defending Super Bowl champions. That said, things have not come easy for Seattle in 2026. Their current 4-3 record means that even with the team’s current second-place position in the NFC West, the Seahawks have little room for error from here on out with the .500 Los Angeles Rams bearing down on them. Meanwhile, at 5-2, the Bears are technically in third place in the NFC North behind the 5-2 Detroit Lions and 6-1 Minnesota Vikings. Chicago has big plans in 2026 and beyond, and you can bet they have no interest in losing a key game on a national stage. The Bears are a somewhat easy team to root for because they’ve endured a lot of mediocre in franchise history. Sure, there’s the ‘85 Bears and a season anyone alive to witness will never forget. However, when Sid Luckman, Jim McMahon, and most recently Jay Cutler (seriously) stand as a franchise’s best quarterbacks, it’s easy to sympathize with any Bears fan’s struggle in the 21st century . Caleb Williams seems ready to join Chicago’s short list of greatest quarterbacks. He very well may hold the top title with the Bears in a few years, if he continues ascending in ways similar to what quarterback Josh Allen found with the Buffalo Bills. If you’re in this one for rooting interests, I’d stump again for the Bears. Since the Bills play the NFC North this season, the interest here is in giving Buffalo a tougher (i.e. teams with more wins) strength of schedule. The Seattle music scene helped shape who I am, and I love when broadcasts pay proper deep-cut homage through music bumpers. However, I’m not here for the Seahawks winning it all again this season. A loss tonight would help knock them down further in the playoff equation. With that, here’s your open thread for Week 8 of Monday Night Football . As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!
author: Matt Byham

title: Te’Cory Couch played like wily veteran for Buffalo Bills in win over Ravens
summary: One of the biggest individual revelations from the Buffalo Bills’ win over the Ravens in Week 8 was the stellar play of Te’Cory Couch, the nickel corner signed from the practice squad before this contest who thrived in slot throughout. He was a component of a much more connected, in-sync back seven that communicated significantly […]
full_text: One of the biggest individual revelations from the Buffalo Bills’ win over the Ravens in Week 8 was the stellar play of Te’Cory Couch, the nickel corner signed from the practice squad before this contest who thrived in slot throughout. He was a component of a much more connected, in-sync back seven that communicated significantly better than the vast majority of Buffalo’s first six contests, particularly in zone and when the Ravens attempted to confuse man-to-man assignments with motions and stacked formations. While I’m on the topic of pre-snap movement and bunch formations, check this first play from Couch that exemplified his discipline and the improved passing off in zone from Buffalo’s linebackers and defensive backs. At the snap, you’ll notice Rashod Bateman in motion. With that motion, Baltimore wanted to widen the path of his vertical route in case Davison Igbinosun jumped the intermediate out-breaker run by Mark Andrews. The route concept also featured Zay Flowers working across the middle underneath, and it would’ve been easy for Couch — aligned in the slot near the bottom of the screen — to jump that slant. He didn’t. Watch as he passed off Flowers to Terrel Bernard before sinking to occupy the area of Andrews’ out-breaker: pic.twitter.com/F8xGFxGe2r — Chris Trapasso (@trapassofilm) November 2, 2026 Absolutely textbook. Couple that with Igbinosun staying home in his deep outside fourth of the field, and there was simply nowhere to throw the football. Now, sure — that play was a simple example of everyone staying true to their zones, but oftentimes offenses bank on one back seven player getting greedy or taking one false step … and that’s when a pass-catching option comes open. Fine dedication to his zone from Couch there, especially for someone with very little experience. Couch manned up well too, even against Flowers on a few occasions. Here, the Bills were in straight-up man across the board, and notice how Couch raised his arm before the snap. I can’t say for sure what that indicated, but I love that he took charge on the communication front, even if it was in visual form. The Ravens snapped the ball with motion, and attempted to cause natural picks at the bottom of the screen with Andrews, Bateman, and Flowers. Couch got physical with Flowers during the allowed five yards beyond the of scrimmage before releasing his hands and running with him as the lightning-quick separator ran a deep over across the field: pic.twitter.com/k8XPWti5pu — Chris Trapasso (@trapassofilm) November 2, 2026 This next play from Couch was low-key outstanding, and it served as a fine demonstration of how abruptly defenders must adjust pre and post snap. A split second before the snap, the Ravens sent Andrews in motion toward the sideline, which widened Couch as the ball reached the quarterback in the shotgun. Because his assignment was the short zone underneath on his side of the field, Couch got a shove on Bateman to disrupt his route timing before turning his attention into the backfield. Notice how quickly he recognized screen, avoided a block from an offensive lineman, and got a hand on Justice Hill to trip him before the veteran back could flip on the afterburners: pic.twitter.com/gKSf8uZ462 — Chris Trapasso (@trapassofilm) November 2, 2026 With Deone Walker bowled over by two Ravens blockers, the 5’10”, 185-pounder was the only Bills defender still standing within 10-15 yards of Hill when he caught the football. Outstanding play from the 27-year-old defensive back. Here, in the low red zone, Couch, Damar Hamlin, and Igbinosun avoided collisions at the top of the screen and Couch didn’t vacate keeping inside leverage on the inside receiver as Flowers and Bateman approached the goal line: He then quickly and effortlessly flipped his hips to follow Flowers across the back of the end zone: pic.twitter.com/dhj8LbDhNZ — Chris Trapasso (@trapassofilm) November 2, 2026 Very calm rep there from Couch again, when a lot of inexperienced defensive backs would’ve panicked or, more simply, not had enough juice to stay with the speedy Flowers across the field. This would not be a proper film session on an scrappy, upstart defensive back if it did not feature an open-field tackle. Nothing schematically intricate here… just Couch (near the bottom of the screen) planting and driving from his short zone to stick Andrews before he could turn up field to move the chains: pic.twitter.com/HGr1EFxqAt — Chris Trapasso (@trapassofilm) November 2, 2026 Yes, of course… the Ravens were massively short-handed at the game’s most vital position against the Bills. But there’s no doubting Buffalo’s secondary played much more like a cohesive unit against Baltimore than at any stage of the past month, if not the entire season to date. And Couch played one heck of a game.

summary: The Buffalo Bills will head to the Midwest this coming weekend to take on the Minnesota Vikings in primetime for Week 9 of Monday Night Football. full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 13: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills attempts a pass against the Minnesota Vikings at Highmark Stadium on November 13, 2022 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills will head to the Midwest this coming weekend to take on the Minnesota Vikings in primetime for Week 9 of Monday Night Football . It’s a marquee matchup of two 6-1 teams, featuring Buffalo’s potent offense against Minnesota’s fearsome defense. As you’d guess with a game of this magnitude, the spread is close — but it’s not necessarily what you’d expect. Entering Week 9, FanDuel Sportsbook has the Bills as three-point road favorites (-3) against the Vikings (+3) . As of publishing, the over/under for this game stood at o/u 46.5. Even considering quarterback Josh Allen, it’s perhaps a bit surprising that Buffalo is favored as the road team against an opponent with what many see as a championship-caliber defense. Buffalo is coming off a 36-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens, while Minnesota dropped its first game of the season in a 19-15 loss to the Detroit Lions. As is typical at this point in any NFL season, injury reports will be a huge priority for anyone looking to get a better read on the potential outcome of this game. The biggest concerns on that front for the Bills are wide receivers DJ Moore (leg) and Joshua Palmer (hamstring), plus right tackle Spencer Brown (back), and running back James Cook III (concussion, cleared to return). There’s also some question as to whether or not quarterback Josh Allen sustained an injury, based on the team’s apparent refusal to run short-yardage sneaks with him against the Ravens. Baltimore linebacker Roquan Smith grabbed and spun Allen’s helmet around, bloodying quarterback’s head. Key injuries to watch for the Vikings include quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring), and safety Theo Jackson (quad). Murray is managing hamstring tightness. Should he be unable to play in Week 9, it’s likely Minnesota then turns to veteran backup quarterback Carson Wentz. The Bills and Vikings have played just 15 times dating back to their first matchup in October 1971. Minnesota leads the all-time series 9-6, having won the last game between the two franchises. That 33-30 overtime loss for Buffalo came in Orchard Park, NY back in November 2022. Josh Allen is 1-1 against the Vikings since entering the NFL, with his first NFL win coming in a 27-6 victory back in September of his rookie season in 2018. That game is part of Bills lore now, thanks to Allen’s hurdle of linebacker Anthony Barr. Think you’ve got what it takes to make a play with the Buffalo Bills in 2026? title: Greg Rousseau passes Darryl Talley on Buffalo Bills’ all-time sack list
summary: Greg Rousseau has another milestone to add to his growing résumé with the Buffalo Bills. The outside linebacker recorded a sack against the Baltimore Ravens giving him 39 for his career and moving him past Darryl Talley into eighth place on the franchise’s all-time sack list.  Talley spent 12 seasons in Buffalo and was part […]
full_text: Greg Rousseau has another milestone to add to his growing résumé with the Buffalo Bills. The outside linebacker recorded a sack against the Baltimore Ravens giving him 39 for his career and moving him past Darryl Talley into eighth place on the franchise’s all-time sack list. Talley spent 12 seasons in Buffalo and was part of the Bills teams that went to four consecutive Super Bowls in the early 1990s. He finished his time with the team with 38.5 sacks in 188 regular-season games. Rousseau, meanwhile, needed just 85 games to move past that total. Not bad for a player who is only in his sixth NFL season. And this season, Rousseau has been making that climb a little faster. With Jim Leonhard taking over as defensive coordinator under new head coach Joe Brady, Rousseau has moved from defensive end to outside linebacker. The change has given him different opportunities to get after opposing quarterbacks, and the results have been hard to miss. Rousseau recorded two sacks in each of Buffalo’s first three games before being held without one against New England. He entered Monday night’s game with six sacks, already within reach of the career-high eight he recorded in both 2022 and 2024. Now, with Talley behind him on the leaderboard, Rousseau has another name to chase. Mario Williams, who played four seasons in Buffalo from 2012 through 2015, sits seventh with 43 sacks. Greg Rousseau records his 7th sack of the season and becomes the 4th Bill with a sack today. https://t.co/aU5vkSctnG — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 1, 2026

title: Takeaways from Bills win over Ravens
summary: The Buffalo Bills beat the Ravens 36-10 in Week 8 at home. Baltimore used three quarterbacks in the contest as Lamar Jackson got hurt his first offensive play of the game and Tyler Huntley suffered a turf toe injury later. Nonetheless, the Bills are now 6-1 entering Week 9. These are my takeaways from Buffalo’s […]
full_text: The Buffalo Bills beat the Ravens 36-10 in Week 8 at home. Baltimore used three quarterbacks in the contest as Lamar Jackson got hurt his first offensive play of the game and Tyler Huntley suffered a turf toe injury later. Nonetheless, the Bills are now 6-1 entering Week 9. These are my takeaways from Buffalo’s victory. The defense did what it should have given the circumstances Of course, I’m not expecting Buffalo’s defense to allow 144 points at 2.9 yards per play very often. Playing a third-string quarterback made things exceptionally easier for that unit in this game. BUT… Buffalo’s defense did exactly what it should hav against an undrafted rookie quarterback thrust into an emergency relief appearance. That’s a positive sign. Even Derrick Henry was held in check — only 11 carries for 53 yards — and Zay Flowers did not have a catch. Joey Fagnano demonstrated some moxie on a handful of throws yet none were completed to the receiver who entered this game with the NFL’s highest yards-per-route-run figure among all qualifying wideouts. So while it’s absolutely correct to mention the caveat regarding this performance from the Bills defense, it was placed in a no-win situation because of the competition level it faced at quarterback. This contest was a reminder that it’s a 60-minute game The Bills have an incredible ability to put forth a C+ / B- performance and either score 30-plus points and/or win by more than one score, both of which happened in this game. Despite the 16-7 lead at the half, Buffalo absolutely squandered quality scoring chances and made mistakes in the first two quarters. The end of half clock management wasn’t ideal. Worked. But the process was off. Overall, it was very disjointed. No doubt. The Bills went from a somewhat pedestrian 2.0 points per drive in the first half to a massive 4.0 points per drive in the second half. And the vibe of Buffalo’s offense and ease at which it moved the football matched those splits. In the third and fourth quarters, the Bills ran it more efficiently and got more pass-catchers involved at all levels of the field. In the end, Josh Allen finished 21-of-34 for 289 yards — 8.5 yards per — with two passing touchdowns, one interception, one sack, and a respectable passer rating of 96.3. While, yes, a team’s own offense does have an impact on the defense, it’s not as if the Ravens third-string unit was out there against Allen and Co. Welcome, back DJ Moore + Ed Oliver Finally, the Bills had one of their receivers make a spectacular grab in a low-percentage situation. Moore’s 49-yarder down the middle of the field was a thing of beauty we frankly haven’t seen much of from Buffalo’s pass-catching group over the past few seasons. His four snags, 82 yards and a score were a jolt to Buffalo’s aerial attack. On the defensive side, Oliver finished with four pressures on 18 pass-rush snaps — good for a whopping 22.2% pressure rate. His bull rush was outstanding throughout, and his first-step quickness gave Baltimore’s interior blocking unit problems all game. The Bills were playing without two key pieces on either side of the ball in Los Angeles and Las Vegas, and their impact was certainly felt in this win. I still think the WR corps needs a boost Despite Moore’s production — and outrageous catch on the long ball — it still feels like, collectively, the Bills receivers aren’t moving the needle enough on a regular, drive-to-drive basis. Now, sure, there’s Dalton Kincaid at tight end, who had an up-and-down contest, James Cook on the ground and through the air and Ty Johnson making something happen on a critical third down. But this offense still doesn’t want to feature Khalil Shakir — despite his awesome dependability — and Coleman disappeared in this game with one catch for four yards. And now, Josh Palmer is working through another injury. I highly doubt the Bills make a move at receiver before the trade deadline. But I would love for them to at least explore that position. As a last resort, how about some Greg Dortch in the offense? I want Allen to be able to lean on his collective of wide receivers a little more this season. There’s the Jim Leonhard we expected (possible springboard?) Leonhard likely was licking his chops when Huntley entered the game, and his eyes probably lit up when Baltimore’s undrafted rookie quarterback was forced into action. Those developments could’ve skewed Buffalo’s defensive philosophy in this one. But nonetheless, Leonhard went blitzing berserk in this victory, and I view that as a positive sign. The Bills blitzed on 64.5% of dropbacks against the Ravens in Week 8, their highest blitz rate since 2021 and the highest blitz rate Ravens quarterbacks have faced this season, according to @NextGenStats . Their blitz rate had not exceeded 39% in any of their previous six games. — Lance Lysowski (@LLysowski) November 1, 2026 Interestingly, Leonhard decided to call the game from the box for the first time this season as well. Should we expect the Bills to blitz on over 50% of the opposition’s dropbacks every week? Probably not. But remember, before this game, Buffalo had the NFL’s 20th-highest blitz rate at just 27.9%. Those blitzes were more creative against Baltimore and, sure, Jackson likely could’ve made some defenders miss in the pocket, but Leonhard’s blitz designs regularly got a free runner to the quarterback. Overall, Fagnano was pressured on 56% of his dropbacks. Huntley was pressured on four of his five dropbacks, and Jackson was pressured on his only one in this game. I wonder — and will be tracking — if this game acts as a springboard for a genuinely aggressive, blitz-heavy defense the rest of the way.
