title: Carolina Panthers 2027 NFL Draft Prospect Profile: Emmanuel Oyebadejo
summary: The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the […]
full_text: GAINESVILLE, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 10: Emmanuel Oyebadejo of the Florida Gators takes the field before the start of a game against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium on October 10, 2026 in Gainesville, Florida. (Photo by James Gilbert/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2027 NFL Draft feels like forever away, and we’re all caught up in the start of the NFL season. Regardless, it’s never too early to look ahead to the Draft. This weekly series will take a closer look at some of the prospects the Carolina Panthers could select in the 2027 iteration of the Draft. In this series, we’ll only be looking at prospects the Panthers could seriously consider. This week our profile will focus on Florida Gators defensive lineman Emmanuel Oyebadejo. Bio Oyebadejo (6’6”, 299 lbs.) was a soccer player in Manchester, England growing up. A growth spurt saw him pivot from the pitch to the basketball court, where he played for England’s U16 and U18 teams. Oyebadejo originally enrolled at the University of Exeter to study medicine. He started playing American football in 2023 when a coach at Exeter saw the mountain of a man on the sideline and recruited him. His natural affinity for the sport caught the eye of Jacksonville State, who recruited him stateside. After an injury before the 2024 season, he played in all 14 games for the Gamecocks in 2025, getting him some national attention from big time programs. In his first season of college football in the US, he put up 43 tackles, 6.5 tackles for loss, 4.5 sacks, two forced fumbles, and five passes defended. He stayed in state and transferred to Florida, where he already has 4.5 TFLs and 3.5 sacks in just six games so far with the Gators. Strengths/Weaknesses Oyebadejo looks like he was built in a lab. He pairs his tall, long, and heavy frame with elite athleticism (4.72 forty at about 300 lbs.). He uses his speed and mass to convert all that momentum into a deadly power rush off the edge but has the versatility to line up anywhere from the B gap to a wide 9 alignment. The level of competition does not seem to bother him too much, notching 2.5 sacks in his first SEC game against Auburn. Obviously Oyebadejo is a raw prospect since he’s only been playing football since 2023. His technique and hand usage need a lot of work, his pad level is often too high, and his tackling is inconsistent. He has also been relegated to a rotational role despite having the raw physical tools to be an every down lineman. Projection Oyebadejo is a unicorn in terms of height, length, weight, strength, and speed. Even though he has only played in about 20 college games, the upside is incredibly tantalizing. To put his physical attributes into perspective: he is taller, heavier, longer, and faster than JJ Watt was coming out of Wisconsin. That’s the type of perfect world scenario teams see in Oyebadejo. Still, right now he’s projected as a Day Two pick because the sample size is just so small. He’d maintain a rotational role at first in the NFL, but that is exactly what the Panthers will be looking for next season. With Jaelan Phillips and the returning Nic Scourton projected to be starting on the edge and Derrick Brown, Lee Hunter, and potentially Turk Wharton (assuming he is not a cap casualty) being your starters on the line, Oyebadejo could be a player to slot in for any of those spots aside from nose tackle. That would allow him to slowly acclimate to the NFL game while learning from some very talented pros in the process. The Panthers also have a history of rostering late-to-football guys who grew up in England; Efe Obada was a great story and fan favorite during his time with the team. What do you think, Panthers fans? If Emmanuel Oyebadejo is available when the Panthers select in the 2027 NFL Draft, should they take him? Sound off in the comments!

title: What’s next?
summary: The 3-4 Carolina Panthers held on to first place in the NFC South thanks to a16-0 win by the 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers over the 3-5 Atlanta Falcons that featured 324 yards rushing and -2 yards passing by the Bucs. This is the company that we keep. The company we don’t keep anymore includes former […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Bryce Young #9 of the Carolina Panthers runs to the sidelines against the Green Bay Packers during the first quarter at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 3-4 Carolina Panthers held on to first place in the NFC South thanks to a16-0 win by the 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers over the 3-5 Atlanta Falcons that featured 324 yards rushing and -2 yards passing by the Bucs. This is the company that we keep. The company we don’t keep anymore includes former defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero and former defensive passing game coordinator Jonathan Cooley. The defense has been a point of contention for Panthers fans in recent years as a sort of chicken or egg scenario. Limited investment and limited success have made it difficult to fully evaluate Evero’s work on a game-by-game basis. The full course of his tenure in Charlotte, however, clearly left head coach Dave Canales dissatisfied. Some will say this firing is overdue. Others will question the timing and ultimate purpose of it at this point in the season. Regardless, we shouldn’t hold our collective breathe in anticipation of major changes for the Panthers porous defense. The fact remains that with Jaelan Phillips in and out of the lineup with injuries and Cam Jackson, Mike Jackson, Jaycee Horn, Akayleb Evans, Nic Scourton, and Thomas Incoom all on injured reserve, the Panthers are basically playing preseason football out there. That is not to say that the defense is the only problem unit the Panthers have. Their offensive line has been a specific and obvious weakness for some time. Starters Taylor Moton, Ikem Ekwonu, and Damien Lewis have all been sorely missed throughout their various injuries. Free agent acquisitions Rasheed Walker and Luke Fortner have simply been complete disappointments. Right guard Robert Hunt’s play and mental focus may have you questioning if he ever actually did return from his 2025 torn bicep. Rookie offensive tackle Monroe Freeling, meanwhile, is doing his best out there. He could be worse, the unit as a whole however could hardly be. They helped prove two weeks in s row that the Panthers cannot win a shootout if they don’t let their quarterback shoot. Enter the 6-2 Denver Broncos, a team with twice as many wins as any team in the NFC South. The Panthers’ Week 9 opponent has a capable passing game and a relatively fearsome defensive line that sacked Patrick Mahomes twice yesterday afternoon. While they only have ten sacks on the season, they may expect to double that total against a Panthers offensive line that has surrendered 11 sacks in the last two games. They are, in short, a competent, competitive NFL team who will provide a solid test for the Panthers. The Broncos are probably the best team the Panthers have faced so far. Early season success against backup quarterbacks may have falsely inflated expectations for Carolina, but they still have limited talent on both sides of the ball. There is enough talent that they could steal a few games if they can shore up their obvious weakenesses at corner, right guard, center, left guard, and left tackle. That will be the test that they have to pass against a hungry Broncos team that is looking to build on their own divisional lead. What us next, in this context, is that test. The next few weeks will be an inflection point for these Panthers. Either they will pull themselves together through adversity or they will squander the hottest start they have had in a season since Sam Darnold was here. I’m not saying that they have to beat the Broncos to save their season, but they absolutely have to look like they belong on the same field as them. If they can do that then they can at least play a competitive December, further injuries permitting.

title: Bears v. Seahawks Postgame: A Statement Victory in Big Jeff’s First Game
summary: First Quarter: The Statement Drive Chicago opened with a grinding 17-play, 80-yard drive that consumed 8 minutes and 32 seconds and ended with Caleb Williams’ 1-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden. It was the first time in 27 games that an opponent had scored on the Seahawks on the opening possession. Jeffery Simmons made an […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Jeffery Simmons #99 of the Chicago Bears warms up prior to a game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images First Quarter: The Statement Drive Chicago opened with a grinding 17-play, 80-yard drive that consumed 8 minutes and 32 seconds and ended with Caleb Williams’ 1-yard touchdown pass to Luther Burden. It was the first time in 27 games that an opponent had scored on the Seahawks on the opening possession. Jeffery Simmons made an immediate impact in his Bears debut with a sack of Sam Darnold. Observation: The Bears set the tone early by sustaining drives and staying physical against a defense that had been difficult to score on. Gooch Hot Take: That opening drive wasn’t flashy—it was the kind of ugly, clock-eating football that tells a contender “we can hang with you for four quarters.” Simmons already looks like the interior disruptor the Bears paid two firsts for. But let’s be clear – that first touchdown drive was EVERYTHING the Bears want to be. Second Quarter: Field Goals and a Late Spark Seattle got on the board with a Jason Myers field goal. Chicago answered with Cairo Santos field goals from 44 and 38 yards to push the lead to 13-3. With 30 seconds left, Jaxon Smith-Njigba beat coverage for a 43-yard touchdown from Darnold (extra point missed), cutting the deficit to 13-9 at the half. Observation: The Bears were efficient enough in the red zone area to take points when available. JSN remains the one consistent explosive piece for Seattle. Upon Further Review preview: We’re going to talk about the QB slide this week. Nothing Bush could do – literally flying through the air with his back turned – on that late Darnold slide. The TV crew thought it was a clear penalty – and maybe it was on the rules – the rules need to change. It’s just ridiculous – and it isn’t protecting quarterbacks. It isn’t even that it produces dumb penalties – because of course you cannot ask defenders to stop in midair. It is the fact that it encourages QBs to slide – which is an uber-dangerous play for them. When QBs become runners – they should just be runners. Gooch Hot Take: Santos quietly outkicked Myers when it mattered. The Seattle punter kind of rocks – respect given. But the other Hawks kicker – the missed extra point on the JSN score was the difference between a one-score game and a more comfortable margin heading into the locker room. Halftime Thoughts That opening 17-play drive was the statement of the half. It wasn’t explosive, but it was the kind of grinding, clock-eating football that shows Chicago can match Seattle’s physicality for a full game. Simmons is already justifying the early returns on the trade. One sack and consistent pressure in his first half as a Bear is exactly the multiplier the defensive line needed. JSN remains Seattle’s entire explosive element. When he’s bottled up, the rest of the offense looks ordinary. The missed extra point on his score was a quiet but meaningful swing. Santos is quietly having a strong night. Two clean field goals kept the Bears in control when the red-zone finishing wasn’t perfect. If Chicago continues to control the line of scrimmage and limit big plays outside of JSN, this is a very manageable second half. Seattle will need more than one or two explosive plays to flip the script on the road. The Bears REALLY need to solve the final drive of the half. This is the second week in a row they’ve allowed a soft touchdown heading into halftime. Third Quarter: Swift Extends the Lead Chicago answered the half-ending JSN score by controlling the third period and pushing the lead to two possessions. The Seahawks were held scoreless as the Bears continued to win the physical battle and sustain drives. Key Sequence The Bears opened the half with the ball and marched 69 yards in 10 plays over 6 minutes and 19 seconds. The drive featured a 22-yard completion from Caleb Williams to Rome Odunze and a 9-yard pass to Kalif Raymond that set up short-yardage situations. D’Andre Swift finished it with a 1-yard touchdown run, and Cairo Santos’ extra point made it 20-9. Seattle’s best chance late in the quarter was erased by offensive pass interference on Jaxon Smith-Njigba, wiping out a gain that would have put them near the goal line and leaving them with second-and-long instead. Observations Chicago’s second drive of six-plus minutes ended in a touchdown, matching the pattern from the opening series. They are controlling the clock and the line of scrimmage against a Seahawks defense that has been hard to move. Williams continues to deliver timely completions under pressure. The connection to Odunze on the drive was another example of him extending plays and finding open receivers. Seattle’s offense remains limited outside of isolated JSN moments. The OPI call was a tough break, but the Bears’ defense is generating pressure and forcing incomplete or short gains. Jeffery Simmons continues to show up as a disruptor in his debut, contributing to the interior pressure that has helped limit Darnold. Gooch Hot Takes Swift’s short-yardage score perfectly complemented the long opening drive. Chicago is winning with sustained, physical football rather than relying on explosives, and that is the harder style for Seattle to counter. The OPI wipeout of JSN’s potential scoring chance was a quiet but significant swing. Seattle is not generating enough consistent offense to overcome those kinds of setbacks right now. I thought it was the right call – JSN clearly pushed off. The only surprise is that the refs actually called it. If the Bears keep stacking six-minute drives and finishing them in the end zone, this game is going to get out of reach even if JSN makes another big play. The Seahawks need a quick answer early in the fourth or the physical edge Chicago has established will decide the night. Fourth Quarter: Controversial Calls, Turnover, and Swift Finishes It The final period featured the night’s most debated moments and Seattle’s closest push. Early in the quarter, Austin Booker blocked a Jason Myers field-goal attempt, preserving Chicago’s two-score lead. On the ensuing possession, Colston Loveland caught a short pass, then fumbled after a hit from DeMarcus Lawrence, who recovered at the Chicago 25. Seattle converted the turnover with a 7-yard touchdown pass from Darnold to Cooper Kupp and a successful two-point conversion to Tory Horton, cutting the lead to 20-17. Chicago answered with two more Swift rushing touchdowns (5 yards each), the second set up in part by a Kalif Raymond screen, to push the final margin to 34-17. A late interception sealed the outcome. Controversial calls and plays: The late-third-quarter OPI on JSN that wiped out a near-goal-line opportunity remained a point of contention. It was the kind of contact that draws flags inconsistently depending on the crew and the moment. The Loveland fumble was forced cleanly by Lawrence, but the timing—right after the blocked kick—flipped field position and briefly brought Seattle back within one score. Earlier in the game, a potential late hit on Darnold by Devin Bush drew criticism as a no-call; the broadcast and social reaction suggested it met the criteria for unnecessary roughness on a sliding quarterback, though no flag was thrown. I don’t agree; even if it is technically a foul, we need to get the game back to reflecting real football. Delay-of-game timing on Chicago snaps and a post-play flag that forced a replay of a down also drew complaints about consistency. Observations and Gooch Hot Takes: Even with the turnover and the OPI debate, Chicago’s response was decisive. Swift’s three rushing touchdowns closed the game after Seattle got within three. Simmons’ early sack and continued interior presence set a defensive tone that limited Seattle outside of the one JSN score and the short Kupp touchdown. The blocked field goal and the…

title: NFC Playoff Picture: Chicago Bears solidify standing with Monday night win
summary: The Chicago Bears were fifth in the NFC coming into Week 8, they fell behind the Detroit Lions on Sunday with their win, and now the Bears are back in the top Wild Card spot after Chicago’s Monday night win. A great development for the Bears is the first loss of the season by the […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - NOVEMBER 02: Rome Odunze #15 of the Chicago Bears celebrates against the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter of the game at Lumen Field on November 02, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears were fifth in the NFC coming into Week 8, they fell behind the Detroit Lions on Sunday with their win, and now the Bears are back in the top Wild Card spot after Chicago’s Monday night win. A great development for the Bears is the first loss of the season by the Minnesota Vikings. With Minnesota at 6-1 and the Bears at 6-2, Chicago likely controls their own destiny in the division. A Bears win over the Vikings would give both team two losses and two NFC North losses as well as two NFC losses. It would move the tiebreaker to the Strength of Victory tiebreaker until the Common Games opponents gets to four games, and Chicago would move ahead of Minnesota on the SOV. In addition to those two NFC North teams winning, the Green Bay Packers won on Thursday night to stick in the seventh and final Wild Card slot. All four NFC North teams are in a playoff spot. With this win over the Seahawks, the Bears have a stranglehold on a playoff spot. The Seahawks drop to 4-4, two games plus a tiebreaker behind Chicago. NFC playoff standings with Bears win 1. San Francisco 49ers (6-1, strength of victory .456) 2. Minnesota Vikings (6-1, strength of victory .400) 3. New York Giants (4-2-1) 4. Carolina Panthers (3-4) 5. Chicago Bears (6-2) 6. Detroit Lions (5-2) 7. Green Bay Packers (5-3) 8. Seattle Seahawks (4-4, 1-1 NFCW) 9. Los Angeles Rams (4-4, 0-2 NFCW) 10. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-5, win over ATL, 1-0 vs DAL+ARZ, 3-2 NFC) 11. Atlanta Falcons (3-5, loss to TB, 3-3 NFC record) 12. Arizona Cardinals (3-5, 1-0 vs DAL+ARZ, 2-4 NFC) 13. Dallas Cowboys (3-5, 0-2 vs TB+ARZ, loss to ARZ) 14. Washington Commanders (2-4-1) 15. New Orleans Saints (2-5, 1-3 NFC) 16. Philadelphia Eagles (2-6) Explaining the 3-5 cluster in the NFC First, you get to one team per division so the Falcons and Buccaneers are against each other. Tampa has a win over Atlanta, so they have the tiebreaker. Tampa vs Arizona vs Dallas is a head-to-head tiebreaker where Atlanta and Arizona move on since they both have wins over Dallas. The Bucs are 3-2 in the NFC vs the Cardinals at 2-4, so Tampa is the 10 seed. Then the Falcons go into a three-way tiebreaker with the Cardinals and Cowboys. It goes straight to NFC record where the Falcons are 3-3 and the Cardinals and Cowboys are 2-4. Atlanta is the 11 seed. The Arizona Cardinals beat the Cowboys so they win the head-to-head tiebreaker in the two-way decision. Arizona is 12th and the Cowboys are 13th.

title: NFL Trade Deadline Rumors: Bears want pass rush and secondary help
summary: A week ago, NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reported that the Chicago Bears and the San Francisco 49ers would be two teams looking to add players at what he said would be a very active trade deadline. “I’ve heard both teams connected to several defensive players,” he said. “Including rushers Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack also DeForest […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: (L-R) Executive vice president Howie Roseman of the Philadelphia Eagles talks with General manager Ryan Poles of the Chicago Bears prior to the game at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images A week ago, NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reported that the Chicago Bears and the San Francisco 49ers would be two teams looking to add players at what he said would be a very active trade deadline. “I’ve heard both teams connected to several defensive players,” he said. “Including rushers Josh Sweat, Khalil Mack also DeForest Buckner. Along with some names who aren’t necessarily on the trade block. I think both Chicago and San Francisco want to be aggressive, and I’ll be shocked if they don’t make a move before the deadline.” Shortly after that report, the 49ers traded for Buckner, and the Bears traded for Jeffery Simmons. Schultz was back on Ryan Clark’s The Pivot podcast today , and he mentioned the 49ers and Bears again. “I don’t think either team is done,” Schultz said. “I think the 49ers are still looking for a receiver and pass rusher. While the Bears want another pass rusher and secondary help. So I wouldn’t rule out another move from either team. There’s a lot of Khalil Mack buzz for both clubs.” Mack has been linked to the Bears for weeks now, but the ‘Niners buzz has been there as well (just not as loud). The winless Los Angeles Chargers need to want to trade him, and ESPN’s Adam Schefter said this morning that they still haven’t given an “indication that they’re willing to trade anybody.” The secondary help Schultz references could be a corner, but I wouldn’t be surprised if they were looking for a veteran safety so they could plug Cam Lewis back into a jack-of-all-trades reserve role. The trade deadline is a week from tomorrow, on Tuesday, November 10, at 3:00 PM CT. Besides Mack, who would you like the Bears to target at the trade deadline?

title: Bears at Seahawks: 3 Props to Play
summary: I feel like it’s been a long time since I’ve written up a props article. Probably because it’s been a week and a half since the Bears faced the Patriots. We had a good week last week; 2 out of 3 ain’t bad, and that raised our season record to 10-11. This week, the Bears […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Luther Burden III #10 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the second quarter of the game against the New England Patriots at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images I feel like it’s been a long time since I’ve written up a props article. Probably because it’s been a week and a half since the Bears faced the Patriots. We had a good week last week; 2 out of 3 ain’t bad, and that raised our season record to 10-11. This week, the Bears have a massive game against the Seattle Seahawks. Both teams are looking to show they are one of the elite teams in the NFC and ready to push for the Super Bowl. The Bears made a huge impact move by trading for Jeffery Simmons this past week, and he is expected to play. Let’s look at the prop plays for this week. As always, odds courtesy of FanDuel. Jaxon Smith-Njigba OVER 99.5 Receiving Yards -113 You hate to lead off the prop plays with a Seattle over, but how do you not expect JSN to gain significant yardage? He’s gained over 100 yards in every game but one this year, and you can’t look at the Bears’ current crop of cornerbacks and think it’s a good matchup for Chicago. The only hope is that with Simmons in the mix, Dennis Allen blitzes less and Kyler Gordon has some success against him. Other than that, you have to expect at least 2 or 3 pretty sizable gains from JSN and another day over 100 yards receiving. Luther Burden OVER 52.5 Receiving Yards -113 In the two games since Caleb Williams’ return, Burden has caught all 12 targets he’s gotten from Caleb for a total of 225 yards and a touchdown. Burden has easily taken over WR1 status in Chicago with Caleb back in the fold, and he should see some shallow crossers tonight with an opportunity to gain some yards after the catch similarly to what happened against New England. Kalif Raymond OVER 16.5 Receiving Yards -113 This last one was between Raymond and Sam Roush. With Cole Kmet out for the year, there’s a hole, albeit a small one, in the Bears offense, and you have to try to figure out who is going to fill the role of a reliable dump-off guy. Roush makes sense, and his OU is only 8.5, but his role has been greatly reduced the last few weeks, and I just don’t know if Ben Johnson will suddenly trust him again due to an injury. Raymond’s role has also been reduced, but I think he’s the guy who sees an uptick in targets. 16.5 yards isn’t much. Raymond should be able to do that in just 1 or 2 catches, but he’s only gone over this total once in the last four weeks, and it was 18 yards. This is more a play that Raymond is on the field more and will see a couple more targets due to the Kmet injury. BONUS: Jeffery Simmons 0.5 sacks or more +154 For the purposes of these articles, I only give straight 50-50 props and stopped dabbling in the plus-money waters a couple of years ago. But wanted to at least drop this one in as a bonus. I think Simmons plays at least 50% of the snaps tonight, and I just think big players like this always have that extra little bit of motivation to show up that first game in a new location. I go back to Khalil Mack’s first half against Green Bay in his debut. I think Simmons makes a couple of impact plays, so corralling San Darnold for a sack feels like a good wager to make.

title: Grade the NFL Trade: Bears trade for Jeffery Simmons gets an A
summary: After the Chicago Bears traded for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans, we asked you to grade the trade, and most of you gave it high marks. We obviously won’t know the true cost of the deal for a few years, but this is a win-now move for a team that feels […]
full_text: Newly acquired Chicago Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons (99) warms up before practice at Halas Hall on Friday, Oct. 30, 2026, in Lake Forest, Illinois. (Terrence Antonio James/Chicago Tribune/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) After the Chicago Bears traded for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans, we asked you to grade the trade, and most of you gave it high marks. We obviously won’t know the true cost of the deal for a few years, but this is a win-now move for a team that feels it’s in a Super Bowl window. The Bears have the head coach and the quarterback they feel can win with, so sending a 2027 and 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fourth-rounder for Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round pick was what it took to bring in a red-level talent for a defense lacking star power. In his eight-year career, Simmons has been named to four Pro Bowls and three All-Pro Teams. He’s coming off a First Team All-Pro nod after racking up a career-high 11 sacks in 15 games for the Titans. The move from the one-win Titans to the 5-2 Bears will boost his profile and improve his chances of winning the Defensive Player of the Year Award. Our partners at FanDuel Sportsbook currently have those odds at +2000, which are the seventh-best. The Bears play on prime time the next two weeks and have two more standalone games slated for Thanksgiving and Christmas, so if Simmons helps turn Chicago’s defense around, he’ll definitely be in the mix.

title: Chicago Bears @ Seattle Seahawks: Week 8 Players to Watch
summary: After captivating the league’s attention (if they weren’t already on notice), the Chicago Bears once again have an elite Primetime matchup with another Super Bowl contender – if not outright favorite – in the current defending champion Seattle Seahawks. Chicago will not only have to tighten up some mental mistakes that have led to 21 […]
full_text: SEATTLE, CO - OCTOBER 15: Nick Emmanwori #3 of the Seattle Seahawks reacts after a play against the Denver Broncos during an NFL football game at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Seattle, Colorado. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images After captivating the league’s attention (if they weren’t already on notice), the Chicago Bears once again have an elite Primetime matchup with another Super Bowl contender – if not outright favorite – in the current defending champion Seattle Seahawks. Chicago will not only have to tighten up some mental mistakes that have led to 21 penalties over the last two weeks, but also deal with arguably the most talented roster in the league at the most difficult stadium in the league. Ben Johnson and Co. have their work cut out for them in what many are saying may be a preview of the NFC Championship game. Let’s get to which players from Seattle will have my attention on both sides of the ball. Offense: Quenton Nelson, #53 – G Anytime you add an All-Pro talent mid-week, he is going to get quite a bit of attention. Fortunately for Chicago, they, too, added an All-Pro talent in the form of Jeffery Simmons – the former Tennessee Titan who played against Nelson’s Colts twice a year. All in all, these two have played each other 13 times over the course of their careers but never surrounded by the talent these two have around them this time. Nelson being added to the Super Bowl champs is the definition of the rich getting richer. Considered by many as the best Guard in the league, Nelson is and has been a dominating force in the middle and figures to provide a jolt to the struggling Seahawks run game while assisting in keeping Sam Darnold clean in the pocket. Considering the offensive line is the one position group in the game of football that relies more on cohesiveness than any other, I am expecting a few hiccups in his first game action, especially within his first 7 days as a Seahawk, but Nelson still has the ability coupled with opportunity to make quite an impact Monday night. If Dennis Allen and his shiny new toy can cause some confusion up front and get after Sam Darnold, Chicago’s secondary will have a chance to create some critical turnovers and give Chicago a chance. If Nelson fortifies the Seahawks OL and helps keep Darnold clean whilst simultaneously opening holes in the run game – it will be a humbling experience for Chicago this week. Defense: Nick Emmanwori, #3 – S When it comes to the former 2nd-round pick out of South Carolina, his impact simply cannot be measured in the box score. And yet, out of all the bona fide ballers on the Seahawks’ vaunted defense, #3 is the one player who keeps opposing offenses up at night more than anyone else. Think of Kyler Gordon but 3 inches taller, 20lb heavier, and runs a 4.3 forty instead of a 4.5. And like Spidey, Emmanwori is deployed all over the defense, presenting unique challenges for any offense. According to Sumer Sports’ Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes), Emmanwori has been deployed in the slot 36% of his snaps, at Linebacker 34%, and 27% at Edge. I love Nick Emmanwori so much pic.twitter.com/DVaSay5Olx — Pete (@thefilmwatcher_) October 5, 2026 How Chicago manages this demon will be crucial. And like I said, they have multiple difference makers on that side of the ball that are capable in wrecking games. From Devon Witherspoon (arguably my FAVORITE Corner in the league) to Leonard Williams and Byron Murphy Jr. (best DT duo in the league) to pass rushers Derrick Hall and Uchenna Nwosu, these Seahawks likely have more than 11 defenders who would start on most teams. That’s not even taking into account dependable veteran difference makers like Safety Julian Love, LB Earnest Jones IV, and DT Jarran Reed. And yet – Emmanwori is more worrisome than them all. If Caleb Williams can avoid Emmanwori and the Bears offense can get a body on him in the run game – Chicago has enough talent on offense to put up points against anyone – Seattle included. But if Emmanwori can confuse the offense, make Bears TE Sam Roush look like the rookie he is, and nullify the impact of Colston Loveland, then Chicago is in trouble. Big game Monday night! Who on Seattle’s squad will you be watching most closely?
author: Bryan Orenchuk

title: Bengals Tuesday Trenches: Pros and cons of a potential Jonathan Taylor trade and more
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are 5-2 for the first time since the 2021 season and are very much in the mix for the AFC North title as we near the midway point of the season. They’re fresh off two needlessly exciting games, both of which saw them fall behind 13-0 before coming back to win. Their […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are 5-2 for the first time since the 2021 season and are very much in the mix for the AFC North title as we near the midway point of the season. They’re fresh off two needlessly exciting games, both of which saw them fall behind 13-0 before coming back to win. Their most recent cardiac-inducing victory came over the Tennessee Titans in overtime by a score of 43-36. While they came out on top in the end, they also lost several players to injury and will likely need to address multiple positions before the trade deadline, whether through trades or free agency. Before we get to that, though….. The Colts are going to trade Jonathan Taylor. It’s going to happen, and the Bengals are reportedly one of five or six teams “ aggressively pursuing ” a possible trade for Taylor, according to Jordan Schultz. So, before we get into some thoughts on Sunday’s game and the upcoming matchup in Spain, here are some pros and cons of a possible trade for Taylor. Pros The first is obvious—Jonathan Taylor is a stud of a running back, and he would immediately upgrade the Bengals’ rushing attack. The Bengals have the second-fewest rushing yards of any team in the NFL and average just 3.7 yards per carry. The coaching staff has desperately tried to create a balanced offense, putting Burrow under center more often than ever before. It’s just not working. Defenses can focus on Burrow, his receivers, and the passing game without giving much thought to the rushing attack. If the Bengals trade for Taylor, that changes, and the offense should be even better because of it. The Bengals also wouldn’t need to worry about replacing Chase Brown after the 2026 season. Brown and Samaje Perine are both in contract years, and Taylor, a true three-down workhorse, could replace them both moving forward. He would take an insane amount of pressure off Burrow. Right now, even as the Bengals try to force a running game, the offense flows through Burrow and his elite receivers. They’ve only scored four rushing touchdowns, and two of those belong to Burrow. Can you imagine if defenses couldn’t drop five or six defensive backs into coverage to deal with Chase and Higgins because they actually had to worry about Taylor? What happens when defensive backs have to creep up in run support and safeties can no longer bracket Chase? Taylor would instantly make the Bengals’ offense much less predictable. And he’s a workhorse. Brown averages only about 13 carries per game, while Perine gets around five. Taylor is capable of handling 20-plus carries per game and has proven he can shoulder the load of an NFL rushing attack. Cons The defense needs all the attention right now. Had we talked about this a couple of weeks ago, I’d have been all on board. That’s not the case anymore, though. The secondary is dealing with injuries and inconsistent play, and linebacker depth is a concern. Outside of the defensive line, the Bengals should seriously consider adding a veteran cornerback or linebacker, especially if DJ Turner is going to miss significant time. The cost would be enormous. The Bengals are already on the hook for Burrow’s $275 million, Chase’s $161 million, and Higgins’ $115 million contracts. The last thing they need is to add Taylor’s $44 million deal to the books. While it would be fun to see Taylor line up behind or next to Burrow, they don’t need to spend that kind of money on a running back when the offense will still flow through Burrow and his receivers more often than not. Taylor makes more sense for a team with a quarterback who needs a strong running game to help carry the offense. There is a possible out after the 2026 season, but it would still cost the Bengals $10 million in dead money. The running back position is devalued in 2026. While there are elite backs capable of doing elite things, some of the NFL’s best offenses have relative nobodies carrying the football. In the 2020s, it’s all about moving the ball through the air. A running back’s shelf life is also relatively short, which is part of the reason the position has been devalued in recent years. It’s a punishing position, and bell-cow running backs typically don’t last very long. The Derrick Henrys of the world are few and far between. Taylor is 27 now, and there’s no guarantee he’ll hold up to heavy use into his early 30s. The trade compensation could also be more than the Bengals are willing to pay. If there really are several teams aggressively pursuing Taylor, the Bengals could find themselves in a bidding war, forcing them to surrender more draft capital than they’re comfortable giving up. Again, had this conversation taken place even a week earlier, I’d have been all for adding an elite running back to an already ridiculously overpowered offense. Not anymore, though. The Bengals need help at cornerback first and foremost. Once they address that, they could still look at adding a veteran linebacker or another edge rusher to help replace Cashius Howell. Taylor would be a luxury the Bengals don’t really need and definitely can’t afford moving forward. I just don’t think he gets them any closer to hoisting the Lombardi Trophy than Chase Brown does in 2026, and I certainly don’t think they want to pay him the more than $21 million he’d be owed in 2027. So my vote is no. View Link Now, if you’re still with me after all that….. Here are some random thoughts on the Bengals’ overtime win over the Titans: The Dexter Lawrence sack late in the game that pushed the Titans out of field goal range was exactly why the Bengals traded away a top-10 pick to acquire him. That was an elite play from an elite player at a pivotal moment in the game. Had he not made that sack, the Bengals could be 4-3 today. Teams continue to do whatever they can to bracket Chase, taking their chances with Higgins at their own peril. Higgins finished the game with 11 receptions for 155 yards and two touchdowns. Once the Titans tried to adjust, Chase got going, too, finishing with 11 catches for 141 yards and a touchdown. Pick your poison, I guess. When the defensive line can’t generate pressure on the quarterback, the secondary struggles to lock down receivers. That’s why trading for a cornerback could be the best move the Bengals make before the deadline. This is the kind of game the 2024 and 2025 Bengals lose. Burrow was both brilliant and weirdly reckless on Sunday. He completed 38 of 48 passes for 462 yards and five touchdowns. However, he also threw three interceptions, a couple of which were pretty ugly, including an underthrow of a wide-open Chase that should have been a touchdown. As long as he’s brilliant more often than he’s reckless, I guess it doesn’t matter. Boye Mafe has been an outstanding signing. The defense’s inability to tackle continues to be a major issue as the Bengals head into Week 9. At this point, what needs to change? The running game wasn’t necessarily ineffective against the Titans, but it was underutilized. Brown averaged 4.6 yards per carry on Sunday, his second-highest average of the season, but carried the ball just 12 times. They were in a shootout, though, so I get it. Five of the Titans’ seven losses have come by six points or fewer. They’re better than their 1-7 record suggests. That being said, the Bengals are the much better team, and I would have liked to see them dominate Tennessee instead of allowing Cam Ward to throw for more than 300 yards for the first time in his career. Next stop: Spain If you’re still with me, the Bengals travel to Spain to face the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday morning as part of the league’s slate of international games this season. The Falcons are 3-5 and are coming off a bizarre shutout loss to the Buccaneers in which Tampa Bay had ZERO passing yards. The Falcons are better than the Titans , and the Bengals can’t afford to let them jump out to a 13-0 lead the way the Ravens and Titans did over the last two weeks. That kind of football isn’t sustainable, and the Bengals need to count…
author: Jason Garrison

title: Shemar Stewart’s time to show the Bengals what he’s made of has come
summary: “While he has the athletic measurements of a No. 1 overall pick, his production left a whole lot to be desired.” “The lack of production relative to the traits is a concern; still, players who move like him are highly coveted.” “He’s also the highest-rated player in this year’s balancing act of marrying future NFL […]
full_text: “While he has the athletic measurements of a No. 1 overall pick, his production left a whole lot to be desired .” “ The lack of production relative to the traits is a concern ; still, players who move like him are highly coveted.” “He’s also the highest-rated player in this year’s balancing act of marrying future NFL potential with on-field production. And his evaluation might be defined by the number “ 4.5″ — as in, 4.5 total college sacks and exactly 1.5 in each of his three seasons .” Those are three quotes from three different draft analysts regarding Cincinnati Bengals edge rusher and 2025 first-round pick Shemar Stewart’s bizarre lack of production in college despite his borderline freakish combination of size and speed. The Bengals, of course, used the No. 17 overall selection on Stewart. To this point in his career, he has two sacks to his name and has played in 12 total games. Most damning, though, was the fact that he was a healthy scratch before the Bengals’ Week 7 win over the Ravens on the road in Baltimore, meaning he was fully healthy and available to the Bengals, and the coaching staff felt they had a better chance to win without him. Of course, he wasn’t the only player to be a healthy scratch, but he was the only first-round pick. Stewart was active in Week 8, but only took six snaps. It appears as though Stewart’s time to prove he was worth the No. 17 overall pick has come. Promising edge rusher and fellow Texas A&M Aggie Cashius Howell suffered a wrist injury that required surgery during their comeback win over the Ravens. The rookie, who has taken 185 defensive snaps before he left in the third quarter against the Titans, which is the third most of any edge rusher on the roster behind Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy, leaves a large void. Now, Stewart will be asked to help fill that empty space, which will finally give him the opportunity to prove the Bengals got it right in 2025. This is especially true considering Cedric Johnson (who has taken 104 snaps) also left the game against the Ravens. He was declared out after suffering an ankle injury in the fourth quarter. He is considered day-to-day, but that doesn’t necessarily mean he’ll be available or at 100% if he is on Sunday morning in Spain. Stewart’s size and speed should make him a nightmare for many offensive tackles. The potential Stewart could have as a pass rusher is why he was selected so early despite the little production. Hopefully, he can help the Bengals remain near the top when it comes to sacks in the league, even though they rarely blitz, which is a testament to their defensive line that Stewart will now look to boost.
author: Jason Garrison

title: AFC North Standings: Bengals survive Titans scare; Steelers take first place
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals survived a wild 43-36 shootout with the Tennessee Titans behind six total touchdowns from Joe Burrow, including a nine-yard scramble for the winning score in overtime. The results provided plenty of drama across the division, but perhaps the biggest takeaway was the Bengals’ defense, which looked disturbingly similar to the unit that […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals survived a wild 43-36 shootout with the Tennessee Titans behind six total touchdowns from Joe Burrow, including a nine-yard scramble for the winning score in overtime. The results provided plenty of drama across the division, but perhaps the biggest takeaway was the Bengals’ defense, which looked disturbingly similar to the unit that plagued Cincinnati throughout last season. Bengals survive overtime shootout vs. Titans The Cincinnati Bengals escaped with a 43-36 overtime victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, but the final score did little to disguise another troubling defensive performance. Joe Burrow threw five touchdown passes and had three interceptions in a game that featured dramatic momentum swings, costly mistakes, and enough defensive breakdowns to remind Bengals fans of last season’s struggles. Cincinnati ultimately prevailed with an offensive touchdown in overtime for just the second time in franchise history. Tennessee wasted little time exposing Cincinnati’s defensive problems, jumping to a 13-0 first-quarter lead. Tony Pollard broke loose for a 40-yard touchdown run, and the Titans repeatedly found opportunities against a Bengals defense that struggled to contain the run and prevent sustained drives. Cincinnati eventually responded behind Burrow, who connected with Ja’Marr Chase for a 30-yard touchdown on third-and-18 and found rookie tight end Jack Endries for another score before halftime. The Bengals took a 14-13 lead into the locker room despite an uneven opening half. Burrow’s afternoon was a study in extremes. His five touchdown passes demonstrated the explosive potential of Cincinnati’s offense, but three interceptions by Tennessee safety Amani Hooker repeatedly threatened to undo that production. Cincinnati benefited from a defensive takeaway of its own when Boye Mafe forced a Cam Ward fumble that Dexter Lawrence recovered, setting up Burrow’s 17-yard touchdown pass to Tee Higgins. Yet the biggest concern was the Bengals’ defense. Despite offseason efforts to improve the unit, Cincinnati surrendered 36 points in regulation to a Tennessee team that entered the game with just one victory. Pollard’s running and Ward’s ability to move the offense repeatedly put the Bengals on their heels. The performance was an uncomfortable reminder of last season, when defensive shortcomings regularly forced Burrow and the offense to compensate for mistakes on the other side of the ball. Steelers crush Browns to take AFC North lead The Pittsburgh Steelers left little doubt about who belongs atop the AFC North on Sunday, overwhelming the Cleveland Browns 27-6. Pittsburgh (6-2) won its fourth consecutive game, avenging an earlier loss to Cleveland and claiming sole possession of first place in the division. The Browns fell to 5-3 after failing to score a touchdown against a relentless Steelers defense. Pittsburgh controlled the game on the ground, with Jaylen Warren rushing for 143 yards on 17 carries and Rico Dowdle adding 56 yards and a touchdown. The Steelers piled up 160 rushing yards in the first half alone, building a 20-6 halftime advantage. Tight end Pat Freiermuth scored on a one-yard sneak with one second remaining in the second quarter, capping a late drive that effectively put Cleveland on its heels. The Steelers’ defense was equally impressive, recording eight sacks, forcing two turnovers and limiting Cleveland to just 34 rushing yards. T.J. Watt collected two sacks, while Patrick Queen contributed 10 tackles, 1.5 sacks and a forced fumble. Cleveland managed minus one yard of offense in the opening quarter, and quarterback Deshaun Watson spent much of the afternoon on his back. Aaron Rodgers completed 13 of 25 passes for 172 yards, including a 58-yard connection to Darnell Washington that set up Warren’s third-quarter touchdown and pushed Pittsburgh’s lead to 27-6. Washington finished with a career-best 94 receiving yards as the Steelers cruised to their 23rd consecutive regular-season home victory over the Browns. Bills crush Ravens , Lamar Jackson lost to injury The Baltimore Ravens suffered a disastrous afternoon in Buffalo on Sunday, falling 36-10 to the Bills in a game that quickly became a nightmare for their quarterback room. Lamar Jackson, who had missed the previous three games with an ankle injury, hurt his thumb on Baltimore’s first offensive play and never returned. Backup Tyler Huntley also suffered an injury, forcing the Ravens to turn to third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano. The loss dropped Baltimore to 4-4 and extended its losing streak to three games. Buffalo jumped ahead 10-0 on Josh Allen’s one-yard touchdown run and a 56-yard field goal by Tyler Bass. Derrick Henry briefly brought Baltimore back into contention with a two-yard touchdown run, but the Ravens struggled to generate offense with their depleted quarterback group. Buffalo led 16-7 at halftime, and Baltimore managed only a third-quarter field goal before the Bills took complete control. James Cook scored on a five-yard run, while Allen connected with DJ Moore for an 11-yard touchdown and Dalton Kincaid for a 23-yard score. Allen’s touchdown pass to Moore was particularly significant, moving him past Jim Kelly for the most career touchdown passes in Bills franchise history. Buffalo improved to 6-1, while Baltimore faces mounting questions about its offense and the health of its quarterbacks. AFC North Standings Pittsburgh Steelers: 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals: 5-2 Cleveland Browns: 5-3 Baltimore Ravens: 4-4

title: Bengals News: Zac Taylor defends Ja’Marr Chase’s passion after heated sideline outburst

The players know it isn’t good enough, the coaches know it isn’t good enough and one player […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have been dealing with slow starts the last two weeks. While they were able to overcome 13-0 deficits in back-to-back weeks, that is not sustainable if this team wants to reach their Super Bowl aspirations. The players know it isn’t good enough, the coaches know it isn’t good enough and one player that hasn’t shied away from that is star wide receiver Ja’Marr Chase. Chase addressed the team at halftime when losing to the Baltimore Ravens. The team responded with 35 unanswered points in a 35-13 win. This week, Chase was seen on the sidelines visibly angry. Bengals News: Is Ja’Marr Chase Upset With the Bengals? Zac Taylor Says He Likes the Competitiveness “You know, that’s just part of it. It’s a tight game. It’s an emotional game. We’ll work through it, obviously. [He had] a big day for us. Came up really big there at the end of the game and overtime. So that’s just one of those things that happens in a football game.” Joe Burrow makes 3-year admission with Bengals’ OT win over Titans “Burrow’s comments stoke a growing confidence in the team’s ability to overcome adversity, even when mistakes threaten to derail a victory.” Bengals’ alarming new problem doesn’t have an obvious fix, and their trip to Madrid could make it even worse “The opening script is working for the opposition and failing the Bengals. That it’s come against a Ravens team without Lamar Jackson and a one-win Titans team makes it all the more discouraging.” A Tuesday flight and a 6-day week: Bengals tweak their Madrid routine for Falcons “Zac Taylor has learned from previous international games and is taking the Cincinnati Bengals to Madrid earlier for their game against the Atlanta Falcons.” Bengals Release Uniform Combination for Week 9 against Atlanta Falcons “This will be the sixth time the Bengals have worn this uniform combination and the first time in 2026. Cincinnati wore the combination three times in 2025. The Bengals introduced orange pants to their rotation ahead of the 2024 season, wearing them a total of nine times.” NFL News: Lions All-Pro LB Jack Campbell remains hospitalized with neck injury A scary scene, but seemingly positive updates have come. NFL trade deadline live updates: Latest news, rumors after Week 8 The in-season trade market has already been active, but with the deadline a week away, we could see even more action. author: Drew Garrison

title: 3 things we learned from the Bengals’ overtime win over the Titans
summary: That’s the second game in a row where the Cincinnati Bengals fell behind 13-0. Only this time, it came against a seemingly outmatched opponent, the Tennessee Titans. This was one that Cincinnati easily could have lost, and that would have been a disaster in a tight AFC North. Instead, it resulted in a thrilling overtime […]
full_text: Photo by Jeff Moreland/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images That’s the second game in a row where the Cincinnati Bengals fell behind 13-0. Only this time, it came against a seemingly outmatched opponent, the Tennessee Titans. This was one that Cincinnati easily could have lost, and that would have been a disaster in a tight AFC North. Instead, it resulted in a thrilling overtime victory that taught us a lot about how the team (especially the defense) has grown. Here’s what we learned. 1. There’s no stopping this offense once it gets going Against the Baltimore Ravens two weeks ago, the Bengals got 35 points in the second half. Then, against Tennessee, the Bengals scored zero points in the first quarter but ended up with 43. Tee Higgins got the ball rolling, and Ja’Marr Chase led the way late. But the engine was, of course, Joe Burrow, who finished 38-of-48 for 462 yards, with five touchdowns, three interceptions, and a rushing touchdown. To put that into perspective, Burrow became the first quarterback since 1951 to get 450 yards, five touchdowns, and a rushing touchdown in the same game. (The fact that the Bengals QB did something that got “Norm Van Brocklin” trending 43 years after his death is saying something.) So when the defense did what it has done so often in recent years (give up long plays and turn borderline starting QBs into superstars), the offense didn’t blink. Burrow and the Bengals just continued to fire downfield, not letting interceptions get in the way, because they know they can outlast anyone. 2. Tee Higgins has gone all the way beast mode It’s not just the 10 catches for 155 yards. It’s the fact that Tee Higgins looks more dominant than he ever has before. He’s manhandling defensive backs, catching in traffic, catching over the top of their heads, and not showboating afterwards. He knows who he is: one of the very best in the game. What’s really noticeable is how easy it seems to be for him. Higgins doesn’t even seem to be going full speed, but he’s getting right by guys because of how confident he is in his route running, hands, and big body, which is always going to win. Higgins now has totaled 148 yards or more in three of seven games. He’s on pace for 104 catches, 1,763 yards, and 10 touchdowns, which has only been done six times before . Forget the WR2 or WR1A talk. Just enjoy the fact that the Bengals have two supremely talented receivers, and neither of them can be contained for an entire game. 3. The defensive line gives them a chance to win games they never used to Burrow pointed out that this Titans game was precisely the kind of contest they’d lost the last three years. And it looked bound to happen again, with Cam Ward driving to get near field goal range with under a minute left. But then Dexter Lawrence got a monstrous sack, grabbing hold of Ward and slamming him to the ground . It was the most dominant sack these eyes have seen since Geno Atkins propelled Deshaun Watson into the air back in 2017. That play brought the Bengals back to life. And it was the kind of play that was missing, especially from the interior of the defensive line, for so many years. It was the result of a beautiful collaboration with Boye Mafe. According to Paul Dehner Jr ., “Lawrence and Mafe gave each other a look” and then we had “Mafe banging into Lawrence’s blocker, helping free the 350-pound wrecking ball to slam Titans quarterback Cam Ward to the ground for a sack.” The two combined for another huge play in the third quarter, when Mafe strip-sacked Ward, and Lawrence picked up the ball and returned it eight yards (he was tragically tripped before he could take it all the way—that would have been an all-time highlight). Those two plays, along with Demetrius Knight Jr. shooting through the gap to tackle Tony Pollard for a safety, showed you precisely the kind of game-changing plays that are possible when you’re consistently winning in the trenches.
author: Dadio Makdook

title: Best available NFL free agent cornerbacks the Bengals could target if DJ Turner misses significant time
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals are 5-2 for the first time since 2021, when they won the AFC Championship Game and went to their third Super Bowl berth in franchise history. Unfortunately, they may have lost cornerback DJ Turner, who suffered an ankle injury in the fourth quarter against the Titans on Sunday. The Bengals came into […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals are 5-2 for the first time since 2021, when they won the AFC Championship Game and went to their third Super Bowl berth in franchise history. Unfortunately, they may have lost cornerback DJ Turner, who suffered an ankle injury in the fourth quarter against the Titans on Sunday. The Bengals came into the 2026 season dangerously thin at the position, opting to focus on safety and the defensive line. If Turner does miss some time, it’s unlikely they’ll be able to just absorb the injury and move forward with the next man up. So, here are some free agent corners the Bengals could bring in for a workout before they head to Spain for their Week 9 game against the Falcons. Jeff Okudah Former Buckeye standout Jeff Okudah could be an interesting option for the Bengals. He was the No. 3 overall pick in the 2020 NFL Draft by the Detroit Lions, but he struggled to live up to that draft position, largely because of injuries and inconsistent play. He most recently played for the Vikings, appearing in six games in 2025 before multiple concussions landed him on IR. The 6-foot-1, 205-pound cornerback has the size and speed to play on the outside, and he could be looking to prove he can put it all together on the field. He’s relatively young, and the Bengals could do worse if they need urgent help. Adoree’ Jackson Jackson could be one of the more realistic options for the Bengals to reinforce the secondary. The former first-round pick spent the ‘25 season with the Eagles, starting 10 games in which he recorded 55 tackles, 11 passes defended, and an interception. Previously a member of the Titans and Giants, Jackson has experience at outside corner and has the athleticism to match up with some of the league’s better wide receivers. Despite being 31, he has a better recent track record than many younger corners still available. Marshon Lattimore The 11th-overall pick out of Ohio State in the 2017 NFL Draft, Lattimore would bring a wealth of experience to the Bengals defense, though there hasn’t been much reported on him since he appeared in 11 games last season in Washington before suffering a torn ACL. Even before the injury, it was clear that the 30-year-old Lattimore was well past his prime, earning a career-low 53.2 PFF grade before the injury. Even so, you won’t find many free agent cornerbacks out there with his experience and talent. Might be time to give him a call and see how his rehab is going. Artie Burns Former Steelers first-round pick Artie Burns is another veteran cornerback available on the market who could draw interest from Cincinnati. The 31-year-old has appeared in 90 career games with 39 starts and has spent time in Pittsburgh, Chicago, and Seattle before he was signed by the Dolphins in 2025. Burns tore his ACL during training camp last summer, which ended his season before it began, which means he hasn’t seen a snap since the 2024 season. He does have experience in the slot and on the outside, but there are younger and more reliable options. Mike Hilton The former Bengals cornerback is still a free agent after spending the 2025 season on the Colts’ practice squad. Hilton would offer the Bengals familiarity, but there’s been little mention of him since last season, and it’s possible the 32-year-old cornerback isn’t considering a return to the NFL. But if he is, the Bengals should give Hilton a call. He may be well past his prime, but there aren’t many guys out there who can come in and have at least a decent feel for the team’s defensive scheme. Jalyn Armour-Davis The former Ravens and Titans corner could be an intriguing option for Cincinnati, especially considering his relatively young age and recent starting experience. The 27-year-old former Alabama standout started 10 games for the Titans in 2025 before suffering a torn Achilles in December. He has excellent size and speed for an outside cornerback, but injuries and inconsistent play have prevented him from establishing himself as a dependable NFL starter. He reportedly is fully healthy and worked out for the Bills and Chargers in October, though he wasn’t signed by either team. Kyu Blu Kelly This could be one of the more intriguing options for the Bengals, especially if Kelly is fully healthy. He’s only 25 years old and enjoyed his most productive season in 2025 for the Raiders. He recorded 40 tackles, defended six passes, and intercepted 3 in 13 games before he suffered a ruptured Patellar tendon in December. Kelly worked out for the Falcons in September, which suggests he has recovered from his injury, but he remains unsigned. Kelly, a former fifth-round pick by the Ravens out of Stanford, could be a solid addition if he’s fully healthy. Trevon Diggs Former Cowboys All-Pro cornerback Trevon Diggs is on the Seahawks’ practice squad and could be signed to the Bengals’ active roster should they go that route. He led the NFL with 11 interceptions in 2021, but struggled with injuries and some inconsistent play in recent years, ultimately leading to his departure from Dallas. At only 28, Diggs still possesses ball skills and the experience to contribute on the outside for the Bengals should they lose Turner for any extended period of time. His aggressive play style sets him up to occasionally give up big plays, and his injury history is a bit of a concern, but he could be looking to prove he still belongs in the league and get a fresh start. Marco Wilson A familiar face could be an option for the Bengals. Wilson is currently on the Panthers’ practice squad and was a member of the Bengals through parts of the ‘24 and ‘25 seasons before he signed with the Dolphins in free agency. Miami released him before the regular season, and he eventually landed on Carolina’s practice squad. The 27-year-old cornerback has 37 career starts in his career, and his familiarity with Cincinnati could make him a potential target if Turner’s injury forces the Bengals to look for outside help. Tre’Davious White Another former All-Pro and another practice squad target, White is currently on the Bills’ practice squad. The 31-year-old veteran was once one of the league’s top corners, leading the league in interceptions in 2019. He has gone through some serious knee and Achilles injuries, but still started 16 games for the Bills in 2025, recording 40 tackles, 10 passes defended, and an interception. He’s not who he once was, but he could be a dependable option for Cincinnati, which also has familiarity with AFC competition in the regular and postseason.
author: Jason Garrison

title: Tee Higgins is on pace for a historic season
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals pulled off an overtime win on Sunday as they knocked off the Tennessee Titans. Led by the offense, the team fought back from three Joe Burrow interceptions to pull off the much-needed win. Now firmly set on the right side of the playoff bubble, as The Athletic gives the team an 84% chance […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals pulled off an overtime win on Sunday as they knocked off the Tennessee Titans. Led by the offense, the team fought back from three Joe Burrow interceptions to pull off the much-needed win. Now firmly set on the right side of the playoff bubble, as The Athletic gives the team an 84% chance to make the playoffs , it was Ja’Mar Chase and Tee Higgins who helped the Bengals pull off Sunday’s win. Higgins continued his impressive season for the team as he is now on a historic pace after posting 10 catches for 155 yards and two touchdowns. That pace? 104 catches for 1763 yards and 10 touchdowns. Would only be done for the 6th time ever in NFL history. Tee Higgins pace: 104-1763-10 For context, that's been done 6 times ever. — Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 1, 2026 People talk a lot about how this Bengals squad has two No. 1 receivers in Chase and Higgins. Now with Tee healthy, we are seeing that sentiment to be true as they both continue to dominate. They have the offense to compete for a Super Bowl. Now all we can hope is that the defense finds a pulse to complement this team’s offense.
author: Ethan DeWitt

title: Bengals News: DJ Turner and Cashius Howell Injury Watch
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals may have some serious issues pop up after their escape from the Tennessee Titans yesterday. Two pretty big names were declared out with injuries fairly quickly after exiting. That doesn’t always mean something, but it could. That is what the watches are for. The biggest name was DJ Turner exiting with an […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals may have some serious issues pop up after their escape from the Tennessee Titans yesterday. Two pretty big names were declared out with injuries fairly quickly after exiting. That doesn’t always mean something, but it could. That is what the watches are for. The biggest name was DJ Turner exiting with an ankle injury after helping on a tackle with Tony Pollard. This hurts for two reasons. The most obvious is that Turner may be one of the best players on the defense, period. He has been super consistent in coverage and has been one of the better tacklers in space. The other reason is that the Bengals have proven their depth at corner has been an issue. The other player is rookie edge rusher Cashius Howell. He may not be the most productive player in the box score, but he gets pressure at a pretty good rate. He has also proven to be a big part of the rotation on the defensive line this season behind Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy. Will these two miss major time, or can they get back out there soon? These are major storylines to follow this week for the Bengals. Bengals News Bengals DE Shemar Stewart Active for Titans After Being a Healthy Scratch vs. Ravens It is good to see that it truly looks like it was an isolated incident that Stewart was inactive last week despite being healthy. However, at some point this guy may need some snaps in games to actually improve. That was supposed to be a reason Al Golden was brought in after Lou Anarumo, right? Postgame Quick Hits | Joe Burrow’s Bengals Grind To Thrilling OT Win: ‘I Looked At Him And Told Him He Was Legendary’ It is rough that it took this kind of effort to defeat the Titans, but any given Sunday a team can come out and really put up the fight of their life. It is frustrating to watch this team try to sleepwalk through lesser teams. The opposing team gets some momentum, and that can carry an entire game if you let it, like it did today. Luckily, the Bengals had just enough to pull out a win at the end of the day. ‘Ask Zac.’ Ja’Marr Chase on how Bengals can avoid slow starts Zac Taylor gets credit for this team’s Super Bowl run and has done some nice things to change the culture in the building. It might be fair to say that this team could benefit from a fresh voice and new ideas. These slow starts have been so consistent that it is hard not to watch and think Taylor and his staff have something to do with it. NFL News Ravens QB Lamar Jackson to undergo surgery on right thumb, will be placed on IR Bengals fans know how bad a season can turn after losing your franchise quarterback to injury. Jackson threw one pass before hitting his hand on a defender’s helmet. It certainly looks like at least one AFC North team will be losing pace with the top of the division now, though. Buccaneers’ Todd Bowles on zero-completion win over Falcons: There’s a ‘first time for everything’ Truly one of the more remarkable things is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers pulling out two wins where they basically called on running back Bucky Irving and the running game to weather the load. The weather had a massive impact on the play calling here, but it certainly isn’t something you will see happen again in a long time. Lions LB Jack Campbell carted off field, evaluated for neck injury at hospital It is always scary to see a player leave in that fashion. It is certainly good that he is receiving the care he needs. Just always helps to remember how violent this sport truly is and that the guys playing it are humans as well. Who Dey! Join Bengals fans on the SB Nation app! title: Browns defensive front problem, and missed tackles, need to improve
summary: With this Browns’ defense, I can tolerate a few big runs being given up if the defense took a chance and was burned. But the 3rd-and-13 resulting in a 51-yard run was a back-breaker, and then the sheer number of missed open field tackles, both against the run and on screen passes, is embarrassing. I […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 01: Jaylen Warren #30 of the Pittsburgh Steelers runs the ball against Jared Verse #8 of the Cleveland Browns during the second quarter at Acrisure Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images With this Browns’ defense, I can tolerate a few big runs being given up if the defense took a chance and was burned. But the 3rd-and-13 resulting in a 51-yard run was a back-breaker, and then the sheer number of missed open field tackles, both against the run and on screen passes, is embarrassing. I don’t expect perfection in the open field, but it’s becoming a consistent problem that is helping extend drives. I’ve also seen various stats out there, indicating the Browns missed between 14 to 16 tackles on the day, which sounds about right from the eye test. Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on defense for the Cleveland Browns ’ Week 8 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Defensive Line Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats DL Mason Graham 44 75% 3 tackles (3 combined). 3 TFL. DL Jared Verse 41 69% 1 assist (1 combined). 1 QH. DL Isaiah McGuire 37 63% 2 assists (2 combined). DL Mike Hall 28 47% 2 tackles, 2 assists (4 combined). DL Maliek Collins 26 44% 2 tackles, 2 assists (4 combined). 1 TFL. DL Sam Williams 22 37% 2 assists (2 combined). DL Adin Huntington 22 37% 1 tackle, 1 assist (2 combined). 1 sack, 1 TFL, 1 QH. DL Derek Barnett 18 31% No stats registered. Teams are starting to expose the Browns’ defensive interior, which has proven to be threatening when teams have to pass, but has been susceptible to runs like this (see below). And then, the second- and third-level haven’t been making tackles in open space to limit the damage a bit more. The Browns allowed four 15+ Yard Runs (one 50+ yarder) in the 1st Half… Three of the four (see below) happened straight between the Defensive Tackles largely because of their very wide alignment… Steelers took advantage. #HereWeGo #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/Gct81sch7D — Max Loeb (@loebsleads) November 2, 2026 While Todd Monken noted that they will have to make an adjustment, it is a concern when you factor in the personnel Cleveland has. However, it also seems like a bit of a scheme issue too, because the intent of the linemen seem clear in trying to rush up the field. I thought the Browns have played smarter at times this season by letting their talented secondary and cover corners make a play, instead of trying to force a big play via a rush up front. Mike Hall returned this week and was one of the team’s top-graded defenders, ranking third by PFF, with a grade of 72.2. However, tackling grades were poor for much of the team, including Hall, Jared Verse , Adin Huntington . In these loses, the frustration from the fan base continues to build toward Verse, who barely makes a visible impact on the game. The biggest story with him in this game was getting dumped on his head after talking in the media about Pittsburgh being dirty. Maliek Collins left the game for a bit with an elbow injury. Linebacker Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats LB Carson Schwesinger 59 100% 4 tackles, 6 assists (10 combined). LB Quincy Williams 58 98% 2 tackles, 3 assists (5 combined). 1 TFL, 1 pass defended, 1 FF. LB Easton Mascarenas-Arnold 2 3% No stats registered. LB Winston Reid 1 2% No stats registered. This wasn’t the finest day at the office for Carson Schwesinger . Although he had 10 tackles, he received a grade of 30.5 from PFF, grading poorly in run defense, tackling, pass rush, and coverage. He appeared to be the man responsible on both of Darnell Washington’s wheel routes that were successful for big gains. He denies that his ankle injury isn’t holding him back, but you know that injuries like that can certainly be a factor. Quincy Williams was back atop the PFF rankings with a grade of 90.0 and a solid run defense grade, for what it’s worth. Cornerback Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats CB Denzel Ward 58 98% 1 tackle, 1 assist (2 combined). 1 INT, 2 passes defended. CB Tyson Campbell 45 76% 1 tackle, 4 assists (5 combined). 1 pass defended, 1 FF. CB Myles Harden 27 46% 2 tackles, 1 assist (3 combined). CB Mekhi Blackmon 13 22% 1 assist (1 combined). Denzel Ward had a fortunate interception, with a PFF coverage grade of 90.1 on the day. His overall grade was only 63.5, though, as he also suffered with tackling and run defense. Tyson Campbell was the Browns’ top-graded defender by PFF, grading out to a 90.8, with some impressive work against DK Metcalf . Campbell left at the end of the first half with an injury, but returned. It’s not his fault of course, but him being injured forced Cleveland to burn a timeout on that final drive of the first half, which may have been the difference in Pittsburgh getting a touchdown vs. only a field goal try. Safety Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats S Grant Delpit 59 100% 2 tackles, 2 assists (4 combined). 1 TFL. S Ronnie Hickman 56 95% 3 tackles, 4 assists (7 combined). S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren 31 53% 2 tackles, 6 assists (8 combined). S Daniel Thomas 2 3% 1 assist (1 combined). It wasn’t a good day for Grant Delpit either, who graded out to a 26.8 by PFF. It’s not ideal when your two defenders who played the most snaps were by far the worst-graded players. Emmanuel McNeil-Warren played 53% of the snaps this week.
