title: Too many sacks for Deshaun Watson and Browns offense
summary: The Browns’ offense clearly didn’t get it done against the Steelers. Sometimes, you look for the ‘what ifs’ to try to make yourself (as a fan) feel a little better about the loss. Overall, it seemed like Pittsburgh had a better physicality. But I would also look to the Browns being 0-of-3 in the red […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 1: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers and Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns interact after a game at Acrisure Stadium on November 1, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Browns’ offense clearly didn’t get it done against the Steelers. Sometimes, you look for the ‘what ifs’ to try to make yourself (as a fan) feel a little better about the loss. Overall, it seemed like Pittsburgh had a better physicality. But I would also look to the Browns being 0-of-3 in the red zone and 0-of-2 in goal-to-go situations. And of course, generally, you can’t take 8 sacks as a quarterback and expect to move the ball consistently with success after that. Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on offense for the Cleveland Browns ’ Week 8 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Quarterback Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats QB Deshaun Watson 66 94% 27-of-39 (69.2%) for 324 yards. 3 carries, 2 yards (0.7 YPC). 1 fumble lost QB Shedeur Sanders 4 6% 2-of-2 (100%) for 2 yards. It’s hard to imagine someone having the stat line that Deshaun Watson did, and yet the offense only ends up with two field goals. But Cleveland fumbling on the opening two possessions, and also seeing their quarterback sacked eight times, tells a lot more of the story. As does the fact that they were down 27-6 in the fourth quarter, resulting in a heavier mix of passes when it didn’t matter. Watson was the Browns’ lowest-graded player by PFF, grading out to a 47.5. I think it was well-earned, to a degree. While Watson made some OK throws, some of the sacks came down to a lack of decisiveness. We’re also seeing that, against better defensive fronts, Watson is not able to escape for yards, something that has bailed him out at times this year. At least Watson gets to face a much easier defense in the Saints next week. Running Back Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats RB Dylan Sampson 39 56% 1 carry, 7 yards (7.0 YPC). 6 catches, 62 yards (8 targets). RB Quinshon Judkins 27 39% 11 carries, 25 yards (2.3 YPC). 2 catches, 24 yards (2 targets). FB Michael Burton 8 11% No stats registered. RB Jaleen McLaughlin 2 3% No stats registered. With Cleveland falling behind early, the ground game couldn’t become the factor that Todd Monken wanted it to be. They tried loading up with a full house formation on 3rd-and-1 on their opening first half drive, telling Pittsburgh, “we think we can get a yard when you know it’s coming.” Nope, it was killed by the defense. The same thing happened on first down from the 2 yard line, Quinshon Judkins stood no chance and was dropped for a loss of 3 yards. Dylan Sampson was one of the Browns’ higher-graded offensive players, grading out to a 67.4. He had 6 catches, although again, much of that came in garbage time. Wide Receiver Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats WR Denzel Boston 58 83% 6 catches, 37 yards (11 targets). WR KC Concepcion 58 83% 3 catches, 37 yards (4 targets). WR Jerry Jeudy 42 60% 0 catches (1 target). WR Malachi Corley 13 19% No stats registered. WR Tylan Wallace 10 14% 1 catch, 3 yards (1 target). WR Isaiah Bond 8 11% No stats registered. Denzel Boston nearly made a great, one-handed touchdown grab, but couldn’t get his second foot down in bounds. I like what someone said before — it’s not the best when Malachi Corley is getting 20% of the snaps, and yet never even gets targeted. It shouldn’t even be an element of surprise thing, but there has to be some form of ‘threat’ that maybe it’s going to be a pass play or something when he’s in the game. KC Concepcion only had 4 targets and 0 touches on the ground, a week after he had career highs. Jerry Jeudy also did not have a catch. Tight End Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats TE Harold Fannin 60 86% 10 catches, 154 yards (12 targets). 1 fumble lost. TE Blake Whiteheart 25 36% 1 catch, 9 yards (1 target). It was a career day for Harold Fannin , who had 10 catches for 154 yards. He did lose a fumble for the second week in a row, but remains a huge threat in the passing game. Fannin was the Browns’ highest-graded player by PFF, grading out to a 76.4. Offensive Line Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats OL Spencer Fano 70 100% OL Elgton Jenkins 70 100% OL Austin Barber 70 100% OL Zion Johnson 70 100% OL Tytus Howard 70 100% With how many sacks the Steelers had, let’s turn to PFF to see how the unit did. RT Tytus Howard was the second-highest graded player on offense, grading to a 75.4. The third-highest? LG Zion Johnson with a 68.0. Fifth-highest? RG Austin Barber with a 65.4. C Elgton Jenkins and LT Spencer Fano did not fare the best, but it wasn’t necessarily catastrophic. Fano was probably the big disappointment on the day. But otherwise, it was what I’d call a mediocre day for the offensive line. They were responsible for some mistakes, but better quarterback play still could’ve made this a different ballgame.

full_text: (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns lost on Sunday. To the Steelers. In Pittsburgh. Once again. It was frustrating, irritating, maddening, and all-around horrible. And that was just on the first two offensive series of the game! The loss left the Browns picking up the pieces after yet another defeat to the Steelers in a game where it looked like Cleveland was playing its first football game ever. Where the team goes from here is entirely up to them. The Browns are still 5-3 and have two games that are winnable if they play well before they hit the bye week. So the Pittsburgh loss does not have to be the defining moment of the season, unless the Browns dwell on it too much and one loss turns into two, which turns into three, and then everyone spends the bye week yelling about the backup quarterback. At that point, the season will be completely lost. Again, it doesn’t have to play out that way. Teams lose games every week and bounce back. But until they show they can do it, it is fair to worry that the Browns may be on the brink of seeing the season slip away. OK, let’s get rolling with today’s edition of the Daily Dawg Chow. title: Browns vs. Saints odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup
summary: The Cleveland Browns opened as 3-point road underdogs against the New Orleans Saints ahead of their Week 9 match-up, according to FanDuel Sportsbook. The over/under on the game is 43.5. The Browns (5-3) are coming off of a 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. It was an unfortunate flashback to the first game of the […]
full_text: TOPSHOT - New Orleans Saints supporters cheer prior to the NFL Paris Game, an American football match between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the New Orleans Saints at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, near Paris on October 25, 2026, the first-ever regular-season NFL game to be played in France. (Photo by Franck FIFE / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images The Cleveland Browns opened as 3-point road underdogs against the New Orleans Saints ahead of their Week 9 match-up, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The over/under on the game is 43.5. The Browns (5-3) are coming off of a 27-6 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers . It was an unfortunate flashback to the first game of the season, when the Browns’ defense looked terrible, and the offense couldn’t put things together. Cleveland’s run defense suffered, and the offense set a bad tone early with fumbling the ball on the opening two possessions. The Browns were able to move the ball well at times, but ultimately couldn’t finish drives, and now they’ve lost the lead in the AFC North. They’ve regrouped before, and they need to do so again to wrap up this road stretch. The Saints (2-5) are coming off of a bye week. Prior to that, they lost a tight 16-10 game to the Steelers in Paris. The Saints have not been able to get their running game going this season, often having to rely on the passing game. Defensively, New Orleans is among the worst in the NFL, unable to stop the run or pass effectively. It certainly lines up to be a winnable game for Cleveland, even though the Saints are favorites. The Browns are 3-0 at home, but 2-3 on the road. The Saints are 0-3 in their home stadium. The over/under for the game is 43.5. What odds would you take if you were placing a bet? title: 2027 Browns mock draft: 3 rounds, 4 picks after Week 8’s loss
summary: If you are a fan who is not interested in the upcoming NFL draft until the Cleveland Browns are eliminated from playoff contention, this three-round Browns mock draft will not be for you. Hopefully the rest of DBN can serve your needs properly. For many, including this writer, the NFL draft is one piece of […]
full_text: If you are a fan who is not interested in the upcoming NFL draft until the Cleveland Browns are eliminated from playoff contention, this three-round Browns mock draft will not be for you. Hopefully the rest of DBN can serve your needs properly. For many, including this writer, the NFL draft is one piece of the whole enchilada that is following our Cleveland football team. If the Browns were undefeated, many of us would still take a quick glance at the upcoming draft, wondering what else they could add to the team. With the tough loss in Week 8 to the Pittsburgh Steelers and having an extra first-round pick , today we take a little bit longer than a glance at the future. Using Pro Football Network’s Mock Draft Simulator , Cleveland adds four prospects at positions of value. Full disclosure, my draft analysis in detail doesn’t really start until the college football season is over; today’s mock is a reflection of where PFN has players ranked and my assessment of the team’s needs. The draft order is based on the current standings in the NFL: 3-Round Browns Mock Draft First Round DE Yhonzae Pierre, Alabama Cleveland’s pass rush needs more, and Pierre can be a big part of that. After eight sacks last season, the third-year player has 3.5 this year to go along with three passes defended, one forced fumble, one INT, and one defensive touchdown. With no quarterbacks available at pick 16, filling the Browns biggest need made the most sense. TE Jamari Johnson, Oregon The next athlete coming from Oregon, Kenyon Sadiq’s backup last year, Johnson is on his way to surpassing his reception, yardage, and touchdown totals easily this season. At 6’5”, Johnson will give HC Todd Monken another weapon to work with in a more versatile offensive system. Second Round QB Dante Moore, Oregon A player who will have a lot of questions heading into the upcoming draft, Moore was likely the second overall pick in 2026 and someone GM Andrew Berry really liked if he had come out. Instead, a horrible late hit and the resulting head injury have him available in the middle of the second round, later than most expect he will fall if he’s healthy. A lot of ifs with Moore, but a swing that makes sense given how the draft fell. Third Round OG Evan Tengesdahl, Cincinnati Drafting for talent over specific need, Tengesdahl is a guard for sure, which could push Austin Barber out to tackle in the future. The value at this point in the mock draft simulation was in the middle of both lines, including a couple of defensive tackle options, but believing in Barber’s ability to move outside provided a bit more confidence in taking Tengesdahl here. title: Browns Week 9 opponent makes coaching change, could impact CLE’s weakness
summary: As the Cleveland Browns dig out from the rubble that was their Week 8 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, which dropped them out of the AFC playoff race and put more focus on the NFL draft order, the team must turn their attention to the future. The NFL trade deadline is just over a week […]
full_text: As the Cleveland Browns dig out from the rubble that was their Week 8 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, which dropped them out of the AFC playoff race and put more focus on the NFL draft order, the team must turn their attention to the future. The NFL trade deadline is just over a week away, with the New Orleans Saints next up on the Browns schedule in Week 9. The Saints are coming off a bye week, following their Week 7 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris, France. New Orleans is just 2-5 this year, after an encouraging start to the season with a close loss to the Detroit Lions and a victory over the Baltimore Ravens. The Saints run game has been among the worst in the NFL, averaging just 86.0 yards per game with a 3.5 yards per carry average. The Browns’ run defense has been a huge weakness for the team, especially versus the Steelers, which makes New Orleans’ decision to change run game coaches that much more interesting: Coming off the bye, the #Saints made a significant change, moving on from run game coordinator T. J. Paganetti, sources say. Run-game issues have plagued the team this year. pic.twitter.com/yBPAkbzG9c — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 2, 2026 Paganetti’s run game last year was also among the worst in the NFL, but the Saints averaged 94.3 yards per game on the ground in 2025, with a strong drop-off this season. Paganetti was brought over with HC Kellen Moore after their shared time with the Philadelphia Eagles. No news on who will take over New Orleans’ run game or why it took the entire bye week for the decision to be made, but Cleveland could see some new wrinkles from the Saints’ rushing attack in Week 9. full_text: Thankfully for Cleveland Browns fans, the clear and present has been the focus of much of the 2026 NFL season. HC Todd Monken and company have won enough games to allow the fanbase to focus on each week instead of already turning most of their attention to the 2027 NFL draft. Due to the extra first-round pick from the Los Angeles Rams and that team’s early injuries and struggles, draft positioning has still been important . Week 8 could have been a turning point for a lot of things circling the Browns: Cleveland was destroyed by the Pittsburgh Steelers , and the Rams dominated the Los Angeles Chargers . Those two results have turned what was a large gap between a LA Top 10 pick and a Browns late-20s pick into a much closer set of selections for Cleveland in the first round of the 2027 NFL draft. Before Monday Night Football , which could change the picks slightly, the Rams are set to select 16th overall, with Cleveland’s own pick coming two slots later, 18th. 2027 NFL draft order Los Angeles Chargers Tennessee Titans Miami Dolphins Indianapolis Colts – Goes to the New York Jets Philadelphia Eagles New York Jets Houston Texans New Orleans Saints Washington Commanders Dallas Cowboys – Goes to the New York Jets Tampa Bay Buccaneers Arizona Cardinals Atlanta Falcons Las Vegas Raiders Baltimore Ravens Los Angeles Rams – Goes to the Cleveland Browns Seattle Seahawks (Play on MNF) Cleveland Browns Carolina Panthers Green Bay Packers – Goes to the Dallas Cowboys New England Patriots New York Giants Cincinnati Bengals Kansas City Chiefs Jacksonville Jaguars Detroit Lions Chicago Bears (Play on MNF) – Goes to the Tennessee Titans Pittsburgh Steelers Denver Broncos Minnesota Vikings San Francisco 49ers Buffalo Bills Where do you think the Browns and Rams picks will end up when the season is over? title: AFC playoff picture, AFC North standings: Browns fall out after Week 8 due to tiebreaker
summary: In the span of one day, the Cleveland Browns went from atop the AFC North and the third seed in the AFC playoff race to third place in the division and out of the AFC playoff picture. A fast fall in a tight division and conference due to a devastating loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers […]
full_text: In the span of one day, the Cleveland Browns went from atop the AFC North and the third seed in the AFC playoff race to third place in the division and out of the AFC playoff picture. A fast fall in a tight division and conference due to a devastating loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8 . The AFC North has all four teams with .500 or better records , with the Baltimore Ravens, expected to be without QB Lamar Jackson for most of the rest of the season , sitting in the basement at 4-4: AFC North Standings Pittsburgh Steelers: 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals: 5-2 Cleveland Browns : 5-3 Baltimore Ravens: 4-4 The AFC as a whole is also quite interesting, with three teams having six wins and five having five victories. Three of the five teams with five victories have already had their bye week, pushing them ahead of the Browns and New England Patriots. New England (5-1) has the conference record tiebreaker over Cleveland (3-3) at this point, taking the final playoff spot currently after Week 8: AFC Playoff Standings Buffalo Bills (6-1) Denver Broncos (6-2, 3-1 AFC) Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2, 3-2 AFC) Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) Kansas City Chiefs (5-2, 5-1 AFC) Cincinnati Bengals (5-2, 4-2 AFC) New England Patriots (5-3, 5-1 AFC) Cleveland Browns (5-3, 3-3 AFC) Las Vegas Raiders (4-4, 3-3 AFC) Baltimore Ravens (4-4, 2-3 AFC) Houston Texans (2-5) New York Jets (2-6, 2-3 AFC) Indianapolis Colts (2-6, 1-5 AFC) Miami Dolphins (1-6) Tennessee Titans (1-7) Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) How are you feeling about the Browns AFC North and AFC playoff chances after Week 8? title: Week 8 proves Browns aren’t there yet, but CLE split the season series with the Steelers
summary: “You win some, you lose some, but you live. You live to fight another day.” I use this quote specifically because it applies to the Cleveland Browns. Yes, the Browns got bullied by the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8. Head coach Todd Monken said the team earned the loss (they did); however, it isn’t the […]
full_text: “You win some, you lose some, but you live. You live to fight another day.” Willie Jones (also known as Mr Jones from the movie Friday) I use this quote specifically because it applies to the Cleveland Browns. Yes, the Browns got bullied by the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8. Head coach Todd Monken said the team earned the loss (they did); however, it isn’t the end of the world. 6-2 and alone in the AFC North would’ve been nice, but you would settle for 5-3 in a year in which no one thought the team would be ahead of schedule. 1st Down: Young teams are often the most inconsistent teams As everyone knows, the Browns have one of the youngest teams in the NFL. The difference is clear when you pay close attention. Going into Pittsburgh and winning was going to be a tough task, but Cleveland didn’t make things easier for themselves at all. The Steelers essentially did what the Browns did to them when the two teams played on Thursday night this season. Granted, the score wasn’t as close this time around, but Cleveland looked like the young team that they are. It’s not necessarily a bad thing, but it’s just the reality of the situation. As far as the game goes, not much went right for the Browns. Most, if not all, of Cleveland’s players did their best to downplay the history of the team not winning in Pittsburgh, only to extend their losing streak and miss out on an opportunity to sweep the Steelers in a season series. 2nd Down: Jared Verse is doing more harm than actual good Leading up to the game, Browns defensive end Jared Verse had some choice comments about the Steelers going back to their last meeting. Some fans liked it (because why not), and others like myself weren’t necessarily annoyed by it but just don’t understand why Verse continues to run his mouth despite not having a sack this season. #Browns Jared Verse on the Steelers and Cam Heyward’s comments this week: pic.twitter.com/c3n2nqNmJz — Ashley Bastock (@AshleyBastock42) October 29, 2026 It’s obvious that the Steelers were aware of it, and judging by the postgame comments by many Steelers players, they don’t respect Verse at all, and honestly they shouldn’t. Jaquan Brisker on Jared Verse’s trash talk earlier in the week prior to the Steelers topping the Browns 27-6 “He should have kept his mouth shut. All that talk, and then to come out with 0 tackles, that’s bad.” “He’s gotta look at himself in the mirror and get better.” pic.twitter.com/tp6WH6Iw9O — Ashley Wenskoski (@AshleyWenskTV) November 1, 2026 Do I understand why Verse is trash-talking? Yes, he’s trying to be apart of the “culture changing” but I would rather have you back up your talk and be productive than talk and be a liability. It’s fair to question if the team picks up his option if the production doesn’t get better but sometimes it’s best to not say anything. 3rd Down: Defense needs to get healthy, OL has bad outing The Browns don’t have their bye week for a few weeks, but the defense has to get healthy to some degree. If you have played any iteration of EA Sports College Football video game, you are likely aware of the Wear and Tear feature. It appears some of Cleveland’s defensive players are in the red area. Defensive tackle Mason Graham isn’t quite 100%, and linebacker Carson Schwesinger hasn’t been healthy all year. The run defense was an issue last week, and it was an issue on Sunday. Defending against trap runs has been an issue for a while, but by the time adjustments were made, the game was already out of reach. After having a stout outing last week, the Browns offensive line had a bad outing. I don’t think the Steelers defensive line is that dangerous, but the Browns offensive line struggled throughout the day. Quarterback Deshaun Watson didn’t help due to him holding the ball for too long trying to extend plays, but the entire offensive line had their fair share of struggles. 4th Down: Browns aren’t a good team… yet but they aren’t a bad team The Cleveland Browns are 5-3. Yet, the conversation will be whether this team is as good as their record may indicate. I’m not sure the Browns are a good football team, guys. — Danny Cunningham (@RealDCunningham) November 1, 2026 Are the Browns a great football team? No, at least not at this moment. Let’s put things in perspective. The team is 5-3 Of the 5 wins this team has, they weren’t favored in 4 (they were favored against the Titans) The team is ahead of schedule Considering how most, if not all, analysts predicted that this team would be one of the worst teams in the league before the season started, the fact that they are 5-3 is impressive. Yes, the team has flaws, but this team is also one of the youngest teams in the league. Look at the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers are winless and have looked objectively awful. You think Los Angeles would like to be in Cleveland’s position right now? Albeit the expectations might be different, the point remains. Yes, Week 8 was terrible, but I don’t believe that should change your view on this team. It could be a lot worse. Extra Points The Browns are more likely to trade for an edge rusher before the deadline, from what I was told (the YaYa Diaby smoke has some traction) Cleveland’s taunting penalties felt as if they were instigated by the Steelers. Tight end Harold Fannin had a career day. Watson had another 300-yard game, but most of the yardage came from YAC or underneath route concepts The Pittsburgh Steelers are 6-2, but I am not moved; I am just waiting for the shoe to drop. A day later, what are your thoughts on the Browns’ Sunday big loss to the Steelers? Join the conversation! title: Browns, Steelers winners and losers: Cleveland was never in the game
summary: The Cleveland Browns versus the Pittsburgh Steelers in the rubber match had plenty of incentive. Both clubs were tied for the lead in the AFC North Division with identical 5-2-0 records. The winner would sit on top of the division on their own. The Browns won the first game 27-24 in Week 4, which was […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns versus the Pittsburgh Steelers in the rubber match had plenty of incentive. Both clubs were tied for the lead in the AFC North Division with identical 5-2-0 records. The winner would sit on top of the division on their own. The Browns won the first game 27-24 in Week 4, which was played in Cleveland. But the Browns are 0-10 playing regular season games in Pittsburgh in the past decade. That says quite a bit. RELATED: STEELERS VS. BROWNS RECAP Pittsburgh came into this game with the league’s #7 run defense. It just so happens that the Browns found their running game last weekend against the Tennessee Titans, so this would become one of the game’s hot topics. In the end, Cleveland was dominated by the Steelers and lost 27-6. So, who played well for the Browns? Who didn’t? BROWNIES – Winners TE Harold Fannin – While Cleveland’s offense could not sustain any drives, Fannin was a single shining star for all four quarters. Early in the second quarter, the Browns were faced with a third-and-six down 10-3. Fannin snagged a 12-yard pass to give the Browns a new set of downs. Steelers bring pressure on 3rd down but Watson finds Harold Fannin over the top for a big gain. Browns down inside the Steelers' five . — Nick Farabaugh (@FarabaughFB) November 1, 2026 On the very next play, he secured a short pass, then rumbled for 22 yards to the Steelers’ 44. As the third quarter was winding down, QB Deshaun Watson found Fannin for a 15-yard gain. Fannin gained 37 yards on the second play of Quarter 4 before being tackled at Pittsburgh’s 39-yard line. With 6:51 remaining, Watson connected with Fannin for 27 yards and, two plays later, for another 10 yards. 12 targets, 10 receptions for 154 yards with a 15.4 yards-per-catch average. on the board thanks to Andre 🙂‍↕️ @meijer | #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/CavYG1jgPv — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 1, 2026 Kickers – Punter Corey Bojorquez had four kicks for 199 yards and a 49.8 average, including one for 58 yards. K Andre Szmyt nailed both field goal attempts. S Ronnie Hickman and S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren – Hickman had a fine game. Midway in the first quarter, he tracked down RB Rico Dowdle from behind after a nine-yard gain. When Freiermuth was open for 28 yards in the second quarter, it was Hickman who took him down instead of the player whose duty it was to cover him. Both players ganged up on Washington after a 12-yard gain early in the fourth quarter. On kickoff coverage, McNeil-Warren had two tackles. He read the run and then nailed Dowdle for a two-yard gain in the third quarter. He tackled Warren, forced a fumble, and then recovered the loose ball that was then overturned. He blitzed when Pittsburgh had the ball at their own five and was able to stop Warren after just two yards. For the game, Hickman had seven total tackles while McNeil-Warren had nine. FROWNIES – Losers The play that lost the game – Cleveland had mounted an 44-yard drive that culminated in a 49-yard Szmyt field goal to cut Pittsburgh’s lead to 13-6. 45 seconds remained before halftime. Pittsburgh QB Aaron Rodgers has made a career out of getting a lot with so little. RB Jalen Warren gashed up the middle for 23 yards. A two-yard completion. Next, 28 yards to a wide-open TE Pat Freiermuth for 28 yards, which placed the ball in field goal range. Rodgers, not wanting to go into the locker room with three points, tossed a short pass to WR Germie Bernard for 15 yards with sloppy coverage by DB Denzel Ward to the one-yard line with five seconds remaining. This one play was the difference going into the locker room, 16-6, and made a defensive stand, or the ensuing touchdown run, which put Cleveland down 20-6. Absolutely the dagger going into the locker room. Penalties – Ahhhh!!!! Every game, the penalties are drive killers. Seven were called in the first half, with five accepted. Nine total for the game for 85 yards. And nothing changes. Seven were called on the offensive line, including two holding calls on rookie OT Spencer Fano. Run defense up the middle – The Steelers rarely ran to the corners. Why? Because they gashed the Browns over and over and over and over up the gut. All day long, MLB Carson Schwesinger was blocked out or moved to the side. All of the defensive tackles for Cleveland struggled to maintain gaps, and the Steelers offensive line just moved bodies anywhere they decided. DT Mason Graham had one tackle for loss, but with 1:56 left. 5️⃣1️⃣ YARDS 🚂 @Nunless2 pic.twitter.com/3d2lNSEUfv — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 1, 2026 DT Mike Hall got a one-yard stop on RB Rico Dowdle in the second half, and not much in the other three quarters. In the second quarter, DT Maliek Collins got RB Warren for minus two, then he celebrated like that isn’t his job on all of the other downs. Pittsburgh had 200 yards on the ground, with most of that on the legs of Warren, who gashed the middle of the Browns’ defense for 143 rushing yards. When safeties are being called on to make the bulk of tackles, there is a huge problem. No pass rush – Rodgers sat back in the pocket all day and got to go through most of his progressions. Where was the pressure? DT Adin Huntington got the only sack of the day, as Cleveland had just two QB hits. Otherwise, nobody got into the face of Rodgers. DE Jared Verse got a QB hit! Yoohoo! Missed tackles – Denzel Ward, Carson Schwesinger, Tyson Campbell, Grant Delpit, Mike Hall, Quincy Williams. These were just the most obvious. Run game – The Steelers came into this game ranked #7 against the run. So, what happened? The Browns tried to run the ball for 34 total yards. All game long, Pittsburgh had seven in the box and, on occasion, eight. Offensive line’s new nickname: Jailbreak – From the opening drive, the Steelers played an all-out pass rush. In the end, there were eight sacks. But in fairness to Deshaun Watson, his escape routes from the pocket, as it was beginning to implode, were not good. On three of those sacks, he simply ran into a Pittsburgh defender trying to escape. Which offensive linemen, you ask? Yes. Offense first half – With 6:34 left in the first quarter, the Browns had lost two turnovers, had four accepted penalties called, allowed three sacks, and had minus one yard. Their first first down was at the 12:40 mark of the second quarter. At halftime, eight rushing yards. Red Zone, third-down efficiency, fourth downs – The Browns got into the Red Zone three times all game, and went 0-3. Meanwhile, Pittsburgh was 3-5. Cleveland was 4-13 on third downs versus 4-11 for the Steelers. The Browns went for it twice on fourth down and did not convert either. All three categories for the Browns provide a glimpse into why the failures occurred. Milk Bones – There is a fine line between fishing and just standing on the shore like an idiot Punch it in @ricodowdle 😤 pic.twitter.com/HUqIExGBY7 — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 1, 2026 CB Denzel Ward – On Pittsburgh’s second possession in the first quarter, they drove down to Cleveland’s nine-yard line. On a second-and-one, Dowdle took it up the middle and met Ward, who had read the play. Ward hit him high at the eight-yard line, rode Dowdle for three yards, and then just let go. On the short pass to Bernard for 15 yards right before the half, Ward had no clue where Bernard was and left him wide open. Ward did secure the interception, but his man, WR D.K. Metcalf, was open and then bobbled the catch, which ultimately landed in Ward’s lap. Two total tackles with two batted passes. TE coverage – The Steelers’ tight ends didn’t have a banner day, but were a very important aspect of their offense and had several long gains. BIG MAN ON THE MOVE 😤 @_Dwfootball11 pic.twitter.com/7QrUrLG0uf — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 1, 2026 Most notable was the 58-yard catch-and-run by Darnell Washington, who had beaten Schwesinger badly from the get-go. He caught the pass at the Browns’ 45-yard line with a seven-yard lead on Schwesinger, and…

title: Cowboys news: Defense banged up physically after collapse to Cardinals
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are licking their wounds after another bad loss at home to the Arizona Cardinals, and are starting the week of preparation for the Indianapolis Colts with a slew of injuries to monitor. The team’s state of play in the first half of the season has produced a losing record that’s going to […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are licking their wounds after another bad loss at home to the Arizona Cardinals, and are starting the week of preparation for the Indianapolis Colts with a slew of injuries to monitor. The team’s state of play in the first half of the season has produced a losing record that’s going to be even harder to climb back from now. Another theme coming out of the Cardinals loss is that perfectly healthy players, mainly George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb, didn’t see the field at critical moments. Cowboys OLB Malachi Lawrence could miss multiple weeks with ankle injury – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com It’s been a quiet few weeks for the Cowboys second first-round pick, and now Malachi Lawrence may be shelved for a few weeks ahead. On Tuesday, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer announced that rookie OLB Malachi Lawrence suffered an ankle injury against the Cardinals and could miss multiple weeks. “Malachi has [an injury] that might be a little bit longer…” Schottenheimer said. “Looks like it could be a few weeks. So just keep doing some more testing, see how he moves around, but a little different than the other guys.” Cowboys DBs Caleb Downs, P.J. Locke in concussion protocol – Charean Williams, Pro Football Talk The Cowboys still can’t defend big plays, and now have two safeties in concussion protocol to start the week. Coach Brian Schottenheimer said defensive back Caleb Downs and safety P.J. Locke are both in concussion protocol. Downs, a first-round rookie, has played 509 defensive snaps — 92 percent — and 45 on special teams. He has totaled 52 tackles, a sack, a pass defensed and two forced fumbles. Locke just returned from injured reserve, missing five games with a foot injury. He returned to practice Oct. 23. The Dallas Cowboys are taking a stance that is very hard to understand ahead of the NFL’s trade deadline – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The Cowboys are still open to adding players under Brian Schottenheimer, despite the stunning lack of consistency defining his tenure right now. The Cowboys are 25 games into the Brian Schottenheimer era, and they have a losing record in that stretch. Part of the reason is they’ve strung together a winning streak only once in those 25 games, when they won three in a row last November. Other than that, they haven’t been able to stack wins. Schottenheimer said it himself earlier this season: good teams stack wins. He said that heading into the Tampa Bay Buccaneers game. Since then, the Cowboys have failed to do it, even with a favorable stretch. Download the SB Nation app today! Fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities and conversations Faster commenting and posting experience! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . NFL Week 8 Sunday aftermath: Ravens’ season on the brink; can Vikings trust Kyler Murray? – Kevin Patra, NFL.com It is still really hard to fathom how the Cowboys managed to give Sunday’s game away. But let’s be real: This was an epic collapse, for which Dallas should be crushed. On Sunday, a confluence of ineptitude caused Dallas to collapse at home to drop to 3-5 on the season. The defense became a sieve in the fourth quarter and couldn’t tackle. I understand that the Cowboys had some injuries, but letting Allgeier look like Jim Brown is not a product of a few missing players. The secondary inexplicably got burned late when all the Cowboys needed to do was keep everything in front of them. Frankly, Arizona could have scored quicker in the fourth quarter if not for a few misses. The defensive breakdowns continue to perplex Dallas this season. 5 reasons why the Cowboys lost to Cardinals – LP Cruz, Blogging The Boys The Cardinals played two different QBs and RBs and racked up yards at will against the Cowboys, while the home team couldn’t execute their own offense. For the second straight week, George Pickens was largely an afterthought. Ten targets over the last two weeks simply isn’t enough for a player with his skill set. Pickens finished with two catches for 48 yards, including a 37-yard reception, and appeared to have a 59-yard touchdown wiped off the board by a holding penalty. Even after proving he could challenge Arizona vertically, Dallas never made a concerted effort to get him more involved. George Pickens’ dwindling snap count among Cowboys’ numerous Week 8 questions – Todd Brock, The Cowboys Wire The front seven has been a work in progress in the three games since Mike Pettine was added to the coaching staff. Things are getting interesting at linebacker. Shemar James played almost every snap, marking his third straight week with over three-quarters of the defense’s reps. Rookie Jaishawn Barham has taken the biggest hit as a result of James’s ascension; his action on just 20% of the defensive snaps was easily his lowest as a Cowboy (and less than even Von Miller’s intentionally spotty workload). James Houston also got a bump in usage; his 20 snaps with the defense were his most of 2026.

title: 5 reasons why the Cowboys lost to Cardinals
summary: There’s something clearly wrong with the Dallas Cowboys. For as much talent as they have, and yes, that phrase has been used so often over the last decade that it’s become cliché, it still rings true. The Cowboys’ front office made a concerted effort to field a better defense, and some of those additions didn’t […]
full_text: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images There’s something clearly wrong with the Dallas Cowboys. For as much talent as they have, and yes, that phrase has been used so often over the last decade that it’s become cliché, it still rings true. The Cowboys’ front office made a concerted effort to field a better defense, and some of those additions didn’t come cheap. Yet the results continue to be underwhelming. The squandered opportunity against the Arizona Cardinals is simply the latest chapter in what has become a disappointing 2026 season. The Cowboys had every opportunity to win this game and failed to capitalize. So where did things go wrong? Here are five reasons the Cowboys lost. Javonte Williams never got going After last week’s performance in Philadelphia, it felt like Javonte Williams and the run game might be turning a corner. Williams set a career high in rushing yards, and there was reason to believe Dallas could ride that momentum into this week’s matchup. That never happened. Williams was given very little room to operate behind the offensive line, and whenever Dallas needed a tough yard, Arizona seemed to have an answer. He was stopped short on a critical fourth-down attempt in the first quarter on Dallas’ side of the field. Later, he was stuffed near the goal line in another key situation. Simply put, it wasn’t his day, nor the offensive line’s, who was just as much at fault. Williams finished with 24 carries for 56 yards, averaging just 2.3 yards per carry. While the running game was certainly a factor in the loss, it wasn’t nearly as damaging as some of the other issues that plagued Dallas throughout the afternoon. They couldn’t stop Tyler Allgeier Tyler Allgeier is a solid running back, but the Cowboys made him look like an All-Pro. Allgeier finished with 191 yards from scrimmage after stepping into a larger role due to injuries in Arizona’s backfield. Once Dallas built its lead, it looked as though the Cardinals would struggle to generate offense consistently. Instead, Allgeier took over the game in the second half. His 63-yard touchdown run perfectly encapsulated everything that’s been wrong with Dallas defensively this season. Missed tackles. Poor pursuit angles. Failure to shed blocks. At no point did it feel like the Cowboys were playing with the urgency necessary to stop him. He followed that up with another explosive run of 52 yards, highlighted by Arizona center Hjalte Froholdt flattening Caleb Downs twice on the same play. More than anything, though, this speaks to a larger issue. The Cowboys simply do not tackle well. They haven’t all season, and they continue to allow explosive plays because of it. Allgeier’s touchdown reception was another example. Multiple defenders converged on him near the goal line, but instead of wrapping up and finishing the play, they allowed him to extend the football across the plane.It’s not that Allgeier is some unstoppable force. It’s that Arizona played with a level of effort and physicality that Dallas failed to match. Mishandling the Double Dip No matter what happens, it’s almost always preferable to receive the second-half kickoff. Whether you’re playing from ahead or behind, having the first possession after halftime gives you a chance to either extend your lead or cut into a deficit. Dallas found themselves in an ideal situation entering halftime. The Cowboys led 14-3 and had multiple opportunities to completely take control of the game if only they hadn’t squandered them. The first opportunity came with just over a minute remaining in the second quarter. Dallas got the ball looking to add points before the break, but the drive quickly went nowhere after a Dak Prescott sack helped force a three-and-out. Then came a second chance. After forcing a fumble, the Cowboys got the ball back with another opportunity to put points on the board before halftime. Unfortunately, Brandon Aubrey missed the field goal attempt, and Dallas headed into the locker room still leading by just 11. The missed opportunities didn’t stop there. Dallas opened the second half with the football and put together an impressive drive that marched deep into Cardinals territory while taking more than eight minutes off the clock. It looked like the exact response a good football team should have after halftime. Instead, Ryan Flournoy mishandled a pass from Prescott and stalled the drive. The Cowboys settled for three points. Had Dallas converted before halftime and punched in a touchdown to open the third quarter, this game likely looks very different. Arizona probably never feels the need to shake things up at quarterback, and the comeback attempt may never materialize in the first place. The Cowboys had multiple opportunities to put the game away and failed every time. They cracked the door open for Arizona and the Cardinals kicked it down. Not Enough Pickens If Dallas truly wanted to establish the run, it would help to feature the one receiver on the roster most capable of forcing defenses to respect the deep ball. For the second straight week, George Pickens was largely an afterthought. Ten targets over the last two weeks simply isn’t enough for a player with his skill set. Pickens finished with two catches for 48 yards, including a 37-yard reception, and appeared to have a 59-yard touchdown wiped off the board by a holding penalty. Even after proving he could challenge Arizona vertically, Dallas never made a concerted effort to get him more involved. That’s been one of the more frustrating parts of the offense lately. There are stretches where Pickens completely disappears for an entire half. While CeeDee Lamb was heavily featured and Ryan Flournoy made some important plays, the Cowboys needed an offensive spark and rarely looked to one of their most explosive weapons. That became even more puzzling as the game wore on. Particularly late in regulation and into overtime, Pickens should have been a focal point. There’s simply too much talent invested in him for Dallas to go extended stretches without throwing him the football. The Cowboys can point to several reasons why the offense came up short. Not utilizing one of their most dangerous playmakers enough belongs near the top of the list. Coaching There’s no easy way around it. Coaching is the biggest reason the Cowboys lost. The defense giving up points is unfortunately nothing new. Allowing 33 points feels almost routine at this stage. It’s disappointing, but it isn’t surprising. What’s becoming increasingly concerning is how the offense is being managed. The questionable decision-making started early. Backed up deep in their own territory, Brian Schottenheimer opened a drive with a quarterback sneak. He followed it with an incomplete pass before calling a halfback draw on third down, effectively waving the white flag and choosing to punt from deep in his own territory. The frustrating part is that we’ve seen this before. The Cowboys are paying significant money to Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, and George Pickens. Yet time and again their head coach removes the game from their hands by calling conservatively in situations where aggression is warranted. It’s reminiscent of the decision-making that has followed Schottenheimer throughout the season. Rather than trust his playmakers to create an advantage, he routinely defaults to the safest possible option. The most damning example came late in the game. Holding a 27-24 lead with just over two minutes left, Schottenheimer had an opportunity to put the game away. Instead of remaining aggressive and forcing Arizona to defend the entire field, the Cowboys became conservative. He effectively challenged a backup quarterback to march the length of the field despite watching Arizona move the ball successfully on multiple consecutive possessions. Again, he trusted his defense over Dak Prescott, CeeDee Lamb, and George Pickens. At best, that’s negligent game management. At worst, it’s coaching scared. Too often this…

title: The third-down call that will haunt Brian Schottenheimer
summary: Coach Brian Schottenheimer has struggled in situational decision making this season. While the offense was able to put up points on Sunday against the Cardinals, the second year head coach again struggled to make sound decisions in crunch time. One of the biggest plays of the game occurred on 3rd and 11 with 4:02 left […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images Coach Brian Schottenheimer has struggled in situational decision making this season. While the offense was able to put up points on Sunday against the Cardinals, the second year head coach again struggled to make sound decisions in crunch time. One of the biggest plays of the game occurred on 3rd and 11 with 4:02 left in the 4th quarter. Arizona had just one timeout left. A field goal here puts Dallas up by two scores. The two most important factors at this moment were chewing clock or forcing Arizona to spend their timeouts and securing the field goal. Going up two scores and leaving Arizona with as little time as possible while forcing them to use their timeouts has to be the mission this late into the game. With 11 yards to go for a first down, coach Schottenheimer decided it was time to put the ball in the air. The risk was an incompletion, stopping the clock. The payoff, while unlikely given the distance, would be a potential game sealer. The ball was batted down at the line of scrimmage. The clock stopped. Arizona retained their timeout. This would come back to haunt the Cowboys just a short time later. The drive took a commendable 6:53 off the clock and put Dallas up by two scores with 3:54 left in the game. This should have been the drive that iced it for the Cowboys. But the third-down incompletion helped Arizona retain a timeout, saving 40 seconds on the next Cowboys possession that went for negative three yards and took just 1:02 off the clock. After getting the ball back with 1:09 left on the clock, Arizona marched down the field on an eight-play, 80-yard drive. With only 10 seconds left in the game, Arizona capped it off with the game tying touchdown, sending the matchup into overtime. Without their timeout on the previous Cowboys drive, Arizona would have gotten the ball back with around 30 seconds left instead of just over one minute. That’s likely Hail Mary territory, as there simply wouldn’t have been enough time to drive the ball down field. The decision to throw the ball in a situation where a conversion was unlikely was an unnecessary risk, and one that came back to haunt Dallas. Much to the chagrin of others, I applauded the decision to run the ball on 3rd-and-8 last week with Hunter Luepke inside the 10. Considering the game situation, it made complete sense. Chew clock, secure the two-score lead, and make a backup beat you in the waning moments. In a similar situation this week, however, the head coach called a head-scratcher that played a key role in the embarrassing loss against the Cardinals. He allowed the opponent to retain a timeout, conserving 40 seconds in a game where the equalizer was scored with just ten seconds left. Coach Schottenheimer and the offense seem to be in a strange limbo state where it’s unclear to them when to play aggressive and when to be conservative in crucial situations. This was highlighted once again in the worst loss of the Brian Schottenheimer era.

title: Cowboys offense failed to capitalize on defensive stops
summary: The Dallas Cowboys defense is not good at football. Relying on the defense would be a horrible strategy. Nothing about the state of the defense surprises us anymore which means that capitalizing on the moments where they are successful is of the highest priority. The Cowboys did not do that against the Arizona Cardinals. Dallas […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys defense is not good at football. Relying on the defense would be a horrible strategy. Nothing about the state of the defense surprises us anymore which means that capitalizing on the moments where they are successful is of the highest priority. The Cowboys did not do that against the Arizona Cardinals. Dallas squandered the defense’s stops On the surface it seems like the Cowboys offense did enough to win the game on Sunday. They scored 30 points, after all. But those 30 points are a little misleading. Consider that one of the Cowboys’ touchdowns came after Shemar James returned an interception to the Arizona 5-yard line. That wasn’t a ton of work to cash in. What we are interested in looking at here is how the offense performed in moments like that, off of stops generated by the defense. There were six in total. In sequence: Cardinals Punt……………… Cowboys Turnover on Downs Cardinals Interception downed at Arizona 5-yard line… Cowboys TD Cardinals Punt………………. Cowboys TD Cardinals Fumble…………. Cowboys Missed Field Goal Cardinals Punt………………. Cowboys Punt Cardinals Punt (OT)………. Cowboys Punt Of the six instances in question the Cowboys offense successfully capitalized just twice, and it only required them to travel a handful of yards as noted. What’s more is it only even happened because of a fumble recovery in the endzone after Javonte Williams had the ball pop loose. The point here is that the Cowboys offense was given six opportunities by their defense to make the opponent pay. They hardly delivered in that respect. Their 30-point performance is a little hollow in that way, and a little might be generous. These are the moments that you have to capitalize on in general in football, but especially when everyone understands that your defense is what the Cowboys’ is this season. Obviously they did not and they paid the price for that.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: 5 players Cowboys should consider trading prior to the deadline
summary: If it looks like a duck, swims like a duck, and quacks like a duck, then it’s probably a duck. The Dallas Cowboys are a duck, and a lame one at that. The time for sugarcoating is over. The Dallas Cowboys are a bad team and it was painfully obvious in their overtime loss to […]
full_text: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images If it looks like a duck, swims like a duck, and quacks like a duck, then it’s probably a duck. The Dallas Cowboys are a duck, and a lame one at that. The time for sugarcoating is over. The Dallas Cowboys are a bad team and it was painfully obvious in their overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals. It should no longer matter they can “technically” still make the playoffs. This team doesn’t deserve such an honor and would only embarrass themselves if they make the postseason. Now is the time to start preparing for the future. That means making some coaching changes/adjustments and actively selling off pieces to acquire some much-needed draft capital. With the November 10 NFL trade deadline quickly approaching, we’ll take a look at latter and Cowboys players who could find their names on the trade block. WR George Pickens George Pickens is having a solid 2026 season, but not quite as impactful as last year. He’s the team’s best trade asset and could net them a high draft pick, but maybe not a top one as he can’t sign a new contract with another team until the offseason. While it’s true Dallas could franchise tag him once again in 2027, it’s probably best for all parties concerned to avoid the drama and part ways now. OL T.J. Bass T.J. Bass proved himself as a quality starting guard in the first four games of the 2026 season while filling in for an injured Tyler Smith when he was on injured reserve. He’ll hit the open market as a free agent after the completion of the season and could command a contract the Cowboys won’t won’t choose to match. Better get something in return now rather than nothing later. WR KaVontae Turpin KaVontae Turpin has missed the last two games with a rib injury, and yet, the Cowboys return game hasn’t seemed to miss a beat. Tyler Goodson has been an upgrade on kick returns and Jonathan Mingo has been surprisingly dependable as a punt returner. The Pro Bowl return man and gadget player could potentially land the Cowboys a much-needed pick for next year if traded. EDGE Rashan Gary The Rashan Gary trade hasn’t worked out the way the Cowboys have hoped. He hasn’t made much of an impact this year and could be considered somewhat of a progress starter for Malachi Lawrence as things stand right now. Some team around the league may be willing to part with a late-round pick next year to acquire his services, and if so, the Cowboys should absolutely jump at the opportunity. CB DaRon Bland Due to his play this season and is inflated contract, it’s probably unlikely DaRon Bland has much of a trade market. Despite that, the Cowboys should absolutely explore the possibility of getting anything in return from their high-priced, underperforming CB. He is destined to be a salary-cap casualty next year and it would be nice to get anything in return, even if it’s just a late-round pick.
author: Brian Martin

title: Cowboys vs. Cardinals Stock Report: Brian Schottenheimer’s offense shrinks
summary: The Dallas Cowboys played down to the moment on Sunday, there is no doubt about that. With a sizable lead in hand, the Cowboys seemed to start envisioning what life would be like at 4-4 and with Brian Schottenheimer’s second winning streak with the team (after 25 career games, mind you). While they were daydreaming […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys played down to the moment on Sunday, there is no doubt about that. With a sizable lead in hand, the Cowboys seemed to start envisioning what life would be like at 4-4 and with Brian Schottenheimer’s second winning streak with the team (after 25 career games, mind you). While they were daydreaming the Arizona Cardinals were rallying. Arizona, a moribund team in today’s NFL, seemed inspired and invigorated while the Cowboys were lost in thought. In the end the Cardinals were winners at AT&T Stadium (why wouldn’t they be?) and the Cowboys were forced to take yet another hard and long look in the mirror. This is that mirror. Stock Down: Brian Schottenheimer I’m not sure which was worse, Schottenheimer the head coach or Schottenheimer the offensive play-caller. You don’t lose a game, let alone blow a huge lead to this season’s Arizona Cardinals team, unless you are a special type of bad. Schotty the head coach allowed for the team to get far too comfortable, but Schotty the play-caller called a timid game in the second half and kept leaving the door more and more open. It has been a long time since it felt like Dallas had an advantage at head coach. Who knows when the next time will be? Stock Down: Dak Prescott As a whole the Cowboys offense was given the ball six times by their defense and ultimately scored just twice. What’s more is that the offense had 12 true possessions (discounting the kneel down at the end of regulation) and failed to net double-digit yardage on seven of them. 7 of 12! Dak Prescott was under some duress (more on that in a moment), but there is no excuse. The franchise quarterback has to do more. Stock Down: Christian Parker How do we say this again ? What amalgamation of words can we use that hasn’t already been offered? Christian Parker is in some truly historic company in the worst kind of way. His unit did deliver the stops early on as noted, but they allowed the Cardinals to gash them all throughout the end of this game. What’s more is that they allowed Arizona to waltz all the way down at the end of regulation to tie, even though they should have won then. Stock Down: Rashan Gary What are you doing committing obvious roughing the passer penalties in critical moments? Rashan Gary was supposed to be among the leaders that the Cowboys were able to bring in to the defensive side of the ball. Game in and game out he seems to offer more questions than answers these days, and he had terrible judgment in a critical moment that was key in the loss. Stock Down: Offensive line This is not about discounting credit and/or blame from Dak Prescott. We have established this. But my word the Cowboys offensive line got pushed around. Perhaps the book is out as we all discussed/feared following the Buccaneers and/or Packers losses, but they were not able to hold on for much against Arizona and in the process a lot of what they wanted to do on offense was jumbled. For a group that had really been turning it around as of late, this was not good. Stock Down: Javonte Williams Keep in mind that one of the touchdowns that the mighty Cowboys offense scored only happened because a Javonte Williams fumble was recovered in the endzone. The offensive line struggled, but so did Williams. This has to be better. Stock Down: Brandon Aubrey Nobody is trying to say that a 61-yard field goal is easy. But Brandon Aubrey is expected to make those. What’s more is that the Cowboys lost this game in overtime; had he made that kick near the end of regulation you can argue that things never come down to that. The inches matter. Stock Down: DaRon Bland Like with Christian Parker as a whole, this is the same story. DaRon Bland continues to get picked on every week. On some level maybe the Joey Porter Jr. trade created a new and worse kind of problem in that sense. Obviously the contract situation is what it is. This is just a huge bummer. Stock Up: Caleb Downs It goes without saying that we hope that Caleb Downs is alright as he entered concussion protocol near the end of this game. Downs was having arguably his best game as a professional early on. He was huge in many respects and was the primary tackler when Dallas held Arizona on fourth-and-goal early in the game. He is living up to the hype. Stock Up: Ryan Flournoy We have all been very excited about Ryan Flournoy for some time, and as of late he is proving why. It is strange how the Cowboys cannot seem to get George Pickens going consistently, but Flournoy is more than making up for it himself. He did have a tough drop, and he has become a reliable receiver for Dak.
author: RJ Ochoa

title: 10 thoughts on the Cowboys loss to the Cardinals
summary: Wow. It’s hard being a fan of the Dallas Cowboys these days, and those difficulties reached a new level after an indescribable 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals. While most of us were guarded against these pesky Cardinals due to the history between these teams, our guard was lowered just long enough to raise […]
full_text: Wow. It’s hard being a fan of the Dallas Cowboys these days, and those difficulties reached a new level after an indescribable 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals. While most of us were guarded against these pesky Cardinals due to the history between these teams, our guard was lowered just long enough to raise our hopes so they could be snatched away yet again. This one was a tough one, and here are 10 thoughts on this really sad Sunday morning showing. 1. The streak continues Another game against Arizona, another loss. It’s just not in the cards. For reasons as mysterious as the Loch Ness monster, the Cowboys cannot beat this football team. Even when it looks like the Cardinals are dead in the water, they find a way to rise up and defeat Dallas. The losing streak now sits at five straight and nine of the last 10 games. It’s frustrating, it’s peculiar, and it’s downright tiring. 2. Getting all the breaks What’s even weirder about this loss is that so many things went in the Cowboys’ favor. They won the turnover battle, they won the penalty battle, and when loose balls were flying around, they were landing in the Cowboys’ hands. Jonathan Mingo muffed a punt. No problem. Javonte Williams fumbled in the end zone. Don’t fret; still a touchdown. Early in the game, the Cardinals receivers were dropping passes left and right, and it just felt like everything was working in the Cowboys’ favor. Little did we know what lay ahead. 3. Sneaky suspicious When the Cowboys get backed up deep in their own territory, they love to waste a down and QB-sneak it. They did it last week against the Eagles, and they did it again on Sunday. Both times resulted in a quick possession, as the Cowboys were forced to punt. Brian Schottenheimer clearly values safety over extending the drive. His team. His choice. If he likes to sneak so much, then why didn’t he do so when he decided to go for it on 4th-and-inches at his own 30-yard line? Instead, he opted to run, and Williams was stuffed behind the line of scrimmage. 4. Other weird stuff The playcalling was weird sometimes, but some of the logic behind the Cowboys’ choices was equally puzzling. Going for it at your own 30-yard line is certainly a choice. In that moment, he chose to be aggressive. We get it. That’s what makes his other passive moments really confusing. Late in the first half, the Cowboys had a shot at a field goal, and they chose to run the ball to get a little closer for Brandon Aubrey, but even still, it was a 60+ yard field goal attempt? Just because he’s capable of booming those kicks doesn’t mean you shouldn’t at least try to get closer. It didn’t seem like a whole lot at the time, but those three points would’ve come in handy later. 5. Second half collapse The Cardinals aren’t viewed as a strong offensive team, but for the Cowboys to still hold them to just three points in the first half was impressive, especially considering the Dallas offense turned the ball over on downs in their own territory. Nice recovery, defense. But as good as they were in the first half, they were equally disastrous in the second half. They surrendered four second-half touchdowns, including three in the fourth quarter alone. The defense allowed two 50+ yard runs from Tyler Allgeier and couldn’t make a stop to save their lives. It was a complete meltdown. 6. One first down, please Despite the late comeback, the Cowboys still had a chance to ice the game. After a failed onside kick, Dallas was sitting in great shape. All they needed was one first down, and the game was over. The Cardinals only had one timeout left, and Mike LaFleur opted to use it on the plus side of the two-minute warning after a running play that went nowhere. This dared the Cowboys to pass on second down because the clock would stop after the next play no matter what. Dallas took the bait; only Prescott took the conservative approach and cautiously fell into a sack after his first read wasn’t there. This resulted in a sack and gave them no chance to get a first down and run out the clock. 7. Another gift After the Cardinals scored a touchdown with just six seconds left, the life was sucked out of AT&T Stadium. The only thing left was for Arizona kicker Chad Ryland to hit the extra point and leave Dallas with another victory. Shockingly, he shanked it, missing his first extra point since 2024, and giving the Cowboys another chance they didn’t deserve. 8. A wasted stop Despite transforming into a red-carpet defense in the second half, the Cowboys surprisingly forced the Cardinals to go three-and-out in their first possession of overtime. It set up a perfect opportunity for the Cowboys’ offense to take control of the game and move into Aubrey range for the game-winner. They never got close. The offense’s final possession was pathetic. It was a quick three-and-out, and they went backwards. The Cowboys punted the ball away and never got a chance again. The defense just didn’t have it in them to make another stop. 9. Under pressure It feels less exhilarating now, but there was a time when it was exciting to see Jacoby Brissett repeatedly succumb to pressure. The Cowboys sacked the Cardinals’ quarterbacks five times, with two coming from Quinnen Williams, and one each from Donovan Ezeiruaku, Von Miller, and James Houston. Defensive tackle Elijah Garcia almost had another one, but Brissett was able to get rid of it at the last second. While most of the damage happened in the first half, it was good to see the Cowboys’ pass rush show some life. 10. Brissett still undefeated Entering the game, Brissett remained the only quarterback from Prescott’s draft class in 2016 whom the Cowboys have yet to beat. They have faced seven quarterbacks from that draft, including Jared Goff, Carson Wentz, Cody Kessler, Nate Sudfeld, Brandon Allen, Jeff Driskel, and Brissett. All of them have fallen to the Cowboys at some point over the years, with the exception of Brissett, and it looked like they would finally be able to check him off the list as well. They had his number so well that he was benched and replaced with quarterback Gardner Minshew. The veteran came to the rescue and kept Brissett’s winning streak against Dak and the Cowboys alive and well.
author: Dan Rogers

title: Cowboys news: Dallas gets upset, embarrassed by Cardinals in OT
summary: It was a game the Dallas Cowboys needed to win. After winning against the Eagles in a decent performance last week, Dallas had the opportunity to gain ground in the division with the Giants on bye. And against a 2-5 Cardinals team, winning seemed like an entirely doable task. For most of the game, it […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images It was a game the Dallas Cowboys needed to win. After winning against the Eagles in a decent performance last week, Dallas had the opportunity to gain ground in the division with the Giants on bye. And against a 2-5 Cardinals team, winning seemed like an entirely doable task. For most of the game, it looked like Dallas was going to get it done, but they didn’t. Dallas Cowboys suffer embarrassing 33-30 defeat against Arizona Cardinals- Mark Heaney, Inside The Star It was a game that was a good summary of the season. Dallas looked good at times, but in a game the Cowboys should have won, the defense couldn’t get the job done. Unfortunately, that momentum didn’t last; after another Dallas punt, backup RB Tyler Allgeier broke free for a 63-yard touchdown run, cutting the lead to 17-10. Offensively, they finally responded: a 37-yard connection between Dak Prescott and George Pickens, followed by a pass interference penalty, set them up at the goal line. Game Recap: Dallas shocked in OT, 33-30- Staff, DallasCowboys.com At this point, there is enough evidence to believe that the Cardinals simply have the Cowboys number. Even after losing eight of the last nine, this one simply should not have happened. The Cowboys won the coin toss and elected to play defense first. And the unit quickly took care of business by forcing the Cardinals to go three-and-out. But Dallas could do no better and punted on their first try as well. Given a second chance, Arizona did what they had to do, crossing into Cowboys territory and setting up Ryland to redeem himself. This time the kicker split the uprights from 42 yards out to give the Cardinals a shocking 33-30 win. 5 instant reactions to Cowboys’ soul-crushing overtime loss to Cardinals- Michel Haney, The Landry Hat It’s tough not to feel as though the season may be coming to an early end. If you can’t beat the Arizona Cardinals at home as a 7.5-point favorite, there isn’t much hope for the tougher games remaining. Defense is too sloppy to hold up against good teams In the first half alone, the Cowboys were flagged for offsides three separate times, all because of Brissett hard counts. Daron Bland was called for defensive pass interference on a quick slant that might not have even been catchable for Michael Wilson. Schottenheimer’s stubborn offensive strategy doomed Cowboys from start- Reid Hanson, Cowboys Wire In a loss this embarrassing, fingers can be pointed in a lot of different directions. However, it’s tough not to start with the defense and head coach. Dallas’ run-pass distribution fell 39-29 in the running game’s favor; the Cowboys were successful on only 32 percent of those runs, garnering an EPA/rush average of -0.26. These numbers spread out over the course of a season would rank Dallas 31 st in both EPA and success rate, yet, for some unexplainable reason, Schottenheimer stuck with it. 3 things we learned about the Cowboys from the Cardinals game- Dyllan Rivers, Blogging The Boys After this game, fans have a pretty good idea of who the 2026 Cowboys are. The offense is decent but wildly inconsistent; the defense has its moments but is largely useless, and the coaching is abysmal. It’s possible for the Cowboys defense to start fast but can’t finish Dallas forced a punt and had a goal line stand on the Cardinals first two drives, respectively. On the third drive, Shemar James snagged the first interception of his young career, creating a seven-point opportunity on the Cardinals five-yard line.

title: Broncos lead NFL in defensive stats; run game has to help fix that
summary: The Denver Broncos found a way to do it again. It being another wild fourth quarter comeback victory — this time against the hated Kansas City Chiefs. The win is great and the team is 6-2 and in prime position to challenge for the AFC’s top seed again this season, but there is always room […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - NOVEMBER 1: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos looks at his play sheet during the second quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, November 1, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images The Denver Broncos found a way to do it again. It being another wild fourth quarter comeback victory — this time against the hated Kansas City Chiefs. The win is great and the team is 6-2 and in prime position to challenge for the AFC’s top seed again this season, but there is always room for improvement and none bigger than the run game. Head coach Sean Payton was asked about the Broncos leading the NFL in defensive snaps and he confirmed that this was an offensive stat more than a defensive one. “There’s a lot that goes into that,” Payton explained on Monday. “That’s a stat I don’t like. It’s a stat that on offense, we have to do a good job of possessing the ball. So that’s something that we pay attention to.” Possessing the ball and sustaining drives is a function that falls far more on the run game than on Bo Nix. Sorry to all you Bo Nix haters out there, but he’s having to try to overcome an anemic rushing attack on every drive which has led to Denver being among the league leaders in three-and-outs. Payton mentioned the run game too and said they are working on that and feels like it will get better. “I think we’re continuing to work at it,” Payton said. “There were some glimpses yesterday. There were also some looks yesterday that we felt could have been blocked better. We’ll continue to work on that, and that’s something that we definitely feel like there’ll be improvement with.” Until yesterday, I would have disagreed with him. Why? Because of his unwavering commitment to J.K. Dobbins up until halftime on Sunday. I have nothing against Dobbins and appreciated his time in Denver, but its clear he is missing something this year. Something that Jonah Coleman seemed to have. Payton finally saw it too and the result was a second half emergence of Coleman as a featured back for Denver. He was a big part of their comeback and why I think Payton might be right that the run game might be improving greatly in the coming weeks. title: Will the Broncos’ big win against the Chiefs make them NFL trade deadline buyers?
summary: The Denver Broncos are the comeback kings of the National Football League. Yesterday, they once again embarked on fourth quarter heroics to defeat the Kansas City Chiefs 28-2. At 6-2, the Broncos are now in first place of the AFC West. It was another gutsy and gritty performance by Denver. Emblematic of the type of […]
full_text: Nov 1, 2026; Denver, Colorado, USA; Denver Broncos defensive tackle D.J. Jones (93) leaves the field after defeating the Kansas City Chiefs at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Denver Broncos are the comeback kings of the National Football League. Yesterday, they once again embarked on fourth quarter heroics to defeat the Kansas City Chiefs 28-2. At 6-2, the Broncos are now in first place of the AFC West. It was another gutsy and gritty performance by Denver. Emblematic of the type of team they’ve forged into since Head Coach Sean Payton took over in 2023. It’s the fifteenth game in a row the Broncos have won in one-score affairs. It was the 200th victory of Payton’s remarkable career. Encapsulating how the team keeps finding a way to grind out big wins in key moments isn’t easy. However, Payton did his best to answer when he felt the Broncos had found their groove as a legitimate contender and went back to last October which was the beginning of a long winning streak for the franchise. “I think honestly, to answer that, I think it has to come from, well, we did it before. I would go back to Philly [2025] at Philly after playing Cincinnati on a Monday. I think that’s the first—that would be where my brain would go where we grew a little bit,” stated Payton. “Then there’s a belief that can get stronger and then there’s experience. Then you’re seasoned a little, but we still have a lot of things to fix. I honestly think that’s where I believe it comes from.” The Broncos didn’t play their best game against the Chiefs in Week 8. Nevertheless, they came out as the victors. Tough teams find a way to win when the stakes are high. Reeling off fifteen fourth quarter points, Bo Nix and Denver’s offense found good footing in critical moments and came away with two big scoring drives. A big part of their success was featuring rookie running back Jonah Coleman. He was missing in action for most of the first half, but Payton dedicated virtually all of the team’s backfield snaps to Coleman in the final two quarters of play. The fourth-round pick wound up with 104 all-purpose yards and 1 touchdown and flashed as a runner and receiver out of the backfield. After the game, Coleman reflected on his performance humbly. He emphasized the importance of teamwork and also praised Broncos Country for showing up. Coleman, like many other players and coaches, all pointed to the noise from fans as being instrumental on the victory—especially at the end with the defense’s impeccable goal line stand. “Like I said, glory be to God, he allowed me to do what I love. I just got to give a shoutout to my offensive line and my teammates for keeping the confidence up the whole game. The game didn’t go our way the whole entire game until the fourth quarter,” stated Coleman. “I went up to all the offensive lineman, the receivers, and the defense and said, ‘It’s going to be a four-quarter game,’ like coach said—just to remind them it’s not over. So, when the fourth quarter hit, that’s when the spark just lit up in the whole team.” The Broncos have now won four games in a row. They are heating up as each week passes. This coming Sunday, they travel to the east coast to take on the Carolina Panthers. If Denver can continue to improve and take care of business on the road, they will enter their bye week at 7-2. All things considered that would be quite remarkable. The big question between now and then is whether or not yesterday’s huge win will cause Denver’s front office to be major buyers before the November 10th trade deadline. Had they lost and went to 5-3, I’m not certain that would have been the case. But now? They have a really good shot at winning the division if they perform well down the stretch. Moreover, a chance at earning the number one seed again in a tough AFC playoff race. Have they seen enough from the players they have in the fold to make a Super Bowl push? Or do they believe there is a piece or two missing that need to be added to achieve this year’s gridiron goal? The clock is ticking and I can’t wait to see what happens in that regard.
author: Christopher Hart
