full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos runs the football past Nohl Williams #20 of the Kansas City Chiefs during the second quarter at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images They did it again. At one point, the Denver Broncos trailed the Kansas City Chiefs by the score of 24-13 late in the third quarter and things looked dire. The offense was stacking three-and-out drives, and the defense could not tackle rookie running back Emmett Johnson. Then it happened. Bo Nix, Jonah Coleman, and this Denver Broncos defense stepped up and scored 15 unanswered 4th-quarter points and had an impressive goal-line stand with seconds left on the clock to win the game. Yet another improbable 4th quarter comeback, and one against a division rival in a game with a lot on the line for the Broncos. A loss would have put them well behind the Chiefs in the AFC West, while a win would have put them back at the top of the AFC West. It was an incredible and thrilling comeback victory, and despite all the naysayers, doubters, and, hell, even their play at times, the Denver Broncos are 6-2, the current 2 seed in the AFC, and leading the AFC West. Stock up and stock down is a weekly series where I go through the Denver Broncos’ 53-man roster and tell you which Broncos players’ stock is going up, down, or remains unchanged. After this huge win, we have a lot of players seeing their stock go up, but there are a few players who will see their stock trending in the wrong direction. Quarterback Bo Nix – Stock up: It wasn’t always pretty or perfect, but it was a classic Bo Nix game. He made some big-time throws in this game, but there were stretches of poor play (by everyone) and some annoying deflected passes. However, when the 4th quarter hit, Nix and the Broncos came alive and scored 15 unanswered points and came back to defeat their rivals, the Kansas City Chiefs. Yet another 4th-quarter comeback win for Nix, who was dealing with a retired journeyman quarterback calling his play disrespectful and some media asking if he should be benched. Nix also gets another head-to-head win against Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs. The haters are going to continue to hate, but Nix just keeps winning football games. Jarrett Stidham – Unchanged: Remains the Broncos’ veteran quarterback. Sam Ehlinger – Unchanged: Remains the Broncos’ third-string quarterback. Running Back Jonah Coleman – Stock WAY up: After veteran JK Dobbins got some run to start the game, rookie Jonah Coleman took over and never looked back. He played 66% of the snaps, including the vast majority of the second-half snaps, and totaled over 100 yards from scrimmage. His highlight play was a 50+ yard catch-and-run late in the game that led to him scoring the go-ahead touchdown. Now, the talk that the Broncos may trade for Jonathan Taylor or Breece Hall continues, but regardless, rookie running back Jonah Coleman has proven that he will be a key part of this offense moving forward. JK Dobbins – Crashing stock: Is it over? It sure seems like it might be over for Dobbins. He finished the game with 7 carries for 13 yards and barely saw the field again after taking an 8-yard loss on one run play. Add in Jonah Coleman taking over the game in the second half and outproducing him, and things look dire. Also, if the Broncos do indeed make a big splash at running back, Dobbins time with the Broncos could come to an end. We’ll see, but things are trending in the wrong direction for Dobbins. Cody Schrader – Unchanged: Was elevated from the practice squad but only saw 2 offensive snaps and 5 special teams snaps. Adam Prentice – Unchanged: He has his role, and he fills it well. Remains the Broncos’ lead blocker and a key special teams player for them. Wide Receiver Jaylen Waddle – Stock up: The stat line will not wow you, but he had a pretty big impact on the game. He caught a touchdown pass from QB Bo Nix and later converted a two-point conversion, which ended up being very important later in the game. He did see his snap count come down a little, but he was likely held back a little bit due to his lingering chest/shoulder injury. Courtland Sutton – Stock up: Saw 4 targets on Sunday and came away with 4 catches for 53 yards, which included an impressive catch off a deflection. He also drew the attention of the Chiefs’ defense on the Broncos’ two touchdown passes, so he had a noticeable impact on the game. Marvin Mims Jr. – Unchanged: Sean Payton wanted to give Mims more touches and snaps, and he did. Mims saw 18 snaps on offense, but didn’t do a ton with those snaps. He had 2 catches for 10 yards, 2 rushes for 19 yards, and was solid in the return game. Pat Bryant is eligible to return next week, so Mims could see his role and snaps take a hit moving forward. Troy Franklin – Unchanged: Franklin played 71% of the snaps but only saw 2 targets and had 1 catch for 3 yards. The playing time is there, but the production is not, and like Mims, the eventual return of Bryant will hurt their playing time and limit their opportunities. Lil’Jordan Humphrey – Unchanged: He is who he is and fills his role on the Broncos. Tight End Evan Engram – Stock down: 3 targets for 0 catches and played 48% of the snaps. He’s out there, but still trailed Adam Trautman in snaps, and Nate Adkins now has 3 touchdowns this season to Engram’s 1. The production isn’t there, and he’s barely a part of the offense right now. Adam Trautman – Stock up: He caught some passes! Had 2 catches for 30 yards, including a 22-yard catch-and-run late in the game. The Sean Payton favorite led all Broncos tight ends in snaps and catches this week, and he’ll likely continue leading them in this role moving forward. Nate Adkins – Stock up: The Broncos touchdown specialist added another on Sunday and now leads the team with 3 touchdown receptions this year. He’s primarily a run-blocking specialist, but Adkins knows how to get open in the red zone and has become one of the team’s top red-zone threats this season. Dallen Bentley – Unchanged: Remains inactive. Offensive Line Garett Bolles – Stock up: The Broncos All-Pro left tackle continues to be one of the best blindside blockers in the game. Ben Powers – Unchanged: I did not notice Powers on Sunday, which is usually a good thing. Luke Wattenberg – Unchanged: Like Powers, I did not notice Wattenberg on Sunday, but I am also no offensive line expert. Quinn Meinerz – Stock up: Stud Mike McGlinchey – Unchanged: I did notice him struggle a little bit a few times, but overall he seemed solid. Again, I am no offensive line expert. Alex Palczewski – Unchanged: Remains the Broncos’ 6th offensive lineman and played 5 offensive snaps on Sunday. Matt Peart – Unchanged: Played on special teams. Alex Forsyth – Unchanged: Played on special teams. Kage Casey – Unchanged: Remains inactive. Defensive Line Zach Allen – Stock up: Remains a stud and the centerpiece of the Broncos’ dominant defensive line. DJ Jones – Unchanged: The Broncos’ run defense was solid up the middle and held Kenneth Walker in check on Sunday. Malcolm Roach – Stock up: Roach has been excellent and one of the more underrated and overlooked parts of this defense. His sack of Patrick Mahomes to end the game will be on the end-of-season highlight reel. Eyioma Uwazurike – Unchanged: Played 45% of the defensive snaps and remains a valuable rotational defensive lineman who allows Zach Allen to take some snaps off. Sai’vion Jones – Unchanged: Played 23% of the snaps and has earned a valuable rotational defensive lineman for the Broncos. Jordan Jackson – Unchanged: Was inactive again. Tyler Onyedim – Unchanged: The rookie remains inactive. Linebacker Alex Singleton – Stock up: Singleton has 101 total tackles this year and is on pace for 200+ tackles. He has put together a good stretch of games and has been a very reliable tackler for the Broncos. He also had a sack in back-to-back games, and his…

title: Game balls for the Broncos comeback win over Chiefs in Week 8
summary: The Denver Broncos pulled off yet another insane comeback win to wrest control of the AFC West from the Kansas City Chiefs. Down 24-13 in the fourth quarter, the Broncos scored 15-unanswered points and put down one of the craziest goal line stands in recent memory. Even now, on Monday morning, I’m still processing how […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - OCTOBER 15: JL Skinner #34 of the Denver Broncos stands on the field during the first quarter of an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High on October 15, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos pulled off yet another insane comeback win to wrest control of the AFC West from the Kansas City Chiefs. Down 24-13 in the fourth quarter, the Broncos scored 15-unanswered points and put down one of the craziest goal line stands in recent memory. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Even now, on Monday morning, I’m still processing how it all went down. Two fourth down conversions for touchdowns. The missed Harrison Butker field goal. It’s wild. It’s the Bo Nix experience. People keep expecting that ride to end, but it keeps rolling. Nix now has one fourth quarter comeback every 3.5 games started and one game-winning drive for every 2.8 games started. Second place on that Hall of Fame-filled list is a mile . It’s a long mile. No one has ever started their career with such “luck” in the fourth quarter. Maybe its time we all just accept that the Bo Nix experience might be here to stay. Here’s who we’re giving our game balls to from the Broncos wild win over the Chiefs: Bo Nix The Broncos quarterback just makes magic happen in the fourth quarter. It may not be pretty the first three quarters, but he finds a way to deliver when it matters most. For the game, Nix finished 20-for-32 passing for 222 yards and two touchdowns. Perhaps the most important stat: no turnovers. With Nix at quarterback, the Broncos have now won 16 consecutive one-score games. It gets better: Nix improved to 12-12 in his career when trailing at any point in the fourth quarter (.500), the best record by any QB since 1970. That’s ahead of Patrick Mahomes (23-33) (minimum of 20 games). As Nix said to Tracy Wolfson on CBS after the game, “Something’s magical about this place. I don’t know. I can’t explain it.” Nix plays a big role in that Mile High Magic. – Ian St. Clair Bo Nix has a 118.9 passer rating when down 1-8 points in 4th quarter (playoffs included). That ranks first among 169 QBs with 75+ attempts in that scenario since 1991 — Josh Dubow (@JoshDubowAP) November 2, 2026 Bo Nix in the 4th quarter in his career 63%, 4,025 yards, 33 TDs, 9 INTs — Liam Hammer (@itshammersports) November 2, 2026 Jonah Coleman Jonah Coleman hit the ground running right off of injured reserve last year and took advantage of the bigger workload, getting all the running back work in the second half and turning it into 100+ yards from scrimmage, the first Broncos back over 100 yards this year. He made it count when it mattered most, ripping off a big play on a swing pass to setup the team in scoring position and then showed great vision at the goal line to punch in his second ever NFL touchdown. He already leads the running backs in first downs, despite spending half the season so far on IR. Trade rumors may continue to swirl, but I think Denver has found their starting running back for this season and into the future. – Jeff Essary JONAH MFING COLEMAN!!! pic.twitter.com/PgsLaqppkH — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 Devon Key, Taylor Rapp, and JL Skinner When both starters go down, it takes a village sometimes to keep the unit together. That village at the safety positions came from Devon Key, Taylor Rapp, and JL Skinner. The defense faltered at points yesterday, but I don’t remember a single time when I felt like it came from any one of these three dudes. When the game came down to a third down and goal from the one, it was JL Skinner too who put the hit stick on reigning Super Bowl MVP to save the game. Have a game ball, all three of you dudes! – Tim Lynch Big time play here by @JlJlskinner to keep the Chiefs out of the end zone. It will get overlooked due to the final play but he came up big there 💪 pic.twitter.com/2j7Hol00ap — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 Malcolm Roach Malcolm Roach gets my game ball for sacking the whiniest baggy-eyed punk the NFL has to offer and helping seal the win for the Orange and Blue. Roach has been with this team for a few years now and tends to fly under the radar, but he’s a baller up front. He had 4 tackles including a tackle for loss in the game and a quarterback hit to his credit as well. The big thing we see from Roach consistently is his ability to attack gaps and peel off blocks to create pressure up front. Give this man some love, Broncos Country! – Sadaraine MALCOLM ROACH YOU'RE A FUCKIN BADASS pic.twitter.com/FVPJ7sBnBQ — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 Alex Singleton Alex Singleton gets my game ball. While he was far from perfect, and still got gashed in the passing game, he played a great game. He had one of the Broncos two sacks, and he finished the game with 14 tackles (6 solo), 1 TFL, and 1 PD. His sack was the sack that pushed the Chiefs out of range for Butker. I may rag on him but he played terribly in the first game against KC, and he made up for that with one of his best games when the Bronco defense needed it the most. – Joe Mahoney SACK SINGLETON pic.twitter.com/AwAr2hgFx5 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) November 2, 2026 Wil Lutz Will Lutz might not be an obvious choice for a gameball, but consider this; he did not miss. The Broncos kicker was 2/2 on FG attempts, and 2/2 on his extra points. Harrison Butker put the Chiefs in a tough spot when he missed his 54 yard attempt late in the 4th quarter. The Broncos went on to score, and Lutz hit the extra point to force the Chiefs into a tough spot, needing a TD to win, and no possibility of kicking a FG to extend the game. Big Nutz Lutz coming through big, helping to seal the win. – Adam Malnati Offensive Line The Broncos’ O-line has gotten a lot of flak this season, and often deservingly so. But the difference in protection between the 1st & 2nd games against the Chiefs is staggering: from pressuring Nix on 48.5% of dropbacks in Week 1 to pressure on just 5.9% of dropbacks in Week 8. The O-line kept Nix clean enough to make the comeback possible. – Taylor Kothe ESPN Research: Chiefs pressured Bo Nix on 2 of 34 dropbacks (6%), the lowest for any team since 2024 Week 5, and the lowest for the Chiefs since 2012 Week 8 Chiefs had a 48.5% pressure rate on Nix in Week 1 — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) November 2, 2026 Sean Payton A tip of the cap to Head Coach Sean Payton. It hasn’t always been pretty, but Broncos keep finding ways to win under his leadership. Yesterday’s impressive comeback victory over the Chiefs was the 200th of his storied career. It couldn’t have come at a better moment beating a rival to reclaim the top spot in the AFC West. Cheers to Payton on the milestone. – Chris Hart Who gets your game ball for the Broncos-Chiefs game? summary: It’s another week and another insane comeback win for the Denver Broncos. This time it came against the previously AFC West leading Kansas City Chiefs. With 15-unanswered points in the fourth quarter and a heck of a goal to go stand to send the Broncos into first place in the division and the second seeded […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - NOVEMBER 1: Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton and Kansas City Chiefs head coach Andy Reid shake hands after the game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on November 1, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s another week and another insane comeback win for the Denver Broncos. This time it came against the previously AFC West leading Kansas City Chiefs. With 15-unanswered points in the fourth quarter and a heck of a goal to go stand to send the Broncos into first place in the division and the second seeded spot in the AFC . The win was also a milestone for head coach Sean Payton who notched his 200th career win and became the sixth-fastest to do it. Shula. Halas. Lambeau. Belichick. Brown. 𝐏𝐚𝐲𝐭𝐨𝐧. Historic win for @SeanPayton . pic.twitter.com/qn6pjEY4j3 — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 2, 2026 What a way to reach that milestone too. Payton was asked about his range of emotions during the final moments of that 200th win and he hit a bit on how special it is to be a part of a great NFL team and the great wins that come with that. I’m screaming at Vance one second and then I’m hugging Vance and shaking Andy’s hand. There’s nothing like it. Sean Payton “Every one of us at some point has to get off this thing, but you don’t want to,” Payton said after the game. “We’re all better having been on it than never at all. So I’ve been fortunate to have been a part of a lot of good players and a lot of good organizations. People that make that happen. So it was emotional. The timing of the game and everything else. I’m screaming at Vance [Joseph] one second and then I’m hugging Vance and shaking Andy’s [Reid] hand. There’s nothing like it. I think the little bit of the curse is that I hate losing probably more than I like winning. So this was a good win.” The ending was special, but what made it so was who they did it again. Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs have been dominant when holding a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter. In fact, they were 80-2 before today. Eighty and Two. The Chiefs were 80-2 with Patrick Mahomes when they had a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter before the 28-24 loss to the Broncos. — Rob Maaddi (@RobMaaddi) November 2, 2026 This is a statement win for the Broncos. It’s a win that can catapult a team down the stretch. For all of the criticism the media and fans have thrown at them, this team is 6-2 and in firm control of their destiny. Maybe its time for all of us to just enjoy this ride…

title: Jonah Coleman makes statement as Broncos RB of the future
summary: During Sunday’s game against the Kansas City Chiefs, it became clear a shakeup was underway at the running back position. When the game began, JK Dobbins was given plenty of opportunity to lay the ground game foundation on which Bo Nix’s passing attack would be predicated. None of Dobbins 7 carries would go for longer […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 01: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos rushes for a touchdown against the Kansas City Chiefs in the fourth quarter of a game at Empower Field At Mile High on November 01, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Imagine if they’d given those Dobbins carries early on to Coleman… pic.twitter.com/2R3LphoGA1 — Mile High Broncos Podcasts (@MHBroncosPods) November 2, 2026 During Sunday’s game against the Kansas City Chiefs, it became clear a shakeup was underway at the running back position. When the game began, JK Dobbins was given plenty of opportunity to lay the ground game foundation on which Bo Nix’s passing attack would be predicated. None of Dobbins 7 carries would go for longer than 6-yards and he would finish his night running for just 13-yards, averaging an unacceptable 1.9 yards per carry. His long of 6-yards was only eclipsed by the -8-yards he managed during a backwards run in the 2nd quarter. It was clear last week against the Cardinals, with his 10 carries for 39-yards and at touchdown, that rookie Jonah Coleman was poised to take a hammer to the running back depth chart. Against the Chiefs on Sunday, he did just that. While patiently waiting for Dobbins to self-immolate on the field, Coleman muscled out 41-yards on 11 carries for a touchdown. While a 3.7 yards-per-carry isn’t anything to get excited about, it’s nearly twice the 1.9 that Dobbins offered. When you factor in Coleman’s receiving stats, 4 receptions for 63-yards compared to Dobbins’ grand total of zero, Broncos Country should have no doubt just whom their bell cow will be going forward. So, why did it take so long for Sean Payton to embrace what all of Broncos Country knew early in the 1st quarter? Coleman was unable to hide his ’it’ factor just as much as Dobbins couldn’t contain the ‘not-it’ oozing from his every pore. Sure, Dobbins is a seasoned veteran who has earned every amount of respect and efference he’s been given, but in the face of the 100+ yards that Coleman produced (especially with carries primarily given to him in the second-half), there is no putting the toothpaste back in the tube. Jonah Coleman is the Broncos future at running back. This doesn’t mean that Dobbins shouldn’t play, be released, or anything like that. If anything, having an explosive playmaker like Coleman in the backfield is a good thing for him. With Coleman, defenses will have to show a greater respect the run and that will translate to better opportunities on the ground (and not to mention in the air) when Dobbins is in. With RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie on IR, it’s going to be the Coleman-Dobbins show for the foreseeable future (barring some blockbuster move as we close in on the NFL trade deadline). Broncos Country saw what JK Dobbins was capable of during a solid performance before being injured last season. While he’s struggled to regain that form and dominance this season, it’s not impossible to think that he can’t regain some of that form in the coming weeks. That Kansas City defense, with all the deflected balls and constant pressure Bo Nix endured, managed to play the Broncos as tough as anyone with Dobbins being the primary victim. The Broncos schedule gets less difficult going forward and with opposing teams keying in on Coleman, Dobbins might find some opportunities to get his game going. However, that maturation will be up to Dobbins. The Broncos have found their star back and it’s Jonah Coleman. Will Dobbins shrink and pout in the face of competition or will he jump in and embrace the future with both legs churning? The future of the Broncos running attack is looking exceptionally bright. Dobbins will have to find a way to complement that or he’ll end up watching from the sideline.

Rookie Jimmy Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury, while Jack Campbell remains in the hospital […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - OCTOBER 11: K.J. Britt #35 of the New England Patriots reacts during the fourth quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders at Gillette Stadium on October 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to a report from ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Detroit Lions are signing veteran linebacker K.J. Britt off of the New England Patriots’ practice squad. The move comes after Detroit suffered two linebacker injuries on Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings. Rookie Jimmy Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury , while Jack Campbell remains in the hospital with a neck injury . No specifics are known at this point about Campbell’s situation, but the team did say that early developments were “positive.” Britt was a fifth-round draft pick for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2021, and ended up playing 59 games for them over four seasons—including 15 starts. Last year, he was with the Miami Dolphins, playing in all 17 games and starting one. This year, he failed to make the Patriots’ 53-man roster, but they kept him around on the practice squad, and he was elevated for the team’s Week 5 game against the Raiders. For most of his career, Britt has served as a special teamer. Across just over five seasons in the NFL, Britt has played 1,303 special teams snaps vs. 994 on defense—and he has logged over 250 special teams snaps in four of his first five NFL seasons. There’s a good chance that will be Britt’s role early in Detroit. With the Lions likely to lean more heavily on the likes of Malcolm Rodriguez, Derrick Barnes, and Trevor Nowaske on defense—with potentially Amen Ogbongbemiga and Joe Bachie mixed in—the Lions will need more experienced depth on special teams and reserves on defense. Britt should be a relatively good fit in Detroit, as a high-effort player who was a captain at Auburn. #GoBucs coach Bruce Arians said that 5th-round pick K.J. Britt "looks like a football player, he walks like one, he talks like one. He’s a captain." The former #Auburn LB @K_Britt10 describes his leadership style: pic.twitter.com/9frvWPxlLW — Kyle Burger (@kyle_burger) May 16, 2021 Detroit should have a good handle on who Britt is as a person and player, as he overlapped with current Lions defensive line coach Kacy Rodgers during his entire time with the Buccaneers.

title: Detroit Lions Week 8 snap counts: How the defense adjusted to multiple injuries
summary: In Week 8, the Detroit Lions moved to 5-2 on the season and 2-0 in the NFC North after taking down the NFL’s last remaining undefeated team: the division rival Minnesota Vikings. Let’s look at the snap counts from this game and see what they mean for the depth chart hierarchy and what we can […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 1: Derrick Moore #8 and Jimmy Rolder #41 of the Detroit Lions celebrate after a sack during the third quarter against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field on November 1, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images In Week 8, the Detroit Lions moved to 5-2 on the season and 2-0 in the NFC North after taking down the NFL’s last remaining undefeated team: the division rival Minnesota Vikings. Let’s look at the snap counts from this game and see what they mean for the depth chart hierarchy and what we can ascertain moving forward. Quarterback Jared Goff: 72 (100%) Josh Dobbs: DNP If you just looked at the box score, you may think Goff was not his usual self, but he showed tremendous poise under consistent pressure—the Vikings blitzed nearly 90% of the time—and kept his head when it mattered. Running back Jahmyr Gibbs: 55 (76%) Sione Vaki: 20 (28%) — 16 special teams snaps (70%) Jacob Saylors: 0 (0%) — 7 (30%) — Injured (neck) Whew, what a game. The Lions ran the ball 16 times for 66 yards in the first half, with Gibbs accounting for 37 yards on 11 carries (3.4 yards per carry), while Vaki had five runs for 29 yards (5.8 ypc). But the dedication to the run game, coupled with more inside trap plays, opened things up in the second half, as Gibbs took his 12 carries for 116 yards (9.7 ypc) and Vaki delivered 36 yards on six carries (6.0 ypc). Gibbs will be all over the highlight reels this week—and deservedly so—but it’s important not to overlook the “huge step” Vaki took in this game and why he was able to earn “a lot of trust” with this coaching staff . Vaki consistently gained positive yardage on his runs, which allowed the Lions to scale back Gibbs’ workload and should give the Lions tremendous confidence moving forward that they have two legitimate options in the backfield. Wide receiver Jameson Williams: 60 (83%) Amon-Ra St. Brown: 52 (72%) Isaac TeSlaa: 26 (36%) Tay Martin: 2 (3%) — 16 (70%) DeAndre Carter: 0 (0%) — 8 (35%) Despite playing the No. 1 defense in the NFL, it was rinse and repeat for the Lions receivers. Their offensive splits and contributions were close to their season average—TeSlaa’s was scaled back a bit due to the Lions’ two tight end sets—as St. Brown was the volume option, Williams was the deep threat (he has a 46-yard reception), and all three were smashing people in the run game. St. Brown’s arena football formation was technically considered a run because Goff threw the ball slightly backward, which gave the Lions another 10 yards to their rushing totals. Kids across Michigan are about to be lining up like this on playgrounds across the state. Amon-Ra St. Brown got a HUGE running start pic.twitter.com/yUUX9nwnra — Brad Galli (@BradGalli) November 1, 2026 Tight end Sam LaPorta: 67 (93%) Brock Wright: 55 (76%) — 5 (22%) Tyler Conklin: 22 (31%) — 1 (4%) Jackson Meeks: DNP ( INACTIVE ) The NFL has struggled with the Vikings’ “double mug” blitzing concepts for some time now, but Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing unlocked the puzzle by deploying two tight ends in the backfield—LaPorta and Wright—and running an inside trap blocking scheme. This unique wrinkle complicated the Vikings’ aggressive approach by countering with their own aggressive downhill blocking and shifting the “gaps” of the Lions’ front. Lions used their TEs in the backfield very effectively today against the Vikings defense. Adding and changing gaps for the defense to account for to get to zone runs and change-ups off of that. The sidecar look on the first few clips has seen an uptick in the NFL the past month pic.twitter.com/7iTkKJ7pLz — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) November 1, 2026 With the Lions finding success in this approach and leaning into it in the second half, Wright saw his highest number of offensive snaps since Week 11 of last season. Additionally, according to The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy, the Lions saw a large uptick in 13 personnel (three tight end sets) , utilizing the formation 16 times against the Vikings (previously they used it 19 times through the first seven weeks) and had a success rate of 73.7%. Offensive line LG Christian Mahogany: 72 (100%) — 4 (17%) RG Tate Ratledge: 72 (100%) — 4 (17%) RT Blake Miller: 72 (100%) — 4 (17%) LT Penei Sewell: 72 (100%) C Juice Scruggs: 50 (69%) — 4 (17%) C Cade Mays: 22 (31%) — Injured (ankle) LT/6th OL: Larry Borom: 1 (1%) — 4 (17%) RG Miles Frazier: 0 (0%) — 4 (17%) C Seth McLaughlin: DNP ( INACTIVE ) The Lions offensive line had a strong game, showing flashes of dominance in the fourth quarter that should remind fans of the 2023 unit that bullied teams. While Sewell was flagged for four penalties, he was a monster in the rushing attack, and the Lions ran behind him all game. The guards continue to excel and improve, while Miller remains steady, which is all you can ask from a rookie against the Vikings’ confusing front. Mays continued to shine since his return, but an early injury knocked him out of the game, and Scruggs stepped back into a starting center role. While the Lions’ run game took off after Scruggs entered the game, I believe that was more due to a second-half shift in blocking philosophy, but that shouldn’t discount Scruggs’ impact, as it’s an incredible luxury to have a player who can seamlessly step in and help the OL dominate. title: Detroit Lions injury updates on 6 players; Jimmy Rolder’s rookie season is over
summary: The Detroit Lions earned a crucial Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings, but several players suffered notable injuries that will carry into the upcoming week and beyond. All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell’s neck injury is the most significant and concerning, and we have the latest updates on his status as well as the latest quotes […]
full_text: Nov 1, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray (1) is sacked by Detroit Lions defensive lineman Jimmy Rolder (41) during the third quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions earned a crucial Week 8 win over the Minnesota Vikings, but several players suffered notable injuries that will carry into the upcoming week and beyond. All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell’s neck injury is the most significant and concerning, and we have the latest updates on his status as well as the latest quotes from coach Dan Campbell in separate pieces. However, six other players were injured and exited last Sunday’s game, and on Monday, coach Campbell updated everyone’s status. LB Jimmy Rolder (hamstring) — may require surgery; his rookie season is over On the same play that injured Campbell, Rolder went down behind the play and was noticeably frustrated, pounding the turf several times. Rolder exited the field under his own power but walked with a considerable limp and was ruled out of the game soon after. On Monday, Campbell said Rolder’s injury could potentially require surgery and was significant enough that it’s clear that “he’ll be out for the season.” After starting the season working his way back from a hamstring injury, Rolder was slowly acclimating to the NFL and was appearing in just his fifth game as a professional. On Sunday, he saw the most snaps of his young career, registering his first career sack and his third tackle for loss of the season. Unfortunately, he’ll now begin another recovery process and will have his eyes set on 2027. D.J.Wonnum and Brian Branch — In the NFL’s concussion protocol Wonnum and Branch were injured while making a tackle in the first half of last Sunday’s game, and both were removed from the field to be examined for concussions. While Branch was able to walk to the locker room with a trainer, Wonnum required the cart to travel back to the locker room. On Monday, Campbell noted that both players are in the NFL’s concussion protocol and will need to complete the steps for recovery before they’re able to return to the field. Fortunately, while Wonnum needed additional support to exit the field, Campbell said he doesn’t appear his concussion is any worse, or better, than concussions other players have suffered. “He and Branch are both in concussion protocol. I really don’t have anything else to (add). I wouldn’t say it was any better or any worse than a concussion anyone else has had, really. So I really can’t swing one way or another for you there—with either he or BB [Branch]. We won’t know until they (progress through the protocols). Today wasn’t a negative, so you go through the next day and see what happens. So, we’ll see.” The NFL’s concussion protocols move in slow incremental steps. Players must pass a series of tests established by the NFL and prove they don’t show any flagged symptoms the following day. The process also includes returning to practice, passing a series of steps, and finally passing a series of medical tests performed by an independent medical professional. So while Campbell noted that they passed the initial step of the protocol process, they still have several other steps to progress through before being cleared to play. C Cade Mays (ankle) — Report: low ankle injury On Monday, NFL insider Jeremy Fowler reported that Mays’ injury was a “low ankle sprain,” and when Campbell addressed the injury at his press conference, he said, “I don’t see him practicing Wednesday,” but did not address a projection beyond that. As a general rule, a “low” ankle injury can last anywhere from one to six weeks, while “high” ankle sprains tend to last six to 12 weeks, so early indications are positive based on historical trends. CB D.J. Reed (hip) — Will not practice to start the week Like Mays, Campbell noted that “I don’t see (Reed) practicing Wednesday,” as he works through a hip injury. On a positive note, Reed was made available to the media in the locker room after the game, something that typically indicates a player does not have a long-term injury. During that session, Reed said he was feeling OK post-game and that the secondary’s rotation has helped the team prepare for injuries. “It’s a next man up business, especially when you play a lot of man (coverage),” Reed told Pride of Detroit. “Things happen, and (defensive backs) coach (Deshea) Townsend says it all the time, ‘everybody has to be ready, everybody has to prepare like they’re starting, because you’re one injury away from being in the starting lineup.’ You’ve got to perform, and there can’t be a drop-off.” RB Jacobs Saylors (neck) — Will not practice to start the week We have the least information on Saylors’ injury. When Saylors exited the game on Sunday, it was reported that he was dealing with a neck injury, but we didn’t get any further explanation on the extent or seriousness of the injury post-game or on Monday. Campbell did say that, “Saylor’s has a little something, and I don’t see him practicing Wednesday,” but nothing more was noted.

title: Jack Campbell injury update: Everything Dan Campbell said on Monday
summary: Just before Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell had his Monday afternoon press conference, the team released the following statement on the status of linebacker Jack Campbell, who was sent to a nearby hospital after a fourth-quarter hit resulted in him, initially motionless, being strapped to a backboard. “Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 01: Teammates react as Jack Campbell #46 of the Detroit Lions is tended to by medical staff after being injured on a play during the fourth quarter of a game against the Minnesota Vikings at Ford Field on November 01, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just before Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell had his Monday afternoon press conference, the team released the following statement on the status of linebacker Jack Campbell, who was sent to a nearby hospital after a fourth-quarter hit resulted in him, initially motionless, being strapped to a backboard. “Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital. Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time.“ Campbell didn’t have a ton of substantive updates beyond that, but he did provide some important information. Here’s everything you need to know about what Dan Campbell said about Jack Campbell on Monday. ‘Your prayers are working’ for Jack Campbell Campbell began the press conference reiterating that the initial news on Campbell is positive, and that the love, support, and prayers are helping. “It’s positive,” Campbell said. “So your prayers are working. Please continue to do that. We’ll leave it at that. So, just continue to pray for him, but it is positive news on Jack.” Players and coaches visited Jack Campbell in the hospital Sunday night Campbell said the team is updated on the specifics of Campbell’s condition, and some of them—including himself—were able to visit Campbell in the hospital, and the environment was optimistic. “I got to go see him last night, and it was good, it was positive,” Campbell said. “Got to see his parents, talked to his wife, and everybody’s in good spirits. ‘It’s about the recovery, and it’s a small setback.’ That’s the family. They’re very positive. So that’s good in that regard.” As for the team, Campbell said “a lot of people went over there,” but not everyone got to see him with Jack going through tests throughout the evening. How the Lions intend to proceed without Jack Campbell at linebacker While it’s still unclear what Jack Campbell’s future in football looks like, the Lions will obviously have to proceed in the interim without him, and Dan Campbell expressed confidence that they have a deep linebacker room to get by. Unfortunately, they’ll also have to be without rookie Jimmy Rolder the rest of the way, who suffered a hamstring injury that will end his season and possibly require surgery. “Luckily, we have some depth in there,” Campbell said. “With (Malcolm) Rodrigo and (Trevor) Nowaske and (Derrick) Barnes. Those three guys. And Amen’s (Ogbongbemiga) been up for us, which is good. And then we’ve got (Joe) Bachie ready to roll.” That said, it certainly sounded like the Lions are open to adding some help at the position. “We may need a little bit of help. We’re looking at everything. We’ll adjust as we go,” Campbell said. “(Lions GM) Brad (Holmes) and I will get together here this afternoon, tomorrow, and figure some of this out.” Keeping Jack Campbell in mind while going about their work It won’t be easy for Lions players to be able to be present at work this week knowing that Jack Campbell is down, but Dan Campbell said they’ve already had discussions on balancing both headspaces. “I think we acknowledge it. It’s not going away. That is what it is, and it’s important. He’s important to us, and that he’s okay is important,” Campbell said. “So we acknowledge that, we talk about it, and at the same time, we get ready for this next opponent. I think you kinda do a little bit of both, honestly.” Jack Campbell’s an ‘unbelievable person’ You likely know by now how well respected Jack Campbell is, but Dan Campbell offered quite the character evaluation of Jack Campbell and what makes him such a special person. “I don’t think I can really even put it into words. It’s one of the reasons why—look, you get voted captain. That says a ton, especially with this group of guys that has been assembled. He earned every bit of that. He’s a guy that—he’s trustworthy, he’s dependable. He’d give you the shirt off his back. He’s just all heart, man, all effort. And just an unbelievable person, he’s just an unbelievable person. Down to earth, very genuine, and he just—there’s not a man on this team that doesn’t respect Jack Campbell, care about him.” Credit to Kevin O’Connell and Vikings’ classy response Campbell made sure to make some time to thank Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell for his respectful response to Jack’s injury. “The other thing I want to bring up—man, you go through these games in this league and the competition of it and everything you go through to try and win, and you’re going against an opponent like we were with the Vikings—just, Kevin O’Connell, man, he’s a class act,” Campbell said. “Just looking out for him, checking in on Jack. I know those guys said a prayer for Jack, and that just says a lot about the humanity of it. Man, we are highly competitive; this league is highly competitive, but it is a brotherhood. It just puts things into perspective, and these are human beings that have families, real lives. So it’s just a classy deal, man.” O’Connell opened his post-game press conference Sunday afternoon talking about Campbell. Thoughts and prayers for Jack Campbell 💜 pic.twitter.com/TXvWDla7RO — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) November 1, 2026

title: Jahmyr Gibbs is the NFL MVP, so far
summary: The Detroit Lions’ victory over the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8 will be a memorable one for the 2026 season. It moved the Lions into a game behind the Vikings for the lead in the NFC North, keeping them at a perfect 2-0 in all-important divisional games. It allowed the 1972 Miami Dolphins to pop […]
full_text: Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) runs against Minnesota Vikings during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Detroit Lions’ victory over the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8 will be a memorable one for the 2026 season. It moved the Lions into a game behind the Vikings for the lead in the NFC North, keeping them at a perfect 2-0 in all-important divisional games. It allowed the 1972 Miami Dolphins to pop the cork on their celebratory champagne as the league’s only undefeated team. And it also set the stage for the NFL to have its first running back since 2012 to claim the league’s MVP award. Jahmyr Gibbs is the best running back in the NFL, and if he’s going to keep doing what he’s been doing over these first couple of months, he should end up being the MVP. If you’re over the age of 40, congratulations, you’ve been gifted—blessed—the unique opportunity to see two of the best running backs in NFL history. I’ve been done with tiptoeing around the comparisons to Barry Sanders—he’s doing stuff like this on a weekly basis: A ridiculous run by Jahmyr Gibbs with some help from a Jared Goff block! MINvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mF4E23wbH9 — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 But it’s not just the highlight plays that paint him as the heir apparent to Sanders; you see it in the numbers, too. Gibbs sports the fourth-best success rate among running backs at 48.4% across 157 carries, but he also has the most stuffed runs—rushes that result in gains of zero or negative yardage—in the NFL (33) and ranks 38th among 46 qualifying running backs in stuffed rate (21.0%) according to SumerStats. Through the lens of modern analytics, it doesn’t get much more Sanders-esque than that. Given the sheer volume of his workload, his success rate becomes that much more impressive among his peers. The three running backs with higher success rates are Blake Corum (75 rushing attempts), Christian McCaffrey (84), and Jaylen Warren (119). The preseason comments about Gibbs becoming the bell-cow running back for Detroit couldn’t have been more prescient, and right now, he’s the frontrunner for Best in Show. Gibbs is averaging the most yards from scrimmage among running backs (149.9 yards), and the next closest player—Kenneth Walker—is over 20 yards off pace. He leads the league in missed tackles forced (51) in just seven games, according to Pro Football Focus. Last year’s leader in missed tackles forced was Bijan Robinson at 86. Gibbs’ current pace of 121 would be the highest recorded figure in PFF’s stat tracking history. He has the most runs of 10+ yards (27) and is currently seventh in yards after contact per attempt (3.56)—second in total yards after contact (559) according to SumerStats. But the real measure for MVP voting will rely on the traditional box score statistics, and Gibbs is on track to hit all the benchmarks to put together a special season worthy of MVP consideration. He’s averaging over 110 rushing yards per game and on pace for nearly 1,900 rushing yards, which really helps put 2,000 yards in perspective given how incredible Gibbs has been. He’s averaging over a touchdown per game (1.4) and on pace for 24 total touchdowns—the highest mark since LaDainian Tomlinson set the single-season record 20 years ago with 31 en route to his MVP award. If it’s not rewriting the history books like LT in 2006, it takes absurd numbers plus a narrative for a running back to win the award. Adrian Peterson’s 2012 season, where he carried a deeply flawed Vikings offense to the playoffs by rushing for 2,097 yards, was the last time those stars aligned. What’s unique about Gibbs’ chance at becoming the first running back to win the award in over a decade is the relative lack of standouts at the quarterback position through eight weeks. Statistically speaking, Joe Burrow is putting together the numbers—first in completion percentage (73%), touchdown passes (20), and passing yards per game (302.1)—but if the Bengals can’t beat out the Pittsburgh Steelers for the AFC North, and if their defense keeps them out of the playoffs for another season, would voters crown him the league’s MVP? Trevor Lawrence’s impressive start to the season includes 17 touchdown passes to just four interceptions, and he leads the NFL in passer rating, so maybe there’s something there if he keeps on pace. If Josh Allen wins the award for his second time in three seasons because he has a bunch of one-yard rushing touchdowns, so be it; at least we’ll know a non-QB will never have a chance to win the league’s MVP moving forward. The NFL has spent the last decade-plus morphing into a pass-heavy league where running backs are sold as replaceable, interchangeable pieces to an offense. Without David Montgomery sharing the backfield, Gibbs is tearing down that narrative. He’s delivering game-breaking efficiency behind an offensive line that’s been good, but not great . While critics might point out that he plays in one of the league’s most potent offenses, anyone watching Detroit each Sunday knows Gibbs is the single biggest key to their success. If the MVP award is truly meant for the player who dictates defenses, transforms and elevates an entire offense, and shoulders great expectations for contender week in and week out, then the 2026 race shouldn’t default to the coronation of just another quarterback—it should belong to the league’s most explosive and irreplaceable player.
author: Ryan Mathews

title: Detroit Lions grades, report card: The run game finally arrives vs. Vikings
summary: Let’s hand out some grades for the Detroit Lions’ gritty 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings. Quarterback: B Jared Goff’s final statline isn’t all that impressive, but he commanded the offense to a relatively successful day. After shaking off a first half of four sacks, Goff successfully avoided negative plays against this harrowing defense. Obviously, […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - NOVEMBER 01: Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) celebrates after gaining a first down during the fourth quarter of a regular season NFL football game between the Minnesota Vikings and the Detroit Lions on November 1, 2026 at Ford Field in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Let’s hand out some grades for the Detroit Lions’ gritty 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings. Quarterback: B Jared Goff’s final statline isn’t all that impressive, but he commanded the offense to a relatively successful day. After shaking off a first half of four sacks, Goff successfully avoided negative plays against this harrowing defense. Obviously, the interception wasn’t on him. You could argue he held onto the ball a little too long in the first half, but the Vikings’ coverage was often very good on those plays. Ultimately, I was impressed by Goff’s ability to stay calm and disciplined despite the tough start. We’ve seen him—and just about every NFL quarterback—get rattled by this defense before, but Goff kept his head, found the open receivers in the second half (7-of-9 for 66 yards, 1 TD) and even threw his body around a little in the run game. Running backs: A+ Per NextGenStats, Jahmyr Gibbs forced 12 missed tackles on his 25 touches on his way to a 153-yard rushing day. But it was Sione Vaki who got a ton of attention for his breakout performance. His 11 carries for 65 yards may not seem like much, but it felt like he was the key to opening up the run game against the Vikings. His downhill running style led to an impressive 45% success rate on runs (Gibbs was 42%). As a team, Detroit produced 10 rushes of 10+ yards against the Vikings—who had given up just 14 for the entire season prior to this game. And a lot of that had to do with the backs’ performances: Entering today, the Vikings defense had just 16 missed tackles on rush attempts on the season In just today's game, they had 15 missed tackles on rush attempts including 12 in the second half (Data: @SumerSports ) pic.twitter.com/iBtQYr611I — Tej Seth (@tejfbanalytics) November 2, 2026 Tight ends: B Early in the game, it felt like the Lions’ tight ends were largely responsible for some protection busts. Sam LaPorta and Tyler Conklin looked directly responsible for one sack each in the first half. However, this unit rebounded in a huge way in the second half. Having one or two tight ends in the backfield really seemed to neutralize the Vikings pass rush, and it opened up some massive rushing lanes, as well. Just look how impactful it was to have some sort of skill position player in the backfield (most often a tight end): Lions had 14 under center run plays today with 2 or more skill players in the backfield. Those runs went for 125 yards, 1 TD, and 11 were successful, per @NextGenStats . — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) November 1, 2026 Wide receivers: C+ Jameson Williams now has five touchdowns in his last three games, as he continues to be a weapon at every point on the field. Amon-Ra St. Brown’s statline is modest (seven catches, 46 yards), but that was on eight targets. His impact was still felt in key moments. Both players were tagged with taunting penalties, and there were times it didn’t feel like they were getting open quick enough. And Williams’ untimely slip on his route not only cost Detroit an opportunity to convert a third down but led to Goff’s only interception on the year. It was far from a bad day from the receivers, but we know they can play better than this. Offensive line: A- It felt like some of the early pressures weren’t on the Lions offensive line, although there were certainly some missed assignments and lost one-on-ones in the run game early. However, everything cleared up in the second half. Despite facing a blitz on 26-of-29 dropbacks (89.7%), the Lions offense allowed a pressure rate of just 24.1%—the third-lowest of any team in Week 8 and Minnesota’s lowest pressure rate of the season. The Vikings’ previous low was 41.3%. I’ve already gone through a lot of the impressive rushing stats, but here’s a few more. The Lions had the sixth best rushing success rate (47.4%) of the week, which was also the highest mark the Vikings have allowed all season. Detroit’s rushing game has been decent all year, but this was the first time it looked like where it was at during its peak days under Ben Johnson. Defensive line: C+ According to PFF, the Lions produced just 12 pressures and NFL Pro had them at a 33.3% pressure rate (14th of the week) with an average time of 3.26 to pressure (third slowest of Week 8). They were fine against the run, but Detroit’s pass rush has slowly been fading a bit over recent weeks. Thankfully, the Lions dialed up a few successful blitzes in this game, and in the rare occasions Kyler Murray was able to escape the pocket, he didn’t do much damage. The interior of the defensive line continues to carry the load. Alim McNeill and Skyler Gill-Howard both had a sack, while Tyleik Williams is a force in the run game and drew a holding penalty. Linebackers: B+ The Lions found a little spark with Jimmy Rolder, who had a sack and a tackle for loss on the game. And coverage didn’t seem to be as big of an issue this week as in previous weeks. While T.J. Hockenson was a bit of a problem, the Lions mostly used defensive backs on him. Secondary: C+ We need to talk about the rebound D.J. Reed is currently going through. He had three pass breakups in this game, and PFF credited him with just a single catch allowed on five targets for 11 yards and an interception. Since Week 5, Reed is the No. 1 graded cornerback by PFF (90.7) with the best coverage grade (91.0). Unfortunately, the rest of the secondary was very up and down. Granted, they often forced Murray to hold the ball long, they still gave up too many big plays and there are still too many coverage busts. Roger McCreary missed a key tackle on Aaron Jones that immediately led to a touchdown. Brian Branch, Chuck Clark, and Christian Izien all had issues on the back end. Obviously, the mistakes didn’t hurt them too much against a Vikings pass attack that just can’t find its identity, but against a better team, Detroit will need to be much cleaner on the back end. Special teams: B Detroit’s coverage units were fantastic against one of the biggest return threats in the NFL. Myles Price managed just 24.0 yards per kick return, well below his 29.7 average. He also didn’t gain a single yard on his one punt return. Jake Bates was okay. He had two touchbacks on kickoffs, although I’m certain the last one was intentional, and his missed his first field goal of the year. But Jack Fox picked up the mantle, putting three of his four punts inside the 20-yard line. Coaching: B+ There were some in-game decisions I didn’t approve of much. At the end of the first half, I think the Lions bled too much clock. Dan Campbell likes to make sure they have the final possession in each half, but when you’re going up against a bad Vikings offense, I think the priority needs to be maximizing your own points rather than being fearful of giving Kyler Murray too much time. I also believe Campbell was wrong to go for a two-point conversion with five minutes still left in the third quarter. Considering the Vikings notoriously score field goals and not touchdowns, being up six rather than five is a pretty significant difference. I don’t think there was enough motivation to try to be up by seven with that much time left. But, a ton of credit goes to offensive coordinator Drew Petzing for a game plan that found actual, real solutions to Brian Flores’ defense. The tight ends in the backfield gave Detroit a numbers advantage in both the run and pass game. Some of the toss action caught the Vikings off kilter, like on Detroit’s 30-yard rushing touchdown. summary: The Detroit Lions may have only scored 19 points against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, but what they were able to do to a previously impenetrable defense was jaw-dropping. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions may have only scored 19 points against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, but what they were able to do to a previously impenetrable defense was jaw-dropping. Especially because going into this game, the Vikings were talked about as one of the best defenses in this league’s history. The Lions’ second-half running game—23 carries for 164 yards (7.1 YPC) and 1 touchdown—not only broke through the 2026 Vikings defense, but they did some stuff that has almost never been done to a Vikings defense led by coordinator Brian Flores. According to Shawn Syed, the Lions’ 16.2 explosive play rate on Sunday was the highest mark of the Flores’ era with the Vikings . According to the FOX broadcast, the Lions forced more missed tackles than any team against this Vikings defense. Colton Pouncy was the first to point out that Detroit’s 230 total rushing yards were the second-most ever allowed by any Flores-led Vikings defense. Or, if you’re a more visual learner, just look at the butt whooping the Lions put on the Vikings via most advanced metrics: my god lmao https://t.co/joOx5v13jU pic.twitter.com/HLwYCqEkEn — Arif Hasan, but NFL 🏈 (@ArifHasanNFL) November 1, 2026 To recap, in the second half, the Lions: Had a 31.7% higher success rate than Minnesota Had 1.25 more points per drive Had 0.765 higher EPA/designed run Had 4.4 MORE yards per carry Had a 51.2% higher rushing success rate than Minnesota It was a truly outstanding performance from the Lions offense, despite the low score. On this week’s PODcast, we break down how the Lions broke through the Vikings’ fortress. We also talk about our thoughts on the Jack Campbell injury, the strides the defense continues to make, and the odd officiating in the game, as well. title: Lions vs. Dolphins odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup
summary: The Detroit Lions (5-2) will travel to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6) in Week 9, in a battle between teams at two very different stages of their roster development. While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they’ve strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins […]
full_text: Aug 16, 2025; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Lions wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa (18) scores a touchdown against the Miami Dolphins in the second quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: Eamon Horwedel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Detroit Lions (5-2) will travel to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6) in Week 9, in a battle between teams at two very different stages of their roster development. While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they’ve strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild under their latest regime. The folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7 points . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. They also have another eight rookies on their 53-man roster, meaning over 25% of the Dolphins roster (14 players) is made up of first-year players. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. In Week 4, they showed signs of improvement, losing to the Vikings by only five points; the Bengals won by just seven in Week 5, and in Week 6, they got their first win of the season, beating the Jets by three points. On Sunday, the Dolphins and Patriots squared off in an AFC East showdown, and while the Dolphins built a 13-3 lead at the half, the Patriots scored 21 unanswered points to go up 24-13 late in the fourth quarter. Willis connected on an explosive touchdown pass at the 2-minute warning to bring them close, but a failed 2-point conversion and a failed onside kick set the final score at 24-19. full_text: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler is reporting that the Green Bay Packers have signed quarterback Cam Miller to their practice squad. The Packers had two openings on their practice squad coming into the week, so the team doesn’t need to make any corresponding roster move to execute this deal. With that being said, Green Bay already had one practice squad quarterback in Kedon Slovis, so there’s a possibility that his job moving forward is uncertain. Miller originally worked out for the Packers in early September, but the team continued to roll with Slovis at the time. Only one other quarterback, UFL MVP Jack Plummer, has worked out with Green Bay since the cutdown deadline . Cam Miller was drafted in round 6 pick 215 in the 2025 draft class. He scored a 6.08 #RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 412 out of 1048 QB from 1987 to 2025. https://t.co/DERSXGeq0I pic.twitter.com/iVLRMNbt7B — RAS.football (@MathBomb) April 26, 2025 Miller was a sixth-round pick by the Las Vegas Raiders in 2025, and the former North Dakota State quarterback spent most of his rookie season on the practice squad. Late in the year, he was poached by the Miami Dolphins, where he spent training camp in 2026 before being released at the roster cutdown deadline. Beyond Miller’s September workout for the Packers, the Minnesota Vikings also kicked the tires on the quarterback about a month ago. In two pre-seasons, Miller has gone 36 of 75 passing for 373 yards, one touchdown, one interception and seven sacks. Here was The Athletic’s Dane Brugler’s blurb on Miller as a draft prospect , when he was graded as a draftable prospect by the analyst: A four-year starter at North Dakota State, Miller was the point guard of former offensive coordinator Jake Landry’s run-heavy scheme (averaged just 21.9 pass attempts per game). A two-time FCS national champion as a starter (2022 and 2024), he set school records for career passing yards (9,720), completions (759) and total offense (11,997). Miller is an intelligent game manager who takes what the defense gives him and relies on timing and placement over pure arm power. The son of a football coach, his mental approach and on-field production showed improvements each season, although he will continue to have his doubters because of the level of competition he faced. Overall, Miller won’t wow you right away because the physical traits are average. The more you watch, though, the more you come to appreciate his decision-making and feel for the position. He can be an asset in an NFL quarterback room as a reserve. title: How will the Packers manage their IR designations?
summary: Each NFL team can use eight activations from the injured reserve in the regular season, with two more in the postseason if teams qualify, per league rules. How the Green Bay Packers manage these returns could define their season down the stretch, as they may have to pick and choose who comes back if they […]
full_text: (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Each NFL team can use eight activations from the injured reserve in the regular season, with two more in the postseason if teams qualify, per league rules. How the Green Bay Packers manage these returns could define their season down the stretch, as they may have to pick and choose who comes back if they have more options than return designations by the end of the season. Let’s walk through the Packers’ options. Brought back WR Savion Williams The Packers have already used two of their eight potential activations this season on receiver Savion Williams and edge defender Collin Oliver, who were both placed on IR at the cutdown deadline with return designations. Williams has already been activated, and he’s currently the team’s starting slot receiver after both Jayden Reed and Skyy Moore went down with injuries. Potentially can bring back ED Collin Oliver (already designated to return – can return now) DL Warren Brinson (can return now) RB Chris Brooks (can return now) WR Skyy Moore (Week 10) DL Jonathan Ford (Week 10) OL Jacob Monk (Week 13) Oliver (calf) has not been brought back yet, but the team has pre-paid his return against the team’s return count with his designation at the cutdown deadline. He’s able to come back to the team immediately, and has been since Week 5. Defensive linemen Warren Brinson (calf) and running back Chris Brooks (ankle) also have missed four games of action, which means they can also return to the active roster this week, if that’s what the Packers choose. The players yet to miss four games, the minimum for players who are placed on the injured reserve, are receiver Skyy Moore (ankle), defensive lineman Jonathan Ford (calf) and offensive lineman Jacob Monk (quadriceps). Moore and Ford have windows that open for their return to the active roster next week, while Monk must wait until at least Week 13. So if you’re counting at home, the Packers have used two of their eight return options (Williams and Oliver) and have five options left for their last six return spots — and the calendar just turned to November. Out for the year WR Jayden Reed TE Thomas Yassmin (reverted to IR after being unclaimed with injured designation) OL Zach Bako-Bewele DL Javon Hargrave LB Edgerrin Cooper S Johnathan Baldwin II (reverted to IR after being unclaimed with injured designation) The players above have either been reported to have season-ending injuries or are players who were waived with injury designations, went unclaimed, reverted to the Packers’ injured reserve and the team has not paid them an injury settlement. That’s a really wordy way to say that Green Bay appears to be squatting on the rights to tight end Thomas Yassmin and safety Johnathan Baldwin II, as they likely want those players to be members of the 2027 roster. PUP List TE Luke Musgrave ED Micah Parsons For the sake of avoiding the “Where’s Micah Parsons?” questions, these are the Packers’ players who began the season on the physically unable to perform list. These players do not count against Green Bay’s injured reserve count. They are allowed to return whenever the Packers wish, at this point in the season. Green Bay has hinted at Micah Parsons opening his 21-day practice window this week, while there has been no timeline provided on the Luke Musgrave front.

title: Zaire Franklin could be back for Week 9
summary: In his Monday press conference, Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur stated that Mike linebacker Zaire Franklin, who has missed multiple games with a hairline fracture in his shin, could practice for the team in Week 9, as he’s “day to day right now.” The Packers have been down both of their starting off-ball […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images In his Monday press conference, Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur stated that Mike linebacker Zaire Franklin, who has missed multiple games with a hairline fracture in his shin, could practice for the team in Week 9, as he’s “day to day right now.” The Packers have been down both of their starting off-ball linebackers recently, as Will linebacker Edgerrin Cooper is currently on the injured reserve with a torn Achilles tendon. Prior to Franklin’s injury, but after Cooper’s, the Will linebacker position was split by Isaiah McDuffie and Ty’Ron Hopper. Post-Franklin injury, McDuffie moved to Mike full-time, allowing Hopper to play Will full-time. The stress put on the linebacker position, a unit that generally plays a significant amount of special teams snaps for Green Bay, has led to the team bringing up Arron Mosby from the practice squad to play in the kicking game over the last few weeks. Beyond the linebacker position, LaFleur had some other comments on the depth chart on Monday. On the kicker front, the team is sticking with Trey Smack, based on his ability to rebound. On the offensive line, LaFleur pushed back on the right guard position not looking good last week, when Laken Tomlinson was moved over from the left side to the right side for the first time in about a decade. At left guard, LaFleur stated that Aaron Banks’ struggles were mostly explained by Banks missing a lot of time recently. 69 of his 91 season-long offensive snaps (76 percent) came last week, as Banks has been dealing with both knee tendinitis and a toe injury in 2026.

title: Matt LaFleur says Packers will stick with running back Josh Jacobs
summary: The Packers are addressing the still-unfolding Josh Jacobs situation by not saying much. During his Monday press availability, Matt LaFleur addressed the additional allegations of abuse levied by multiple women against the running back by saying he didn’t have much to say.   “Obviously, we’re aware of the prior allegations on Josh and we’re going to […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Green Bay Packers looks on against the Carolina Panthers during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Packers are addressing the still-unfolding Josh Jacobs situation by not saying much. During his Monday press availability, Matt LaFleur addressed the additional allegations of abuse levied by multiple women against the running back by saying he didn’t have much to say. “Obviously, we’re aware of the prior allegations on Josh and we’re going to allow the NFL to do its process, but I would anticipate him being a member of us moving forward,” LaFleur said. “That’s really all I have to speak on [that].” Jacobs entered a no-contest plea in his abuse and criminal damage case earlier this year, and the additional allegations came to light after the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department released documents pertaining to Jacobs’ 2026 arrest . The additional allegations date to 2022 and 2021, when Jacobs was a member of the Las Vegas Raiders. Jacobs spent six weeks on the Commissioner Exempt list earlier this season. He was not fined and could still be suspended. The NFL has yet to issue a definitive ruling on his case, possibly because video footage of the incident resulting in Jacobs’ arrest in May still has not been released — and may never be. General manager Brian Gutekunst has yet to speak publicly on Jacobs’ situation (he typically addresses the media just once during the season after the conclusion of training camp), but LaFleur’s remarks make the Packers’ position pretty clear: they’re not going to do anything until the NFL makes its own ruling. Jacobs has been central to the Packers’ backfield operation since he returned, playing more than 52% of the Packers’ snaps in their Week 7 loss to the Lions, then lining up for 71% of their snaps in their Week 8 win over the Panthers. He’s carried 32 times for 75 yards and a touchdown while catching 11 passes for 68 yards and a touchdown in those two games.

title: Green Bay Packers News: Ty’Ron Hopper is having his moment
summary: Ty’Ron Hopper was famously a virtually invisible man for his first two years in Green Bay. You’ve heard the numbers, but permit me to recount them again. Over his first two seasons with the Packers, Hopper lined up for just 144 snaps on defense. He played more on special teams, but considering how many of […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - OCTOBER 29: Ty'Ron Hopper #59 of the Green Bay Packers lines up before the snap during an NFL football game against the Carolina Panthers at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ty’Ron Hopper was famously a virtually invisible man for his first two years in Green Bay. You’ve heard the numbers, but permit me to recount them again. Over his first two seasons with the Packers, Hopper lined up for just 144 snaps on defense. He played more on special teams, but considering how many of his reps came on kickoff coverage and return, a good number of those snaps involved him doing literally nothing as the ball sailed into the end zone for a touchback. Prior to injuries to Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin, there were 21 games in Hopper’s career where he was active but never appeared on defense. In 15 games, he recorded zero tackles — despite being in uniform and on the field, he had the same measurable impact on the game that you or I did. But with those aforementioned injuries clearing the way, Hopper has blossomed. Thursday night he had a remarkable statistical performance, recording multiple passes defensed, an interception, and a sack, an outing only duplicated in recent Packers history by Charles Woodson, which is pretty excellent company to keep. None of this, for what it’s worth, is evidence that Hopper is about to become a core part of the Packers defense. Anybody can have a good game or two; putting together consistently good performances is what separates the metaphorical men from the boys. But this is far more than we’ve seen from Hopper to this point, and, if nothing else, it should be evidence that he can do good things for the defense when he’s on the field. Considering how little he’s been on the field so far, that’s a huge step forward.
