title: Los Angeles Chargers news: Bolts earn ‘D’ in loss to Rams
summary: The Chargers led the Rams with less than two minutes remaining in the first half. By the time they went into the locker room, they were down 10-9. The final score was 24-9. It was another disaster ending to a game in which the Chargers showed “something.” They had three drives reach the red zone […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 01: Head coach Jim Harbaugh of the Los Angeles Chargers reacts after a play against the Los Angeles Rams in the second quarter of a game at SoFi Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chargers led the Rams with less than two minutes remaining in the first half. By the time they went into the locker room, they were down 10-9. The final score was 24-9. It was another disaster ending to a game in which the Chargers showed “something.” They had three drives reach the red zone and they only managed three field goals. That wasn’t enough in a game where the Rams offense was held without a first down until that very last drive of the first half. It’s a sad time when the offense almost looks “good” after scoring nine points, but that’s how low the bar was set after their first six games. CBS Sports’ John Breech felt exactly the way Chargers fans probably did watching Sunday’s loss. That’s why he gave the Bolts a “D” grade for their seventh consecutive loss to begin the season. “ The Chargers offense is broken. This team had a bye in Week 7 to get things fixed, and somehow they actually looked worse. One problem is that Justin Herbert looks like a shell of his former self. Herbert has turned the ball over at least once in every game this season and he added to that total with two bad interceptions against the Rams. It’s very possible that he’s just not a fit for Mike McDaniel’s and if that’s the case, then the Chargers might want to think about moving on from McDaniel. ” Do you agree with the grade? title: Matthew Stafford dealing with elbow soreness, per McVay
summary: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford is dealing with right elbow soreness, according to head coach Sean McVay. Stafford was seen icing his elbow after Sunday’s win over the L.A. Chargers and McVay reiterated on Monday that the quarterback has been dealing with soreness in his throwing arm. The Rams received a mixed bag of […]
full_text: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford is dealing with right elbow soreness, according to head coach Sean McVay. Stafford was seen icing his elbow after Sunday’s win over the L.A. Chargers and McVay reiterated on Monday that the quarterback has been dealing with soreness in his throwing arm. Rams QB Matthew Stafford left the locker room yesterday with a bag of ice wrapped to his right arm. Sean McVay said he's dealt with some soreness in the arm, but deferred to Stafford on how he's feeling — Adam Grosbard (@AdamGrosbard) November 2, 2026 The Rams received a mixed bag of injury updates Monday as they begin preparations for their next game, in addition to Stafford dealing with right elbow soreness, but Jaylen Watson and Trent McDuffie received encouraging updates following Sunday’s contest. Stafford’s elbow is an important situation to monitor throughout the week, particularly with the veteran quarterback continuing to lead the Rams’ offense through the second half of the season. Meanwhile, the Rams received some positive news regarding their secondary, as both Watson and McDuffie appear to be trending in the right direction after suffering injuries during Sunday’s game. Terrance Ferguson also has a chance to return to practice this week, providing another potential boost to the Rams’ offensive personnel. Sean McVay also announced that Myles Garrett (knee) would start his practice activation window (21 days) . Matthew Stafford (Elbow) Stafford’s right elbow soreness will be one of the primary injury storylines to watch as the Rams begin their weekly preparation. The veteran quarterback has been instrumental in keeping Los Angeles competitive, and any issue involving his throwing arm naturally deserves attention. The Rams will likely take a cautious approach with Stafford throughout the week, balancing the need to prepare for Sunday’s matchup with the importance of keeping their franchise quarterback healthy. The extent of Stafford’s soreness and how it impacts his practice participation will be worth monitoring as the week progresses. For now, the Rams will be hoping the issue remains manageable and does not become a significant obstacle heading into their next game. Here’s what Sean McVay said when asked by @AdamGrosbard about Matthew Stafford having an ice pack on his right elbow after the game: pic.twitter.com/7O6WQSFGpv — Nate Atkins (@NateAtkins_) November 3, 2026 Jaylen Watson (Shoulder) & Trent McDuffie (Back) The Rams received more encouraging news regarding two key members of their secondary. Watson, who suffered a shoulder injury during Sunday’s game, reported that his shoulder was feeling good when he came in for treatment Monday. That is an encouraging early development for a cornerback who has been an important part of the Rams’ defensive backfield. McDuffie also received a positive update after dealing with his own injury during the game. The cornerback’s back was reportedly feeling better when he arrived for treatment Monday, giving the Rams reason to be optimistic about his availability moving forward. Both players’ progress will be important to monitor throughout the week, especially as Los Angeles looks to maintain its defensive depth and consistency. While Monday’s updates are encouraging, the Rams will still need to evaluate both players as they work toward returning to full health. Terrance Ferguson (Ankle) Another potential positive development involves rookie tight end Terrance Ferguson. Head coach Sean McVay indicated that Ferguson has a chance to practice this week, opening the door for a possible return to the field after dealing with an injury. Ferguson’s availability would give the Rams another option in their passing game and provide additional depth at tight end. His ability to get back onto the practice field would also be an important step toward potentially returning to game action. The Rams will have to see how Ferguson responds to increased activity before determining whether he is ready to play. title: Rams PFF grades: Offensive line pancakes Chargers in win
summary: The Los Angeles Rams defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 24-9 to move to 4-4 on the season. The Rams have two winnable games on deck against the Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals to potentially put together a four-game win streak and move to 6-4. But before we get ahead of ourselves, let’s put a cap […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams defeated the Los Angeles Chargers 24-9 to move to 4-4 on the season . The Rams have two winnable games on deck against the Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals to potentially put together a four-game win streak and move to 6-4. But before we get ahead of ourselves, let’s put a cap on the team’s win over the Chargers. These are the Pro Football Focus (PFF) grades from the game with important notes. Top five grades on offense 1 – Steve Avila, LG: 86.1 PFF counted four pressures on Matthew Stafford across 26 dropbacks. The quarterback was sacked only a single time. The offensive line was credited with only one of these pressures, which suggests Stafford was inviting pressure with his play. Steve Avila did not allow a single pressure. He was also effective in the run game with a grade of 82.9. 2 – Kevin Dotson, RG: 79.0 Dotson also did not allow a pressure. He posted a run grade of 79.9. This was by far his best grade of the season, which is encouraging because he has not looked like himself. Dotson has strung together two positive performances and could be trending in the right direction. 3 – Puka Nacua, WR: 78.4 The offense runs through Puka Nacua. He caught 11 of 12 targets for 80 yards with a score. 65 of his yards came after the catch point, and he averaged nearly six additional yards per catch. With a 1.5 average depth of target (ADOT), Nacua was doing the hard work for nearly every yard he gained. 4 – Coleman Shelton, C: 76.9 Shelton received a poor pass protection grade of 57.5 with no pressures allowed. He shined in the run game at 79.5. 5 – Warren McClendon, RT: 74.7 McClendon is the only lineman to allow a pressure. Still, he finished with a strong pass protection grade of 70.8 with even better marks in the run game at 74.6. Other notes on offense The Rams had 110 yards after the catch point in the passing game. Matthew Stafford had 157 passing yards on the day. Just 30% of his yardage total on the game were “air yards”, which underscores how suffocated the passing game felt at times. Stafford finished with an ADOT of just 3.8 yards down field with a 2.26 second time to throw. That is about as short and fast as it gets. Top five grades on defense 1 – Trent McDuffie, CB: 86.6 McDuffie intercepted Justin Herbert and nearly returned for a defensive scheme. He made five defensive run stops from the secondary with nine total tackles. Herbert looked his way often with eight targets. McDuffie allowed six receptions for 47 yards, of which 45 came after the catch with a long of 30. 2 – Omar Speights, MLB: 85.6 Speights’ best work came this week in pass coverage with a grade of 91.5. He allowed three catches on four targets for 14 yards. Nate Landman is still the starter in the middle of the defense. He played 42 snaps, and that suggests his role as an every-down player is diminishing. Quentin Lake was the “green d0t” guy. Speights played 35 snaps. 3 – Tyler Davis, DT: 83.3 The interior defensive line continues to step up without Poona Ford and Kobie Turner. Tyler Davis was the emerging player this week, and he ranked third on the defense in run grade behind McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. He also added two pressures as a pass rusher. 4 – Quentin Lake, DB: 77.9 Lake snatched the first of two Justin Herbert interceptions on the day. In total he allowed three catches on four targets for 30 yards. Lake did not miss a tackle on six attempts. He rushed the passer on three occasions. 5 – Emmanuel Forbes, CB: 75.9 Jaylen Watson suffered a shoulder injury and played 41 of the total 61 defensive snaps. Forbes was the biggest recipient of this additional playing time with 17 snaps. The corner was targeted one time and allowed just one catch for a yard, including five yards after the catch. Other notes on defense Aaron Donald, Braden Fiske, and Byron Young were the three lowest graded defenders this week at 54.9, 53.1, and 49.7, respectively. That doesn’t happen often. It’s still encouraging that someone other than the usual suspects stepped up in a stifling defensive performance.

title: Rams finally share good news about Myles Garrett
summary: Myles Garrett will return to practice with the Los Angeles Rams this week, head coach Sean McVay told reporters on Monday. Garrett’s 21-day practice window will be opened at some point this week, meaning that the Rams have 21 days from then to either activate him to the 53-man roster or they will have to […]
full_text: Myles Garrett will return to practice with the Los Angeles Rams this week, head coach Sean McVay told reporters on Monday. Garrett’s 21-day practice window will be opened at some point this week, meaning that the Rams have 21 days from then to either activate him to the 53-man roster or they will have to put him on IR for the rest of the season. If history is any indication, Garrett should be playing with the Rams again within three weeks, and probably sooner. Garrett has not suited up for L.A. since Week 1’s loss to the San Francisco 49ers due to a knee injury. McVay also said that tight end Terrance Ferguson could return to practice this week also. Sean McVay says OLB Myles Garrett will practice this week and have that 21-day practice window opened. McVay also said TE Terrance Ferguson has a good chance to return to practice this week as well. — Stu Jackson (@StuJRams) November 2, 2026 The Rams traded a first-round pick, Jared Verse, and more to the Cleveland Browns for Garrett in the offseason, but he has yet to record his first sack with L.A.. That could change as soon as this weekend’s game against the Washington Commanders. However, it wouldn’t be unexpected for the Rams to wait another week after that, or even until L.A. returns from a bye the week after. The good news is that after almost two months of waiting, Myles Garrett is almost finally back to the field.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Do the Rams have an impressive win yet this season?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have won their last two games to get back to .500, but have they done anything yet to make fans confident that the franchise is headed in the right direction? The Rams have four losses: 49ers 27-7, Denver Broncos 30-26, Buffalo Bills 37-34, and Arizona Cardinals 18-16. The Rams have four […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have won their last two games to get back to .500, but have they done anything yet to make fans confident that the franchise is headed in the right direction? The Rams have four losses: 49ers 27-7, Denver Broncos 30-26, Buffalo Bills 37-34, and Arizona Cardinals 18-16. The Rams have four wins: Giants 28-6, Eagles, 24-20, Raiders 35-21, and Chargers 24-9. The combined record of the four teams that the Rams have lost to is 21-9 , and five of those losses belong to the Cardinals. The other three teams have six wins each and are in first place. The combined record of the four teams the Rams have beaten is 10-19-1 , including the winless Chargers. The Giants are in first place but they have feasted on one of the easiest schedules and worst divisions in the NFL. If the Rams had defeated a team that is good — and they almost did, twice — the perception of L.A. would be different. However, they didn’t and football is a game where your reputation is decided by inches. Do you think the L.A. Rams beating the Giants by 22 points is impressive enough to earn respect? Or do they need to beat a good team (something that they literally can’t do until face the Packers on November 25) before praising Sean McVay for winning the last two games? In my opinion, the Rams don’t have an impressive win this season. If anything, their loss to the Broncos may be more impressive than their wins over the Raiders or Giants. Their loss to the Cardinals may cancel that out. However, we haven’t seen L.A. at full strength yet. If Myles Garrett returns this season, it’s like adding a big name at the trade deadline. Davante Adams will be back at some point. Can the rest of the roster stay in tact when it happens? It’s impressive to not be even worse with that many injuries, but the Rams still need a game where they showed up early and finished off a good team before fans can be totally confident in a rebound.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams see surprising name move up edge depth chart
summary: It wasn’t a thing of beauty, but the Los Angles Rams stacked a second straight win on Sunday, knocking off their housemates, the Los Angeles Chargers, 24-9. L.A. evened their record at 4-4 and while the offense is struggling with finding depth to move the needle for injured playmakers, the defense is developing contributing backups. […]
full_text: It wasn’t a thing of beauty , but the Los Angles Rams stacked a second straight win on Sunday, knocking off their housemates, the Los Angeles Chargers, 24-9. L.A. evened their record at 4-4 and while the offense is struggling with finding depth to move the needle for injured playmakers, the defense is developing contributing backups. One such player is edge Wesley Bailey, an undrafted Rams rookie from Louisville. Bailey’s college profile read as a highly athletic prospect with NFL frame, length, and motor, but raw technical skills and an unrefined toolbox of moves. L.A, started him out slowly, active but only a couple of special teams reps in Week 1, then a lane opened up for him with the Myles Garrett injury . Bailey has made the most of the break. On Sunday he had his biggest workload of the season, 32 reps (52%). For the day, he logged five tackles, a pressure, and had the sweet fourth quarter strip sack. You can see his growth in both game logs and on the field, consistently getting more reps and incrementally adding production. Still in the learning phase, he’’ll need to get get better at setting the edge and dropping into flat coverage, but his twitch and effort clearly stand out on film. He’s proven to be a solid value at the league minimum salary. Here’s a review of the snap counts from Sunday. Players, their snap counts and percentage of play time in bold. Quarterback Matthew Stafford (54, 100%) Stafford really appears to be bothered by pass rush pressure this season and it seems out of character with his fearless, gunslinger nature. He was effective on the quick underneath throws, but when forced to hold the ball and read, struggled with accuracy. The Rams have to figure out a way to allow him time to stretch the field and not let the passing game continue to be compressed. Running back Blake Corum (17, 31%) Kyren Williams (37, 69%) Another ham and egg performance, the duo combined for 27 carries, 129 yards, and two touchdowns. Both have over a 50 percent success rate for the season. Through Weeks 1 through 6, Williams was the clear RB#1, getting 70% of snaps, 64% of touches, and 65% of yards. Now it appears that the two are alternating full drives, while KWill is still getting more snaps, Corum’s touches and production are very similar. Blake Corum with the smooth move and TD! LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YP3lqMMQYg — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Wide receiver Puka Nacua (52, 96%) Konata Mumpfield (27, 50%) Tutu Atwell (21, 39%) Jordan Whittington (4, 7%) CJ Daniels (2, 4%) Nacua (368) passed Robert Woods for #9 on the Rams all-time receptions list. Atwell contributed an explosive play. Completed or not, the Rams should throw 2-3 of those per game, if only to loosen up the underneath areas. Mumpfield continues to be a non-entity in the passing game, getting the bulk of snaps, but few targets and even less production. Whittington’s offensive reps continue to trend down. Daniels got to mop up work as the Rams went into victory formation. Tight end Tyler Higbee (45, 83%) Davis Allen (40, 74%) Max Klare (25, 46%) Tight end usage flip-flopped at halftime. Rams used multiple tight ends on 25 percent of reps in the first half and upped it to nearly 70 percent in the final 30 minutes. Blocking was the word of the day, the unit was targeted only four times with three catches for 28 yards. Higbee had a couple of concentration penalties. Watch replays of the Rams touchdown runs, Allen is a part of most of them. Klare received substantial worthwhile reps, mostly blocking, but he did get out on a few routes. Offensive line Alaric Jackson, Steve Avila, Coleman Shelton, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon (all 54, 100%) 52.6 percent of their designed runs coming out of man/duo blocking schemes, highest in the NFL. On those plays, the Rams put up Top 10 in yards per carry, success rate, and explosive run rate. Early in Sunday’s game, the line gave up a lot of pressure, but settled down in the second half. Coming out of the gate with a stronger commitment to the run game could help alleviate this. Special teams Shaky at best, but with nothing glaringly damaging. This may be the best case scenario for the rest of the season. Defensive line Braden Fiske (45, 74%) Aaron Donald (40, 66%) Ty Hamilton (25, 41%) Tyler Davis (20, 33%) Larrell Murchison (19, 31%) The Rams defensive line is doing quite well making up the voids of Kobie Turner and Poona Ford. Some of it is the level of competition, but good work is good work. Donald is getting into game shape, his pressure and quick pressure rates are rising weekly. Fiske appears to be getting more pressures. Hamilton has raised his play time in three straight weeks and looks sound, particularly when lined up as a nose tackle. Davis’ reps went down from the past three weeks. Murchison’s usage has been edging up since being called up from the practice squad. Edge Byron Young (46, 75%) Josaiah Stewart (34, 56%) Wesley Bailey (32, 52%) Darryl Peterson ( 15, 25%) Young was quieter than normal, but Stewart played better than he has in weeks. Looked very active and provided some nice pressure and run stops. Bailey looks to have distanced himself as E#3. Peterson had a big jump in snaps, but didn’t record a stat. Ball went out of bounds, but this forced fumble from Wesley Bailey was 🔥 LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sJhAgAK9nr — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Off-ball linebacker Nate Landman (42, 69%) Omar Speights (35, 57%) I thought Speight played well for the second week in a row. Landman didn’t have the green dot on Sunday, wonder if this is a one-off occurrence or if the Rams see that subbing him out for big dime personnel groupings is a better against short passing offenses. Safety Kamren Curl (61, 100%) Quentin Lake (61, 100%) Kamren Kinchens (33, 54%) Jaylen McCollough (15, 25%) L.A. is using dime personnel (six defensive backs) packages at a league-leading 43 percent. Lake is lining up primarily deep or at linebacker and playing less in the slot this year. The Rams are doing a good job of getting him lined up against tight ends, a matchup that he’s best suited to. Curl quietly is third on the team in tackles and tackles for loss. Kinchens had a season low in snaps, while his play percentage is down this season, he brings excellent tackle production per snap. McCollough’s snaps were down as well. It makes sense to sub him onto the field for either of the linebackers in any down/distance situation with four yards to go. Cornerback Trent McDuffie (49, 80%) Jaylen Watson (41, 67%) Josh Wallace (41, 67%) Emmanuel Forbes (17, 28%) L.A. has really leaned into using man coverage at 37.6 percent, second most in the NFL. How good have McDuffie and Watson been? Both are in the NFL’s Top 5 for least completion percentage allowed for cornerbacks. What’s really outstanding is their ability and willingness in run defense. Wallace got beat for an explosive, but over his 2026 body of work has been solid. Forbes has found a role as a backup in the the new-look secondary. Trent McDuffie with the TFL 💪 LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/tLUs5vekkg — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Going forward Hard to argue that the Rams have turned the corner. In the midst of a five-game weak spot in the schedule, they are 2-1 and need to finish this track at 5-1. Next Sunday, the Washington Commanders, on their home turf, should provide a test. Standing at 4-4, fans will have to stay optimistic and watch the standings/playoff seedings. Parity will keep the wildcard openings within reach, but the Rams will have to stack wins, ugly or not.

title: Bears can do Rams a favor on Monday Night Football
summary: Monday Night Football brings a double-edged sword for the Los Angeles Rams in the NFC playoff picture. The Chicago Bears will travel to face the Seattle Seahawks. A loss would move Seattle to 4-4 and tied with the Rams in the NFC West race. Both are well behind the 6-1 San Francisco 49ers, at least […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - OCTOBER 22: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after defeating the New England Patriots in the game at Soldier Field on October 22, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Monday Night Football brings a double-edged sword for the Los Angeles Rams in the NFC playoff picture. The Chicago Bears will travel to face the Seattle Seahawks. A loss would move Seattle to 4-4 and tied with the Rams in the NFC West race. Both are well behind the 6-1 San Francisco 49ers, at least for now. But a Bears victory isn’t a straight-forward win for LA. Assuming the NFC South and NFC East are unlikely to produce a wildcard entrant, the Rams are indirectly competing with the Bears and other NFC North teams for one of three non-divisional winner berths. The Minnesota Vikings currently lead the north. They suffered they first loss on Sunday and fell to 6-1. The Detroit Lions and Bears are tied for second at 5-2, and the Green Bay Packers are hot on their tails with a 5-3 record. Moving to 4-4 was a positive step for the Rams. They are still behind all the aforementioned teams, barring a Seattle loss on Monday night. Fortunately for LA, they have two very winnable games on deck headed into their bye week. They’ll face the 1-4-1 Washington Commanders before a rematch with the Arizona Cardinals. And while the Cardinals at 3-5 are just a single game behind LA, they are navigating a quarterback controversy. Arizona benched starter Jacoby Brissett against the Dallas Cowboys. Gardner Minshew provided a spark to lead the Cardinals to a surprising win over Dallas. Rookie Carson Beck could also factor into the starting QB conversation two weeks from now, especially since the Cardinals probably need to see him play before they position themselves to draft another signal caller this spring. It’s still early in the NFL season. There is much up in the air. Still, the NFC playoff picture is taking shape. The Rams aren’t only competing against the Seahawks. They are indirectly involved in the NFC North standings. The results for Monday Night Football will give more clarity. The Bears could do LA a favor by sending Seattle to 4-4 and tied with the Rams.

title: Rams’ optimism growing for Myles Garrett’s return
summary: The reported level of optimism around the Los Angeles Rams and the potential return of Myles Garrett is growing. The hope is that Garrett is back sooner than later, and though he may not be back in Week 9, he could be back any time after. The Rams will likely need Garrett if they hope […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - NOVEMBER 01: Los Angeles Rams defensive end Myles Garrett (95) looks on during the NFL game between the Los Angeles Chargers and the Los Angeles Rams on November 01, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The reported level of optimism around the Los Angeles Rams and the potential return of Myles Garrett is growing. The hope is that Garrett is back sooner than later, and though he may not be back in Week 9, he could be back any time after. The Rams will likely need Garrett if they hope to make a serious postseason run. To be clear, it’s reported optimism with regard to the Rams and Garrett. Until Garrett actually suits up for a game, the team and their fans are going to have to wait. It’s encouraging that the Rams think Garrett is heading back to the lineup, but it’s speculation. The Rams thought that Garrett’s knee would be fine for the season too, it hasn’t been. All this to say that even if the Rams are optimistic, they can be wrong. This is a developing situation as time will tell if the Rams optimism pays off, and if it’s fairly placed. Or, if the team’s excitement will lead to more disappointment as the team, the fans and Garrett wait for him to take the field. LA Rams Get New Myles Garrett Update Before Chargers Game (heavy.com) “Once again, there is optimism that Myles Garrett returns to practice this week,” NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported on “ NFL GameDay ” on X on November 1. “I know there was optimism last week. Much more this week. He should practice and should be on the field playing relatively quickly.” Rams On SI’s Blaine Grisak offered a “key note” in the wake of Rapoport’s latest report. “Even if Garrett returns to practice, that doesn’t mean he will play vs. WAS,” Grisak posted . “It only means Rams would open up his 21-day window…which would expire after the bye.” Rams Head Coach Sean McVay Hilariously Says He Will ‘Crush’ Aaron Donald (heavy.com) “McVay was asked about the play after the game and he said the following: “Aw man, I’m going to give him such a hard time about that. I mean, I saw what he was thinking because it’s going right in front of you and he’s thinking, ‘I’m going to scoop and score,’ and he knocks that [expletive] out of bounds, I mean, what the [expletive]. So, his face he couldn’t even look at me and make eye contact after that.” He also reportedly said, “I’m gonna crush him for that,” per J.B. Long.“ Matthew Stafford and Rams overcome slow start, rally past winless Chargers 24-9 (foxsports) “INGLEWOOD, Calif. (AP) — Aaron Donald sprinted after Justin Herbert’s loose fumble with almost nothing but open turf between him and his first touchdown for the Los Angeles Rams . But footballs bounce funny, and this one skittered out of bounds before the diving, scrambling Donald could scoop and/or score. The 35-year-old superstar stayed down in exaggerated exhaustion, and his teammates applied some fake first aid before the Rams finished up their victory. “Oh man, I’m going to give him such a hard time about that,” coach Sean McVay said. “He couldn’t even look at me. At least we can laugh about it right now.”“ 3 initial takeaways from Rams’ Week 8 win: offense sputters early, defense locks in (ramblinfan) “The passing offense was largely ineffective throughout the game. With the exception of a handful of plays, the Rams sputtered. Failing to attempt many runs early in the game allowed the Chargers to control the clock, double the home team in yards gained, and keep the Horns on their heels throughout the first half. Fans didn’t need that type of scare. Could LA somehow find a way to get back to running the football? 3 initial observations from Rams’ 24-9 win over Chargers 1. Run game fixed early offensive sputters The Rams ran for miles in Week 7 against the Raiders. But against a similarly poor Chargers run defense, they continued to pass. That’s very questionable play calling, as the offense entered the game without tight ends Colby Parkinson and Terrence Ferguson, or wide receiver Davante Adams.“ Rams send Chargers to 0-7 for first time since Jim Harbaugh was their QB (sports.yahoo) “The Rams overcame a slow start to beat the Chargers, 24-9 , evening their record at 4-4. The Chargers remain the NFL’s last winless team, falling to 0-7. After some early offensive struggles, the Rams dominated the middle eight minutes of the game to win an ugly one. They scored the go-ahead touchdown just prior to halftime and increased their lead on their opening drive of the second half, keeping the Chargers at arm’s distance for the rest of the game. It’s the worst start to a season for the Chargers since 2000, when Jim Harbaugh was quarterback.“ Matthew Stafford and Rams overcome slow start, rally past winless Chargers 24-9 (espn.com) “Herbert has thrown an interception in all seven games this season, but the Chargers also struggled to run the ball. McDaniel, who retained play-calling duties despite the Bolts’ winless start, called back-to-back successful flea-flickers to get the Chargers moving toward their second field goal in the second quarter. “I think the turnovers are what’s stopping us, and that’s something we have to clean up,” Herbert said. “When we’re not converting on third down and not scoring points in the red zone, it’s tough in that regard.” The Chargers haven’t scored a TD in their last nine quarters of play, yet the Rams were pretty terrible themselves early on at SoFi.“ Rams Player Facing Potential Discipline From NFL After Chargers Game (heavy.com) “The Los Angeles Rams’ win over the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8 could be punctuated by the NFL dishing out punishment for Braden Fiske . Fiske drew a flag for a penalty that is on the NFL’s list of fineable offenses. During the fourth quarter on a third-and-9 play from the Rams 41-yard line in the eventual 24-9 victory, Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert attempted a pass to running back Kimani Vidal that fell incomplete. Omar Speights was credited with bringing the play to an end.“ Sean McVay’s unusual kicker experiment leaves Rams with little margin for error (sports.yahoo) “Keep in mind, it’s exceedingly rare for an NFL team to carry two kickers. Roster spots are too valuable. But we’re talking about the Achilles toe of a team with championship expectations. Sunday’s results were, well, meh. Karty is still dialing in the so-called “dirty” kickoffs, and two of them fell short of the landing zone — the area between the goal line and the 20 — which gave the Chargers the ball on the 40, prime position to start a drive. And a third kickoff just eked into the landing zone, hitting the ground at the 19. “Probably the worst kickoff day I’ve had since last year,” said Karty, who until this week had been back at his alma mater, Stanford, working on his kicks. “I think I was trying to do too much on a couple of those.” 2026 NFL season, Week 8: What We Learned from Sunday’s games (nfl.com) “ Rams rumble over Chargers in battle of L.A. Sean McVay’s offense got off to an ugly start, failing to record a first down in its first five drives. The Rams finally broke through with less than 90 seconds remaining in the first half on a Matthew Stafford 40-yard bomb to Tutu Atwell . The home squad skated from there, scoring 21 straight to blow out their SoFi Stadium mates. The Rams came out at halftime and saddled up the rushing attack. After just 10 yards on the ground through two quarters, Blake Corum and Kyren Williams blasted their way for 129 rushing yards and two touchdowns on 27 carries for the game. Corum started the second half generating chunk gains, juking defenders out of their shoes. He capped the drive with a 23-yard scamper to give L.A. a lead it wouldn’t relent. Finding paydirt on both sides of halftime seemed to break the Chargers. The successful rushing attack stabilized an offense that was stubbing its toe early. After a wobbly start, McVay’s squad has battled back to .500, with games against Washington and…

title: Josh Jacobs faces scrutiny following celebration in 2-touchdown performance
summary: Week 8 was kind to the Las Vegas Raiders, as the Raiders managed to get a big win and end a four-game losing streak. But let’s see how the weekend fared for a few old friends: Josh Jacobs, K’Lavon Chaisson and Gardner Minshew. Josh Jacobs Score: 27-19 Packers win Stats: 21 carries, 39 yards, 1 […]
full_text: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 8 was kind to the Las Vegas Raiders , as the Raiders managed to get a big win and end a four-game losing streak . But let’s see how the weekend fared for a few old friends: Josh Jacobs, K’Lavon Chaisson and Gardner Minshew. Josh Jacobs Score: 27-19 Packers win Stats: 21 carries, 39 yards, 1 TD, 6 catches, 13 receiving yards, 1 receiving TD Outside of the two touchdowns, Jacobs didn’t perform well on Thursday night. Instead, the talk surrounding the running back after the game was about one of his celebrations. Jacobs was recently removed from the commissioner’s exempt list after getting arrested for domestic violence, for which he reached a plea deal to avoid jail time. After scoring on Thursday, Jacobs celebrated by putting his hands behind his back and having a teammate seemingly release him from handcuffs, sparking controversy. Jacobs said it was an ode to the gospel song, “Break Every Chain” (h/t ESPN’s Rob Demovsky ). Additionally, three more women have accused him of physical abuse , which came to light after the game. "repeatedly expressed remorse" https://t.co/RkuzHhnd6r pic.twitter.com/pIsknGPCB3 — Josh Norris (@JoshNorris) October 31, 2026 K’Lavon Chaisson Score: 27-10 Commanders win Stats: 4 tackles, 1 sack, 3 QB hits Chaisson hasn’t been having a great season with just 2.5 sacks heading into Sunday. However, he lived in the Philadelphia Eagles’ backfield in Week 8. The pass-rusher managed to get one sack and had several pressures throughout the night to cap off the Commanders’ big win. However, he did get flagged for a couple of roughing the passer penalties that almost ruined the performance. Gardner Minshew Score: 33-30 Cardinals win in OT Stats: 17/23, 188 yards, 3 TDs, 0 INTs Minshew hadn’t played a snap during the regular season until Cardinals’ head coach Mike LaFleur decided to bench starting quarterback Jacob Brissett (10/19, 119 yards, 0 TDs, 1 INT). That decision was the difference in the game, as Arizona scored 30 of its 33 points in the second half and overtime after Minshew entered the contest. The former Raiders’ starting quarterback led scoring drives on five of his six possessions to pull off a 14-point second-half comeback.

title: Trey Zuhn III gets vote of confidence from Klint Kubiak after Las Vegas Raiders Week 8 win over New York Jets
summary: Right guard has been a trouble spot on the Las Vegas Raiders’ depth chart so far this season. Through eight games/weeks, the Raiders have already had three starters at the position: Jackson Powers-Johnson, Caleb Rogers and Trey Zuhn III. Week 8 against the New York Jets was Zuhn’s crack at it, making his first NFL […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Right guard has been a trouble spot on the Las Vegas Raiders’ depth chart so far this season. Through eight games/weeks, the Raiders have already had three starters at the position: Jackson Powers-Johnson, Caleb Rogers and Trey Zuhn III. Week 8 against the New York Jets was Zuhn’s crack at it, making his first NFL start, and the rookie played well enough to get a vote of confidence from head coach Klint Kubiak. “I thought Trey was calm in there. I thought he was well prepared,” Kubiak said during his Monday post-game press conference (h/t The Athletic’s Sam Warren ). “That was not a surprise, but I thought he played well. I think there are things that he’s going to want to improve on. But I was pleased, along with the coaching staff, with the effort that he put on the field and what his future looks like for us.” Kubiak didn’t outright say that Zuhn will remain the starting right guard moving forward, but it’s hard to imagine that the third-round pick will be sent back to the bench after his performance. According to Sumer Sports , he recorded three “impact plays”, which tied for the third-most of the team’s offensive linemen and only two behind the team leader, center Tyler Linderbaum. Additionally, the Raiders struggled to run the ball during a four-game losing streak in October, and the offense recorded the most rushing yards ( 95 ) it’s had since the team’s last win in Week 3. Also, quarterback Kirk Cousins was only sacked once on Sunday, giving even less reason to make a change to the offensive line heading into next week’s matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. Kubiak dropped a few other interesting nuggets of information on Monday, as a handful of other highlights from his presser are below: On whether the workload split between running backs Mike Washington Jr. (25 carries) and Ashton Jeanty (two carries) will continue, he said: “It’s always a moving target…Who is playing the best ball at the time. It’s a 17-game regular season where things change every week. (via Warren ) Cornerback Darien Porter (groin) left the game after one play, and his status for Week 9 is up in the air as the Raiders will monitor his progress throughout the week. (via Warren ) Jermod McCoy replaced Porter initially instead of Hezekiah Masses because Kubiak said the coaching staff wanted to get McCoy some exposure, and “that’s going to continue”. (via Warren ) On McCoy’s and Masses’ performances: “I think obviously Zeke made some plays for us. Had a big tipped pass. Jermod, his first action, he’s gonna continue to get better. He’s got plenty of things to improve on, as does Zeke, as does DP, as does everybody. But we feel like we’re gonna continue to rotate those guys through.” (via Warren ) Veteran cornerback Eric Stokes was picked on by the Jets, but the Raiders never considered benching him, according to Kubiak. “I think the Jets had a really good plan overall. And I think, again, when you play defensive back in the NFL, at some point you’re gonna get beat, but how do you respond when that happens? And when a defensive back gets beat, everybody knows about it. But if a guard loses in the run game, it’s not discussed as much. So you gotta have thick skin; you’ve gotta be able to move on to the next down. And so, I’m really glad we got No. 5.” (via Warren ) Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway only played 13 snaps, partially due to a stinger, which the team will monitor throughout the week. (via Warren )
author: Matt Holder

title: Kirk Cousins silences quarterback change talks in Week 8 win over New York Jets
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders entered Week 8 needing a win to end a four-game losing streak and to tread water in the AFC Playoff race. While the New York Jets held a two-possession halftime lead, it was mission accomplished for the Raiders by completing the second-half comeback, winning 38-33. That leads to a much more […]
full_text: (Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders entered Week 8 needing a win to end a four-game losing streak and to tread water in the AFC Playoff race . While the New York Jets held a two-possession halftime lead, it was mission accomplished for the Raiders by completing the second-half comeback, winning 38-33. That leads to a much more positive tune for this week’s winners and losers. WINNER: Kirk Cousins After going winless in October, there were plenty of calls for Fernando Mendoza’s tenure in Las Vegas to begin on the first day of November. However, Klint Kubiak stuck by Cousins with the team still in the postseason hunt, and that decision paid off on Sunday, as the veteran quarterback had arguably his best game of the season. Cousins completed 19 of 26 passes for a season-high 73.1% completion percentage, in addition to 247 yards and his fourth three-passing touchdown performance of the campaign, mixing in a rushing score and the viral “Wellness Celebration” in the process. So, the quarterback accounted for all four touchdowns that the Raiders scored in New York, while also tossing a pair of “big-time throws” for a season-high 6.9% BTT rate and no “turnover-worthy plays”, according to Pro Football Focus . That should buy the 38-year-old at least two more starts with the Silver and Black in the conversation for the AFC’s third wild card spot. Kirk Cousins called this TD dance his "Wellness Celebration:" pic.twitter.com/xztbCkhxSH https://t.co/umKWpl9k3N — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) November 2, 2026 WINNER: Brock Bowers Bowers could probably be a winner every week, but he gets a special shoutout for posting the highest PFF receiving grade (92.2) of any pass-catcher in Week 8 (pre- Monday Night Football ). He did that by hauling in seven of nine targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns, while catching two of three contested targets. For the season, Bowers ranks tied for second among tight ends in receptions (41) , first in yards (547) and tied for second in touchdowns despite missing the first two weeks. LOSER: Eric Stokes It was pretty clear that part of the Jets’ offensive game plan was to attack Stokes in the passing game. The corner was targeted 11 times, seven more than any other Las Vegas defender, and he gave up seven catches for 81 yards and a touchdown, per PFF . New York was able to attack his biggest weakness — subpar change of direction skills — designing several out-breaking routes against him. Stokes managed to somewhat salvage his outing by recording a couple of pass breakups in the red zone versus go or fade routes. However, he had little to no answer for wide receiver Adonai Mitchell, who caught seven of five targets (one drop) for 73 yards and a touchdown against the Raiders’ top corner. Putting it simply, the Silver and Black need a better performance from their best coverage defender if the team is going to be a legitimate playoff contender in the second half of the campaign. WINNER: Taron Johnson Heading into the game, I wrote about how Johnson needed to have a strong performance in coverage to slow down red-hot rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. , who had 11 catches for 218 yards and two touchdowns in the two prior games combined. Johnson rose to the occasion, as Cooper was held without a target and quarterback Geno Smith didn’t even test the veteran nickelback . He may not have made any splash plays, but Johnson fulfilled his assignment by taking away a crucial part of New York’s passing game. LOSER: Run Defense The Athletic’s Ted Nguyen posted a stat on X/Twitter that’s pretty mind-boggling for Jets head coach Aaron Glenn and offensive coordinator Frank Reich: New York had 23 rushes for 140 yards (6.1 ypc), but just four carries for 26 yards (6.5 ypc) in the second half. Also, running back Braelon Allen averaged 7.0 ypc (21 rushes, 147 yards), logging a career high in rushing yards with 121 heading into halftime. In other words, Vegas’ run defense was still awful, and the unit holding New York to just 10 points in the third and fourth quarters says more about the ineptitude on the other sideline than it does about a changing of the tide in the desert. For context, the Jets have a negative 0.12 EPA/rush for the season, according to Sumer Sports , but had a positive 0.08 EPA/rush on Sunday. WINNER: Red Zone Defense Don’t get it twisted, Las Vegas defense still had a bad game despite the win. On top of the rushing numbers above, New York threw for 290 yards and averaged 0.34 EPA/pass . But, to give credit where credit is due, part of the reason the Raiders were able to stay in the game was that the defense buckled down in the red zone. The Jets got down there six times but only converted those opportunities into touchdowns twice, posting a negative 0.01 EPA/pass and negative 0.29 EPA/run inside the 20, per Sumer . Keeping offenses away from the scoring area is still a work in progress, but Rob Leonard’s crew managed to limit the damage enough to keep the offense within striking distance. WINNER: Mike Washington Jr. Was Washington particularly spectacular on Sunday? No, but it’s impossible to ignore the fact that he received 25 carries to Ashton Jeanty’s two. Also, the Raiders’ rushing attack did a much better job of staying on schedule than it has since the season opener. To be fair, the Jets were down their best run defender in defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat, and this was a small sample size of just one game. But given how bad the Raiders have been at running the ball, Kubiak has to ride the hot hand and keep Washington as the feature back until proven otherwise. WINNER: Dylan Laube Laube gets a shoutout for the second week in a row because he’s making a big difference in the return game. He came into the contest leading all qualifying kick returners in yards per return, and increased his lead by taking a 95-yarder to the house, currently sitting at 34.1 yards per return, per PFF . That’s 3.1 yards more than anyone else, and he’s the first player in the league to score on a kick return and the first two to do it for the franchise in a decade and a half!
author: Matt Holder

title: Raiders rally with resurgent 2nd half to ground Jets 38-33 in road win
summary: A tale of two halves. It’s a hackneyed description of sporting events in general, however, what occurred within the confines of MetLife Stadium in New Jersey between the visiting Las Vegas Raiders and the host New York Jets epitomized that classic phrase. Gang Green came out like gangbusters at home going 5-for-5 on each of […]
full_text: (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images A tale of two halves. It’s a hackneyed description of sporting events in general, however, what occurred within the confines of MetLife Stadium in New Jersey between the visiting Las Vegas Raiders and the host New York Jets epitomized that classic phrase. Gang Green came out like gangbusters at home going 5-for-5 on each of its first-half offensive possessions to build a 23-14 advantage at halftime. And after Braelon Allen’s hard-charging 21-yard gallop in the third quarter, the Jets went an impeccable 6-for-6 with points scored after each of those drives orchestrated by offensive coordinator Frank Reich and quarterback (and former Raider) Geno Smith. The Silver & Black, meanwhile, produced just 103 yards on offense and a single touchdown — a ridiculous one-handed grab by tight end Brock Bowers — while reserve running back and dynamic kick return man Dylan Laube made a house call on a 95-yard kickoff return (the first of the 2026 NFL season, by the way) and only possessed the ball for 10:43 compared to the Jets 19:17 time of possession. But that Allen breakaway-touchdown was the last end zone visit for the Jets. The Raiders put forth an exhibition in complementary football in the second half going 3-for-3 on their offensive possessions to outscore New York 24-10 as the J-E-T-S, L-O-S-T a game in which they dominated in the first half. The Silver & Black’s display of resurgence and resilience (which had been lacking in the four-consecutive losses) produced a rally and a 38-33 Las Vegas win to snap the four-game slide and get the team back to .500 at 4-4 overall. “I thought halftime-wise, our guys (said), ‘We’re not happy,’” Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said after the game. “We made some adjustments and the guys just played harder. Our guys kept battling.” Kirk Cousins has the Raiders back on top in a high-scoring game LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jQI5vkJ8Xb — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 With Las Vegas opening up the third quarter with a methodical 10-play, 65-yard drive that culminated in Bowers’ second touchdown (two-yard variety), Rob Leonard’s much-maligned defense held its own against Reich, Smith, and Co. in the second stanza limiting the Jets offense to two punts, a field goal, and ending the game with an interception. That just showcases the dramatic 180-degree turn the two teams did after trading touchdowns at the onset of the third quarter. “It’s just about taking a stand,” Raiders edge rusher Crosby said. “At some point it really comes down to winning your one-on-one’s and outworking the man in front of you. That’s what I felt like we did. We came out with an attitude in the second half and I feel like we played a lot better collectively.” With the defense no longer rolling out the carpet in red zone, Kubiak and his offense led by veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins went to work besting head coach Aaron Glenn’s Jets defense. Another 10-play, 65-yard drive ended with Cousins’ one-yard QB sneak to cut the deficit to 30-28 late in the third quarter. Las Vegas’ ensuing drive after a New York punt was a nine-play, 84-yard end zone visit that featured a screen pass to running back Ashton Jeanty who fell after the catch but got up untouched for a 45-yard gain. That helped set up the Cousins-to-Nailor connection for a touchdown (the tweet above) to generate a 35-30 lead for the Raiders. The two teams traded field goals late in the fourth (which became the eventual final score) and Las Vegas safety Jeremy Chinn made up for a 15-yard penalty unnecessary roughness on his hit on Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson with a game-ending, toe-tap interception of Smith’s last-gasp end zone heave. There’s plenty of areas of opportunity for the Raiders — namely beating a good team rather than dropping bad teams — but snapping the skid with a road win is a good sign nonetheless. Jeremy Chinn seals the game with an interception in the end zone. pic.twitter.com/pvIsIWO9NZ — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Let’s hit the quick slants as fast as Laube sprinted past the Jets special teams on his kick return touchdown: —Cousins is simply thriving in his reunion with Kubiak as he threw three touchdowns and totaled 297 yards on 19 of 26 passing. He was sacked once but continues to be an accurate ball distributor in Kubiak’s Raiders offense. The 38-year-old quarterback even had a unique celebration on his touchdown plunge. —Raiders rookie running back Mike Washington Jr. paced the ground game with 25 carries for 83 yards (3.3 yards per carry average) and a long of 15. He out-touched his much higher drafted teammate Jeanty (two carries for nine yards). Kubiak said after the game the call to put the ball in Washington’s hands was his and Jeanty remains a “big part” of the Raiders offense. —Bowers and fellow tight end Michael Mayer continue to be active targets as the former finished with seven receptions for 92 yards and two touchdowns while the latter had five catches for 53 yards. Jeanty was sandwiched between the two hauling in three passes for 64 yards. —Middle linebacker Nakobe Dean paced the Raiders defense with 12 total tackles. Chinn was second with 10 total stops. Pass-rush wise, Crosby racked up a sack as did nose tackle Tim Keenan III. Speaking of Keenan, he’s every bit of his listed 6-foot-2 and 327-pound frame — if not even bigger than that. —Smith was letting it fly in the first half showcasing that he still can throw a nice deep ball. He did have bouts of inaccuracy but finished 20 of 32 for 290 yards with two touchdowns and a pick. He was sacked twice. His favorite targets — wide receivers Adonai Mitchell and Garrett Wilson — were productive with the former having seven catches for 142 yards and a score and the latter with six grabs for 83 yards. What a throw from Geno Smith and what a catch by AD Mitchell 😱 LVvsNYJ on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cxPa0KclpY — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 —Once Raiders rookies Treydan Stukes gets the NFL speed and timing down, the pass breakups he had against the Jets can turn into takeaways (interceptions). He jumped too early on Smith’s end zone pass to rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq on New York’s opening drive and again on Mitchell’s deep catch (tweet above). Ditto for rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses who also jumped too early on a would-be pick of Smith in the fourth quarter. Quotes of Note “The Silver & Black (were) out. We heard them, they were loud. They supported us pregame, all during the game and especially in that fourth quarter. That was really special, very grateful for our fans. Our players (were) very resilient, played four quarters of football. It wasn’t all pretty, but it’s not always going to be pretty. It’’s finding a way to win.” —Las Vegas Raider head coach Klint Kubiak on the well-traveled Raider Nation fan base who were vocal in MetLife Stadium “I’ve always tried to not ride the roller coaster. But that also means when things are going well, I’m a little more steady. You’ve just got to believe that if you keep playing, there’s a good chance you’ll be there in the fourth quarter.” —Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins on the second-half explosion compared to getting stonewalled in the fist half Up Next The Raiders draw quite the challenge this coming Sunday with the 6-1 San Francisco 49ers. The Niners will head to the desert for the Week 9 matchup inside Allegiant Stadium and come off a bye week. San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan is no stranger to Kubiak (the younger and elder, Klint’s father Gary) and is eager to get his NFC West-leading team back in the win column after being stunned by the Atlanta Falcons in Week 7 29-20.

full_text: (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 8 saw the Las Vegas Raiders get a much-needed win to not only end a four-game losing streak, but also reinvigorate the Raiders’ playoff hopes. On that note, let’s check in on the rest of the AFC West to see how the weekend treated the Denver Broncos, Los Angeles Chargers and Kansas City Chiefs. Chiefs vs. Broncos Score: 28-24 Chiefs win KC Key Stats: QB Patrick Mahomes: 30/41 (73.2%), 321 yards, 3 TDs, 0 INTs RB Emmett Johnson: 1 carry, 15 yards, 5 catches, 128 receiving yards, 1 receiving TD WR Rashee Rice: 7 catches, 53 yards, 1 TD EDGE George Karlaftis: 2 tackles, 1 sack, 3 PDs LB Nick Bolton: 9 tackles, 1 QB hit DEN Key Stats: QB Bo Nix: 20/32 (62.5%), 222 yards, 2 TDs, 0 INTs RB Jonah Coleman: 11 carries, 41 yards, 1 TD, 4 catches, 63 receiving yards WR Jaylen Waddle: 3 catches, 39 yards, 1 TD LB Alex Singleton: 14 tackles, 1 sack, 1 PD DT Malcolm Roach: 4 tackles, 1 sack After the Chiefs cruised to a 31-10 victory over the Broncos in the season opener, Denver managed to even the season series with a huge fourth-quarter comeback. Down 11 points heading into the final frame, the Broncos scored 15 unanswered points to pull off the win. It took a missed field goal by Harrison Butker and a goal line stand to finish the job, but Denver made it happen to take control of the division heading into the second half of the season. For the second week in a row, Kansas City’s opponent managed to keep Walker in check. The running back was held below 70 rushing yards for the second time this season and didn’t eclipse triple digits for just the third time. Instead, the focus was on each team’s rookie back, with Johnson serving as the Chiefs’ leading receiver and Coleman amassing more than 100 yards from scrimmage. KC Next week: vs. Jets DEN Next week: @ Panthers Chargers vs. Rams Score: 24-9 Chargers lose LAC Key Stats: QB Justin Herbert: 24/32 (75.0%), 257 yards, 0 TDs, 2 INTs RB Kimani Vidal: 8 carries, 23 yards, 2 catches, 7 receiving yards WR Ladd McConkey: 4 catches, 86 yards CB Tarheeb Still: 3 tackles, 1 INT EDGE Tuli Tuipulotu: 4 tackles, 1 sack What’s there to say about the Chargers at this point? They’re litterally the worst team in the league, sitting as the only winless club through eight weeks. The offense is attrocious, failing to score a touchdown while Herbert looks like a shell of himself. One might think that would lead to a change at offensive coordinator, but it seems like head coach Jim Hargbaugh is content rolling with Mike McDaniel moving forward. Harbaugh: "Uh, yes, not gonna address… pic.twitter.com/ez8jpkGEB5 — Noah Furtado (@bynoahfurtado) November 2, 2026 Standings Denver 6-2 (+7 point differential) Kansas City 5-2 (+36) Las Vegas 4-4 (-9) Los Angeles 0-7 (-76) In Other Raiders’ Links: Raiders playoff standing gets a boost: Las Vegas is still a few games out of the AFC West lead, but see where they fit into the wild card race after Week 8 . 17 things we learned vs. Jets: “Sunday, in the second quarter, the third-year backup running back returned a kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown,” S&BP’s Bill Williamson wrote. “It was the Raiders’ first kick return for a score since Jacoby Ford did it 15 years ago. full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Drake Maye #10 of the New England Patriots looks to pass while pressured by Chop Robinson #44 of the Miami Dolphins in the second quarter of a game at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins took a ten-point lead into halftime on Sunday against the hated New England Patriots. Unfortunately, they were dominated in the second half of play — being outscored by Drake Maye and company 21-6 while ultimately falling by a final score of 24-19 on a soggy day in South Florida. While losing is never fun, the Dolphins continue to play their opponents tough each and every week. I forecast better days ahead for this organization when general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan is able to infuse the roster with more talent this offseason. FINS UP Our Fins Up player of the week is pass rusher Chop Robinson. Robinson finished Sunday’s game against New England with three tackles and two sacks of opposing quarterback Drake Maye according to Pro Football Reference . In addition to his two sacks, Robinson had eight pressures on the day — good for a 47.1% pressure rate against New England according to Hussam Patel of the 5 Reasons Sports Network. That mark is the second-highest pressure rate of any NFL defender in a single game this season. Miami’s pass rusher now leads the National Football League in pressure rate with a 26.6% mark for the entire year. FINS DOWN Our Fins Down player is Jonah Savaiinaea. Miami’s second-year offensive lineman had been trending up through the first portion of the season when you compared his play to that of his abysmal rookie season. Sundays game against the Patriots was more reminiscent of his dreadful rookie season than his promising second year. Miami’s starting left guard, Kadyn Proctor, missed Sunday’s game due to a concussion, which caused center Aaron Brewer to have to help his replacement, Jarrett Kingston, more than he was able to help Savaiinaea against New England. That was not a recipe for success. While Miami’s starting right guard has delivered massive improvement in 2026, Sunday’s poor showing proves he still has plenty of work to do if he wants to consider himself a quality starting offensive lineman in the National Football League. Savaiinaea and the entire Dolphins offense should benefit from the return of Proctor this upcoming Sunday when Miami hosts the Detroit Lions at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens.

title: The Good, Bad & Ugly from the Miami Dolphins Week 8 loss to the New England Patriots
summary: The Miami Dolphins entered Sunday’s matchup against the New England Patriots looking to build on their first victory of the 2026 season. For 30 minutes, it looked like Miami might actually be capable of putting together back-to-back wins. Then the second half happened. The Dolphins took a 13-3 lead into halftime before watching the Patriots […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Christian Gonzalez #0 of the New England Patriots tackles Ollie Gordon II #0 of the Miami Dolphins in the fourth quarter of a game at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins entered Sunday’s matchup against the New England Patriots looking to build on their first victory of the 2026 season. For 30 minutes, it looked like Miami might actually be capable of putting together back-to-back wins. Then the second half happened. The Dolphins took a 13-3 lead into halftime before watching the Patriots score 21 unanswered points to take control of the game. Miami’s offense disappeared, its defense couldn’t find an answer for Drake Maye, and running back Ollie Gordon II provided an unfortunate reminder that the Dolphins still have some growing up to do. The Dolphins and head coach Jeff Hafley are now left wondering what could have been after another frustrating afternoon. Let’s take a look at the good, bad, and ugly from Miami’s 24-19 loss to the Patriots. GOOD Miami’s first half performance Miami entered halftime with a 13-3 lead over New England with strong performances on both sides of the football. The defense created an early turnover when Jacob Rodriguez forced an Efton Chism fumble with a thrilling peanut punch, and Miami’s offense took advantage of the opportunity with a field goal. Malik Willis and the offense eventually put together a touchdown drive late in the second quarter when Willis completed a one-yard touchdown pass to Malik Washington with eight seconds remaining in the half, giving Miami a 10-point advantage. It was the type of drive the Dolphins desperately needed. The touchdown gave Willis and the offense some much-needed momentum heading into the locker room. Unfortunately, the momentum quickly faded, as did the Miami Dolphins’ lead… BAD Miami’s second half performance For as good as the Dolphins played in the first half, the second half saw the team come crashing back down to earth. Miami was outscored 21-6 in the second half, allowing Drake Maye and the Patriots to walk (and throw) all over them en route to a crushing loss. Maye and the Patriots stormed out of the locker room looking like a completely different offense. The Patriots’ quarterback connected with Kyle Williams for a long 43-yard touchdown early in the third quarter, then led another scoring drive that ended with a two-yard touchdown run of his own. The biggest problem wasn’t that the Patriots scored 21 points during the final two quarters of play — it was how quickly Miami lost control of a game it had spent the first half controlling. Hafley and his coaching staff will need to go back to the drawing-board to figure out how to keep Miami from losing another double-digit halftime lead as the season progresses. UGLY Ollie Gordon II has ugly display on Miami’s sideline following penalty There is a difference between being frustrated and allowing that frustration to boil over into something that costs your team. Ollie Gordon II crossed that line on Sunday. Early in the third quarter, Gordon was called for a taunting penalty after a short run against the Patriots. The 15-yard penalty was crushing, and head coach Jeff Hafley responded by pulling Gordon to the sidelines and admonishing the young player for his mistake. Gordon did not take kindly to that decision. The running back was seen screaming at Hafley on the sideline, with Malik Willis also getting caught up in the confrontation. Nobody is going to criticize Gordon for being competitive. The young man plays hard and wants to win. Those are good things. But there is a time and a place for that kind of emotion. Gordon had just committed a penalty that hurt his team. Instead of accepting the consequences and moving on, he turned the situation into an ugly sideline spectacle. Gordon has been thrust into a significant role following De’Von Achane’s season-ending knee injury, and the Dolphins need him to be productive. But they also need him to be accountable for his actions. Gordon has shown plenty of promise this year — he has the talent to become an important piece of Miami’s offense, not just this season, but moving forward as well. Now he needs to show that he can handle the emotional side of the game too. ___ The Dolphins snatched defeat from the jaws of victory on Sunday against the Patriots. The loss drops the team’s record to 1-6 on the year. Do you think they can get back on the right side of the scoreboard with a victory against the visiting Detroit Lions next week? Let me know in the comments below or on Twitter at @MBrave13 . Fins up .

title: Week 8 Observations: First Loss, Same Problems
summary: First and foremost, prayers for Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell. As of this writing, all I’m seeing is that he was taken to the hospital and is being evaluated for a neck injury. Wishing for very good news soon. When something like this happens, it puts meaningless complaints about the team and gameplay into perspective. […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-OCTOBER 25: Head coach Kevin O'Connell of the Minnesota Vikings looks on from the sidelines during an NFL football game between the New York Jets and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 27, 2026 (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images First and foremost, prayers for Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell. As of this writing, all I’m seeing is that he was taken to the hospital and is being evaluated for a neck injury. Wishing for very good news soon. When something like this happens, it puts meaningless complaints about the team and gameplay into perspective. Get well, Jack Campbell, and hoping for a full recovery. We’re all Lions fans now. Vikings Get Their Reality Check The Minnesota Vikings lost a game they deserved to lose. Our winning was unsustainable, and today’s outcome was predictable once the competition improved. There would inevitably come a time when Flores and special teams couldn’t carry the team to victory. That day came at Ford Field in Week 8. The offense failed the test. We’re now 6-1 and facing considerable headwinds: a ridiculously underachieving offense, a dominant defense that has recently shown vulnerabilities against the run, Will Reichard suddenly missing kicks, and an absolutely brutal upcoming stretch of games. This is not the time to focus on the defense or the kicker. Both will be fine. The former spent nearly 36 minutes on the field. Fatigue lays the foundation for missed tackles, and the Vikings had double digits in the second half. They may also have been (justifiably) pressing for a turnover first, since our offense is about as reliable as a cheap paper umbrella. Jahmyr Gibbs being the best running back in football didn’t help. In the end, despite the Lions rushing for 230 yards, Jared Goff was sacked four times and held to a Vikings-esque 176 yards passing. The Lions were held to 5-for-13 on third down and scored 19 points at home, despite averaging 31 points per game coming into the game. Meanwhile, Will Reichard remains a superhero in my book. Not a concern. Mere hiccups for the king of aura, vibes, and stellar hair. The Offense Has Run Out of Excuses Last week, I gave the offense this week and next against a similarly porous Bills defense to get things right. And by “right,” I meant sniffing 30 points. After another week in which even 17 was out of reach, I’m moving it up. I’m now ready to slam the ejection-seat button. #Vikings offense this season: • 29th in yards per game • 30th in passing yards per game • 31st in offensive TDs per game • 27th in PPG • 27th on 3rd down • 28th in yards per play • 32nd in first downs per game pic.twitter.com/mEIrNzcsEc — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 1, 2026 In 20 quarters as a starter, the Kyler Murray-led Vikings offense is averaging just 17 points per game. He has just 5 TDs and 3 INTs, with two of the passing touchdowns coming because Justin Jefferson was ridiculous. After the Saints’ game inspired confidence, things were about to turn around; they haven’t. His QBR for the Lions game was only 36.8. Nothing looks easy right now. Everything is a slog. The passing game is an occasional T.J. Hockenson seam-route catch that breaks up a series of three-and-outs. Yes, it’s an exaggeration, but it’s rooted in some truth. I was really excited about the Murray signing in the spring because of the dual-threat capability we haven’t had consistently for over 20 years. With a few highlights here and there, that hasn’t materialized as I envisioned, either. Coming into today's game, the Lions had allowed more passing yards and more passing touchdowns than any team in the NFL. Midway through the third quarter, Kyler Murray has 86 passing yards. At some point, it is, indeed, his fault. — The Daily Norseman (@DailyNorseman) November 1, 2026 There are three possibilities. Scenario A is that Kevin O’Connell is putting Murray in advantageous situations to score 24+ points a game, but Murray is repeatedly failing to execute the offense efficiently. Scenario B is that, more often than not, KOC hasn’t put Murray in a position to succeed by maximizing his skill set and adjusting the play calling to his strengths. Scenario C is that it’s a little bit of both. I suspect the last one, if a little bit more A than B. Regardless, the responsibility to fix it falls to KOC, the head coach and de facto offensive coordinator. If it’s A, he owes it to the rest of the team to see what Carson Wentz can do. If it’s B, he needs to swallow his pride, own his mistakes, and step out of his comfort zone. If it’s C, they need to work together to find the quickest viable way to meet in the middle and get things rolling right away. Like tomorrow. Or today. Better yet, yesterday. But what’s with the urgency? We’re 6-1! It’s only Week 8; there’s plenty of time! Umm, no. There really isn’t. Two playoff spots go to the winners of the NFC East and South, leaving five spots for the following seven teams: Vikings, Lions, Packers, Bears, 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams. A 10-7 record might not be enough this year. More on this in a bit. Either way, outside help at quarterback seems unlikely. The only viable plug-and-play trade target is Kirk Cousins. The Raiders’ eyes would light up if Nolan Teasley’s name appeared on the caller ID. They’d hold all the cards, and given our desperation, the price could likely be prohibitive. And that’s assuming they’d even do it, since at 4-4 they’re still theoretically alive for the playoffs in a competitive AFC and Cousins is having a strong season. Hey, if there’s one silver lining this week, at least we didn’t lose and didn’t have to watch J.J. McCarthy lead the Giants to another victory. Next week? All bets are off. You couldn’t have botched the QB situation any worse than the Vikings have over the past three seasons. It’s truly something to behold. 6-4 Incoming? Spoiler for my Week 9 game preview in a few days: I can’t pick the Vikings to beat any top-tier team right now, given how this offense is playing. What’s the point of doing these articles if I’m not honest? There’s a real chance the Bills beat us comfortably in front of a nationwide audience on Monday night. Josh Allen is the most difficult quarterback in the NFL to defend. Playing at Lambeau Field is never easy, and it’s on a short week. Then comes the 6-1 49ers on a neutral field, with Brock Purdy playing like an MVP. Looking at 6-4 on November 23rd is a distinct possibility, and memories of 2003 would shift from a whisper to a bullhorn in all directions. You are what your record says you are until your record catches up with who you really are. I’m afraid we may be in that boat, and I’m not the only one thinking so. Without saying a word, Justin Jefferson’s expressions throughout the game spoke volumes, as did his decision not to address the media afterward. Silence is often the most effective form of communication. He deserves better. The Super Bowl-caliber defense and special teams deserve better. This locker room likely doesn’t reflect a 6-1 team. Right now, the “QB Whisperer” is a 5-star restaurant serving cold pizza and stale French fries. If your goal is to raise a playoff participation banner at U.S. Bank Stadium next September, possibly sneaking into the playoffs and being one-and-done, then this team is for you. If you want to actually win a Super Bowl, something drastic has to happen at QB right away. We’ve already squandered the bye week that would’ve bought us time. If that means scrapping the 2022-2026 modern West Coast offense playbook and starting over with plays tailored to Murray’s unique strengths and comfort level, fine. If it’s benching Murray for Wentz, fine. If it’s bringing Cousins in here before the deadline, fine. The status quo is no longer acceptable, and the excuses jar is empty. Fix it.
