title: 3 new trade targets for the 49ers at receiver
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are working the phones for receiver help. According to Jay Glazer, the 49ers had a deal in place with the Minnesota Vikings to bring back receiver Jauan Jennings, which was ultimately nixed by Jennings himself. The good news is the 49ers are looking to add receiver help. The bad news is […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images). | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are working the phones for receiver help. According to Jay Glazer, the 49ers had a deal in place with the Minnesota Vikings to bring back receiver Jauan Jennings, which was ultimately nixed by Jennings himself. The good news is the 49ers are looking to add receiver help. The bad news is they might be aiming very low by targeting Jennings. The trades have slowed down, and that’s understandable, as Sunday’s games would help reveal teams who are now sellers. Through eight weeks, the sample size is good enough for teams to be truthful with themselves about the outlook for 2026. Yes, that means you, Los Angeles Chargers. Sunday’s games have helped add potential targets at wide receiver. Let’s look at three new names for the 49ers to target. Rashod Bateman, Baltimore With Baltimore looking at a lost season with the potential season-ending injury to Lamar Jackson, the Ravens have to consider moving players for draft capital. Zay Flowers is there to stay, and the Ravens drafted Ja’Kobi Lane and Elijah Sarratt. Bateman signed a three-year extension worth $36.75 million. $16.5 million was guaranteed at signing, with another $3.5 million guaranteed. With only 19 catches this season, Bateman is an afterthought in the Ravens’ offense. Better days aren’t ahead if Snoop Huntley or the emergency third QB has to finish the season. As a separator, Bateman holds a 1.42 separation score against man coverage (25th in the NFL) and a 1.79 separation score against zone. Perfect low-risk, high-reward move at the deadline. Elic Ayomanor, Tennessee The Titans are going nowhere fast, and the future is built around Carnell Tate, with the chance of landing Jeremiah Smith in the draft. Ayomanor is 6’2” and the perfect addition for Purdy and his affinity for taller receivers. Ayomanor has just 13 catches for 211 yards and a touchdown on the season. The 49ers did scout him at his pro days, and they would have control over the young receiver moving forward. John Lynch and the front office should return to Ayomanor and call Robert Saleh and the Titans about his potential price. Ayomanor would raise the floor of the receiver room and improve the depth. Malik Washington, Miami Now, stay with me here. Washington is more of a weapon, like Deebo Samuel, but the young receiver has shown juice, and his speed should be coveted. The Dolphins spent two draft picks on Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell, and the team is rightfully excited about both players. Washington scored on Sunday and has a total of 31 catches, 329 yards, and a touchdown. Washington is more of a complementary piece, which only works in tandem with Mike Evans, but his speed and YAC ability could boost the receiver room. Miami may not look to move him, but the sixth-round pick should receive some attention, and the 49ers should gauge his price.
author: Jason Aponte

title: Brandon Aiyuk hires new representation; aims to play in the NFL again
summary: The San Francisco 49ers haven’t needed to do anything regarding Brandon Aiyuk since they placed him on the Left Squad list in December 2025. That transaction immediately removed Aiyuk from the 53-man roster, and the team no longer has to pay him. Aiyuk’s contract was tolled, or paused. To return to the league, Aiyuk must […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images | Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images The San Francisco 49ers haven’t needed to do anything regarding Brandon Aiyuk since they placed him on the Left Squad list in December 2025. That transaction immediately removed Aiyuk from the 53-man roster, and the team no longer has to pay him. Aiyuk’s contract was tolled, or paused. To return to the league, Aiyuk must formally apply for reinstatement. Per Over the Cap, a “ forfeitable breach ” of contract allowed the 49ers to recover portions of previously paid signing or option bonuses. According to multiple national reporters, Aiyuk is ready to return to the NFL — or at least attempt to. ESPN’s Adam Schefter tweeted that Aiyuk hired Drew Rosenhaus for representation. Rosenhaus said he is “working on getting him back to work and playing again in the NFL.” The 49ers don’t have to do anything. After Aiyuk spent the past offseason in a parasocial relationship with the Washington Commanders, he might not want to go to a team whose season is all but over. Washington does play in the NFC East, and that division is up for grabs. They also just lost Terry McLaurin, and Adam Peters is their general manager. After those social media antics, it’d be surprising to see a team offer Aiyuk anything more than a minimum contract. But it’s the NFL, and the Chiefs prove every month that they don’t care what kind of person they sign. So Aiyuk likely ends up in Kansas City if he’s granted his wish to be released. A wide receiver-needy team may be willing to part ways with a late conditional pick ahead of the trade deadline. The odds feel close to a long shot that we see Aiyuk on a football field again in 2026.
author: Kyle Posey

title: 49ers fill practice squad spot with a veteran wide receiver

They don’t need a corresponding move after defensive tackle Naquan Jones was poached by the Houston Texans. Hodge was released on October 1 as part of an injury settlement. full_text: (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are bringing back wide receiver KhaDarel Hodge to the practice squad. They don’t need a corresponding move after defensive tackle Naquan Jones was poached by the Houston Texans . Hodge was released on October 1 as part of an injury settlement . He played a significant role for the 49ers early in the season. He played 30 of 54 snaps against the Arizona Cardinals earlier in the year. Over three weeks, Hodge had played the fourth-most snaps. At the time, a healthy Jordan Watkins had only played 13. Hodge earned a roster spot by covering kicks. Now that he’s healthy, the 49ers will welcome back a versatile player like Hodge with open arms. Kyle Shanahan will let us know which wide receivers will be practicing this week on Wednesday. There’s media availability for a “bonus” practice on Monday. We’ll get a glimpse at which wideouts are on the field for the Niners. There will be injury updates for Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel, and Demarcus Robinson. If the team is adding Hodge to the practice squad and keeping Brandin Cooks on the active roster, it’s a sign Robinson might need more time — unless there are other roster-shuffling moves to make room for Robinson.

title: 49ers vs. Raiders odds: All signs point to points
summary: The San Francisco 49ers are taking on the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 9 after a week off. The Niners are big favorites in a game that’s expected to be high-scoring. According to FanDuel Sportsbook, San Francisco opened up as 9.5-point favorites with the total set at 51.5. That ties for the highest total this […]
full_text: (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are taking on the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 9 after a week off. Faithful, take 49ers game day wherever you go! Stay connected to the action and share every reaction with fellow 49ers fans on the SB Nation app. Join the live game-day chat Browse with fewer ads Seamlessly jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . The Niners are big favorites in a game that’s expected to be high-scoring. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , San Francisco opened up as 9.5-point favorites with the total set at 51.5. That ties for the highest total this season and the second-largest point spread. Raiders games have been video game-esque. They just beat the Jets 38-33. They let the Rams score 35 in Week 7. The Bills scored 33 in Week 6, and Drake Maye dropped 45 the week prior. Geno Smith threw for 290 yards. Adonai Mitchell was unguardable, while Garrett Wilson had a “quiet” 83 yards. It was a different story against the Rams. Kyren Williams and Blake Corum each ran for over 90 yards. Let’s just say the 49ers aren’t going up against the 2000 Ravens. Klint Kubiak has the Raiders’ offense functioning. Ashton Jeanty was not the lead back against the Jets. Instead, rookie Mike Washington got the carries, with 25 compared to Jeanty’s two. That offense runs through Brock Bowers, who had 10 targets against the Jets. Bowers finished with seven catches for 92 yards and two touchdowns. Kirk Cousins, who threw three touchdowns, has no problem tossing it up to Bowers in contested situations. Bowers has double-digit targets in all but two games this season. He’s a monster, so you understand why Vegas goes out of their way to feature him. The 49ers haven’t covered the spread in a couple of weeks. They’ve also gone under the total in back-to-back weeks. For a while there, it felt like this would be a dead-on over team. Will things change this week?

title: Will Mac Jones be a trade target for QB-needy teams?
summary: According to Ian Rapoport, the Baltimore Ravens will look to add help at quarterback after Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that could sideline him for the rest of the season, and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley will miss an extended period with turf toe. That leaves Baltimore with only a QB3. “I do expect the […]
full_text: (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to Ian Rapoport, the Baltimore Ravens will look to add help at quarterback after Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that could sideline him for the rest of the season, and backup quarterback Tyler Huntley will miss an extended period with turf toe. That leaves Baltimore with only a QB3. “I do expect the Baltimore Ravens to go out and consider some QB trades, and kinda discuss, ‘How bold do you wanna be?’ Do you want to go out and spend a lot of capital for a quarterback in a season that may be lost because you don’t have Lamar? Or is it going to be a stopgap, and then you end up a seller? These are real decisions that general manager Eric DeCosta and the rest of the Ravens brass.” Rapoport mentioned Tyson Bagent, who was the backup for the Bears under now-Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle last year, as an option. He also brought up Jacoby Brissett, who was benched in Week 8 by the Arizona Cardinals. “There are some options. There aren’t great options, but there are some options out there.” Mac Jones has an expiring contract. He has no ties to Doyle and the Ravens, but he has starting experience and proved he can win last season. The San Francisco 49ers still might value Jones more than those on the outside think they should, given how much they relied on a backup in 2025. It’s a move that doesn’t make sense, but the Vikings, despite their record, are struggling at quarterback. Surprise, surprise: Kyler Murray doesn’t look the part. But why would the 49ers make a playoff contender better? That’s essentially the landscape for quarterback-needy teams in the playoff hunt. It’s slim pickings, and that means Mac Jones is likely here to stay.

title: Jauan Jennings nixed a trade to return to the 49ers
summary: According to Jay Glazer, the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings recently had a trade agreement in place to bring wide receiver Jauan Jennings back to the Niners, but the deal fell through after Jennings made it clear he didn’t want to return to the team that drafted him. Jennings, who was targeted twice this […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - OCTOBER 25: Jauan Jennings #14 of the Minnesota Vikings reacts against the Indianapolis Colts in the fourth quarter at U.S. Bank Stadium on October 25, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to Jay Glazer, the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings recently had a trade agreement in place to bring wide receiver Jauan Jennings back to the Niners, but the deal fell through after Jennings made it clear he didn’t want to return to the team that drafted him. Jennings, who was targeted twice this past week and caught two passes for 11 yards — bringing his season total to four receptions for 43 yards — reportedly likes the direction the Vikings are headed and wants to be part of that organization. Here’s what he posted on his Instagram after the Vikings suffered their first loss: Jauan Jennings recent IG post: pic.twitter.com/i2X7nsiqkJ — VikingzFanPage (@vikingzfanpage) November 1, 2026 Here’s what Glazer had to say before kickoff on Sunday morning on Fox: “Here’s a little scoopage that nobody knew. The 49ers, who traded for DeForest Buckner, also had trade terms worked out for Jauan Jennings, their former receiver, with the Vikings. But it was contingent on him hopping on a FaceTime with Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch and saying, ‘OK, yeah, I wanna come back.’ But he didn’t. He actually said, no, I wanna stay here in Minnesota. Hey Vikings fans, he likes what you have going on over there.” Jennings would give the Niners a big-bodied, gritty blocker you can trust on third and medium. The problem with Jennings is that everything shrinks when he’s on the field from a passing-game perspective. But familiarity would have been key here, as the Niners, assuming whenever they agreed to this trade, were short at wideout and could plug and play Jennings in multiple roles. Jennings got into a heated argument with Kyle Shanahan on the sideline in the first half of 2025 . Jennings is no stranger when it comes to wearing his emotions on his sleeve. He had an incident with Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell. We’ll see if any more details come out about this nixed trade, like the potential compensation. If Jennings is the only receiver the Niners are eyeing, or if it’s a player of similar value, then that’s the team telling us they are counting on some of the other injured wideouts to return to the lineup, including De’Zhaun Stribling.

full_text: (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Houston Texans are reuniting with veteran defensive tackle Naquan Jones, per Aaron Wilson . Jones appeared in three games for the San Francisco 49ers this season at defensive tackle after the team suffered a rash of injuries at the position. Jones last appeared in Week 5. But with the return of James Thompson and Mykel Williams, the team no longer needed a nose tackle in the next two games. Jones was with Houston in training camp. The Texans released him in August before he joined the Minnesota Vikings. That’s where the Niners poached Jones from a little more than a month ago . This opens a practice squad spot for the 49ers, who will inevitably feel ahead of this week’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Defensive tackle CJ West, out since September 23 with a bone chip in his knee , is one of the candidates to return from injured reserve once the team returns from its bye. West could return to the active roster, and Sebastian Valdez could head back to the practice squad. Valdez was promoted to the active roster to begin October . You run the risk of losing him to another team, but it’s a numbers game, and somebody will be out of a job once more bodies return from injury in the second half. The 49ers practice on Monday, so we could find out the roster move as soon as Monday morning.

Still, McCaffrey, one of the most indispensable players on a then-unbeaten team, returned when he was clearly compromised: McCaffrey had to pull up when chasing Falcons linebacker Kendal Daniels on a fourth-quarter interception. The 49ers are hardly alone when it comes to putting a hobbled player back in a game. But their almost annual flood of injuries has inspired extra scrutiny. General manager John Lynch, unwittingly, might not have helped matters when he suggested a surprising possible source for McCaffrey’s hamstring discomfort. “If you ask Christian,” Lynch said on KNBR, “that’s just because they dug in it so hard during the game to try to keep him going.”

summary: Mixed into Sunday’s dominating win against the Atlanta Falcons was the bad news of OLB Yaya Diaby sustaining injury. Diaby exited the game with a knee injury with 6:32 left in the first quarter. Following their edge rusher’s departure, Tampa’s defense didn’t miss a beat. The Bucs’ defense was pristine against the Falcons, allowing just […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - SEPTEMBER 27: Tampa Bay Buccaneers Linebacker Yaya Diaby (0) rushes the passer during the regular season game between the Minnesota Vikings and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on September 27, 2026 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida.(Photo by Cliff Welch/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Mixed into Sunday’s dominating win against the Atlanta Falcons was the bad news of OLB Yaya Diaby sustaining injury. Diaby exited the game with a knee injury with 6:32 left in the first quarter. Following their edge rusher’s departure, Tampa’s defense didn’t miss a beat. The Bucs’ defense was pristine against the Falcons, allowing just eight first downs, zero third down conversions, and forcing four turnovers, all while holding Atlanta off the scoreboard entirely. Diaby’s knee injury is hoped to be non-serious, however, even in its non-serious state, Tampa’s edge rusher is expected to miss time . Without Diaby in the fold, at least for the short-term, players like Rueben Bain Jr., Al-Quadin Muhammad, and David Walker will need to step up to fill the void (7 sacks on the season so far between those three). Tampa Bay, their defense in particular, does have a tough stretch of games coming up— Starting with Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears this week. Ben Johnson’s usage of Caleb Williams will certainly test Todd Bowles’ recent success. In four games played this season, Williams has five touchdowns, 1,000 yards, and just one interception. To his credit, Todd Bowles has been on his game lately. His defense has held their last two opponents to 13 points total and forced eight turnovers. The Bucs have rolled through the NFC South competition so far this season, Diaby’s contribution to that in the season’s box score— 11 tackles, 3 sacks, and an interception. The team has improved their record to 3-5 and while they are technically in second place (due to Carolina having already had their bye week) the Bucs officially control their own destiny from this point forward.

title: Do Titans fans believe in Cam Ward again after Week 8?
summary: On Sunday morning, our Jimmy Morris posed an important question to the fanbase. Are Tennessee Titans fans done with Cam Ward? 72% of fans voted that Ward is NOT a franchise quarterback. The comments were a mixed bag of results. Perhaps we should pose the question again following Sunday’s performance. It was arguably a career-best […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 18: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans looks on against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Sunday morning, our Jimmy Morris posed an important question to the fanbase. Are Tennessee Titans fans done with Cam Ward ? 72% of fans voted that Ward is NOT a franchise quarterback. The comments were a mixed bag of results. Perhaps we should pose the question again following Sunday’s performance. It was arguably a career-best showing for Ward against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. Everyone had the Titans getting blown out in this game following the Jeffery Simmons trade. Instead, the Titans traded blows with a high-octane offense, losing 43-36 in overtime. Cam Ward was excellent against an underrated Bengals defense. The sophomore No. 1 overall pick completed 26-of-40 passing attempts for 304 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions. It was Ward’s first-ever 300 yard passing game. It wasn’t a perfect showing for Ward. He lost a fumble on a ball-security issue that arose in the pocket. On a key 3rd-and-3 with under one minute remaining, Ward took a Dexter Lawrence sack that definitely took Joey Slye outside of field goal range. Had the Titans gained 5-10 yards on that rep, they were lining up for a game-winning attempt at the end of regulation. It was still an excellent showing for Ward. He looked like a different quarterback. Ward looked comfortable, confident, and aggressive while operating Brian Daboll’s scheme. The Titans now head into the Week 9 bye. Daboll and the Titans appeared to have figured something out versus the Bengals. The evidence was hinted at during the Cleveland Browns game. They need to continue building on both the mindset and results against a stout Jacksonville Jaguars defense in Week 10.

summary: Yesterday was Cam Ward’s best performance with the Tennessee Titans. He threw for 304 yards and rushed for 41. It was by far the most comfortable he has looked with Brian Daboll as his offensive coordinator. It is hopefully a performance that he can build on going forward. The best outcome for the Titans is […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 01: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans passes the ball during the third quarter against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Yesterday was Cam Ward’s best performance with the Tennessee Titans. He threw for 304 yards and rushed for 41. It was by far the most comfortable he has looked with Brian Daboll as his offensive coordinator. It is hopefully a performance that he can build on going forward. The best outcome for the Titans is for Ward to develop into the quarterback they thought he could be when they selected him with the first overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. Even with most people, myself included, thinking Ward doesn’t have it in him, there is still time for him to prove that wrong. Consistency is going to be the key for him. We saw a couple of really good performances from him last season, but he was never able to stack positive games. It’s a shame the Titans have their bye this week right when it looks like the offense is finally starting to come together. The Titans play the Jacksonville Jaguars, Dallas Cowboys, the Jaguars again, and the Washington Commanders coming out of the bye. All three of those teams are pretty bad against the pass. In fact, the Indianapolis Colts, who rank 12th in passing yards per game allowed, are the best defense that the Titans face the rest of the way. Let’s see if they can take advantage. And one note for those of you worried about draft position: the Titans’ defense ranks 31st against the pass this season. If the Titans are going to win any of those games, they are going to have to consistently get into the high 20s or 30s to have a chance to win. They did it yesterday, but that was just one game. Based on the balance of what we have seen this year, I wouldn’t bet on that happening, but hey, at least shootout losses are fun to watch.

title: Stefon Diggs, Jayden Daniels among best Commanders from Week 8 win
summary: Another victory means it is time to crown the Boss Hog of the week. Marcus Mariota took home the crown following a Week 3 win over Seattle, so let us see where the votes swing today.  As a quick reminder of the rules: each week represents a standalone vote. At the end of the year, […]
full_text: Another victory means it is time to crown the Boss Hog of the week. Marcus Mariota took home the crown following a Week 3 win over Seattle , so let us see where the votes swing today. As a quick reminder of the rules: each week represents a standalone vote. At the end of the year, I will tally up all the weekly winners to crown the official, definitive Boss Hog of the Season. Without further ado, let us look at the standout performers. Here is your first nominee for this week’s award following a 27-10 victory over Philadelphia : Jayden Daniels Stat Line: 16-of-29 passing, 217 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT | 2 carries, 23 rushing yards It was not always pretty, but grit wins games. The first quarter was undeniably rough, featuring a couple of sloppy drives to start the evening. Showing real leadership, Daniels even lit a fire under his teammates after that sluggish start. Once the game slowed down, the offense found its rhythm and exploded for 27 unanswered points. While they did leave some points on the table by missing a few touchdowns, Daniels did exactly what a franchise quarterback is supposed to do. He put the team in a position to win. He was absolute money with the deep ball, going a perfect 3-for-3 on throws of 20-plus yards. It may not have been a flawless masterpiece, but it was a resilient, winning performance. Stefon Diggs, Treylon Burks and Antonio Williams Stat Line(s): Burks: Three catches, 81 yards (Long of 53 yards) Williams: Five catches, 54 yards Diggs: Three catches, 38 yards, 1 TD Sometimes, greatness requires a group effort. With the offense missing Terry McLaurin , the entire receiver room had to step up on the national stage. They delivered in a massive way. Things started off rocky when Burks suffered a brutal drop on third down, but he didn’t let it shake his confidence. He came alive as the game went on, looking like he is truly coming into his own with this team. Burks’ highlight of the night was an explosive 53-yard snag that came while beating elite cornerback Quinyon Mitchell over the top — proving he is turning into a phenomenal reclamation project for this franchise. Alongside him, Antonio Williams proved to be a move-the-chains artist, snagging five crucial grabs to keep drives alive. Veteran Stefon Diggs did what he does best, hauling in a beautiful 8-yard strike for the game’s only passing touchdown. This collective unit played admirably under pressure, and they will need to bring that same unified energy into next week’s battle. Daronte Jones Stat Line: 10 Points Allowed, 5.0 Sacks, zero points conceded in the final three quarters Who says a coach can’t win a Hog? Jones has come under serious fire lately for his unit’s inabilty to put together a complete game of football. Facing a heavily injured Philadelphia squad, this was an absolute “prove-it” moment, and Washington responded by delivering their most dominant defensive performance to date. His aggressive, blitz-heavy scheme began hitting home perfectly, generating a staggering 44% quarterback pressure rate. By neutralizing the Eagles and pitching a shutout over the final 45 minutes, Jones showcased coaching excellence under heavy scrutiny. Drew Stevens Stat Line: 4-for-5 field goals (56-yard long), 1 PAT | 13 Total Points When the offense takes a quarter to wake up, you need your special teams unit to keep you in striking distance. Stevens did exactly that. After missing an early 55-yarder, he showed absolute ice in his veins by bouncing back to drill a monster 56-yard field goal late in the first quarter to get Washington on the board. He went on to hit three more field goals throughout the night, locking down points whenever the offense stalled. In a game where leaving points on the table could have cost the Commanders, Stevens accounted for nearly half the team’s scoring and kept the pressure firmly on Philly. Nick Cross Stat Line: Nine total tackles (5 Solo), one TFL Cross turned in a relatively solid game, acting as an eraser on the back end. His signature moment came in the third quarter when the defense was completely suffocating Philly’s momentum. He sniffed out an in-line blocking adjustment, blew past the tight end and crashed through the line to drop the runner for a massive 3-yard loss on third down. Providing that kind of punishing security on the back end is exactly what makes a true defensive anchor. The Defensive Front Stat Line: Five Sacks, one Forced Fumble Two silly roughing-the-passer calls aside, this defensive front seven played an excellent football game. Stepping onto the national stage without cornerstone defensive tackles Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw, the remaining rotation refused to break. Instead, the defensive line generated non-stop heat from the first whistle to the last, harassing the backfield to the tune of 5 total sacks — one of which resulted in a critical, momentum-shifting forced fumble. Rookie linebacker Sonny Styles also continued his high-impact work, generating pressure and flying downhill to clear out plays. Because it was impossible to separate everyone’s individual hustle in such a unified clinic, the entire front seven gets a well-deserved collective shoutout on this week’s ballot. This team is still far from a finished product, but they are certainly not out of any fight yet. The hope now is to keep this momentum rolling and continue stringing together wins against a highly inconsistent Rams team next week. Cast your votes in the poll below — who is your Week 8 Boss Hog?

title: Commanders injury update: Jeremy McNichols reportedly out for months
summary: The Commanders just got Jeremy McNichols back. Now they’re faced with losing him again.   The veteran running back and the team’s best pass protector from that position is reportedly out multiple months with a foot injury, despite the fact he’s still seeking opinions on how best to treat it.   That news was broken by […]
full_text: The Commanders just got Jeremy McNichols back. Now they’re faced with losing him again. The veteran running back and the team’s best pass protector from that position is reportedly out multiple months with a foot injury, despite the fact he’s still seeking opinions on how best to treat it. That news was broken by Washington Post reporter Tashan Reed on Monday evening. While #Commanders RB Jeremy McNichols is getting additional opinions on his foot injury tomorrow, he's expected to miss multiple months, per source. Bill Croskey-Merritt (groin) is already on injured reserve. Washington's healthy RBs: Rachaad White, Austin Ekeler, Craig… — Tashan Reed (@tashanreed) November 3, 2026 Head coach didn’t spill the beans but alluded to the fact there was belief the injury was significant. “He does have a midfoot injury,” Quinn said in his Monday afternoon press conference. “I’m concerned it’s serious. They’re gonna do some more scans as we get through tomorrow. But it’s enough that we’re concerned today. I’ll give you an update as it goes to Wednesday, but it’s something that the team for sure is concerned with.” McNichols suffered a significant quadriceps injury that kept him out most of training camp and all of the preseason. He started the season on injured reserve and missed the first five games. He returned to play in Week 6 against San Francisco, went through the bye and then suffered this foot injury during Sunday night’s victory over the Philadelphia Eagles . Here are #Commanders RB Jeremy McNichols’ final two plays before he left the game with a mid foot injury The team is concerned that it is a significant injury pic.twitter.com/sbFGN0u9hQ — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) November 2, 2026 That will force the Commanders to add a running back, especially with Bill Croskey-Merritt currently on injured reserve rehabbing a groin injury. He must miss at least two more games on IR, but could be out longer than that. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler are the team’s only healthy rushers, so at least one must be added. It could be practice-squad options Craig Reynolds or Devin Neal. Or the Commanders could look outside the current roster. “It’s definitely something that, once we go through the scans to see where we’re at, we have some [backs] on practice squad as well,” Quinn said, before news of the injury’s severity broke. “And with Bill not available to come back until the [Cincinnati] week, that’s something that we’ll have to discuss and see what the next would be if Jeremy in fact can’t go this weekend.” The Commanders waived sixth-round rookie Kaytron Allen – that may have been a mistake – and had talented, undrafted rookie Robert Henry poached off their practice squad. Maybe in a fortuitous development for Washington, Henry was released by Seattle on Monday and is now subject to waivers. Robert Henry Jr. just happens to be available on waivers as of this afternoon. I wonder in #Commanders will be interested in a reunion. https://t.co/l6Ud5yX2JL — John Portis (@gibbriggins) November 3, 2026 Whether the Commanders (re-)claim Henry or not they’re searching for a backup option, though White and especially Ekeler are worthy of taking significant carries.

title: Washington Commanders Whiteboard: Notes and observations from Week 8
summary: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and […]
full_text: Before the advent of media devices, football coaches at all levels used simple whiteboards to outline plays, map out player positions and explain schemes in real time. Nowadays digital playbooks and tablets have taken over, but coaches still use whiteboards on occasion to impart information quickly and effectively. The following are some quick notes and observations from the Washington Commanders ‘ 27-10 win on Sunday Night Football. Dan Quinn and the Washington Commanders continue to start slow Coming out of a bye week in which Dan Quinn stressed the need for the team to win “ four quarters of football ,” the Washington Commanders came out looking flat to start the game. Jayden Daniels was horribly inaccurate in the first quarter, completing only four of his first 11 attempts for 26 yards on his way to a lackluster first half. Jayden Daniels' first-half stats against the Eagles. 52.38 percent completion (11/21) 96 passing yards 1 touchdown 0 interceptions 14 rushing yards (1 carry) 1 sack against 73.8 passer rating (ESPN) pic.twitter.com/W55LC0FIvU — Riggo's Rag (@RiggosRag) November 2, 2026 The penalties and miscues Washington’s coaching staff had vowed to clean up during the bye week continued to plague the team early as Washington’s offense had 4 penalties, 1 dropped pass, 1 fumble, and 1 missed field goal during the first three drives of Sunday night’s game. The Commanders would finish with 7 penalties for 50 yards in the first half, after simplifying their offense in an attempt to clean up the pre-snap mistakes. The NFL average for an entire game this season is right around eight per team. The net result was a 10-0 deficit to start the contest, before Jayden rallied his offense , scoring 13 unanswered points to take the lead before the half. The offense would go on to score 27 total points , and while the bounce back from the Commanders was nice to see, they aren’t going to win many games spotting teams multiple scores early while incurring self-inflicted wounds at the same time. Despite the inaccuracies, Jayden Daniels has yet to throw an interception this season. The defense had their best performance of the season After failing to limit their opponents to less than 23 points in the first six games of the season, Daronte Jones’ defense showed up on Sunday night. They held the Eagles’ offense to just 10 points, getting to quarterback Tanner McKee all night and generating pressure on 46.5% of drop backs , a season-high, with 10 pressures and a sack coming on 12 blitzes. Washington's 83.3% pressure rate on blitzes in win over Philly was the second-highest by any defense in a game this season, per @NextGenStats https://t.co/LopsRxJsHI pic.twitter.com/lJnegwVm7a — Around The NFL (@AroundTheNFL) November 2, 2026 The defense entered the game without two starters on the defensive line, as Javon Kinlaw and Daron Payne were ruled out earlier in the week. Multiple players stepped up in their absence, including Charles Omenihu (4 tackles, 2 SOLO, 1 sack, and 1 TFL) and Shy Tuttle (6 tackles, 4 SOLO, 1 sack with 2 TFLs). Edge defenders Dorance Armstrong and K’Lavon Chaisson gave rookie right tackle Markel Bell fits all night. Chaisson finished with 7 pressures , the second most of career. Overall, the defense had five total sacks on the night. Charles Omenihu with the big sack on Tanner McKee! pic.twitter.com/LWP4jNzTHD — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) November 2, 2026 Great game from #Commanders EDGE K’Lavon Chaisson (#45) vs Eagles Consisently brought the pressure & was getting held/double-teamed on a good amount of reps #RaiseHail pic.twitter.com/7WFuRMGBMC — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) November 2, 2026 The secondary also looked improved, with Trey Amos playing significant snaps ( 87% ) in his second game of the season. They kept McKee under 200 yards in passing until the final play of the game, when the Commanders allowed a 34-yard pass to tight end Eli Stowers. Rasul Douglas had his second interception of the season, and Nick Cross was flying around all night, leading the team with 9 tackles (5 solo), including one tackle for a loss. Kain Medrano and Mike Sainristil recorded zero defensive snaps on the night, playing exclusively on special teams. What a stop by Nick Cross 💪 PHIvsWAS on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/uVutiv5DS9 — NFL (@NFL) November 2, 2026 While the Eagles’ offense has not been good, credit the Washington Commanders’ defense for getting the job done in prime time. Antonio Williams’ break out will have to wait another week The absence of Terry McLaurin had many speculating that Antonio Williams was headed towards a break out performance on Sunday night, and while the rookie did play his most offensive snaps (83%) of the season, his production was relatively low. Daniels couldn’t find Williams early, with 30 of his 54 total receiving yards coming on a tough reception in the fourth quarter. It was a group effort from the Washington Commanders’ pass catchers, with Treylon Burks continuing to act as a deep threat. The former Tennessee Titan led the team in receiving with three receptions on five targets for 85 yards including a long of 54 yards. Antonio Williams led the Commanders with: 💥 7 targets (25.9% share) 💥 5 receptions first game out of bye without Terry McLaurin pic.twitter.com/hEtwKFSizo — Colin McTamany (@Colin_McT) November 2, 2026 Fun take on 989 by the #Commanders and David Blough 989 is a passing concept with three vertical routes: two outside go's and a middle post. The Commanders adopt it and innovate to get a 54-yard pickup They start in a standard empty look but shift to have Ekeler and Chig both… pic.twitter.com/7q85er8jYj — Grant Mitchell (@FullCommandShow) November 2, 2026 The offense was frequently stopped short of the end zone, although kicker Drew Stevens kept putting points on the board, going 4-for-5 on the evening after missing the 55-yarder early. Daniels and offensive coordinator David Blough were able to a secure a touchdown in the second quarter using a variation of the bunch set they showed on Stefon Diggs’ Week 1 touchdown. Eventually, Rachaad White would also punch in a rushing touchdown at the end of the game. Liked this from David Blough: 1st clip – Diggs TD from Week 1 vs Eagles. Bunch set, set up for Diggs to win inside on a quick seam. 2nd clip – Diggs TD from last night vs Eagles. Same set up, Diggs fakes the quick seam, takes off on a fade pic.twitter.com/XyJu51wH0R — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) November 2, 2026 Rachaad White punches it in for his first rushing touchdown for the Commanders! pic.twitter.com/il7kvzvw5z — COMMANDERS FOOTBALL (@HogsHaven) November 2, 2026 How meaningful was this win for the Washington Commanders? The Philadelphia Eagles were missing several key players that contributed to their poor performance, but Washington was missing several important pieces of their own, including Laremy Tunsil, Terry McLaurin, Bill Croskey-Merritt and Daron Payne. While this helps to keep the Commanders’ win in perspective, it won’t score the team any points going forward. In some many ways, the Commanders’ victory met the bare minimum requirements of what needed to happen Sunday night. It was nice to see the secondary gel and the defensive line finally generate some pressure, but the team continues to suffer from slow starts, penalties, and undisciplined play. While the win preserved the possibility of claiming the division crown in a weak NFC East, Dan Quinn and his staff will need to do a lot more in the coming weeks to take advantage of the improved strength of schedule ahead. Remaining NFL Strength of Schedule Weeks 8-18 (rest of season) Easiest: 1. Jaguars 2. Bengals 3. Texans 4. Cowboys 5. Bucs Hardest: 32. Ravens 31. Steelers 30. Jets 29. Chargers 28. Chiefs pic.twitter.com/LwZK6u7kYq — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) October 27, 2026

title: Dan Quinn: Penalties kept us from playing a complete game
summary: The Washington Commanders were big home favorites against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday Night Football. Those odds looked silly in the 1st quarter when they fell behind 10-0. The final score was 27-10 after the Commanders rallied to score 27 unanswered points, and evened the series with the Eagles for the season. Washington is now […]
full_text: The Washington Commanders were big home favorites against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday Night Football. Those odds looked silly in the 1st quarter when they fell behind 10-0. The final score was 27-10 after the Commanders rallied to score 27 unanswered points, and evened the series with the Eagles for the season. Washington is now 2-4-1 and two games behind the 1st place Giants. Dan Quinn needed that win more than any other head coach in the NFL this weekend, but one win won’t save the season and his job. He lamented the penalties that continue to be a problem for this team, and said they prevent them from playing a complete game. Quinn said they played 3 out of 4 quarters last night, but he’s still looking for a complete game this season. Quinn was asked about RB Jeremy McNichols who left Sunday night’s game with a foot injury. There is concern the mid-foot injury is serious, and McNichols could be out for a while. The team has two RBs on the practice squad (Craig Reynolds, Devin Neal), and there are options available on other practice squads or in free agency. Bill Croskey-Merritt (groin) has to miss the next two games as he remains on injured reserve. Too many penalties: Dan Quinn on Zoom: "We need plenty of work on penalties, false starts in particular, and corrections that eliminate beating ourselves. That's the thing that kept us honestly from playing what I would consider like a complete game" — Martenzie Johnson (@10zJohnson) November 2, 2026 Pass rush: Dan Quinn is addressing the media right now. He said he liked the way the front seven worked together in the pass rush. title: Commanders vs. Eagles (game two) – Studs and Duds
summary: What a day to be a fan of the Commanders! full_text: What a day to be a fan of the Commanders! In a primetime nationally televised game at home against a division rival, on a day where the Arizona Cardinals came from behind to defeat the Dallas Cowboys in Arlington and the Giants were on a bye, Washington took it to the Eagles at home! It wasn’t a perfect game by any means and Dan Quinn failed to get his four quarters of complete football , but fans will take this win however they can get it. Washington is set to host the 4-4 Rams at home next week before a pivotal Thursday night clash with the Giants. Below are my Studs and Duds of the game, followed by some notes. Studs: WRs Treylon Burks/Antonio Williams: Someone needed to step up for the injured Terry McLaurin and both Burks and Williams did just that. Despite an easy would-be first down drop in the first quarter, Burks led the team in receiving yards (81) while Williams led the Commanders in receptions (five) and targets (seven). I really like what I saw from this duo. Antonio Williams is pretty damn good! pic.twitter.com/0dlUv2iQYX — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 Another absolute BEAUTIFUL route by Treylon Burks – good for 55! pic.twitter.com/b8En71yS1V — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 Nice route by Burks. He’s certainly been targeted early tonight. pic.twitter.com/85Y90kdSdS — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 Burks making up for some early miscues by making an acrobatic catch on this pass pic.twitter.com/z5580LtWEb — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 CB Trey Amos: In his second game back, Amos looked the part! The second-year corner was sticky in coverage all evening and should have had his first interception of the season if it was not for a bogus roughing the passer call on K’Lavon Chaisson. He had four total tackles (three solo) and led the team with two passes defended. Amos almost get the pick pic.twitter.com/ubGuBRj96k — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 This is why is so vital having Amos back! pic.twitter.com/vsLWVHnTfr — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 EDGE Dorance Armstrong: Armstrong had a huge strip-sack of Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee in the third quarter which Charles Omenihu recovered. He had seven total tackles, one for a loss, the sack and three pressures. It was easily his best game of the season since his return, and maybe one of his best as a Commander. DL Charles Omenihu: Omenihu played like it was Halloween evening, as he was a demon all game. He had four tackles, one for a loss, a sack and a fumble recovery. Omenihu with the big sack! pic.twitter.com/k8QnM4naEU — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 DL Shy Tuttle: I didn’t see much of a drop-off at all with Tuttle taking over for the injured Daron Payne. Actually, I think Tuttle had a very nice game, collecting six total tackles (four solo), two for a loss, a sack and three pressures. Tuttle gets a free run and notches his second sack of the season. pic.twitter.com/RsTPyZi4LF — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 RG Sam Cosmi: Cosmi did get flagged for a false start early in the first quarter, but other than that, he was rock-solid, locking down Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis for most of the game. K Drew Stevens: Yes, Stevens missed a 55-yard field goal in the first quarter, but the rookie hit four others, with his longest from 56 yards out. If it wasn’t for his leg, the Commanders may not come out on the winning side of this one. Stevens, who missed earlier from 55, nails this one from 56! pic.twitter.com/42yJKRcNok — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 Duds: LG Chris Paul: Despite what advanced metrics may try to tell you, Chris Paul is a liability out there at left guard. His slow foot speed and reaction skills are putting Jayden Daniels in harm’s way every week. Chris Paul beat one-on-one (also holds but it wasn’t called)😞 pic.twitter.com/tA8WxAjrzm — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 OTs Brandon Coleman and Josh Conerly: Both Coleman (to be expected) and Conerly struggled with the Eagles pass rush. Both players didn’t look very good in the run game and yet again, both were called for pre-snap penalties. The disastrous season for Coleman continues, while it feels Conerly is regressing a bit lately. Come ON Conerly!!! Jeez – your gonna get JD killed pic.twitter.com/w1MMYHCnVR — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 Brandon Coleman just false-started on the X-point. Fourth pre-snap penalty and we’re not even at the half — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 My GOODNESS Brandon Coleman – can you AT LEAST get in the GD WAY!!! pic.twitter.com/SVECZ74lQI — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 HC Dan Quinn: Yes, Washington got a much-needed win at home against a division foe, but the team came out again in the first half, after a bye week, and looked unprepared and undisciplined. More pre-snap penalties plagued the offense, and the crowd let the team know it by reigning down boos from the stands early in the game. In his early week press conference, Quinn stressed the importance of playing four complete quarters of football. His team fell short of that yet again. 5th pre-snap penalty by Washington – this time it’s Conerly. — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 THIRD pre-snap penalty – right after a horrible screen play Crowd is booooing pic.twitter.com/46Fel6bSVH — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 Notes: QB Jayden Daniels was off in the first half. Let’s make no excuses about this. He, however, looked very sharp in the second half and really elevated his game hitting some big throws and using his legs when needed. His connection with Treylon Burks and Antonio Williams seems to be growing and he found Stefon Diggs for his fifth touchdown of the season. It seemed like the cascade of boos reigning down from the fans early in the game may have ignited a fire in him. Beautiful punt return by McCaffrey just before the half! pic.twitter.com/8Snh2kSNCo — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 TE Chig Okonkwo could have had a much bigger game if it wasn’t for his fumble in the first quarter and Jayden missing him on two pretty open throws. he did make a spectacular grab on a big third down conversion early in the third quarter. Absolutely AMAZING catch by Chig on 3rd down!!! pic.twitter.com/jSpNwupva3 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 Perfect throw. Fumble by Chig😡 Just a HORRIBLE three play series by Washington Embarrassing pic.twitter.com/T3iZzEie1Q — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) November 2, 2026 WR Stefon Diggs had a relatively quiet game but did secure his fifth touchdown of the season on a toss from Daniels in the second quarter. He finished with three receptions for 38 yards and the score. full_text: The Daily Slop – 2 November 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Commanders end the game with 27 unanswered points. Fans are pumped. pic.twitter.com/fasK0xkzzS — George Carmi (@Gcarmi21) November 2, 2026 Articles Commanders.com Instant Analysis: Rocky start, strong finish, key NFC East win The Commanders (2-4-1) emphasized the importance of being competitive for all four quarters coming out of their bye week. They still have some work to do there; head coach Dan Quinn said he thought they played well in three. They were still plagued by pre-snap penalties — they committed four fouls in their first nine plays — and had a fumble and a missed field goal on their opening two drives. Once the Commanders started to pick up steam, however, it was difficult for the Eagles to slow them down. They outgained the Eagles 318-201 for the rest of the night, recording 16 first downs and averaging nearly six yards per play. “After that TD drive [from the Eagles], I thought, ‘Okay, that’s it. There we are,'” head coach Dan Quinn said after the game. It still was not pretty; the Commanders had to send Drew Stevens out to kick four field goals — an issue Quinn said must be cleaned up — but their defense bought them time by putting consistent pressure on Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee and the rest of Philadelphia’s offense. The Commanders generated pressure on 46.5% of dropbacks — a season high, according to NFL+. It led to five sacks from the unit, one of which resulted in a fumble and recovery deep in Eagles territory. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE ESPN Can this win ignite a turnaround for Washington? The Commanders needed this win if just to settle a nervous building, knowing they couldn’t afford to lose to a wounded Eagles team at home. But if the Commanders beat the Rams at home next week, then they can talk about turnarounds. Washington committed nine penalties, one of which wiped out an interception deep in Philadelphia territory and continued a season-long theme. Quarterback Jayden Daniels wasn’t that sharp, but he made big plays and averaged 13.5 yards per completion against a defense that was healthier than it has been. Daniels got his first win since Oct. 5, 2025, and Washington’s defense hounded Tanner McKee all night and held Philly to 3.4 yards per play until late completions boosted that average to 3.9. Maybe this win doesn’t represent a turnaround, but the Commanders did what was necessary. Trend to watch: With Terry McLaurin done for the season, Washington needs other receivers to help more. Sunday night, Treylon Burks, who is taking over for McLaurin at the X spot, caught three passes for 81 yards, including a 53-yarder. Rookie slot receiver Antonio Williams caught a career-best five passes for 54 yards, including a 30-yard grab. Both receivers set up field goals with their long catches. — John Keim To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Commanders Instant Reaction: Depleted Front Delivers the Biggest Answer Against Eagles The penalties didn’t disappear after the bye , but Washington’s pass rush took over, and Rachaad White finished the job on the ground. With McLaurin out and three defensive tackles unavailable , Washington needed contributions from the players taking on more work. Antonio Williams got involved early , Charles Omenihu made his return count, and Stevens answered his opening miss with four straight makes. Those contributions helped the Commanders overcome another night of costly mistakes and keep their season alive. Washington’s defensive front finished this game. Dorance Armstrong was still making plays against the run, and Odafe Oweh beat Jordan Mailata off the edge for a late sack. A season-high five sacks is the production Washington has needed from this group; Washington did it without Daron Payne, Javon Kinlaw, and Jer’Zhan Newton, while holding Saquon Barkley to 30 yards on 13 carries. K’Lavon Chaisson’s late sack helped put Philadelphia in a desperate situation, and Rasul Douglas took advantage when McKee floated a ball up for grabs. Chaisson’s penalties were costly, but he also helped Washington close this game. After having an earlier interception erased by a flag, the defense made this takeaway count. Washington Post (paywall) Commanders take care of business against flailing Eagles in prime time For the Eagles (2-6), it was their sixth loss in a row. They were without starting quarterback Jalen Hurts, No. 1 wide receiver DeVonta Smith and a bevy of other core players because of various injuries. While Philadelphia had a better record before kickoff — and Washington has a lengthy injury report of its own — the Commanders were the superior team on paper. Daniels started to get groove back in the second quarter. He completed 7 of 10 passes for 70 yards and one touchdown in the period. Despite being shorthanded, the defensive line thrived. It generated consistent pressure on Philadelphia quarterback Tanner McKee and sacked him five times. While it must be noted that Barkley was playing through injury, Washington still deserves credit for limiting the Eagles to 3.1 yards per carry. With the D-line rolling, the secondary locked down Philadelphia’s passing attack. McKee only passed for 212 yards and threw an interception. It was easily the best performance of the season for defensive coordinator Daronte Jones’s group. The defense held the Eagles scoreless for eight consecutive possessions, forced two turnovers and was instrumental in the Commanders’ comeback. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) Commanders hand Eagles sixth straight loss. Can Washington build off this win? The Commanders didn’t seek outside help after losing Terry McLaurin for the rest of the season because of a patellar tendon injury. They relied on their in-house talent and, for the most part, their prudence paid off. Early mistakes by Washington’s pass catchers — a dropped pass, a fumble — turned into a standout performance from the Commanders’ skill players. Tight end Chig Okonkwo, who earlier fumbled after a short catch deep in Philadelphia’s territory, had perhaps the catch of the year on a third-and-6 in the third quarter. Receiver Treylon Burks led the way with 81 receiving yards on three catches, veteran Stefon Diggs caught the team’s lone passing touchdown and rookie wideout Antonio Williams had five catches for 54 yards. All had grabs that could’ve been incompletions To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) The Commanders, after an awful start, shut down Philly’s offense and won a critical divisional game Quinn got the complementary football he constantly talks about — good plays by the defense feeding into scoring drives by the offense. Luke McCaffrey had his best night of the season returning kicks. Drew Stevens nailed a huge 56-yard field goal late in the first quarter to get the Commanders on the board. If he’d missed, the Eagles would have taken over near midfield, ready to add to their lead. And Daniels came back from a big hit by Eagles linebacker Nolan Smith late in the first half that knocked the wind out of him. In the second half, he hit tight end Chig Okonkwo for 21 yards on a great catch by Okonkwo, found Treylon Burks on a double-move for a 53-yard strike that set up another Stevens field goal, and got Antonio Williams on a 30-yard vertical route in the…

title: NFL Power Rankings: Stacking all 32 teams for Week 9, plus best in-season trades
summary: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 9? We made our 1-32 list and picked the best trade deadline acquisitions of all time.
full_text:
If you've felt like games have been closer than ever in the 2026 NFL season , you're not wrong. There have been 71 games decided by one score (eight points or fewer), tied with 2022 for the most through Week 8 in NFL history, per ESPN Research.

 So how do teams start to really separate at this point of the season? Well, the easiest way might be by making big trades before  the Nov. 10 deadline . (Some teams have already been active , with the Bears adding former Titans DT Jeffery Simmons and the 49ers bringing back  DT  DeForest Buckner .)

 To preview how important the deadline can be, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to pick the best in-season trade acquisition by each team in their franchise's history. That includes the acquisition of draft picks who eventually became stars, like the Cowboys using a pick earned from the Herschel Walker trade to select running back Emmitt Smith in the 1990 draft.

 To form the 1-32 list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another. Here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

 
 The Broncos are in the top five of our rankings for the first time this season after defeating the Chiefs -- their fourth win while trailing in the fourth quarter this season. Quarterback Bo Nix now has 13 fourth-quarter comeback wins over his career, which is the most by any quarterback in their first three seasons since starts were first tracked in 1950. And Denver is now the favorite to win the AFC West on DraftKings . 
 The NFC North is the only division with all four teams in the top 15 of our rankings, starting with the Bears at No. 5 and ending with the Packers at No. 14. Minnesota dropped its first game of 2026 against Detroit, which scored the first fourth-quarter touchdown against Brian Flores' defense this season. The Bears, Packers and Lions also are all 4-1 in their past five games, as well .  
 Entering Sunday, the Ravens had -215 odds to make the playoffs on DraftKings. Those odds are now +280 (10th in the AFC) after their blowout loss to the Bills , and they're down six spots from last week's Power Rankings. Baltimore lost two quarterbacks to injury Sunday ( Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley ), which puts undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano  into the spotlight for their Thursday night matchup against Jacksonville (if he isn't out because of injury ). The Ravens have lost three straight games. 
 
 Let's get into the full list, starting with the a different No. 1 team from last week .

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 1. Buffalo Bills (6-1) 
 Week 8 result: Beat the Ravens 36-10 
 Week 8 ranking: 2 

 Best in-season trade acquisition ever: LB Cornelius Bennett in 1987

 

 Dubbed the "Trade of the Decade," the Bills acquired Bennett as part of a 10-player, three-team deal that sent Hall of Fame running back Eric Dickerson to the Colts. Bennett became a fixture on the Bills' Super Bowl defenses, notching 52.5 sacks and 19 forced fumbles in nine seasons with Buffalo, including three seasons with All-Pro honors. Only Bruce Smith and Darryl Talley have more career tackles in a Bills uniform than Bennett. -- Nick Suss 

 
 

 

 2. San Francisco 49ers (6-1) 
 Week 8 result: Bye 
 Week 8 ranking: 1 

 Best in-season trade acquisition ever:  DE Fred Dean in 1981

 

 Apologies to RB Christian McCaffrey  ( acquired in 2022 ), but you can draw a direct line between the Niners landing Dean and the rise of their dynasty. Upon Dean's induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame , former owner Eddie DeBartolo Jr. said "the greatness of the 49ers began with Fred Dean's arrival in San Francisco." The Niners sent a second-round pick to the Chargers in October 1981 for Dean with an eye toward bolstering the pass rush. Over the final 11 games, he recorded 12 sacks and earned first-team All-Pro honors. Dean added another in the playoffs as the Niners won their first Super Bowl (XVI) against Cincinnati. San Francisco won Super Bowl XIX as well, with Dean contributing four sacks in that postseason run. -- Nick Wagoner 

 
 

 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (5-2) 
 Week 8 result: Beat the Colts 42-7 
 Week 8 ranking: 6 

 Best in-season trade acquisition ever: WR Jakobi Meyers in 2025

 

 Of the eight in-season trades in which the Jaguars acquired a player for immediate help, adding Meyers last season stands out. Brian Thomas Jr . was out because of an ankle injury, Travis Hunter was out for the season because of a knee injury , Dyami Brown was dealing with a shoulder injury, Parker Washington had yet to emerge, and the Jaguars led the NFL in drops (19) when they sent fourth- and sixth-round picks to Las Vegas the day before the deadline. Meyers' precise route running and sure-handedness sparked an offense that averaged 22 points before his arrival to averaging 33 points after he joined the team. -- Michael DiRocco 

 
 

 4. Denver Broncos (6-2) 
 Week 8 result: Beat the Chiefs 28-24 
 Week 8 ranking: 8 

 Best in-season trade acquisition ever: WR Haven Moses in 1972

 

 The Broncos acquired Hall of Famer Gary Zimmerman just before the start of the 1993 regular season, so the wayback machine had to be fired up to get to the best in-season trade. The Broncos acquired Moses from the Bills via a one-for-one swap for Dwight Harrison. Moses played nine full seasons for the Broncos after the 1972 season, averaging at least 17 yards a catch in eight of those years and having 44 total touchdown catches. He is in the team's Ring of Fame and played on the franchise's first Super Bowl team in 1977. -- Jeff Legwold 

 
 

 5. Chicago Bears (6-2) 
 Week 8 result: Beat the Seahawks 34-17 
 Week 8 ranking: 7 

 Best in-season trade acquisition ever: DE Montez Sweat in 2023

 

 Three seasons before the Bears sent three draft picks , including two first-rounders, to Tennessee to acquire All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons , GM Ryan Poles got aggressive in 2023 to land Sweat. Chicago sent a 2024 second-rounder to Washington in exchange for Sweat, who led both the Commanders (6.5) and Bears (6.0) in sacks in 2023, making him the first player in NFL history to lead two different teams in sacks in the same season. Sweat recorded his first double-digit sack season and reached similar production in 2025, when he led Chicago with 10 sacks. Coach Ben Johnson called that season the best of Sweat's career. -- Courtney Cronin 

 
 

 6. Kansas City Chiefs (5-2) 
 Week 8 result: Lost to the Broncos 28-24 
 Week 8 ranking: 4 

 Best in-season trade acquisition ever: WR Kadarius Toney in 2022

 

 The Chiefs had one of the league's best offenses in 2022 and still added Toney, acquiring him from the Giants for a 2023 third-round pick and a 2023 sixth-round pick. He wasn't a major part of the offense, but he made contributing plays to help the Chiefs to the No. 1 seed in the postseason. The greatest game in Toney's career was Super Bowl LVII , when he scored a touchdown and generated a pivotal 65-yard punt return in the second half to help the Chiefs complete their comeback victory. That punt return is the longest in Super Bowl history. -- Nate Taylor 

 
 

 7. Minnesota Vikings (6-1) 
 Week 8 result: Lost to the Lions 19-15 
 Week 8 ranking: 3 

 Best in-season trade acquisition ever: DE Jim Marshall in 1961

 

 As they began their inaugural season, the Vikings acquired five players from the Browns in exchange for second- and 11th-round picks in the 1962 draft. Marshall was among that group and went on to become one of the best players in franchise history.  What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

full_text:

 The long-flowing trench coat is the star of this fit, but I love the commitment to the bit with black-tinted sunglasses and black combat boots supporting the look.

 Secondary shoutout to Lake's teammate -- Rams receiver Puka Nacua -- who also went with a trench coat vibe, except his is layered with an inner black leather jacket with overlapping lapel from luxury brand Umit Benan.

 Monday night drip

The Seahawks had their fair share of ties, too, including from wide receivers Tory Horton  and  Jaxon Smith-Njigba .

 

 

 Sunday's best

title: Falcons' James Pearce back from suspension, expected to play
summary: Pearce served an eight-game league suspension stemming from a February domestic violence arrest.
full_text:
James Pearce Jr . returned to the Atlanta Falcons ' roster Monday after an eight-game league suspension stemming from a February domestic violence arrest. 

 Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said last week that he plans to play Pearce on Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals , a game that will take place in Madrid (9:30 a.m. ET, NFL Network). Stefanski said he is not sure how much Pearce will play in his first game back.

 Pearce was suspended by the NFL due to a violation of the personal conduct policy at the end of training camp. He practiced with the team throughout camp. Pearce returned to the Falcons four weeks ago, but could not practice as part of the terms of an NFL suspension. He met individually with coaches and support staff, including a counselor. Pearce is expected to return to practice Wednesday.

 "He's done everything that we've asked of him, everything that he's been allowed to do," Stefanski said. "He's done a great job."

 Pearce, 23, was arrested Feb. 7 after allegedly ramming his vehicle into his ex-girlfriend and WNBA player Rickea Jackson's car several times near a Doral, Florida, police station. Police responded, and Pearce allegedly fled in his car before crashing and then fleeing on foot.

 Pearce was facing felony charges of aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing police and resisting arrest, as well as misdemeanor stalking, before entering into a one-year pretrial diversion program that allowed him to avoid trial. Those charges will be dropped if Pearce stays out of trouble for that year period, passes random drug tests and remains compliant with a mental health treatment program.

 Jackson filed a petition for a protective order against Pearce in February, and she dropped it in lieu of the intervention program. Pearce must also stay away from Jackson for a year as part of that program.

 

 Pearce had 10.5 sacks as a rookie last season and finished third in AP Defensive Rookie of the Year voting. Without him so far this season, the Falcons are seventh in the league in quarterback pressure rate (40%).

 Pearce declined to speak with the media during training camp and was prohibited from doing so during his suspension.

 The Falcons will get a one-week exemption for Pearce to be on the team's 53-man roster. The team waived linebacker Jared Ivey and defensive end Drake Jackson on Monday, as well.

 Stefanski said he doesn't necessarily see any challenge in adding Pearce to a pass-rushing group led by defensive ends  Za'Darius Smith  and Cameron Thomas and interior defensive linemen Gervon Dexter Sr ., Maason Smith and Brandon Dorlus . Stefanski said Monday that defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring) will be out Sunday. Smith leads the team with 4.5 sacks.

 "I see it as a positive to add a good player to the mix," Stefanski said. "I think the way [defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich] and the defensive staff have constructed this rush plan, obviously married up with the coverage plan, I think it's beneficial to all parties to do your job like you mentioned, but adding another good player to the mix is a good thing."

 Ulbrich said he has sat down with Pearce and believes Pearce "is in a great space."

 "Got to peek at him working out there," Ulbrich said. "He can't obviously participate with us, but some of the stuff he did physically looks good, looks like he's been working. So excited to get him back. ... Feel like he's in a really good place."

title: Record-setting deal? Trade? A look at Lamar Jackson's cloudy future with Ravens
summary: It's possible that Jackson's final snap with the Ravens ended with injury Sunday night.
full_text:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. -- Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson walked off the field while looking in disbelief at his misshapen and battered right thumb, a stunning turn of events that has become the lasting image amid the uncertainty surrounding the rest of this season as well as his future with the team. 
 
 After Sunday's 36-10 loss at the Buffalo Bills , Ravens coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson will undergo surgery and that his injury is "potentially" season-ending. There are more questions about what lies ahead next offseason for Jackson, given that 2027 is the final year of his contract and includes a massive salary cap hit. 
 
 It's possible that Jackson's final snap with the Ravens ended with his right hand colliding with Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau while Jackson was trying to throw a pass. His scintillating era of deep downfield passes and elusive scrambles with Baltimore might have closed with Jackson exiting the stadium with his right hand in a brace, which served as another reminder about how injuries have derailed some of his most recent seasons. 
 
 "I would absolutely hate him playing in a different uniform," said Rex Ryan, a former Ravens defensive coordinator and current ESPN analyst. "Ray Lewis always played for the Baltimore Ravens. And there is a statue of him, and there's going be another one of Lamar Jackson right by him. You are the Baltimore Ravens. To me, he needs to stay in Baltimore. Is there another situation that he wants to play in more than a Baltimore Raven?" 
 
 Jackson's future with the Ravens is clouded because his $84.34 million cap figure next year is considered untenable because of Baltimore's challenging cap situation. The Ravens are $45.94 million over the cap in 2027, which is the worst in the NFL, according to Over The Cap. 
 
 Over the past 10 months, Ravens owner Steve Bisciotti and general manager Eric DeCosta have publicly stressed urgency about getting a contract extension with Jackson. But there have been no signs that the sides are close to a new deal, which has only heightened the speculation of what might happen after this season. 
 
 
 
 "I'm optimistic," DeCosta said two months ago on Sept. 2. "We would love to get a deal done as soon as possible." 
 
 Jackson, who doesn't have an agent and represents himself, has the final say because he has no-trade and no-tag clauses. It's possible that Jackson is waiting for others to reset the quarterback market before signing a new deal with Baltimore. 
 
 Young star quarterbacks such as  Caleb Williams , Drake Maye , Jayden Daniels and Bo Nix are eligible for contract extensions after this season. The highest-paid player in the NFL is currently Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes , who is averaging $63 million per season. 
 
 If the Ravens aren't comfortable heading into the final year of Jackson's deal without an extension in place, they could explore a trade. Jackson would likely need to give Baltimore a list of teams for whom he would be willing to waive his no-trade clause. 
 
 The other factor is level of compensation for Jackson. When he's healthy, Jackson is among the top players in the NFL. A two-time NFL MVP, he ranks second in career passer rating (102.7) and first in career rushing yards by a quarterback (6,666).  
 
 But Jackson has struggled to stay healthy lately, missing 18 games due to ankle, hamstring, back, knee and thumb injuries over the past six seasons. If Jackson misses the rest of this season, he would have started and finished 14 of 34 games in 2025 and 2026. 
 
 "We want another window, and Lamar knows that," Bisciotti said 10 months ago. "I think that he's amenable to doing something that mirrors the last deal he did, although the annual number will be a little higher. But I'm hoping that it's plug a new number in the same contract he signed last year and move on." 
 
 With how Baltimore has flopped without Jackson, this season has underscored how much the Ravens need Jackson. But they also need a new deal with Jackson sooner rather than later.
